# musubix5 clean foundation design

## Architecture constraints

- Runtime: Node.js 20 or newer, TypeScript strict mode, ESM.
- No `any`, broad catch, silent fallback, or success-shaped failure.
- Canonical JSON uses sorted object keys, UTF-8, and one trailing LF.
- Persisted `order`, not wall-clock time, establishes chronology.
- Every normal record binds an active positive CHANGE generation; legacy
  generation-less records read as generation 1 without rewriting.
- Source-of-truth journals are append-only. Mutable JSON files are derived
  projections and never chronology authorities.
- Stateful persistence validates and journals under its required lease set.
  TDD runners and source-pair execution hold no CHANGE, maintenance, projection
  or append lease; DES-M5-023 defines short preflight and commit sections with
  optimistic input/target revalidation between them.
- musubix3 and musubix4 remain read-only.

## Design-approved execution-policy projection

Canonical encoding is UTF-8 JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, no
insignificant whitespace, and exactly one trailing LF byte.

```json
{"architecture":{"forbidCycles":true,"rules":[]},"attestation":{"githubOidc":{"mode":"off"},"maxAgeSeconds":3600,"maxFutureSkewSeconds":60,"mode":"local","trustedPublicKeys":[]},"codeGraph":{"mode":"compatible"},"commands":[{"args":["run","typecheck"],"command":"npm","name":"typecheck","required":true,"timeoutMs":120000},{"args":["run","build"],"command":"npm","name":"build","required":true,"timeoutMs":120000},{"adapter":"vitest","args":["vitest","run"],"command":"npx","name":"test","required":true,"timeoutMs":180000},{"args":["scripts/run-codegraph-tests.mjs","--report","{reportPath}"],"command":"node","name":"codegraph-tests","required":true,"tddArgs":["--test-id","{testId}"],"tddReport":{"format":"musubix-json","path":".musubix/cache/test-results/{testId}.json"},"testReport":{"format":"musubix-json","path":".musubix/cache/test-results/codegraph.json"},"timeoutMs":300000},{"args":["run","test:compat"],"command":"npm","name":"compatibility","required":true,"timeoutMs":180000},{"args":["run","pack:check"],"command":"npm","name":"pack-check","required":true,"timeoutMs":120000},{"args":["run","pack:smoke"],"command":"npm","name":"pack-smoke","required":true,"timeoutMs":180000}],"formal":{"minModeledFraction":0,"solver":"none","timeoutMs":12000},"mutation":{"mode":"compatible"},"requiredChecks":["requirements","design","constitution","trace","graph","commands"],"schemaVersion":1,"tdd":{"redPreflightCommands":[]},"thresholds":{"design":1,"implementation":1,"tests":1},"workflow":{"maxAgeSeconds":3600,"maxEventSkewMs":null,"maxFutureSkewSeconds":60,"maxTranscriptBytes":125000000,"maxTranscriptLineBytes":1000000,"mode":"compatible"}}
```

`qualityProfile` is excluded because the projection contains every effective
policy field and the profile label has no independent enforcement effect.
`language` is display-only. `workflow.maxEventSkewMs: null` canonically means
that the optional event-skew bound is disabled, and
`workflow.maxTranscriptLineBytes` is the materialized default. The
`workflow.maxTranscriptBytes` value is an explicit approved increase to
125,000,000 bytes, within the REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-007 bound, so the complete
107,405,647-byte source can be processed without truncation.

The musubix5-only orchestration extension is also design-approved. It is
disabled by default at both repairable boundaries but fixes positive limits
before verified-auto can be enabled:

```json
{"approvalAutomation":{"design":{"mode":"manual","producerRepairLimit":3,"repairPlannerBudgetUnits":1000,"reviewerBudgetUnits":1000},"release":{"mode":"manual"},"requirements":{"mode":"manual","producerRepairLimit":3,"repairPlannerBudgetUnits":1000,"reviewerBudgetUnits":1000}}}
```

### Test runtime extension policy (generation-8 contract)

Following ADR-0009's approvalAutomation contract, the optional TOP-LEVEL
`.musubix/config.json.testRuntime` is a versioned extension, not a command
member. Its entire normalized value and expected digest are fixed here BEFORE
design approval. Use canonicalBytes (UTF-8 object-key ordering, compact JSON,
preserved array order and exactly one trailing LF) and lowercase SHA-256.
The exact six fields below are closed; unknown keys, additional/missing input
paths, different command names/order or policy values reject. No implicit
defaults or configurable expected-digest override is allowed.

```json
{"calibration":{"maxWidthMs":1,"samples":8},"commandNames":["codegraph-tests","compatibility","test"],"inputs":[".musubix/config.json","package-lock.json","package.json","packages/analysis/src/adapters.ts","packages/analysis/src/candidate-gate.ts","packages/analysis/src/canonical.ts","packages/analysis/src/config.ts","packages/analysis/src/gate.ts","packages/analysis/src/parallel-runtime.ts","packages/analysis/src/process.ts","packages/analysis/src/tdd-source-pair.ts","packages/analysis/src/tdd.ts","packages/analysis/src/test-runtime.ts","scripts/run-codegraph-tests.mjs","scripts/test-runtime/coordinator-reporter.mjs","scripts/test-runtime/stable-wall-clock.mjs","scripts/test-runtime/vitest-setup.mjs","tests/global-setup.ts","tsconfig.build.json","tsconfig.json","vitest.config.ts"],"kind":"stable-test-wall-clock-v1","reporterMode":"append-after-native-v1","schemaVersion":1}
```

Expected profile SHA-256:
`f9fbe94729722eaaea1f1e49bbaf6c48053ea1ed6a8498a2287dbfe4a20bf06e`

This is the normative policy digest, not a prediction of future implementation
file hashes. The 21 listed paths are the COMPLETE runtime-specific inventory:
snapshot each regular file's full raw bytes, mode and size, with no glob,
symlink, field omission or implicitly discovered helper. In particular config
means the full raw config file; only its testRuntime object is normalized for
the separate policy comparison. Record raw implementation input hashes per
execution after implementation. Additional runtime helpers require an explicit
inventory/design revision; built-in Node modules and locked external packages
are not extra local paths. The ordinary candidate/workspace source/dependency
closure still binds production code beyond this runtime-specific inventory.

Existing loadApprovalProjectionConfig filters top-level keys using its allowlist
BEFORE parseConfig; that list contains commands but not testRuntime, just as it
excludes approvalAutomation/candidateGate. It is intentionally NOT expanded or
otherwise changed. The current approval.ts design projection is therefore
unchanged when this exact top-level instance is later added. Approval covers
these normative bytes and expected digest, not a new projection exception or
transfer of an old approval. After current generation-8 requirements/design
approval (including any explicit design-only supersession), fresh Red precedes implementing extension parsing/digest enforcement,
adding the config instance, and deriving the new candidate-gate member.
After Red, packages/analysis/src/test-runtime.ts holds the expected digest in
a closed constant table keyed by (kind,schemaVersion). Runtime compares the
effective canonical policy with that constant, not a live approval record or
normative-file lookup. EVIDENCE-001 and the fresh gate-fingerprint regression
prove constant == normative design digest == effective config digest. Policy
changes require a NEW kind and fresh design approval before implementation,
never replacement of the value under an existing approved key. Detached and
standalone runs use the same versioned constant/profile without an approval
ledger dependency. No pre-Red parser, candidate-gate edit or config instance
is authorized. Governance approval and runtime verification remain distinct.

The `gate-input-fingerprint-v1.config` value is the following derived canonical
object. `approval` is the inner `approval` value from the requirements-stage
projection; `approvalAutomation` and `candidateGate` are the inner values of
their wrapper blocks; `executionPolicy` is the complete unwrapped execution-
policy block and carries the single execution-policy `schemaVersion`.
The new sibling testRuntime is the exact versioned object above, with the
pre-fixed profile digest above. This is gate fingerprint input, NOT approval
projection config. Its derivation in candidate-gate.ts is post-Red work;
legacy projects with no design-declared extension retain the old object with
no testRuntime member, null or default. Do not claim the current binary already
produces the generation-8 fingerprint before implementation.

## DES-M5-001: Compatibility oracle adapter
Responsibilities: Build the pinned musubix3 v0.1.18 source, capture command contracts, execute the approved Node.js and operating-system matrix, normalize only approved package or executable tokens, and compare observable CLI, API, configuration, package, and filesystem behavior.
Interfaces: `BaselineOracle.acquire()`, `BaselineOracle.capture(invocation)`, `ContractComparator.compare(expected, actual)`.
Constraints: The pinned commit and fixture hashes are mandatory; `MUSUBIX3_Z3` and `MUSUBIX3_LEAN` are not renamed during normalization; mismatches are classified and cannot be silently accepted.
Requirements: REQ-M5-COMPAT-001 REQ-M5-COMPAT-002 REQ-M5-COMPAT-003 REQ-M5-COMPAT-004 REQ-M5-COMPAT-005 REQ-M5-COMPAT-008 REQ-M5-COMPAT-009 REQ-M5-COMPAT-011 REQ-M5-COMPAT-012 REQ-M5-COMPAT-013
ADRs: ADR-0002 ADR-0007 ADR-0036
Depends-On: DES-M5-003

## DES-M5-002: Public CLI and package facade
Responsibilities: Expose the `musubix5` executable, compatible command hierarchy, the complete candidate-snapshot lifecycle, public baseline creation and current-workflow verification, public library exports, package assets, and isolated-installation behavior.
Interfaces: `runCli(argv, environment)`, `parallel baseline create <change-id> [--root <directory>] [--json]`, `workflow verify-current [--session-id <uuid>] [--transcript-root <path>] [--compatible] [--root <directory>] [--json]`, `candidate-snapshot create <change-id> [--root <directory>] [--json]`, `candidate-snapshot list [--root <directory>] [--json]`, `candidate-snapshot show <change-id-or-snapshot-id> [--root <directory>] [--json]`, `candidate-snapshot delete <change-id-or-snapshot-id> --deleted-by <name> --confirm [--root <directory>] [--json]`, `change-record <change-id> requirements|design --operation-id <id> [--json]`, `workflow declaration supersede WORKFLOW_INVOCATION_REUSED --skill <skill> --phase <phase> --recorded-at <timestamp> [--index <n>] --approver <name> --reason <text> --confirm [--json]`, `release-operation authorize <operation-id>`, `release-operation validate <operation-id>`, `release-operation status <operation-id>`, package exports `./domain`, `./analysis`, `./attestation`.
Constraints: Only the `musubix5` bin is published; every other intentional difference requires registered governance artifacts; command handlers return typed outcomes mapped centrally to exit codes. Baseline creation delegates all state rules to DES-M5-012: malformed identifier/usage is exit 2 `CLI_ERROR` whose detail retains `WORKSPACE_CHANGE_ID_INVALID`, while `WORKSPACE_BASELINE_CHANGE_INVALID`, `WORKSPACE_BASELINE_CONTEXT_INVALID`, `WORKSPACE_BASELINE_COMMIT_REQUIRED`, `WORKSPACE_BASELINE_DIRTY`, and `WORKSPACE_BASELINE_CONFLICT` are exit 1 domain envelopes. Current-workflow verification delegates discovery, sanitization, verification, and persistence to DES-M5-018; it renders sorted ambiguity candidates and never constructs a shell command from discovered paths. `WORKFLOW_CURRENT_MISSING`, `WORKFLOW_CURRENT_AMBIGUOUS`, and `WORKFLOW_SESSION_MISMATCH`, including a syntactically malformed `--session-id`, are exit 1 domain envelopes; other malformed options, unsafe roots, `WORKFLOW_SANITIZE_INVALID`, `WORKFLOW_TRANSCRIPT_SIZE`, `WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_INVALID`, duplicate-source/event failures, and strict transcript verification failures retain exit 2 `CLI_ERROR` with the originating diagnostic in detail. Approval-precondition rejections surfaced by DES-M5-006 are emitted as exit 2 `CLI_ERROR` envelopes, using JSON on stdout when `--json` is requested, and include the DES-M5-006 recovery text verbatim without rewriting it. A phase-checkpoint operation ID matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`; malformed supplied IDs and use on unsupported phases are pre-lease exit 2 `CLI_ERROR` with no persistence. Use on an initial requirements/design checkpoint or omission when supersession is required is determined under the CHANGE lease after pending-checkpoint recovery, may leave those recovery completions persisted, and then exits 2 without journaling the requested operation. Exact scoped checkpoint replay is exit 0; divergent reuse or a distinct operation against a still-current checkpoint is exit 1 `CHANGE_GENERATION_DUPLICATE`; invalid persisted checkpoint-journal evidence is exit 1 `CHANGE_CHECKPOINT_JOURNAL_INVALID`, while status remains exit 0 with `ready: false`. Malformed workflow selectors or timestamps, negative/non-integer indices, unsupported correction diagnostic codes, blank reason, or missing confirmation/approver/reason are exit 2 `CLI_ERROR`; multiple implicit active CHANGEs are exit 1 `CHANGE_GENERATION_MIXED`; an abandoned/null or otherwise ineligible known sole CHANGE is exit 1 `CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE`; fencing loss is exit 1 `LEASE_FENCED`; other well-formed selectors or evidence that do not resolve the required correction state are exit 1 `WORKFLOW_DECLARATION_CORRECTION_INVALID`; success and exact replay are exit 0. The `candidate-snapshot` parent and subcommand help are additive and deterministic. `create` validates syntax, treats its CHANGE argument as a confirmation token for the sole implicit active CHANGE, and calls DES-M5-012 with read-only approval/quality evaluators supplied by DES-M5-006 and DES-M5-015; DES-M5-012 invokes those evaluators again under the CHANGE lease before append. `list` and `show` combine DES-M5-012 structural projections with DES-M5-006 approval and DES-M5-015 quality/gate evaluation without acquiring a lease; `delete` supplies the same evaluators to DES-M5-012 for protected tombstone persistence and under-lease protection revalidation. Candidate lifecycle exit 2 `CLI_ERROR` covers usage, workspace availability, invalid snapshot evidence, snapshot-attributable journal defects for `create`/`delete`, and every shared-chain defect observed by `list`/`show`; candidate lifecycle exit 1 preserves conflict, protection, replay-actor, approval/quality, and checkpoint-journal domain diagnostics for `create`/`delete`. Create, projection, and deletion JSON contain exactly the fields defined by REQ-M5-WORKTREE-005 through REQ-M5-WORKTREE-007; live projection deletion keys are omitted. Human output renders the same state plus executable guidance and never exposes origins or secrets.
Batch-Checkpoint-Diagnostics: `CHANGE_WORKSPACE_DRIFT`, `CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY`, and `LEASE_FENCED` are included in every closed domain-error allowlist for a command that can acquire a CHANGE or change-projection lease, including `change-record`, candidate lifecycle, integration finalization/resume, reopen, abandon, and checkpoint recovery; they map to exit 1 and retain their code prefixes in JSON and human output. Recovery callback errors pass through with their original typed diagnostic and exit class before marker creation; they are not remapped to a generic integration conflict. Named lease acquisition reports the requested lease rather than the legacy repository-order wording.
Source-Supersession-CLI: Add the distinct `tdd source-supersession` command family; no existing maintenance command aliases it. The following grammar is exhaustive; every invocation also permits `[--root <directory>] [--json]`. `SCOPE` expands to required `--change <changeId> --generation <positive-integer> --operation-id <id>`; IDs match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`. `TARGET` expands to required `--test <testId> --cycle <cycleId> --terminal-kind <green|refactor|migration|source-supersession> --terminal-order <positive-integer> --terminal-sha256 <sha256> --old-fingerprint <sha256> --requirement <requirementId> --command <configured-name>`. Digests are 64 lowercase hex characters. All supplied selectors are confirmation values, never permission to infer another target.

- `tdd source-supersession prepare SCOPE TARGET --mode test-only --old-block <regular-file> --hunk-review <regular-json-file> --reason <text>` creates a sealed review after fresh synthetic-pair verification.
- `tdd source-supersession prepare SCOPE TARGET --mode behavior-change --replacement-cycle <cycleId> --reason <text>` seals an independent genuine replacement Red/Green link; old-block reconstruction is not required for this mode.
- `tdd source-supersession approve SCOPE --artifact-sha256 <sha256> --approver <name> --confirm` records dedicated exact-hash approval, not requirements/design approval or TDD credit.
- `tdd source-supersession record SCOPE --artifact-sha256 <sha256> --approval-sha256 <sha256>` admits the sealed request and writes its journal-first terminal. The artifact contains the mandatory full target and mode; they cannot be overridden here.
- `tdd source-supersession resume SCOPE --request-sha256 <sha256>` completes only a matching journaled operation's missing suffix; a completed match returns its stored result.
- `tdd source-supersession replay SCOPE --request-sha256 <sha256>` is read-only, requires a completed exact match, and returns the stored result with zero appends.

Preparation rejects a reused operation ID with divergent artifacts; a changed preparation requires a new ID, new reports and new approval. `prepare` and `approve` alone are never supersession completion. Missing/extra options, unknown enum values, blank reason/approver, missing confirmation, malformed hashes/IDs/integers, mode-incompatible options and unsafe paths are exit 2 `CLI_ERROR`, with closed `details.reason` enum `missing-option | unknown-option | invalid-enum | blank-value | confirmation-required | invalid-selector | mode-option-conflict | unsafe-path`. Readable but invalid JSON/schema is a domain rejection, not missing usage. Success and completed exact replay exit 0; domain, pending, ledger and registered lease failures exit 1; operational I/O failures are exit 2 `TDD_SOURCE_IO_FAILED` as specified by DES-M5-023, never a success-shaped domain result. Human output preserves diagnostic code and reason; JSON uses the same typed envelope and stdout convention as this facade. `prepare` success contains exactly `{schemaVersion:1, operationId, artifactPath, artifactSha256, mode, target, scope}`; `approve` success exactly `{schemaVersion:1, operationId, artifactSha256, approvalPath, approvalSha256}`; record/resume/replay success is the immutable DES-M5-023 result (no invocation-local replay boolean).
Source-Supersession-Governance: The exact additive registry is the design table below, authorized by already-approved REQ-M5-COMPAT-013 and REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006. No requirements/inventory amendment is prerequisite to implementing these rows. DES-M5-001 implements registry assertions in `packages/analysis/src/compatibility-oracle.ts` and `tests/compatibility-oracle.test.ts`; DES-M5-002 updates help in `packages/cli/src/main.ts`, fixtures in `tests/cli-help-contract.test.ts` and `tests/cli-json-error-contract.test.ts`, and `docs/migration-guide.md`. Preserve the pinned baseline fixtures byte-for-byte; register candidate-only additions and recalculate only candidate aggregate fixture hashes. CHANGE-0017 remains generation 5 with the approved Requirements set; the normal stale-design review/approval/checkpoint precedes Red/implementation, without an artificial requirements revision or bootstrap reset.

## DES-M5-003: Canonical serialization and identity service
Responsibilities: Canonicalize typed records, hash bytes, derive canonical repository and candidate identities, verify producer identity, and expose deterministic comparison helpers.
Interfaces: `canonicalBytes(value)`, `sha256(bytes)`, `canonicalRepositoryIdentity(origin, repositoryRoot)`, `identityForCandidate()`, `verifyBinding(record, context)`.
Constraints: Canonical bytes exclude schema-declared display metadata only; no caller may invent its own hashing or path normalization. Repository-aware callers obtain configured origin values with `git config --get-all remote.origin.url`, without `url.*.insteadOf` rewriting, use the first value because Git fetch uses the first configured URL, and always supply the absolute `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` path as the missing-or-empty-origin fallback parameter. `canonicalRepositoryIdentity` implements the exact REQ-M5-WORKTREE-001 grammar and normalization order, returns only `repository:<sha256>`, and never logs or returns the raw origin. Callers discard all acquired origin values after canonicalization and must not persist, return, or render them in evidence, manifests, diagnostics, or wrapped errors. Every persisted, compared, manifested, fingerprinted, runner-derived, or reported `repositoryId` originates from this interface.
Requirements: REQ-M5-COMPAT-003 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-002 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-003 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-005 REQ-M5-QUALITY-003 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-001
ADRs: ADR-0003 ADR-0005 ADR-0010 ADR-0014

## DES-M5-004: Ordered journal and lease service
Responsibilities: Allocate repository-wide order values, serialize stateful writers and the shared CHANGE projection, maintain fencing tokens, verify journal chains, rebuild projections, diagnose corruption, recover interrupted requirements/design writes, and persist generation-qualified records supplied by their owning coordinators.
Interfaces: `withChangeLease(changeId, operation)`, `withChangeProjectionLease(operation)`, `withOrderLease(operation)`, `writeChangeProjection(expectedLeases, evidence)`, `allocateOrder(session?)`, `append(record, session?)`, `verifyJournal()`, `classifyJournalDefect(recordPath, records)`, `rebuildProjection(kind)`, `loadByIdempotencyKey(key)`, `phaseCheckpointOperation(changeId, generation, phase, operationId)`, `reconcilePendingPhaseCheckpoints(root, changeId, expectedLeases: ChangeProjectionAppendLeaseSet): Promise<{ recoveredPhaseCheckpoints }>`, `generationOrderKey(changeId, generation, phase, scopeId?)`.
Constraints: Authoritative normal and bootstrap journals are tracked under `.musubix/journal`; the repository common Git directory contains shared leases, scratch files, the control-worktree locator, and the DES-M5-PARALLEL-004-owned managed parallel workspace/heartbeat area; stateful writes target the designated control worktree; a fresh clone verifies the tracked chain and seeds the next order from its maximum valid order. Requirements/design supersession appends a normal-journal `change-phase-checkpoint` record whose idempotency key is exactly `change-phase-checkpoint:<changeId>:g<generation>:<phase>:<operationId>` and whose schema-v1 payload/envelope exactly follow REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005 `Checkpoint-Journal`. Workspace requirement-batch recording appends `change-batch-checkpoint-v1` with the identity and exact payload owned exclusively by DES-M5-022 before order/projection mutation; DES-M5-004 provides generic journal, order, and lease primitives but never imports or calls the workspace coordinator. Expensive workspace fingerprint preparation occurs before write-lease acquisition. Every read-modify-write of `changes.json` has one outermost command coordinator acquire the target CHANGE lease and then the repository-wide `change-projection` lease before loading the writable projection; inner recovery, order, and projection helpers receive the already-acquired lease handles and never reacquire either lease, and no path acquires either lease while holding the global order lease. DES-M5-004 requirements/design recovery and DES-M5-022 batch recovery independently scan their owned valid journal kinds and project only persisted payloads, reusing an existing exact order identity or appending it once when absent. Gate and status remain read-only and report pending records without projecting them. New workflow corrections are normal-journal records and their JSON file is a deterministic projection rebuilt in ascending journal order; duplicate or divergent orders are a non-pass merge diagnostic. Each lease waits 25 milliseconds for at most 400 attempts, uses a 30-second TTL, and renews every 10 seconds. Expired named leases are reclaimed with an incremented fencing token by atomically moving the stale lease directory before creating the successor; stale holders cannot renew or authorize a write. The projection writer creates and syncs a temporary file, immediately verifies both persisted lease owners and fencing tokens, and performs a platform-safe atomic replacement only while both remain current. Generic lease primitives surface a typed acquisition timeout naming the requested lease kind; outer command coordinators apply the diagnostic mappings below. Stale projection-write ownership maps to `LEASE_FENCED`, and no failed writer reports success.
Order-Session: `allocateOrder(session?)` and `append(record, session?)` acquire the order lease only when no session is supplied. A supplied append session is a non-reentrant capability whose current fence is asserted before mutation and allows recovery inside a finalization scope without reacquisition.
Lease-Set-Type: DES-M5-004 owns `ChangeProjectionAppendLeaseSet = Readonly<{ changeLeases: readonly ChangeLeaseHandle[]; projectionLease: ChangeProjectionLeaseHandle; appendSession?: AppendLeaseSession }>`: `changeLeases` contains exactly one handle per distinct selected CHANGE in byte-wise CHANGE ID order, `projectionLease` is the repository-wide change-projection handle, and the append session is optional only for ordinary lifecycle/checkpoint coordinators whose journal/order primitives acquire it internally. Finalization supplies all three, and DES-M5-MULTI-CHANGE-002 materialization asserts the append session is present as well as every supplied handle being current. Recovery validates that its selected CHANGE belongs to the supplied set, awaits every journal/order/projection mutation, and never reacquires a supplied lease.
Lease-Renewal: `withRenewingLease()` schedules renewal every 10 seconds and first reads the durable fencing counter for the named lease; any value other than the handle's fencing token marks the lease lost before a temporary owner is written. It then verifies the current owner token/fence, creates its temporary owner file strictly inside the held lease directory, renames it over that directory's `owner.json`, and re-reads both the owner and durable fencing counter. A stale-directory takeover increments the durable counter, so path recreation cannot let the expired holder re-authorize itself. Mismatch, missing paths, or renewal failure mark the lease lost, and operations repeat the durable-counter plus owner check before journal append, order append, and projection rename. Long synchronous trace, graph, or fingerprint work occurs before lease acquisition so it cannot starve renewal callbacks. Only command wrappers for the enumerated REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 lifecycle read-modify-write paths map both CHANGE and change-projection acquisition timeouts to exit 1 `CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY`. Every change-projection acquisition timeout retains that diagnostic; candidate/finalization CHANGE and append timeout mappings belong to DES-M5-MULTI-CHANGE-003, and unrelated existing CHANGE-lease consumers retain their prior diagnostics. Acquisition-time fencing tokens in `change-batch-checkpoint-v1` records are audit-only positive integers, are not compared with a later replay holder, and are not replay credentials. This audit-only rule does not cover finalization lease-context records: their CHANGE/projection/append tokens are used for exact persisted context/marker binding and monotonic-floor comparisons against current resume handles under DES-M5-MULTI-CHANGE-008.
Batch-Checkpoint-Boundary: Batch-specific append, key derivation, replay comparison, and schema validation are not owned by this service. DES-M5-004 exposes only generic `append(record, session?)` and `loadByIdempotencyKey(key)` primitives for those operations; DES-M5-022 composes them with DES-M5-007 validation. DES-M5-004 neither imports DES-M5-007 nor calls `appendBatchCheckpoint()`, preserving the dependency direction DES-M5-022 → DES-M5-007 → DES-M5-004.
Source-Supersession-Boundary: DES-M5-023 likewise composes these generic primitives with DES-M5-007 validators for `tdd-source-supersession-v1`. It owns request/key derivation and missing-suffix recovery; this service never imports or calls that coordinator or selector. The source coordinator acquires CHANGE, change-projection, then append leases and supplies all live handles to suffix writers. Every TDD read-modify-write uses the same short projection critical section, merges into the latest ledger, and never reacquires a supplied handle. Preparation and runner execution remain outside the projection/append critical section; admission rechecks the frozen inputs under live leases. Journal envelope order is separate from the later operation evidence order, allocated only after durable journal append. Existing batch checkpoint and finalization recovery, lease-context semantics, diagnostic mappings and ownership stay unchanged.
Journal-Classification: Snapshot create/delete attribute predecessor/hash defects to the later record, duplicate/out-of-sequence defects to the deterministic non-canonical or lexicographically greatest path, and classify the earliest defective order; list/show intentionally use a uniform candidate-journal error, while gate/status use `CHANGE_CHECKPOINT_JOURNAL_INVALID`.
Requirements: REQ-M5-APPROVAL-008 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-002 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-003 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-004 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-005 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-005 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-006 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-007
ADRs: ADR-0003 ADR-0010 ADR-0014 ADR-0015 ADR-0035 ADR-0036
Depends-On: DES-M5-003

## DES-M5-005: Lifecycle state machine
Responsibilities: Enforce predecessor rules, create/resume/abandon versioned CHANGE generations, parse CHANGE document status for repository-current selection, persist phase transitions, reject cross-generation evidence, and expose resumable CHANGE status.
Interfaces: `transition(changeId, generation, requestedPhase, evidenceHeads)`, `recordApprovedPhase(changeId, phase, { operationId? })`, `reopen(changeId, requirementIds?, idempotencyKey): { generation, resumed }`, `abandon(changeId, { reason, approver, confirm })`, `activeGeneration(changeId)`, `resolveChangeContext(root, { changeId?, maintenance?, confirmationToken? })`, `projectPhaseCheckpoint(record): { semanticPhaseKey, orderPhaseKey, ordinal }`, `contemporaneousPredecessor(change, predecessorPhase, dependentOrder)`, `status(changeId)`, `resume(invocationId)`.
Constraints: A transition commits only after validation and required evidence checks; reopen is lease-bound and idempotent, starts only at impact, resolves the exact current CHANGE requirement set, creates qualified order keys, and owns the cross-generation unchanged-fingerprint exemption while preserving `--allow-unchanged` for ordinary initial recording; every later transition revalidates the CHANGE requirement set and emits `CHANGE_GENERATION_REQUIREMENTS` on drift; abandoning requires nonblank reason/approver and confirmation, leaves no active generation, and permits only reopen plus non-credit targeted maintenance; within one CHANGE the greatest non-abandoned generation is active. Implicit repository context selects the sole explicit active document or status-less legacy document whose chronology has a positive generation without terminal full-set quality, a null generation after abandonment, or no chronology, counts it toward the one-active limit, and classifies a status-less chronology with terminal quality and no later active/abandoned generation as completed without rewriting it. Multiple active/legacy-active documents return `CHANGE_GENERATION_MIXED` and persist nothing; an explicit CHANGE ID never falls back to implicit selection; `maintenance: true` permits only the named read-only status, branch-retaining cleanup, and REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005 candidate-snapshot list/show/delete maintenance operations, including exact snapshot-ID maintenance for foreign or unknown CHANGE history, and grants no evidence credit. Per-requirement batch predecessor checks are independent; optional Refactor occurs only after Green; unsupported formal obligations are classified without proof credit. Malformed supplied operation IDs and unsupported phases fail before lease acquisition. Initial requirements/design use or missing supersession IDs are decided only after CHANGE-lease acquisition and pending recovery, may retain those recovery writes, and journal nothing for the rejected request. Under the CHANGE lease, DES-M5-005 invokes DES-M5-004 recovery and scoped replay lookup before checking whether the phase is currently valid. Exact replay returns exit 0 even after full projection; divergent reuse returns exit 1 `CHANGE_GENERATION_DUPLICATE`; a different operation ID against a current checkpoint also returns that diagnostic. With no scoped record and an invalidated checkpoint, the service validates the current approval manifest, computes fingerprints/requirements, derives the next phase-scoped ordinal, journals first, appends or reuses the ordinal-qualified order record, and atomically replaces `changes.json`. Supersession is exempt from unchanged-fingerprint rejection because approval head plus operation ID is the audited identity; `--allow-unchanged` is neither required nor replay-bound. Reopen and abandon first validate syntax and lifecycle eligibility without a lease, then acquire the CHANGE lease, revalidate eligibility, reconcile the departing active generation exactly once from journaled inputs, and only then snapshot or abandon it. The public semantic phase key remains `requirements` or `design`; the evidence-order phase is ordinal-qualified as `requirements:<n>` or `design:<n>` after ordinal 1, exactly as quality uses `quality:<n>`. The projection stores the current checkpoint in `phases.requirements` or `phases.design`, moves prior entries to `requirementsHistory[]` or `designHistory[]`, stores `requirementsOrdinal` or `designOrdinal` on every current and historical checkpoint, and stores operation ID on each superseding checkpoint. Validation resolves singular-phase order through the persisted ordinal-qualified evidence-order key and validates every history entry. Cross-phase ordering uses the contemporaneous predecessor: for a dependent record at order O, select from the predecessor phase's current plus history entries the greatest order strictly less than O; thus each design checkpoint binds the requirements checkpoint preceding it and each Red batch binds the design checkpoint preceding that Red, while later supersession never retroactively inverts historical phase order. Missing contemporaneous predecessors remain `CHANGE_PHASE_ORDER`. Each generation snapshot includes both named history arrays and ordinals; reopen copies them into `generationHistory`, clears them from the new active generation, and restarts requirements/design ordinals at 1. RecordedAt diagnostics use each entry's own distinct order. Other stale states re-enter through the approval cascade or a new generation.
Projection-Serialization: The outermost coordinator for impact, requirements, design, full-set or batch Red/Implementation/Green, quality, abandon, reopen, and checkpoint recovery acquires CHANGE then change-projection leases exactly once, passes those handles to recovery and `writeChangeProjection()`, reloads `changes.json`, re-resolves sole-active or explicit CHANGE selection, and repeats generation, requirement-set, duplicate, predecessor, and unchanged-fingerprint validation against that locked projection before journal/order mutation. Every path persists through `writeChangeProjection(expectedLeases, evidence)` and never calls the generic JSON writer for `changes.json`.
Projection-Shape: `requirementsOrdinal` or `designOrdinal` is present on every current and historical requirements/design checkpoint; persisted `operationId` is present only on superseding checkpoints at ordinal 2 or greater, and ordinal-1 checkpoints omit the key entirely rather than storing `null`, an empty string, or a generated value.
Candidate-Maintenance: `candidate-snapshot create` is the sole explicit-ID confirmation-token exception and still requires the sole implicit active CHANGE. List/show are lease-free maintenance. Delete may target active, abandoned, completed, foreign, or unknown exact snapshot history under a persisted-ID lease; completed protected history must be made sole active and reopened before deletion.
Requirements: REQ-M5-APPROVAL-008 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-001 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-002 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-003 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 REQ-M5-QUALITY-002 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-005 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-006 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-007
ADRs: ADR-0003 ADR-0005 ADR-0010 ADR-0013 ADR-0014 ADR-0015 ADR-0035
Depends-On: DES-M5-003 DES-M5-004 DES-M5-007

## DES-M5-006: Approval manifest service
Responsibilities: Resolve domain-scoped normative paths and effective configuration projections, bind CHANGE generation, select the active or historical immutable candidate through DES-M5-012, read release blobs from that candidate commit, derive evidence CHANGE identity through a closed precedence selector, bind candidate gate projection, classify every included or excluded path including current and legacy generated trace locations, produce canonical schema-v1 manifests, record exact-hash approvals, classify release recovery, and propagate supersession.
Interfaces: `prepareApproval(stage, domain?)`, `recordApproval(input)`, `validateApprovals()`, `requireApproval(root, stage, config, domain?)`, `selectReleaseCandidate(context): CandidateSelection`, `evidenceChangeIdFromBytes(path, bytes): string | null`, `readReleaseApprovalDigest(root, candidateCommit)`, `releaseApprovalStatus(snapshot): current|missing|stale|not-current`, `classifyReleaseApprovalDiagnostic(code)`, `supersedeFrom(change)`.
Constraints: Requirements and design use `approval-normative-path-set-v1`, active `changeId` plus generation, and effective defaulted projections; no active generation rejects preparation, validation, and recording. An incomplete active generation permits requirements/design approval but release preparation/recording fails with `CHANGE_GENERATION_INCOMPLETE`. When `requireApproval` rejects any non-approved status, its recovery guidance names the published `musubix5 approval validate` command and never a `musubix3` executable. Release is domain-less, resolves active CHANGE/generation internally, obtains its persisted immutable commit, typed Git entries, and blob bytes from DES-M5-012, and obtains the candidate-bound `repositoryId`, `candidateCommit`, and `gateInputFingerprint` projection from DES-M5-019, never from caller-selected identities or mutable worktree bytes. `evidenceChangeIdFromBytes` first enforces the `.musubix/evidence/**` and lowercase `.json` scope from `path`, then parses bytes and returns the first nonempty string at `changeId`, `metadata.changeId`, or `result.changeId`; non-object nested values fall through, deeper traversal is forbidden, and malformed or unowned evidence returns null. Candidate-gate envelopes are the legacy `result.changeId` writer; every new or revised evidence schema must also persist top-level `changeId`, so the lower-precedence selectors remain compatibility fallbacks rather than a preferred writer contract. `readReleaseApprovalDigest` is lease-free and non-mutating, independently validates the current release approval and candidate binding in a supplied evidence root, and returns its artifact SHA-256 or a classified non-current diagnostic. Blob hashing uses DES-M5-003 `sha256(bytes)`; symbolic-link and Gitlink classification uses only tree-derived mode and object-type data. `approval-manifest-schema-v1` contains exactly `schemaVersion`, `stage`, optional `domain`, optional `changeId`, optional `generation`, `artifacts`, `projection`, and `exclusions`; `artifacts` binds only included raw blob hashes, `exclusions` binds only path/reason pairs, displayed excluded hashes remain outside the aggregate, and NFC UTF-8 path byte order overrides generic object-key ordering for path-keyed data. Canonical serialization, generation rules, domain rules, exclusion precedence, and all diagnostics follow REQ-M5-APPROVAL-007; exclusion rule 2 recognizes exact `.musubix/trace/index.json` and legacy `.musubix/features/*/trace.json` with the same `generated-trace` reason during migration. Both release approval destinations are excluded producer-independently; manual confirmation is mandatory; bootstrap approvals authorize development only and generation-bound native approval is required before release. New release approval accepts exactly one live repository-matching generation-current snapshot selected by DES-M5-012 and materializes QA from that commit. Candidate commit parsing and approval candidate comparison accept lowercase hexadecimal object IDs of length 40 through 64 and reject shorter, longer, uppercase, or non-hexadecimal values. Zero non-deleted records is `APPROVAL_CANDIDATE_MISSING` with `candidate-snapshot create <active-id>`; foreign-only, legacy, non-current-generation, multiple, invalid, unresolvable, or unreachable records are `APPROVAL_CANDIDATE_UNAVAILABLE` with list/delete/create guidance, deleting obsolete or replacement-required repository-matching snapshots only when applicable. Historical read-only approval validation uses the canonical REQ-M5-RELEASE-002 rule and never sources a new approval or makes legacy evidence eligible. An active-document approval that byte-exactly binds a sole live commit remains protective even during mixed authoring. Reopen makes the generation-bound approval non-current. Candidate blobs are always read from the selected commit, never later branch HEAD or mutable worktree. Diagnostic placeholder hashes and the shared classifier remain consistent for status, parallel readiness, and release-operation wrappers.
Source-Review-Manifest-Boundary: Preserve the exact requirements/design normative path set while keeping only the dedicated versioned DES-M5-023 review/blob and approval paths outside that set. They are not specification artifacts, general approvals or new release exclusions. The source coordinator receives this service's read-only approval evaluator through DES-M5-002 dependency injection; this service does not import the source coordinator. Tests must prove independent manifest hashes/currency for dedicated creation and immutable source-approval integrity, without exempting any CHANGE, requirements, design, ADR or constitution bytes.
Requirements: REQ-M5-APPROVAL-001 REQ-M5-APPROVAL-002 REQ-M5-APPROVAL-007 REQ-M5-APPROVAL-008 REQ-M5-APPROVAL-009 REQ-M5-APPROVAL-010 REQ-M5-COMPAT-013 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 REQ-M5-RELEASE-002 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-005 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-006 REQ-M5-WORKTREE-007
ADRs: ADR-0002 ADR-0004 ADR-0008 ADR-0010 ADR-0033 ADR-0036
Depends-On: DES-M5-003 DES-M5-004 DES-M5-005 DES-M5-007 DES-M5-012 DES-M5-019

## DES-M5-007: Evidence registry
Responsibilities: Validate evidence schemas, CHANGE generation, ownership, producer and input bindings, dependency heads, currency, append-only workflow-correction projections supplied by DES-M5-018, status taxonomy, and derived projections.
Interfaces: `appendEvidence(kind, record)`, `currentEvidence(query)`, `classifyCurrency(record, context)`, `project(kind)`, `bindGeneration(record, activeGeneration)`, `validatePhaseCheckpointJournal(records)`, `validateBatchCheckpointJournal(records)`, `unprojectedPhaseCheckpoints(generation?)`, `unprojectedBatchCheckpoints(generation?)`, `validateWorkflowCorrections(records, workflow)`, `validateSourceSupersessionJournal(records)`, `validateSourceReviewArtifact(bytes, approval)`, `sourceSupersessionProjection(journal, order, chain, tdd)`, `sourceSupersessionConflict(scope, target?)`.
Constraints: Every normal evidence kind binds the active generation; every evidence `repositoryId` is supplied by DES-M5-003 `canonicalRepositoryIdentity`; legacy missing generation reads as generation 1; bootstrap remains separate; abandoned or superseded generations never satisfy current evidence. Phase-checkpoint and batch-checkpoint journal validation enforce their registered envelope/payload, derived idempotency key, chain, positive audit fences, and scoped identity uniqueness before projection; invalid evidence is non-waivable `CHANGE_CHECKPOINT_JOURNAL_INVALID`. `unprojectedPhaseCheckpoints` is always rendered as an array for active, superseded, and abandoned summaries and contains generation, phase, operation ID, ordinal, and journal order without independently changing readiness. Gate and status likewise always render `unprojectedBatchCheckpoints`. The scanner accepts only exact optional canonical `g<N>:` plus `red|implementation|green` plus optional canonical scope grammar, treats unqualified phases as generation 1, excludes `superseded-*` and all other phase kinds, and rejects malformed generation/scope encoding as `EVIDENCE_ORDER_SCHEMA`. Before subtraction it groups every scanned order by `(changeId, generation, scope-or-derived-key, phase)`; duplicate members are all labeled `invalid` and cause gate exit 1 and status `ready: false` with `CHANGE_CHECKPOINT_JOURNAL_INVALID` regardless of projection or journal presence. Nonduplicate proper subsets are matched phase-by-phase against active `tddBatches` or the exact historical generation's `tddBatches`, using persisted scope or `batchForKey`; nonduplicate full sets are matched against the corresponding singular active or historical phase. Remaining parseable entries are `interrupted`, `legacy`, or `invalid` according to valid, absent, or invalid journal evidence. Unaddressable journal corruption is repository-level only. Interrupted and legacy entries are informational/non-credit; invalid entries are non-credit and fail closed. Workflow corrections are non-credit audited evidence and malformed chains remain non-pass; DES-M5-018 owns workflow declaration waiver/correction mutual exclusion before DES-M5-007 consumes their projections; normative specifications are never generated evidence; foreign, stale, skipped, unsupported, flaky, waived, failed, or superseded records do not become pass.
Source-Supersession-Validation: Own pure schema, identity-graph and prospective-ledger validation for the versioned structures specified by DES-M5-023, plus read-only pending conflict classification. A completed candidate requires exact unique journal/order/chain/projection linkage and immutable source-approval integrity; valid incomplete suffixes are pending/non-credit, and missing scope or corrupt linkage is invalid, never repository-wide pending. These functions consume values and generic DES-M5-004 primitives, not coordinator imports. Source approval verifies persisted hashes/bindings, not continuing equality to current dependency/production snapshots. Current environment currency is deliberately outside this evidence type.
Requirements: REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-001 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-002 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-003 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-004 REQ-M5-EVIDENCE-005 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 REQ-M5-COMPAT-013 REQ-M5-WAIVER-001
ADRs: ADR-0003 ADR-0005 ADR-0010 ADR-0014 ADR-0015 ADR-0035 ADR-0036
Depends-On: DES-M5-003 DES-M5-004

## DES-M5-011: TDD cycle ledger
Responsibilities: Execute configured test adapters, validate authoritative TEST IDs, record Red/Green/Refactor observations, separate batch scopes, and resolve canonical coverage. Expose the explicit additive source-supersession coordinator owned by DES-M5-023; compose its admission/recovery with ledger validation, without routing it through migrate, refactor, void, or repair.
Interfaces: `recordRed(input)`, `recordImplementation(changeRecord)`, `recordGreen(input)`, `recordRefactor(input)`, `assignmentCycleComplete(binding)`, `selectCurrentCycle(generation, requirementId, integrationProvenance?)`, `validateTddEvidence(root, purpose)`, `migrateTddFingerprint(root, testId, approver)`, `voidTddCycle(root, testId, approver, reason)`, `sourceSupersession(operation, request, dependencies)`, `sourceSupersessionConflict(writerScope, explicitTarget?)`.
Constraints: Red and Green come from `tdd` commands; Implementation comes from the matching generation-bound `change-record` checkpoint; all three bind one generation, requirement batch, and candidate lineage with strictly increasing order; per-batch predecessor checks are independent; assignment admission checks cycle completeness without provenance, while coverage selection requires consumed parallel commit-range provenance and classifies unconsumed cycles `PARALLEL_TDD_UNCONSUMED`. When `integrationProvenance` is omitted, the ledger reads the current provisional or verified consumed-range projection through DES-M5-007; this keeps gate/status independent of parallel implementation modules while still failing closed on absent or invalid provenance. Every candidate, cycle, and parallel-start commit parser accepts lowercase hexadecimal object IDs of length 40 through 64 and rejects shorter, longer, uppercase, or non-hexadecimal values. Coverage selection never crosses the active CHANGE scope or generation; `validateTddEvidence()` invokes DES-M5-TDD-005 outside its active-cycle loop for source-currency validation. `migrateTddFingerprint()` and `voidTddCycle()` own their public message strings, exit classes, and persistence behavior while using DES-M5-TDD-005 operation scoping, verified-event precedence, bounds, fallback, and structural-guard rules; a selected CHANGE with no active generation is treated as no active maintenance scope. Refactor follows current Green; legacy full-set and requirement batches never merge for coverage.
Source-Supersession: Every TDD writer uses DES-M5-023's lease migration and source-aware integrity/prefix classifier, then the read-only scoped conflict check before requested writes; unrelated tests and ordinary change-record checkpoints continue. The classifier recognizes valid journal-backed prefixes before legacy orphan/repair checks, without bypassing genuine corruption or existing repair pending. Only a completed, verified additional terminal participates in source currency and void selection. Test-only retains its original cycle's eligible coverage exactly once; behavior-change evaluates only the independent replacement cycle's ordinary eligibility once. Neither operation manufactures Red/Implementation/Green, missing checkpoints, ownership adoption, or consumed-range provenance. The ledger passes approval, trace, runner, lifecycle, and candidate evaluators as typed callbacks supplied by the facade; the lower coordinator does not import those higher-level coordinators.

## DES-M5-TDD-005: Effective source-currency cycle selector
Responsibilities: Resolve exactly one effective TDD cycle per test for source-fingerprint currency checks from verified monotonic evidence, independently from active-CHANGE coverage filtering.
Interfaces: `Readonly<EffectiveTddCurrencySelection> { cycle, order, fingerprint }`; module-private `TddCurrencyIndex`, `TddCycleScopePredicate`, `TddEventScope { terminalScope?, voidScope?, workScope? }`, `buildTddCurrencyIndex(evidence, order, validlyVoidedCycles, chainIndex?)`, `greatestVerifiedEvent(index, testId, eventScope)`, `phaseLinkageValid(order, chain, chainIndex, cycle, phase, phaseEvidence)`, `terminalFingerprintEvidence(index, cycle)`, and `effectiveLatestCycle(index, testId, upperBoundExclusive?, scopePredicate?): EffectiveTddCurrencySelection | undefined` in `packages/analysis/src/tdd.ts`; `validateTddEvidence(root, purpose)`, `migrateTddFingerprint(root, testId, approver)`, and `voidTddCycle(root, testId, approver, reason)` in DES-M5-011 consume the same index; `CODE-M5-TDD-EFFECTIVE-LATEST-001` in `packages/analysis/src/tdd.ts`; `TEST-M5-TDD-EFFECTIVE-LATEST-001`, `TEST-M5-TDD-MAINTENANCE-SCOPE-001`, and their unannotated companion cases in `tests/tdd-generation-scope.test.ts`.
Constraints: `validateTddEvidence()` retains its active CHANGE and generation predicate for requirement coverage, active-cycle phase-order/provenance/completeness diagnostics, and related generation-bound checks. A selected CHANGE with no active generation retains validation's existing `CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE` exit-2 failure, while migration and void treat that maintenance state as no active operation scope and consider all cycles for the test. The active scope predicate is `(cycle.generation ?? 1) === activeGeneration` and absent `changeId` or equality with the active CHANGE ID; stale-check membership adds valid Green evidence. After global chain validation and void-linkage validation, validation derives target test IDs from stale-check membership, while operation work-event, migration target, and void candidate scoping use the active scope predicate without requiring Green. Without an active CHANGE, every test ID with valid Green evidence is targeted and migration/void may consider all cycles for that test. Membership reads persisted fields after normal phase-recording ownership adoption and does not infer ownership from requirements or paths. It builds `TddCurrencyIndex` once with cycles grouped by test ID and a `(cycleId, testId, phase)` chain-record index whose entries retain each record and chain position; predecessor digest is derived from the preceding chain record and multiplicity from the matching-entry count; exactly one chain record matching `(phase, cycleId, testId)` must exist in the complete chain, and that unique record's position determines the expected predecessor digest. The index exposes verified events and selectors, while each consumer supplies independent terminal, void, and work predicates through `TddEventScope`. Validation passes all-scope terminal and void predicates plus the active-scope work predicate when a CHANGE is active; migration passes the active scope for all three event kinds while active, and without an active CHANGE passes all-scope terminal/void predicates plus the selection-dependent work qualification computed after the unbounded terminal selection; void passes the operation scope for all three event kinds. Validation considers eligible terminal selections and valid voids across all scopes. With an active CHANGE it considers open Red or linked non-passing Green work events only from cycles satisfying the active scope predicate. Without an active CHANGE it first selects the greatest eligible terminal without a void bound; unscoped work events always qualify, while scoped work events qualify only when `(changeId, cycle.generation ?? 1)` equals that unbounded terminal selection's scope, and no eligible terminal means no stale diagnostic. This work scope is fixed before any valid-void bound changes the effective terminal. Foreign or prior-generation scoped open work cannot suppress an active stale diagnostic. The greatest qualifying work event suppresses `TDD_TEST_STALE` until passing Green or valid void, preserving in-progress TDD behavior without widening active suppression. Validation resolves at most one effective selection per target ID across all CHANGE scopes and generations, then iterates those selections outside the active-cycle loop. Source file text is memoized by current trace path, while computed fingerprints are memoized by test ID so multiple annotated tests in one file remain independent. A target ID with no current trace test node or no eligible selection emits no `TDD_TEST_STALE`; existing trace, global chain/order, and applicable active-cycle diagnostics remain authoritative. An eligible cycle has valid Red and Green evidence whose verified Red order is strictly less than its verified Green order, is not validly voided, and satisfies the unique complete-chain match for each credited phase; both Red and Green payload/hash-chain/monotonic-order linkage are accepted by `phaseLinkageValid()`, chain-record matching verifies cycle and test identity for every phase, and order-record test identity is additionally required for void evidence. Valid void records are subject to the same unique complete-chain match rule; duplicate void-chain records are unverified. `terminalFingerprintEvidence()` returns one readonly `{ cycle, order, fingerprint }` selection using the greatest verified order from Green; valid Refactor with verified linkage; and migration with verified linkage plus a trimmed non-empty approver. Migration recording rejects a blank or whitespace-only approver before persistence with the existing thrown `An approver is required to migrate TDD fingerprint evidence.` error and exit code 2, and the migration diagnostic uses the same trimmed predicate, so malformed historical approvers emit `TDD_LEGACY_OR_UNSCOPED_EVIDENCE` and cannot gain selector priority. Consumers use returned fingerprints or cycles directly and do not re-sort raw phase fields. When the greatest event in a consumer's event scope is a valid void, it calls the selector with that void order as `upperBoundExclusive`; otherwise it selects without a bound. While a CHANGE is active, migration's terminal, void, and work candidates are restricted to the active scope predicate; without an active CHANGE migration applies validation's no-active qualification rules. If no cycle for the test exists in any scope, migration throws `No TDD cycle found for <testId>.` with exit 2; if cycles exist globally but no eligible terminal exists in the active operation scope, or if the greatest qualifying event is open or non-passing work, it throws `<testId> has no valid Green phase to migrate.` with exit 2 and persists nothing. Cycle-ID-less or chain-unverified records cannot become the selected eligible migration terminal and use the retained no-valid-Green error rather than the legacy missing-cycle-ID guard. After verified selection, any persisted migration record, whether valid or malformed, retains `<testId> has already been migrated.` with exit 2 and is never overwritten or duplicated; malformed migration evidence remains diagnosed and requires a genuine new Red/Green cycle to establish later current evidence. The void boundary is defence-in-depth under a valid globally increasing order log, and a later verified terminal fingerprint becomes current normally; a cycle whose terminal Refactor or migration lies at or above an explicit bound is excluded as one terminal selection rather than falling back to its earlier Green. Active-scope migration does not mutate or use foreign void candidates, so a successful active migration can remain globally non-current when repository-wide validation is bounded by a later valid foreign or prior-generation void; operators complete or abandon the active CHANGE before repository-wide repair. `migrateTddFingerprint()` uses the index's order-derived greatest event and effective selector instead of array position, then uses `selection.cycle` for not-already-migrated and migration-recording checks and `selection.fingerprint` for the legacy-current comparison; no selection yields the retained no-valid-Green rejection without persistence. `voidTddCycle()` first preserves `No TDD cycle found for <testId>.` as an exit-2 error when no cycle for the test exists in any scope. It then scopes candidates with the active scope predicate when a CHANGE is active and considers all cycles for the test otherwise. Before building the verified index it applies the current missing-cycle-ID and missing-chain guards to the array-last cycle within that operation scope solely to preserve their exit-2 messages; the missing-chain guard's companion “another cycle exists” test uses only cycles in the same operation scope. These structural guards run before valid-Green and already-voided selection, and array position grants no target or fallback priority. It then computes the order-greatest verified event among terminal fingerprint evidence, valid voids, and work events for the operation scope. A terminal-fingerprint greatest event is classified by the cycle's valid Green and throws the existing valid-Green error whether Green, Refactor, or migration supplied its terminal order; a valid void greatest event throws the existing already-voided error; a greatest work event of either kind—valid Red on a cycle without valid Green, or linked non-passing Green—becomes the target when its cycle has no persisted void record and no valid Green. A cycle bearing an unverified void record is never overwritten or re-targeted; it returns `{ voided: false, reason: "<testId> has no verifiable dangling TDD cycle in the current operation scope." }`, exits 1, and persists nothing. These retained throws remain exit-2 CLI errors and retain their existing “latest cycle” message strings, where latest now means order-greatest verified cycle event; structural-guard and verified-event precedence may change which retained message applies to a repository state. If cycles exist globally but no linked target event exists in the active operation scope, it returns the same `{ voided: false, reason }`, exits 1, and persists nothing. Before append it requires `effectiveLatestCycle(index, testId, greatestWorkOrder, operationScopePredicate)` to return an eligible fallback, so the fallback is restricted to the same active scope predicate used for targeting when a CHANGE is active and to all cycles when none is active; the no-fallback reason string remains byte-identical to the existing text even though fallback eligibility is determined by verified order and active operation scope. Valid evidence-order sequences are repository-wide unique, so eligible ties are unreachable; a repository-wide invalid or duplicate order log is diagnosed globally, causes the index to expose no verified selections, and therefore cannot produce a stale diagnostic. A missing eligible record suppresses only `TDD_TEST_STALE`; existing global chain/order diagnostics and applicable active-cycle missing, malformed, legacy-provenance, Red, and Green diagnostics remain unchanged, and excluded foreign evidence does not create a new diagnostic solely because no currency candidate exists. A stale diagnostic uses the current trace node path. Foreign, prior-generation, superseded-for-coverage, and modern legacy-unscoped cycles that still possess verifiable cycle/order/chain linkage can participate only as candidate fingerprints for a target test and grant no coverage, provenance, or parallel-consumption credit; pre-order-log evidence without that linkage remains ineligible. Array-position supersession classification remains an explicit out-of-scope legacy behavior and does not determine source-currency selection. DES-M5-TDD-005 is a read-only selector over the DES-M5-011-owned `tdd.json` evidence inside the shared module. DES-M5-011 owns externally observable migration/void messages and exit classes; this selector constrains the verified selection and scope conditions that determine their applicability. The changed source-currency work-event suppression and stale-diagnostic applicability, active-scope applicability and verified-selection precedence of retained migration messages, active-scope applicability of the void-fallback message, applicability of retained `tdd void` messages, foreign-only active-scope exit-1 result, trimmed migration-approver rejection and diagnostic applicability, and active-scope restrictions for migration/void are intentional behavioral differences registered under REQ-M5-COMPAT-013 and ADR-0023; public CLI shape, established exit classes for retained conditions, and help text remain unchanged. The regression fixture proves generation-1 unscoped membership, generation-2 exclusion of generation-less evidence, scoped membership, active open-Red and non-passing-Green suppression, foreign open-Red non-suppression, no-active-CHANGE and selected-CHANGE-with-null-generation maintenance behavior, unscoped and same-scoped work suppression, unbounded-scope-before-void behavior, valid-Green targets, and persisted ownership-at-evaluation behavior; it places an older modern-unscoped cycle after a newer completed-CHANGE scoped cycle in the evidence array for a targeted ID, gives the newer cycle a current matching fingerprint and greater verified terminal order, and asserts no `TDD_TEST_STALE`. Companion cases cover migration open-work rejection, active-scoped unbounded and void-bounded migration selection, active-scope-only-cycle migration no-valid-Green message, migration cycle-ID/migration-repeat message precedence including malformed migration no-overwrite recovery, active migration bounded by later foreign void during validation, trimmed migration recording and malformed historical approvers/linkage with exit-2 rejection, bounded migration rejection, no-cycle exit-2 preservation, operation-scoped missing-chain guard, scoped structural-guard and precedence preservation, active-scoped void fallback exclusion of foreign and prior-generation terminals with retained no-fallback reason, active-scoped and no-active order-latest verified void admission/rejection including Refactor/migration terminal precedence and Red-to-non-passing-Green target success with retained exit classes, already-voided and unverifiable void targets with exact reason text, duplicate phase and void-chain multiplicity including no overwrite of unverified void evidence, repository-wide invalid order, an out-of-scope cycle whose verified Green order is not strictly after its verified Red order being ineligible and supplying no terminal fingerprint or `TDD_TEST_STALE`, no eligible cycle, missing trace node, source-text and per-test cache isolation, current-path diagnostics, two test IDs in one source file, latest valid void selection, post-void terminal selection, and source assertions that the compatibility registry row and migration-guide entry remain present.
Source-Terminal-Extension: The preceding (a) Green, (b) verified Refactor, (c) verified algorithm-migration contract is retained, with an explicit `terminalKinds: "legacy" | "source-currency"` selector input. Only `"source-currency"` adds (d) completed verified source-supersession terminals. DES-M5-007 supplies schema/integrity-validated journal, order, chain, review-approval, and projection joins, never a pending candidate. Validation and void targeting/fallback use `"source-currency"`; migration always uses `"legacy"` for both greatest-event and terminal selection, so (d) never supplies its target or fromFingerprint. The existing work/void scope predicates and exclusive upper bound apply unchanged. A cycle's greatest verified terminal, including (d), at or above the bound excludes that cycle entirely, not just (d); there is no fallback to its old Green. Pending work supplies no new suppression. Maximum verified order, not array order, chooses the effective terminal. Test-only selections return the original cycle; behavior-change selections return the linked replacement cycle; one cycle is evaluated once. The successor graph uses terminal identities, not fingerprints; DES-M5-007 rejects self-links, cycles, branches, duplicate linkage, and more than one successor, while distinct identities may validly carry fingerprint A to B to A.
Retained-Maintenance: Migration preserves blank-approver/no-cycle/no-valid-Green guards and their existing precedence. An existing migration still throws exit 2 `<testId> has already been migrated.`. A real legacy-algorithm drift returns exit 1 `{ migrated: false, reason: "<testId>'s recorded fingerprint does not match its current source under the superseded algorithm; this is real drift, not an algorithm-only change. Run a genuine Red/Green cycle instead." }` with zero evidence writes. Only the existing algorithm-only success records migration and exits 0, without changing or duplicating (d). Refactor retains exact testId/requirement/command cycle selection and compares current fingerprint against the original Red, never against (d). A mismatch takes precedence over duplicate Refactor and throws exit 2 `The test changed after Red; run the Red phase again.` with zero evidence writes. With matching Red, valid Green, other preceding guards passed and fresh selected pass, an existing Refactor throws exit 2 `tdd:<cycleId>:refactor is already present in monotonic evidence order.` with zero evidence writes; without that duplicate it succeeds normally. This also applies after A to B to A. Void whose greatest qualifying event is (d) throws exit 2 `<testId>'s latest cycle has a valid Green phase; only a dangling cycle can be voided.` with zero evidence writes and never retires (d). Genuine later dangling work retains structural/valid-void/scope guards and may use (d) only as a qualifying bounded fallback. Fixtures containing only (a)-(c) retain exact results, messages, and exits; stale-parallel repair's authorized target scope is unchanged.
Source-Currency-Boundary: For completed (d), compare only its authoritative new test fingerprint with `testFingerprintFromText(currentNode, currentText)`. Snapshot, dependencies, helper, runner, config, production, HEAD and candidate are immutable admission/audit inputs, not continuing source-currency predicates. Their later ordinary changes neither stale this terminal nor require another source review. A new test-block drift emits `TDD_TEST_STALE`; an actual runner failure emits the ordinary runner/gate failure separately. Persisted review/approval hash or binding tampering is source-approval invalid and non-ready, not a waived stale result. General approval cascades, implementation currency, coverage, current parallel provenance and candidate-gate validation remain independent.

## DES-M5-012: Workspace manager
Responsibilities: Create and identify baseline, candidate, QA, parallel assignment-attempt, integration-attempt, and detached verification workspaces; validate and persist the public control-worktree baseline lifecycle; preserve unrelated dirty paths outside baseline creation; persist, inspect, select, and retire immutable candidate snapshots; project legacy and tombstoned history; enumerate candidate Git entries without reading the worktree; track generated-output ownership; materialize QA at the exact selected commit; and recover rejected candidates.
Interfaces: `captureBaseline(root, changeId): BaselineWorkspace`, `createPublicBaseline(root, changeId): BaselineWorkspace`, `resolveControlWorkspace(root, changeId): ControlWorkspaceIdentity`, `currentBaseline(root, changeId): BaselineWorkspace | null`, `createCandidate(changeId)`, `createQa(candidateId, matrixJob)`, `createParallelAssignment(input)`, `createParallelIntegration(input)`, `createParallelVerification(input)`, `persistCandidateSnapshot(root, changeId, evaluators): CandidateSnapshotWriteResult`, `listCandidateSnapshotRecords(root): CandidateSnapshotStructuralProjection[]`, `showCandidateSnapshotRecord(root, selector): CandidateSnapshotStructuralProjection`, `deleteCandidateSnapshot(root, selector, deletedBy, evaluators): CandidateSnapshotDeleteResult`, `resolveCandidateSnapshot(root, context): CandidateSelection`, `projectCandidateSnapshot(record, context, evaluation): CandidateSnapshotProjection`, `candidateTreeManifest(commit): { entries, artifactManifestDigest }`, `listCandidateEntries(commit): { rawPath, nfcPath, objectId, gitMode, objectType }[]`, `readCandidateBlob(commit, objectId)`, `createQaAtCommit(commit, matrixJob)`, `compareTrackedTree(workspace, commit, phase: 'pre' | 'post')`, `collectOwnedChanges(changeId)`, `recover(candidateId)`.
Constraints: `createPublicBaseline` executes the REQ-M5-WORKTREE-004 first-match validation order before entering `captureBaseline`: syntax, active-generation ownership, registered control-worktree identity, immutable HEAD, clean non-ignored state, then prior-baseline conflict. Control identity is derived from the Git common-directory workspace registry and exact branch/change/generation metadata, not path-name inference alone. It acquires the CHANGE lease, repeats context/head/clean/conflict checks under the lease, then uses idempotency key `workspace:<changeId>:baseline:<commitSha>`; exact replay returns the existing journal projection and no append. `assertPlanBaseDescendsFromBaseline` retains `PARALLEL_WORKTREE_CONFLICT` but appends argument-array-safe recovery guidance for the public baseline command. Candidate work requires an immutable baseline commit; each workspace role or attempt owns one branch or detached worktree under the Git common directory; parallel workspaces cannot modify baseline, QA, control, or another attempt; byte, mode, staged, unstaged, deleted, and untracked identities are preserved. Snapshot creation and resolution obtain repository identity only from DES-M5-003 `canonicalRepositoryIdentity`, discard the acquired raw origin before constructing any record or diagnostic, and verify exact commit existence plus required branch/ref reachability. Identity mismatch is `APPROVAL_CANDIDATE_UNAVAILABLE` for direct consumers and states the credential-free GitHub HTTPS origin requirement without exposing the raw origin; each affected generation must persist a repository-matching replacement snapshot and regenerate all candidate matrix gate records before readiness can recover. DES-M5-016 wraps non-current approval or snapshot failures as `RELEASE_OPERATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED`. New creation records use payload `recordVersion: 1`, generation, repository, branch, 40-to-64-character lowercase hexadecimal commit, SHA-256 `candidate-tree-manifest-v1`, and creation time; stable ID/path derive from journal order. Legacy records are absence-only `recordVersion: 0` projections with nullable generation/digest/time and remain listable/showable/deletable; they still participate in active/historical release selection and deletion protection. Repository-matching live records, not greatest order, define selection; one live candidate per CHANGE is enforced until append-only deletion. Creation idempotency binds CHANGE, generation, commit, digest, repository, and latest repository-matching tombstone epoch; replay precedes cleanliness, while divergent branch payload is `JOURNAL_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Create holds the CHANGE lease for authoritative workspace re-resolution and invokes injected approval/quality evaluators both before and under the lease; DES-M5-012 does not import DES-M5-006 or DES-M5-015. Structural projection owns record parsing, deletion, repository, commit reachability, conflict, and legacy facts; caller-supplied evaluation owns requirements/design approval, quality, candidate-gate, release-approval, protection, replacement, eligibility, and guidance composition. Historical multiple-record projection remains readable: exact-ID show/list return stale release approval, unprotected state, and conflict guidance rather than failing. Delete resolves exactly one record, revalidates journal selection and injected protection under the persisted CHANGE lease, refuses protected snapshots, and appends `workspace-candidate-snapshot-deleted` with actor/time, approval audit fields, and sorted invalidated states; same-actor replay returns the stored tombstone and different actor fails. Snapshot and tombstone journal defects use REQ-M5-WORKTREE-005 attribution; read-only inspection stays lease-free. QA and parallel verification workspaces disable checkout content conversion and smudge/clean filters; tracked comparison refreshes the index and compares Git object IDs rather than worktree byte hashes. Pre-gate comparison permits no tracked differences; post-gate comparison derives its allow-list internally from the closed `generated-trace` and `gate-self-reference` patterns, treating exact `.musubix/trace/index.json` and migration-era `.musubix/features/*/trace.json` as generated-trace, and otherwise emits `RELEASE_CANDIDATE_TREE_MISMATCH`; ignored/untracked caches are outside comparison. Entry enumeration and blob reads address immutable Git objects and never fall back to worktree paths. QA workspaces are materialized at the snapshot commit, so later journal commits are outside tree comparison.
Materialization-Support: DES-M5-012 supplies workspace and copy primitives to DES-M5-MULTI-CHANGE-002, which exclusively owns asynchronous `materializeOperationalState`, supplied-handle validation, recovery callback invocation, post-recovery baseline capture, and stable copying of candidates, evidence, and journal state; it never acquires leases. DES-M5-MULTI-CHANGE-003 exclusively owns finalization's byte-sorted CHANGE → change-projection → repository append lock ordering, acquisition, retention, and renewal and supplies those handles to materialization.

## DES-M5-013: Bootstrap runner
Responsibilities: Start independently of normal orchestrator state, validate explicit authority, execute bounded operations in a candidate workspace, and persist bootstrap history in bootstrap-scoped ledgers.
Interfaces: Internal `bootstrapRun(manifest)`, `bootstrapResume(runId)`, `bootstrapStatus(runId)`, `requestNormalIngestion(runId)` entry points, invoked by repository-local `scripts/musubix5-bootstrap.mjs`.
Constraints: The launcher is excluded by the package `files` allow-list, verified absent by `pack:check` and `pack:smoke`, and never routes through `musubix5` argv parsing, completion, root help, command help, `help [command]`, or unknown-command/usage-error handling. Evidence and budget services are parameterized by an explicit store root; bootstrap always receives the bootstrap root; the normal evidence registry rejects bootstrap producer identity; no implicit invocation; no writes to normal approvals or mandatory evidence; no readiness, publish, tag, or push authority.

## DES-M5-014: Analysis adapters
Responsibilities: Provide compatible requirements/design validation, shared-index trace build/load/check/impact with legacy feature-trace fallback, graph, formal, mutation, correspondence, workflow, attestation, and knowledge operations.
Interfaces: Compatibility-preserving domain and analysis exports plus CLI handlers for each inventoried command; trace persistence `.musubix/trace/index.json` plus ignored cache; read-only migration fallback `.musubix/features/*/trace.json`.
Constraints: Formal results distinguish modeled pass, modeled fail, unsupported, and solver error; generated artifacts use the evidence registry and cannot mutate normative inputs; workflow CLI handlers delegate sanitization and reconciliation to DES-M5-018. Trace writers use ADR-0028 shared persistence, never create feature-local trace output, and retain legacy feature files only as read-only fallback until successful migration removal. In DES-M5-015 matrix mode, trace, graph, knowledge, formal, mutation, and correspondence intermediates are redirected to ignored scratch storage and never write tracked `.musubix/evidence/{trace,graph,knowledge}` or other tracked cache paths; only the closed generated-trace/gate-self-reference paths may differ after execution, where generated-trace includes current `.musubix/trace/index.json` and migration-era `.musubix/features/*/trace.json`.
