## DES-M5-015: Quality and readiness engine
Responsibilities: Run required commands and deterministic checks, collect quality input fingerprints through the shared evidence selector that excludes current and legacy generated trace paths, classify every generation-bound evidence state including workflow correction projections, aggregate readiness, and expose compatible gate/status JSON.
Interfaces: `runGate(scope, persistenceMode?)`, `getStatus(scope)`, `refreshEvidence(scope)`, `candidateGateStatus(changeId, generation, commit)`, `candidateSnapshotEvaluation(structuralProjection, releaseClassification): CandidateSnapshotEvaluation`, `candidateSnapshotNext(change, projections): string[]`.
Constraints: Required commands cannot be empty; only the active generation contributes; no active generation or an active generation without terminal quality produces `CHANGE_GENERATION_INCOMPLETE`, gate exit 1, status exit 0, and `ready: false`, without blocking requirements/design approval; `CHANGE_GENERATION_REQUIREMENTS` is re-evaluated on every status/gate call; configuration cannot remove mandatory evidence kinds. Gate and status validate but never reconcile checkpoint journal records, always expose DES-M5-007 `unprojectedPhaseCheckpoints` and `unprojectedBatchCheckpoints` on active, superseded, and abandoned summaries, continue evaluating the current projection for informational phase/interrupted/legacy entries, and treat historical entries as non-current. Invalid requirements/design checkpoint journal evidence reported by DES-M5-007, or any batch entry labeled `invalid`, including duplicate order identities detected before subtraction, emits non-waivable `CHANGE_CHECKPOINT_JOURNAL_INVALID`; gate exits 1 and status exits 0 with `ready: false`. Unaddressable journal corruption uses the same repository-level diagnostic without inventing an entry. A valid workflow correction suppresses only its target declaration's reused/missing pair, emits informational `WORKFLOW_DECLARATION_SUPERSEDED`, grants no credit, and never suppresses a canonical or unrelated diagnostic; malformed correction evidence emits `WORKFLOW_DECLARATION_CORRECTION_INVALID`. Normal mode journals only its owned quality/check result records under CHANGE/order leases and does not invoke phase-checkpoint recovery. Matrix mode is explicitly non-journaling, acquires no shared repository lease, writes its authoritative canonical result artifact outside the QA worktree, and keeps any informational caches in ignored scratch storage; only later DES-M5-019 control-worktree ingestion creates normal evidence. Release readiness reads candidate matrix records only through DES-M5-007 projections, preventing an ESM import cycle with DES-M5-019. DES-M5-015 consumes DES-M5-012 structural records plus release classification supplied by DES-M5-002, produces quality/gate/replacement/eligibility/guidance evaluation, and never imports or calls DES-M5-006. Its injected pure/read-only evaluator never calls DES-M5-012 while DES-M5-012 holds a lease. Domain requirements/design and approval/quality recovery always precede snapshot actions. With no live repository-matching record, including foreign-only and tombstoned-only history, it inserts exact create before release actions only when create preconditions are current. A sole `replacementRequired` record inserts protected reopen recovery when needed, then delete, and inserts create only after current preconditions. A sole valid basis with non-pass gates emits gate-run guidance and never delete/create. Multiple live repository-matching records emit list plus one ascending-order delete command per record, never create in the same response. Gate/status classify every shared chain defect as `CHANGE_CHECKPOINT_JOURNAL_INVALID`; list/show retain their uniform read-only candidate-journal classification.

#### G9 r29: root-coordinated online approval recovery

<!-- G9-R29-ONLINE-BEGIN -->

**Status and precedence.** R29 was the final Generation-9 recovery interface
and is immutable non-current history. It changes no requirement statement or acceptance criterion,
requirements approval, six-ID CHANGE scope, D0/order3821, gapKey, historical
raw evidence, or permanent one-invocation rule. It supersedes only the r28
offline shutdown, private-runtime, guardian, observer and handoff mechanism.
Every r27/r28 artifact and failed/unknown outcome remains immutable diagnostic
history and grants no current authority. No further r28 retry, cap increase,
micro-compaction, runtime copy, guardian build, observer run or `/exit` is
permitted by this design.

**Authority, coordination and transcript split.** `C29` is the exact control
worktree, its Git common directory, and every repository authority path that
the native design approval command may read or mutate. `S29` is the live root
Copilot transcript/session stream. `G29` is a session-owned, content-addressed
coordination root outside `C29` and `S29`, bound to repositoryId, controlRoot
and gapKey. `S29` remains writable so the root conversation can present,
receive consent and record ordering; it is never treated as quiescent, searched
as repository authority, or accepted as a substitute for native approval
bytes. During Epoch A the root controller may perform only the exact reviewed
read-only observations, write `S29`/`G29`, dispatch the one native approval
child, and seal the r29 authority records in `G29`. The sole permitted Epoch-A
`C29` mutation is the native approval-record child's declared delta. Epoch B
separately permits only the exact predeclared P and claim paths bound by
`EpochBExpectedDelta29`; it does not reopen the Epoch-A write set.

**Closed writer policy, inventory and pause.** Before presentation, seal
`OnlineWriterPolicy29`, a role/capability-class allowlist without volatile
PIDs. It includes root command execution, background agents, schedulers,
control executors, database/WAL projectors, IDE/source-control integrations,
and approval/change/order/journal writers. After consent and before intent,
enumerate every live principal with either (a) a writable descriptor to `C29`,
(b) a repository mutation capability, or (c) queued work that can invoke such
a capability. The concrete `OnlineWriterInventory29` binds PID/startTicks/
bootId for processes and a stable controller identity for platform principals;
every row must be an instance of a presented policy class. Planned ephemeral
read-only observers, the fence holder and the single approval child are
declared classes with exact command shapes; any other new instance stops.
A pause request is not an acknowledgement. Each non-root mutation principal
must be identity-gone or provide a controller-verifiable acknowledgement that
queued work is empty, mutation entry is disabled and no writable `C29`
descriptor remains. The root controller acknowledgement disables every tool
shape except the declared read-only checks, fence-holder control and one
approval dispatch. Unknown class, uncontrolled capability, missing
acknowledgement or changed concrete inventory stops before intent. A process
that writes only `S29` is outside `C29`; if it also has repository capability,
that capability must still be paused.

**Fence and native runtime binding.** Before presentation, create and fsync one
stable no-follow fence inode at
`G29/fence/<repositoryId>/<gapKey>.lock`, then seal its path, device, inode,
mode, UID/GID and link count. Creation is outside the epoch and outside `C29`.
After consent, launch the exact attached long-lived fence-holder command
`/usr/bin/flock --exclusive --nonblock <fence-path> /usr/bin/sleep infinity`;
bind its PID/startTicks/bootId and verify contention from an independent probe.
The holder has no `C29` descriptor or mutation capability. It remains alive
through approval verification and deterministic P seal, is terminated by
specific PID only, and its actual wait is captured before writer resumption.

`OnlineRuntimeBinding29` binds canonical path, device/inode, mode, UID/GID,
size and SHA-256 for `/usr/bin/node`, the exact built native CLI entry,
`/usr/bin/git`, loaders/libraries and every executable observed in a
review-time copied-fixture dry run. It also binds argv exactly
`["/usr/bin/node","<C29>/dist/packages/cli/src/main.js","approval","record",
"design","--root","<C29>","--approver","<approver>","--artifact-sha256","<manifest>",
"--confirm","--json"]`, cwd `C29`, stdin `/dev/null`, and a closed environment
with `PATH=/usr/bin`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, `TZ=UTC`,
owned fixed `HOME` and `TMPDIR` under `G29`,
`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`,
`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2`,
`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.fsmonitor`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false`,
`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=/dev/null`.
The dry run must demonstrate
the same exec-role closure without mutating actual `C29`; post-wait identity
checking detects rather than prevents an unreviewed exec and classifies it as

for this online route because no host runtime byte is copied, retained or

**Presentation and consent.** After zero-finding review, prepare the native
design manifest and present every exact artifact path, artifact hash, runtime
binding hash, writer-policy hash, prepared fence identity, command shape,
permanent one-invocation consequence and residual risk in one root assistant
message.
The next ordinary root `user.message` must explicitly approve that exact
presentation. Tool/agent output, forwarded text, `ask_user` output and any
r27/r28 consent are invalid. Drift in any presented byte or identity requires
new review, presentation and consent before intent; consent never authorizes
P, D1, implementation or release.

Bind the presentation and consent to the root session UUID, event identities,
raw UTF-8 byte ranges and SHA-256, source/role/parent linkage and transcript

missing events or mismatched bytes invalidates consent before intent. No other

**One online invocation and Epoch-A exact write set.** Source inspection of
`recordApproval`/`writeJson` establishes that design recording reads the

Under the verified fence and acknowledged writer pause, run a full read-only
SearchRecheck over the approval inputs and current approval/order/journal

SearchRecheck is two independent no-follow enumerations A/B with stable

The full native text validator must return exactly requirements `approved`,

Launch exactly one native
`approval record design` child using the reviewed manifest hash and explicit
approver; capture complete stdout/stderr, EOF and actual wait status with
65,536-byte bounds per stream. Overflow or incomplete capture is `unknown`.
No wrapper,
controller, agent or root code may write approval bytes. No nonzero, signal,
timeout, lost wait, missing outcome, malformed output or ambiguous post-state
permits a second dispatch.

**Postcondition and continuation.** After the child returns, recheck runtime and fence identities and repeat the
complete SearchRecheck. All `C29` paths outside `ExpectedDelta29` must be
byte-identical; the final design approval must equal the native-produced bytes
and no staging file may remain. Success requires exit 0, exact agreement
between the prepared manifest, design approval and native validation,
requirements `approved`, design `approved`, and a complete `OnlineOutcome29`.
The post-record full text validator must return exactly requirements
`approved`, design `approved`, release `stale`, empty stderr and its documented
nonzero release-not-ready exit. Post-enumerations may differ from pre only by
the exact `ExpectedDelta29`; all other paths and identities remain equal.
Any uncertainty is `unknown`, preserves all bytes, releases no recovery
authority and permanently forbids reinvocation.

Verified success creates `HistoricalEvidenceGap29`,
`RetainedDesignHistory29` and `RecoveryAuthority29`, binding the unchanged r16
loss, r23/r26 custody, r27/r28 retained history, requirements/design approvals,
fresh consent, concrete inventory, fence holder, intent, exact delta and
outcome. Seal `OnlineApprovalResult29` without a future release reference,
terminate the Epoch-A holder by specific PID, capture its wait, verify lock

their mutation entries stay disabled across the short A-to-B boundary; they

is the prerequisite for Epoch B. This ends the one-shot approval lock epoch
without pretending P exists or permitting HEAD drift.

P uses a separate Epoch B under the same prepared fence inode: recollect the
concrete writer inventory, pause/acknowledge it, reacquire the lock, and perform
a fresh complete SearchRecheck bound to the exact current approval and
`RecoveryAuthority29`. It requires the current Git HEAD/control identity to
equal `RecoveryAuthority29.controlHead`, defined as the full lowercase Git HEAD
object ID returned by `git rev-parse HEAD`; the worktree/approval delta remains
separately bound by SearchRecheck. Drift is terminal because the approval
allowance is consumed; it never requests another approval or rebinds authority.
`PermanentPBridge29` binds the concrete
Epoch-B inventory, holder and SearchRecheck and keeps the immutable allocation
identity `authorityKey =
9dc882e33a5b453757c4b3a5ca16593aac43fc8375cde648c74e8e50553c482b` and
`pId =
fe27129bcb82de2245c321e2a8af1e01704a87101fb6013e497881b4c77cd690`.
The fixed authorityKey is namespace/allocation identity only and grants no

Before the first Epoch-B write, seal `EpochBExpectedDelta29` in `G29`. Its
baseline is the exact Epoch-A post-state SearchRecheck, and it enumerates every
permitted final P-tree, registry/index and claim path with its expected type
and final SHA-256. Every timestamp, sequence, nonce and identity used by those
bytes is fixed in this seal; no wall-clock value, UUID or random byte is
generated after it. Each path also names the existing atomic publication
mechanism and any exact same-directory transient pattern; transients must be
absent in the final state and every other `C29` path must remain
byte-identical. The post-Epoch-B SearchRecheck must equal that baseline plus
exactly this allowlist.

After Epoch B verifies the deterministic P as sealed and wholly unclaimed,
reverify the bridge/P seal bytes, current design approval, authority and
controlHead while the same fence remains held, then append the one
`GapCampaignClaim` under that fence using the presealed deterministic bytes.
Immediately before the claim write, fsync `ClaimDispatch29` in `G29` with the
presealed claim hash, exact target/publication identity and
`abortAfterSeal:false`. It is a write-ahead boundary, not proof that a claim
exists.
A claim is durable only when its existing journal/file publication has
completed its required fsync, every transient is absent, an independent
no-follow reread matches the presealed final hash, and the sole claim
registry/index edge resolves it. If `ClaimDispatch29` exists, or any claim/transient path is observed, the abort
path is permanently unavailable. No dispatch record plus complete under-fence
claim/transient absence permits abort. No dispatch record plus any observed
claim/transient is `ambiguous` and still requires the release-intent path.

Before holder termination, seal `EpochBReleaseIntent29`. A normal controller
uses the verified post-Epoch-B SearchRecheck and disposition `verified`. A
resumed controller after a crash between claim dispatch and intent sealing
must first reacquire or prove continued ownership of the same fence, inspect
all predeclared claim/transient paths and seal the intent with disposition
`verified`, `present-unverified` or `ambiguous`; the latter two permanently
poison recovery credit but still permit release. Thus a failed post-claim
SearchRecheck cannot strand paused writers. The intent makes only holder
termination, release observation and
`EpochBReleaseRecord29` sealing idempotently resumable; it never permits
another approval, P write or claim. A resumed controller must match the bound
holder identity, prove it is gone, reacquire the same inode and reproduce the
release-intent disposition before sealing the release record. A null claim
after dispatch is `ambiguous`; `recoveryCreditAllowed` must equal
`claimDisposition == "verified"`. A normal run
also captures the actual wait status. Only a `verified` disposition may feed
`RecoveryAdmission-v6`; a poisoned disposition grants no authority or credit.

Any terminal condition before a durable claim seals `AbortReleaseRecord29`
only after a complete under-fence SearchRecheck proves every claim and claim
transient path absent. Abort and claim are mutually exclusive. For a
between-epochs abort, the Epoch-B holder reference may be null, but the paused
inventory and claim-absence SearchRecheck are still required; if lock
reacquisition is needed, use the prepared inode before sealing abort. The
record grants no recovery authority, P/claim/D1 credit or reinvocation, but
authorizes writer resume; `WriterResumeRecord29` then records the actual
resume. Thus `consumed-no-reinvoke`, between-epoch drift, Epoch-B drift and
partial pre-claim P failure preserve all bytes and block recovery progress
without leaving repository writers permanently paused. A dispatched, present
or durable claim cannot use the abort path and must finish the idempotent
release-intent sequence above.

`RecoveryAdmission-v6`
retains v5's field set but requires `PermanentPBridge29`,
the verified `EpochBReleaseIntent29`, `EpochBReleaseRecord29`, the claim, r29
authority, online outcome, fresh Epoch-B SearchRecheck and P-seal references;
D1 operationId is H(v6). Repository mutation entries remain disabled after
Epoch-B release while the root performs admission and D1 under all existing
guards. Only after D1 is durable may writers resume and
`WriterResumeRecord29` be sealed. A terminal or poisoned path instead resumes
writers immediately after its abort/release record and never enters v6. R29
performs no Red, implementation, Green or release action.

**State machine.**
`draft -> reviewed -> fence-prepared -> presented -> consented ->
writers-paused -> fenced -> rechecked -> intent-sealed -> dispatched ->
waited -> verified-success -> authority-sealed-P-absent ->
epoch-A-release-recorded-writers-paused -> epoch-B-fenced ->
epoch-B-rechecked -> P-sealed-unclaimed ->
claim-rechecked -> claim-dispatch-sealed -> claim-write-attempted ->
claim-classified ->
epoch-B-release-intent-sealed -> epoch-B-release-recorded ->
admitted -> D1-durable -> writers-resume-recorded`.
Drift before `intent-sealed` returns to `draft` without
invocation. Intent without a complete verified outcome, including a crash
before observed spawn, enters terminal `consumed-no-reinvoke`. Terminal states
before `ClaimDispatch29` and with complete claim absence use
`AbortReleaseRecord29 -> writers-resume-recorded` without recovery credit.
After the dispatch seal, or if any claim/transient exists without that seal,
every result uses the idempotently resumable Epoch-B release-intent path; only
disposition `verified` may continue to admission and D1, while poisoned
dispositions release and resume without credit. Only
`verified-success` may create the authority result. Only a fresh successful
Epoch-B SearchRecheck may seal P; no approval reinvocation is possible.

**Atomic separate fence.** The launcher creates the stable regular owned
K/lock with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, writes its bounded permanent gapKey
header, fsyncs file/parent, and never unlinks, renames or replaces its inode.
If already present, verify exact header/uid/mode/single link and reuse inode;
partial/foreign header stops. Supervisor opens it with O_NOFOLLOW and
fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB); EWOULDBLOCK means safe-stop, not takeover.
Only the holder may read/modify state.json. The first absent-state case is
legal ONLY with no existing state.pending, receipt, intent/registry/authority
or evidence of a prior generation; allocate generation=1. Otherwise decode
the complete index, verify previous holder PID/startTicks/bootId is dead or
released and allocate old generation+1, never reset or infer from a clock.

Owner is actual supervisor pid/startTicks from /proc and bootId from the
kernel. PID reuse or another boot is not an identity match. Renew every
10 seconds: verify held FD/inode/owner/current generation, increment renewal,
write the full canonical next index exclusively to state.pending, fsync,
reverify owner/generation/inode, atomic os.replace to state.json, fsync K.
All reads/writes are serialized by that SAME held flock; acquisition and
kernel release are atomic, index publication is atomic rename. Kernel flock
does not expire by wall clock; missing/late renewal stops the current writer,
never lets another writer steal a live lock. Native lease TTL is irrelevant.
Every boundary and immediately before any native dispatch verifies lock
FD/inode, uid/link count, complete current index and live owner/generation.

Release records phase=released/owner=null via the same atomic protocol and
fsync, archives exact index bytes in fence-release.raw BEFORE flock
unlock/close. RootHandoff verifies that immutable raw, not a later mutable
state.json or reconstructed release. Normal exit releases only after sealed
result/receipt and quiesced descendants. On process death the kernel drops
flock; unknown dispatch/index/pending state is preserved and stops. No
unlink-stale-lock, arbitrary SIGKILL, takeover of a live process, inferred
success, index reconstruction or retry directory. A new holder cannot
invoke an old sealed intent. R27 complete pre-guard custody remains immutable
and read-only; its evidence eligibility does not authorize overwriting an
r28 launch whose owner died. This bounded r28 interface permits no automatic
same-consent process relaunch. New process/launch after loss needs a new
reviewed revision and fresh consent, preserving the old custody for explicit
revalidation, never recreation. Incomplete custody keeps r27's terminal rule.

OUTSIDE GapPolicy; it includes only pinned prior bytes, its finite
observations, resource tables, fixed grammar and non-substitution flags,
never these literal hashes, current document bytes, current/future design
manifest, consent or its own hash. Thus adding these literals to approved
documents creates no self-cycle. Any change to policy inputs requires
recomputation and new reviewed documents/consent, but never resets gapKey.
After recording, `approvalLaunch` refers only to the sealed prefix through
approval-verified. Later claim/D1 entries extend its hash chain separately,
never mutate that prefix or introduce a backwards/self dependency.

RawSearchEvidence is the exact schema of the retained scan; semantic
validation independently sums its regular-row sizes/counts, checks sorted
unique paths, two exact declared roots, true stability, zero errors/matches
and absence of the expected raw SHA. SearchRecheck.report uses that same
schema; derive ONE canonical enumeration object directly from that report's
two ordered rows arrays, projecting only
`{path:path,kind:"regular"|"symlink"|"other"}` over the two roots, represented
as exactly `{control:[...],session:[...]}` with sorted unique paths.
Store it once in I-source. Independent no-follow filesystem enumerations
before and after reading the report's files are reduced to the SAME sorted
path/kind projection in memory; their actual observed H values populate
enumerationBeforeSha256/AfterSha256 and both MUST equal enumeration.sha256
and H(the report-derived enumeration). Never emit two unbounded duplicate
enumeration files or invent before/after equality from the report alone.
Enumeration mismatch stops without retaining a successful SearchRecheck;
retain bounded failure output under its reserved owner. File-read stability
is checked separately.
The original snapshot is not retroactively claimed to have these extra
recheck observations. HistoricalEvidenceGap.recheckSearch resolves a
SearchRecheck, not the older report alone. Search per-file hashes are
observations, not Ref edges to all searched contents.

ApprovalCustody is a new archive of AVAILABLE r23 bytes, never a reconstructed
r16 archive. Before replacing live r23, retain its exact raw record and
all 68 exact approval-map artifact bytes, plus the four before-edit document
bytes as documentHistory. Source rows have exact path/mode/size/hash,
UTF-8-path sorted unique sets; approvals map equality is mandatory.
Current r25 design bytes cannot substitute for r23 design bytes. After this
design edit, use only already-retained before-edit bytes that reproduce the
r23 raw hashes, not semantic recreation. Every Source resolves through
`object/archive/<sha256>`. Seal exclusive no-follow/no-replace/fsynced
read-only custody with exact object set; verify before native record.
Future r25 approval raw bytes and all approved artifacts likewise enter
revision-25 immutable currentCustody with its exact four current documents
immediately after recording and before preparation;
failure safe-stops. Never overwrite or append objects to the original D0
archive. The native approval command alone does NOT enforce these guards.

RetainedDesignHistory.availableObservations and GapPolicy.availableObservations
are the SAME finite array: the unique raw objects from the ten-role pinned
table above, the sixteen DIRECT entries (including empty-output duplicates)
of the exact pinned r23ArtifactIndex, and the five additional rows below.
Map each to object/archive/<rawSha256>, deduplicate ONLY identical hash/size
and sort by raw SHA ASCII bytes; no caller selection or extra entries.
Verify each direct index entry's exact file bytes/size/hash before mapping.
Do NOT recursively follow ANY Ref, path, hash or URL inside these observation
contents, including launch stdout/stderr, approval.artifacts, platform
priorAttempt, safe-stop embedded Native/Ref data, or nested artifact indexes.
They are opaque retained observations after their specified local semantic
checks, not a transitive raw closure. D0, r23/current custody, requirements
and new actual native/execution evidence retain their independent complete
verification; this finite history rule never disables their mandatory edges.

The three r16 stderr objects are the same zero-byte SHA already in the

Scalars describing r16's unavailable raw approval
remain descriptions, not unresolved mandatory Refs. Missing ANY required

**State, ordering, single-use and replay.** No native order is allocated by

order 3821 / record

and every preceding order/journal byte remain unchanged.

The recovery exclusion is an owned fenced interprocess launch lock shared
by every approval/recovery entry point, separate from native CHANGE/
projection leases. Hold it across final guard and approval call so native
commands may acquire their own leases without nesting/deadlock; recheck
fence, native head and live bytes at every boundary. Acquire no native
CHANGE/projection lease while builds or runners execute. Writers bypassing
the cooperative lock make the route ineligible; detected drift stops.
All launch entries are canonical closed objects; sequence starts at 1,
increments by one, and previousSha256 is B of the preceding exact entry,
null only at 1. `inputs` is a sorted unique Ref array whose complete raw
closure resolves. `outcome` is null only for intent/claim; actual returns
bind exact argv, cwd, exit/status and stdout/stderr through a Ref. Validate
state-specific inputs, not merely the action label. No timestamp proves
archive-before-record or consent-before-record; ordered observed writes
and bound raw outputs do. The historical r16 11-entry launch chain retains
its original schema and bytes and is checked separately, not re-encoded
as this schema.

The exact action payload contract is below; `inputs` contains ONLY the
listed Refs, sorted by Ref.path, deduplicated only for byte-identical refs.
Referenced entry means the preceding canonical entry bytes published
immutably, not an index number supplied by the caller.

| Action | inputs resolve to | outcome resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| guard-verified | GapConsent, ApprovalCustody revision 23, SearchRecheck | GapGuardSnapshot |
| record-intent | preceding guard entry, GapRecordIntent | null |
| record-return | preceding intent entry | GapCommandOutcome |
| approval-verified | preceding return entry, new raw approval, ApprovalCustody revision 25 | GapApprovalVerification |
| claim-campaign | RecoveryAuthority, GapPSeal, GapCampaignClaim | null |
| campaign-stop | GapPSeal, final PreparationCharge, and prior claim entry ONLY if a claim exists | GapCampaignStop |
| D1-intent | prior claim entry, GapD1Intent | null |
| D1-observed | preceding D1-intent entry | GapD1Observed |

GuardSnapshot binds the exact six-ID native history and five archived Source
rows; its validators resolve actual raw command output, not booleans alone.
For the POST-record native `approval validate --json`, require exactly the
three unique stages requirements, design, release in native order.
Requirements and design MUST be approved with recorded and current artifact
SHA equal to, respectively, the pinned requirements manifest and the freshly
consented design manifest; recompute/verify their complete current native
manifests and raw approval records. Release MUST be stale, and may be
non-current ONLY for that stage; missing, rejected, invalid, foreign,
approved or any other release status stops this scoped guard. Require
overall valid=false, actual process exit=1, signal=null, parseable native
JSON with no operational error and no diagnostic error outside the stale
release classification. Requirements/design diagnostics are empty. Release
and top-level diagnostics must be the same singleton with code
`CHANGE_GENERATION_INCOMPLETE`, severity `error`, path
`.musubix/evidence/approvals/release.json` and the native message
`CHANGE_GENERATION_INCOMPLETE: release approval requires the matching active CHANGE generation.`.
No additional diagnostic is ignored. That exit 1 is the EXPECTED guarded result, never
an overall passing validation or waiver of release readiness. Exit 0/2,
missing/duplicate stages, stale requirements/design, wrong manifest or any
other failure stops. Before native record, only requirements approval must
already be current; the pinned r26 design is expected stale after r27 edits
and cannot satisfy the post-record predicate. The historical r25 validator was
still blocked at that post-record predicate. Native record itself must
return exit 0, as below. GapRecordIntent argv is the existing `npx musubix5 approval record
design --approver <human> --artifact-sha256 <current-manifest> --confirm`
in exact control cwd, with no alternative command/extra options. Outcome
must match that intent, actual parent wait exitCode=0/signal=null and raw
stdout/stderr; validation then independently reads the new native approval
and matches approver, manifest, all 68 artifacts and custody. A command
exit alone does not prove approval. GapCampaignClaim fixes the SAME sealed
P and empty, schema-valid attempt ledger. Seal P with reserved metadata
FIRST, append exactly one claim bound to that P SECOND, author source THIRD;
this is mandatory, never optional "if needed". No source write/attempt
before durable claim. The authority
is bound to P/W through this claim and v3 admission, not through invented
fields in unchanged reservation schemas. GapCampaignClaim.pSeal resolves the
sole verified GapPSeal; its reservation/genesis/authority edges equal the
claim and registry. A stop first finalizes the full actual retained ledger
as P-charge-sealed; GapCampaignStop.preparationCharge is that immutable
final object's Ref, never an incremental ledger or future placeholder.
Its pSeal is the same sole seal, and claim is null ONLY if no claim was
ever appended (for example, authority drift while sealed-unclaimed).
The stop never manufactures a claim or a successful attempt.
D1Intent.operationId equals B of resolved canonical v3
admission, requirements is the exact sorted six-ID set, and its native tip/
fingerprints are actual pinned raw sources. D1Observed validates the real
native record chain/projection, operationId and actualOrder > 3821; it never
uses a predicted order. No new native producer/schema is asserted.

The one-time claim registry is append-only under that fenced lock; its
hash-chain and all claim/stop/D1-intent/D1-observed entries are retained in
excluded custody. Admission preparationEvidence binds only the actual
pre-P-charge-seal prefix and fixed post-P-charge-seal suffix reservations, NOT future
D1-intent/D1-observed bytes (which would form a hash cycle). The reserved
W suffix is bound later by actual D1 outcome/diagnostic payloads. Unreadable, missing-after-
claim, truncated, competing or divergent entries block; exclusive durable
no-replace claim plus fsync/rehash must precede the first authoring write.
Replay verifies the same authorityKey/approval/raw gap/campaign/P and native
journal, never uses timestamps or a new random key. An exhausted, stopped
or invalidated campaign cannot be restarted under the exception; design
reapproval alone cannot issue a second claim for this fixed gap key.
Source/design/input drift, a second missing artifact, any preexisting g9
Red, a changed archived test or non-D0 priorDesign before the sole D1 stops.
Crash after native journal append follows only existing journal-first
recovery from persisted bound inputs; no new ordinal/operation is invented.
Post-D1 exact replay may verify the same D1 at most once in projection,
but never recreates preparation or grants an additional HOST window.
A later design revision needs separate reviewed authority and preserves
this consumed exception and disclosure; this is not a general reapproval
escape hatch.

**R26 reservation identity, publication and exact replay.** Reservation P
is the unchanged PreparationReservation-v4 object; P-charge-sealed refers
to the separate final PreparationCharge, NEVER to the reservation seal.
Define `pId=H(["CHANGE-0017",9,"preparation-reservation",authorityKey])`.
The sole physical P root is
`.musubix/cache/g9-recovery-v1/campaigns/<gapKey>/p/<pId>/`;
`pPath` is that root plus `header/P.json`. Its Ref is still the existing
`object/archive/<B(P bytes)>`; pId is a deterministic allocation identity,
not the content hash or a new native order. The sibling
`.musubix/cache/g9-recovery-v1/campaigns/<gapKey>/w-gap/` owns the W suffix;
it MUST NOT be under a P output root.

Before any reservation byte is written, hold the fenced exclusion and
claim the deterministic `p/` allocation using no-replace ownership
registration. GapPRegistry fixes gapKey/authorityKey/pId/pPath, actual
authority Ref, exact computed P Ref and slot-table Ref; it contains NO
claim, seal, final charge or stop hash. Its registry path/fence records
are gap-P-lifecycle. `header/P.json` and `header/seal.json` (GapPSeal)
belong to the existing P-header slice; table bytes belong to P-table and
the empty attempt/owner-ledger genesis to P-charge. Registry and genesis
contain no seal/claim/final-charge/stop reference; later ledger entries
never replace these immutable genesis bytes. GapPSeal refers only
to these previously verified objects; no backwards hash edge. P-header's
16,384 bytes/4 files, P-table's 262,144/2 and every other cap are unchanged.
Register pending/staged file paths and owners BEFORE their first write.
Use the same deterministic owned pending paths, fsync files/directories,
and no-replace publication; publish the seal marker LAST after reopening
and rehashing the complete exact object set. No random retry directory.
This creates P-sealed-unclaimed; no source or execution attempt exists yet.

Before initial seal, replay or claim, enumerate the entire campaign `p/`
allocation domain and its registered pending paths. Require zero P for
initial publication, or exactly one complete matching P at the derived
root for replay. A second seal request with identical canonical P/table/
registry/authority inputs returns that existing seal without writing;
different bytes at the same identity, another pId/path, multiple P roots,
foreign authority, unregistered bytes or extra seal files fail closed.
Never pick the newest/first P, delete the other, move it out of the walk,
allocate a replacement or erase its charges. Registered partial publication
remains owned retained evidence and BLOCKS claim; it is not a sealed P
and this correction grants no partial-byte reconstruction/overwrite.
An inability to establish unique complete allocation leaves the task
blocked, not a fabricated GapCampaignStop/complete charge.

Crash after complete seal and before claim is deterministic:
re-read the unique registry/P/table/seal/genesis, recheck current approvals/
authority, budget, fence and zero claim/final charge, enter
P-sealed-unclaimed, then append the one claim referencing that stored
P/seal. Do NOT reseal, reset genesis, rewrite old fencing evidence or
allocate another P. A new live fence is verified separately and its
retained registry/fence bytes remain owned; it cannot alter the immutable
seal. Crash after claim uses exact existing claim replay, never another
claim/P. Presence of a final charge or stop forbids claim/source recovery.
If authority drifts after a valid unique seal but before claim, freeze
P writes, seal complete actual accounting, then write the W stop with
claim=null. Before any valid unique P exists, ordinary bounded guard-failure
observations are non-campaign diagnostics; no GapCampaignStop is emitted.
The persistent gapKey still allows only one campaign/one D1. A changed
authorityKey cannot evade the gapKey allocation/claim registry.

**R26 final-charge/stop hash DAG and physical ownership.** On any campaign
failure before the normal charge boundary, first quiesce and reap P
writers, inventory every retained byte (including registered partial/
failed output), finalize the actual P ledger and publish its final
PreparationCharge exactly once under P-charge. Include the unique P,
header/seal, table, registry/fence/claim, real attempts and shared outputs
according to existing owner/selfBytes rules. If this complete accounting
cannot be verified/sealed within its cap, remain blocked with actual
bounded diagnostic bytes; do not mark complete or emit a successful stop.
Only after verifying P-charge-sealed may W publish GapCampaignStop and
its campaign-stop launch entry. A pre-claim failure may have zero attempts
and claim=null; complete accounting is not a successful preparation run.

The directed references are P/registry/genesis -> P seal -> optional claim
-> final P charge -> W stop/entry; arrows mean earlier inputs are bound by
later objects, not that earlier objects contain later hashes. Neither P
seal nor any P-owned inventory/root/ledger/charge contains a stop Ref.
GapCampaignStop binds the final charge, never the reverse. W root walks
resolve that Ref as an already owned immutable INPUT; they do not inherit
W ownership or charge its raw P bytes again. Each physical path/device/inode
has exactly one registered owner and appears in exactly one accounting
root. Overlapping P/W roots, unowned paths, duplicate owners or a stop in a
P root reject. Explicit copied bytes are new physical allocations and must
receive their own correct owner/cap; a Ref is not a copy. Final P walks
exclude the sibling W suffix, so later stop/entry bytes cannot change the
final P inventory or create a recursive hash. This typed ownership walk
does not traverse opaque finite historical observations from the prior
rule. Stop publication is no-replace/idempotent for
`H(["campaign-stop",gapKey,pId,B(final PreparationCharge)])`; exact replay
uses identical retained reason/claim/seal/charge bytes, divergent reuse
stops. A stop consumes the one shot and grants no D1 or restart authority.

**RecoveryAdmission-v3 and unchanged execution boundary.** Start with the
closed v2 field list below, set schemaVersion=3 and kind=
`change0017-g9-recovery-admission-v3`, REMOVE priorDesignApprovalHistory,
and ADD exactly `historicalEvidenceGap:Ref`, `recoveryAuthority:Ref`,

requirements, D0, repository and root/head at every existing binding edge
through authority, admission, sourceSnapshot, P/W and actual execution
evidence. New gap/history edges exist in the v3 triad; claim/admission
transitively bind unchanged P/W schemas, without adding gap fields to them.
Resolve all Ref bytes, rebuild the complete v3 object from raw sources
through a separate consumer parser, and compare canonical bytes/H to the
submitted admission and actual native operationId. No preassembled expected
object or gap flag substitutes for this reconstruction.

Native CLI/checkpoint schemas are unchanged: H(full v3 admission) occupies
the existing operationId and is resolved by the design-level admission
consumer. Native valid approval/checkpoint alone is insufficient. Re-read
the real tip and current native fingerprints before D1; do not reserve
3822, rewrite 3821 or claim tooling existed then. D1 proves only actual
prepared readiness after current approval, not HOST, diagnostic, 27-shape
feasibility, freeze, Red, implementation or release. Their existing order,
fresh actual checks and non-credit/credit separation remain mandatory.

**Canonical encoding and resolver.** All v2 tooling objects are UTF-8
canonicalBytes: recursively sorted object keys, compact JSON, exactly one
terminal LF, safe integral JSON numbers only, no duplicate keys, BOM,
invalid UTF-8, embedded NUL, trailing bytes or unknown fields. Hash B is
raw SHA-256; H is B(canonicalBytes(value)). Arrays are ordered, never
silently sorted by a reader. Set arrays must already be sorted/unique.
The normative type schema below is a closed JSON object algebra: each
`{field:Type}` lists ALL required keys (`T|null` is required nullable, not
optional); `[T]` is an ordered array; quoted alternatives are exact enums;
`int` is a safe signed integer; `uint` is 0..9007199254740991; `pos` is
1..9007199254740991; `sha` is `[0-9a-f]{64}`; `text` is nonempty Unicode
without NUL; `bytes` is canonical base64; `path` is a normalized relative
POSIX path, no empty/dot/dotdot component, absolute prefix or backslash.
This syntax defines the canonical JSON schema, not a new runtime language.
An implementation may compile it to JSON Schema 2020-12 with every object's
additionalProperties=false and required=all keys; it may not broaden it.
`Source`, `Ref`, `Range`, Native and existing content-address grammars keep
their earlier exact definitions. New enums/types below are local to v2.

`string` may be empty (argv and environment values may legitimately be
empty); `bool` is JSON true/false. No arbitrary type names are legal except
the closed earlier types explicitly imported above. Budgets is the exact
existing literal object; all its caps still apply. Bootstrap source is
additionally <=65,536 bytes; BuildSpec and PolicySpec are each <=4,194,304
bytes, and the explicitly materialized 9,587-case FixtureDefinitions is
<=33,554,432 bytes (not subject to the C-source cap). Each schema source/
table reference counts in the existing closure/dependency/inline limits. Source paths in
PolicySpec name the actual newly approved design and retained frozen
source bytes; type names sort by UTF-8 bytes, tables by ID, syscall rows by
number, environment by name, tokens by name, images by pathToken, mounts
parent-first (component count then UTF-8 target), writers/registrations by
their indicated ID/sequence. No generic regex/glob/eval/plugin predicates.
`machine:Ref` resolves one closed GitDef-shaped state machine, including
non-Git rules with maxUnknownCommit=0; transition IDs are fixed by spec.
Policy tokens are exactly C, G, HOME, TMP, VARTMP, TOOL, AUDIT and PROC;
HOST_PROC is a driver-held source handle OUTSIDE ProcBindPlan, NOT a trace-policy
token or a second tracee /proc alias; build/
seed views additionally use ROOT, BUILD, BUILD_OUT, PRIVATE, SEED_SOURCE,
SEED_DIST and OBSERVATIONS as applicable. R/Q NEVER occur in policy.tokens:
their identities enter only the ordered Registration ledger after native
allocation. Resolve most-specific token then component-safe suffix; ambiguous
aliases or a writable overlap lacking an explicit narrower rule reject.

PolicySpec ruleTables includes byte-ranges for all retained write-set,
private-allocation, fixed-parent, Git and C/R/private-blob tables. Data
transcription is checked against those ranges and the source-bound r14
inventory/model, not accepted solely because it validates structurally.
Registry entries are NOT a wildcard grant. The tracer derives registration
at the stopped first syscall from the known process/argv, selected test/
ordinal, unique next frozen call/loop slot, actual path and stable parent.
It journals pending before resumption, owned only on native successful
allocation, collision on native EEXIST without adoption or slot consumption.
Registration.identity is null for pending/collision and the actual stable
new inode identity for owned; the parent identity remains the observed
parent, not a substitute for the allocated inode.
There is no registration socket, environment override, tracee annotation,
test modification or post-exit registration transport. Ambiguous writer/
source-slot attribution fails closed. In JS, a source label denotes the
frozen statically proved caller route plus observed process/operation-state
predicate, NOT an invented native PC-to-JS-stack observation. If the real
fixture cannot distinguish required routes from those observations, source
authoring cannot invent instrumentation: stop for a design correction.

ca22cf892aa1fb85bbbfa59647742aba1987600f07c054430354ef14de835113.
It is fixture input/evidence of observed pinned Git, not an authorization
log to replay as if executed now. Its 222 operations/7 commands and eight
exec observations retain per-writer flags, umask/mode, successful and
ENOENT/EEXIST routes. Spec transcription uses symbolic Q/SIX/full object IDs,
not historical PID/suffix/commit literals. Preserve init's four config-lock

access BEFORE fanout, after known trees/COMMIT_EDITMSG. Independently

**Syscall census transition and two-stage budget (r22).** PolicySpec.syscallCensus
resolves the closed Census object below with complete=false and scope=design.
It is the retained pre-source design census, not a future preparation claim.
TracePolicy.preparationCensus resolves scope=preparation, complete=true for
ONLY its declared seed/fixture corpus and already-built fixture actor. It
does NOT claim the absent runtime or official shapes were run before D1.
Its predecessor is the design census. PolicySpec.requiredSyscalls is an
independent, fixed source/rule-derived table: all syscalls mandated by the
retained r14 Git, directory, C/R/private-blob and writer rules, including
fsync/fdatasync and create-only directory/file synchronization, MUST remain
routed even when absent from empirical startup observations. Each row
binds the exact approved design/frozen source byte range, rule ID and
allowed writers. Rule-source bytes, not runtime execution, justify that
row before D1. Existing startup observations justify the fixed harmless/
compatibility groups; they are not a license to add new syscall permissions.
No required row may be denied solely because its image has not executed
the absent runtime. Operand/path/fd/state/writer handlers still enforce it.
Post-D1, after the existing HOST edit and isolated runtime completion, run
the 12+12 diagnostics and all 27 official-shaped NON-CREDIT feasibility
calls under these same fixed rules. Produce scope=runtime-feasibility
census from those actual reports/TraceLogs, exact completed source/input
hashes and environments, then seal RuntimeCensusBinding before freeze or
any Red/credit. Its policies are the pre-D policy and the two-field
completed-build supplement; it references those policies, never replaces
their hashes or adds a third supplement field. Every observed operand
must be covered by the fixed rules and every expected image/source shape
present; any gap stops before Red. It does not convert unobserved but
rule-required operations into denials. BootstrapRequest.purpose distinguishes
these discovery runs from official credit; official requests require the
sealed binding, while diagnostic/feasibility requests have null binding
and remain non-credit. NamespaceProof binds that request purpose/binding.
The sequence is source-defined rules -> preparation corpus/policy -> D1
(only if the whole-program hard-cap reservation below was already sealed
from actual preparation and available source contracts) -> completed
runtime -> diagnostic/feasibility census -> binding
-> freeze/replay -> Red. No impossible pre-D1 official completeness claim.
The source-bound r18 design Census is retained as

5594d5e8e94fc4dbc3a8ea87781f3bf70ede2257dcafc4cbcfc8c0270be5ae51,

trace pair totals 71,655,205 bytes. These are observed counts/projections,
not native TraceLog sizes or worst-case proofs. -q retains terminal events;
the earlier -qq probes are preserved but not completeness evidence.
The census scope includes each executable image (including interpreter,
loader, env, shell, Git helper, Node, static Go/esbuild, Python, compiler,
cc1, assembler, linker and seed observer), its script/library/header/
dependency closure and each admitted ArgvRule/command shape. Bind raw

observer bytes/options, repetitions, raw traces and reconstruction tool.
versions has exactly one image-path-keyed row for every images member;
aliases sharing one raw executable image keep their distinct exec/script
bindings but do not invent different binary versions. A tool without an
intrinsic version (dash) binds its installed package version observation
AND raw executable bytes; version text alone never authenticates an image.
Record native results and completed/unfinished/resumed joins; signals,
exit and exec identity changes cannot be counted as syscall entries.
Unknown images, undeclared shapes/syscall numbers, foreign ABI/x32 and
unresolved trace rows deny before continuation. A census grants no write/
process permission; the fixed handler must still admit every operand.
No number may become RET_ALLOW merely because a probe happened to use it.
Future tracer/bootstrap images cannot be censused before they exist.
The approved executor must extend the inventory, repeat the exact namespace
and environment census and audit the fixed table before admitting them.
An observed new required syscall not handled here stops for design review;
it is not permission for an executor to add an allow rule.

**Byte ownership and metadata admission (r22).** All sizes are raw stored
bytes, including LF, descriptors, indices, failed/staged durable bytes and
terminal reserves, not filesystem block allocation. No uncompressed shadow
copy may be retained. One physical content-addressed object has one owner;
an actual duplicate physical copy charges again. Deltas may refer to shared
immutable storage without copying. The parent records exclusive owner
assignment before each write and reserves both owner and ancestor aggregate
capacity. Partial files and aborted writes remain charged by actual size.
Deduplication requires the same verified device/inode under immutable custody,
not equal semantic values, equal hashes or a ref alone. The input-store rules
below are the only zero-byte alias exception. No owner can borrow another's cap.

Request metadata owns request/delta, selected header/entry/proof copies,
NamespaceProof, both ProcMountInventory objects, token/credential/action/
map/host inventories, outcome/Terminal/ParentObservation, conservation/
closure/cleanup, TraceLog, per-case envelopes/actual comparisons, indices,
WireObject/WireStream descriptors and retry evidence. Data owns compressed
event/registration/argv/stdout/stderr/mountinfo/seed streams and captured
native output bytes. Shared objects are not recopied in this sum. A metadata
descriptor is external raw canonical JSON unless the following file table
explicitly calls it a WireObject payload. There is NO implicit compressed
envelope containing the stream/event descriptors. Nested children belong to the same
request; they do not create a new quota or namespace/request envelope.
The schema-derived floor must use complete populated objects, 64-hex hashes,
realistic 160..240-byte Ref paths, up to 512-byte host paths, 8 policy tokens,
three proc topology rows, six maps, actual array cardinalities and all output
owners. Empty-array/"x" skeletons are not a metadata-fit measurement.
The retained r20 schema already implies roughly 18..20 KiB per simple request
and >33 KiB for env-hop before event payload; neither 16 nor 32 KiB is an
admissible total cap. R22 requires a model of that realistic floor and a
separate upper-cap admission check; longer inputs or larger inventories
must fail the declared metadata cap, never truncate paths or omit objects.
The r22 session model uses 176-byte Ref paths, a 190-byte host root, eight
tokens, three proc rows per inventory and six map files. It enumerates
physical files and traverses every per-case output Ref, including Ref values
inside decoded Events. It also tests the 240-byte Ref/512-byte host limits:
longer objects must fit the same cap or fail, never be truncated. Model
counts and hashes live in g9-design-r22-metadata-floor.json; they are SIZE
MODELS, not executions, universal lower bounds or future success. The 4,096
terminal reserve is added to the modeled nonterminal total even when a
terminal is already modeled, conservatively. Actual event volumes, input
cardinalities and every aggregate still require the dispatched guards.

**Complete batch-case file ownership.** A "per-case envelope" here means
one of the five explicit WireObjects, not an archive, directory exemption,
implicit descriptor deduplication or a new generic Ref decoder. Their
WireObject descriptor and compressed payload are two physical files each.
The parent owns request/common namespace metadata once per batch. Within
each exclusive cases/<four-digit-index> directory the following is exhaustive
for the retained successful case; partial/failure files keep the same owner.

| Reachable case files | Exact writer | Physical representation | Charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| BatchHandoff | bootstrap driver before fd3 publication | external WireObject descriptor + compressed canonical payload; decoded bytes supplied in sealed memfd, no raw disk copy | slot metadata |
| TraceLog | per-case tracer after sealing its streams | external WireObject descriptor + compressed canonical payload | slot metadata |
| Terminal | per-case tracer after log fsync | external WireObject descriptor + compressed canonical payload | slot metadata |
| actual, comparison | bootstrap driver after native tree/cleanup verification | each external WireObject descriptor + compressed canonical payload | slot metadata |
| each TraceLog.chunks[].ref | per-case tracer | one external raw WireObject descriptor per event chunk | slot metadata |
| each event chunk's .data | per-case tracer | exact zlib stream with required exec/registration flushes | slot data |
| TraceLog.registrations/stdout/stderr and every ExecRecord.argv | per-case tracer | each external raw WireStream descriptor; one external raw WireObject descriptor per referenced chunk | slot metadata |
| every registration/stdout/stderr/argv chunk's .data | per-case tracer | exact compressed raw stream bytes; argv decodes the canonical original string array, registrations the complete ordered JSONL | slot data |
| TraceLog.handoff.filter | per-case tracer | raw reconstructed classic-BPF file, byte-equal to policy.seccomp.program, <=2,048 bytes; one physical copy per case, not assumed free/shared | slot metadata |
| summary.json | per-case tracer | raw canonical Terminal, byte-identical to stdout Terminal and decoded Terminal WireObject | slot metadata |
| captured supervisor stdout/stderr | bootstrap driver | bounded driver capture, not tracee stdout/stderr; compare drained stdout Terminal against summary.json and the decoded Terminal without writing a second stdout copy; unexpected output is retained with its stream descriptors and fails the batch | slot metadata descriptors / slot data payload |
| failed write/staging/driver journal and finalization bytes | writer attempting publication | any retained partial file under the same case root | same metadata/data class as its intended output; failure reserve for bounded terminal/journal |

All input refs in these objects resolve the sealed input catalogue; all
proof-local output refs resolve only the nonce-bound case/shared observation
roots and the fixed typed consumers above. Each different physical output
copy is charged, even with identical bytes. The driver does NOT rewrite a
tracer's raw output into a compressed second authority copy: batch mode
directly writes the declared WireObjects, including TraceLog/Terminal.
The mandatory raw summary is the one explicit duplicate and is counted.
No retained raw handoff/log/actual/comparison, extracted event file or
unlisted transport archive is permitted. Empty streams still have a
WireStream descriptor (chunks=[]); nonempty streams have every chunk
descriptor and payload. Multiple execs/chunks grow these exact families,
not a fixed allowance that silently drops later files. The eight-token/
one-exec/one-chunk size model is not a bound on actual cardinalities.
The BPF <=2,048 cap is an additional check on the unchanged fixed generator;
it cannot remove an allow/trace/deny row to fit. Failed comparison, encoding,
summary mismatch or any cap failure stops the entire batch non-credit.

At each final ledger seal independently walk actual stored outputs AND the
input store, reconcile outputRoots with all owners/requests and the sealed
input identity registry, and reject missing, duplicate-owner or unreferenced
bytes. Each root commits H(the path-sorted array of
{path,sha256,size,device,inode,owner,canonicalPath,chargedBytes} for every
actual regular file below it), with paths relative to that root, files=count
and storedBytes=sum(chargedBytes). Zero-charge alias rows remain in the
commitment and require the exact identity checks below; compute that
canonical array hash incrementally without persisting a second giant
per-object ledger. Roots are disjoint, no-follow, each assigned exactly one
owner before writing. A root may be a regular-file leaf (one inventory row
using its basename) or a directory (rows relative to it); never follow a
symlink or use overlapping roots. At most four roots per request plus 32 shared roots
(1,096 for P); each root row <=768 bytes, each attempt row <=2,048 bytes.

root commitment does not remove any evidence. PreparationCharge excludes its OWN file
from outputRoots;

list of all per-case object Refs. P-charge's 2 MiB cap includes the final
ledger, its bounded append journal and sealing receipt combined; one
canonical snapshot may be published, not 266 retained full-prefix copies.
