| P05 | seed-retry:NN(i):01 | i=1..2 | seed | null | 1 | null | null | null | seed | seed | BS |
| P06 | probe:NN(i):00 | i=1..8 | probe | i | 0 | null | null | null | none | probe | BS |
| P07 | probe-retry:NN(i):01 | i=1..2 | probe | null | 1 | null | null | null | probe | probe | BS |
| P08 | fixture-probe:01:00 | once | fixture-probe | 1 | 0 | env-hop | positive | null | none | fixture-probe | BS |
| P09 | fixture-probe:02:00 | once | fixture-probe | 2 | 0 | ancestor-mkdir | null | 36 | none | fixture-probe | BS |
| P10 | fixture-probe-retry:01:01 | once | fixture-probe | null | 1 | null | null | null | fixture-probe | fixture-probe | BS |
| P11a | fixture:F:C:00 | non-21 fixture F/case C in definition order | fixture | null | 0 | F | C | null | none | case-class(F,C) | BS |
| P11b | fixture-batch:ancestor-mkdir:NN(b):00 | fixture 21, b=1..37 | fixture | null | 0 | ancestor-mkdir | null | b | none | fixture-batch | BS |
| P12 | fixture-light-retry:NN(i):01 | i=1..16 | fixture | null | 1 | null | null | null | fixture-light | fixture-light | BS |
| P13 | fixture-heavy-retry:01:01 | once | fixture | null | 1 | null | null | null | fixture-heavy | fixture-heavy | BS |
| P14 | fixture-batch-retry:NN(i):01 | i=1..2 | fixture | null | 1 | null | null | null | fixture-batch | fixture-batch | BS |
| W01 | diagnostic:plain:NN(i):00 | i=1..12 | diagnostic | i | 0 | null | null | null | none | diagnostic | PS |
| W02 | diagnostic:observed:NN(i):00 | i=1..12 | diagnostic | i | 0 | null | null | null | none | diagnostic | PS |
| W03 | feasibility:NN(i):00 | i=1..27 | feasibility | i | 0 | null | null | null | none | feasibility | PS |
| W04 | official:NN(i):AA(a) | i=1..27, then a in attempts(i) | official | i | a | null | null | null | official if a=1 else none | official | PS |
<!-- G9-R22-DERIVATION-END -->

Concatenate P01..P10, then ONE P11 segment, then P12..P14. Expand
P11 by the exact 22 fixture IDs in the fixture table: at each non-21
fixture emit P11a in its exact case order; at fixture 21 emit P11b with
ascending b; then continue fixture 22. Never put all P11b before P11a or
group cases by budgetClass. case-class(F,C) is fixture-heavy iff
F=pack-clean-env (all six cases) OR (F=git-helper AND C=positive);
otherwise fixture-light. Batch b covers flattened zero-based indices
[256*(b-1), min(256*b,9398)), directory cases then Git cases.
Concatenate W01, W02, W03, W04. Every numeric domain is ascending.
attempts(i)=[0] for i=13,14,27, and [0,1] for every other i.
Thus W04 is INTERLEAVED ordinal-then-attempt, starting
official:01:00, official:01:01, official:02:00, official:02:01,
not all primaries followed by retries. Table position, not execution time,
defines zero-based Merkle index. P has 266 entries; W has 102.

Seed ordinal is ALWAYS null, including build/dist indices; their launch
index belongs to BootstrapRequest.index, not ReservationEntry.ordinal.
Pool retries have null ordinal/fixtureId/caseId/batchIndex even after
allocation; never mutate a sealed leaf to insert the failed primary's
target. PreparationRetry plus request fields bind that target and exact
class independently. W has no diagnostic/feasibility retry pools.
The independent verifier expands this table from approved definition
bytes and validated contracts, byte-compares the supplied array and
recomputes its hash/root; a schema-valid alternative order/ordinal is not
admissible. Shared owner rows, input-store objects and safety margin are
NOT ReservationEntries and never acquire Merkle membership.

Membership uses an immutable header plus ONE selected entry and Merkle
proof, not a catalogue of every campaign slot. Parent AND independent
verifier reconstruct the full canonical ordered entry array from BudgetSpec,
the retained definition schedule and PostSourceContract; check every slot,
class/cap/contract digest and recompute slotsSha256=H(array) and slotsRoot.
Checking only a supplied root/proof or trusting a producer table is invalid.
Pad N leaves to next power of two by repeating the final leaf;
leaf=SHA256("leaf\\0" || canonicalBytes(entry)); internal node=
SHA256("node\\0" || leftDigest32 || rightDigest32), where \\0 means one
NUL byte. Proof index/count/side order/depth must match N and index.
Reject missing, duplicate, out-of-range or cross-reservation membership.
Header, selected entry and SlotProof are immutable request catalogue roots.
The header is a typed OPAQUE leaf: its approval/budget/source/P-charge refs
are verified by the parent's sealed-authority validation, not transitively
recatalogued by each child. W's P/charge links obey the same closed rule.
Other opaque kinds or unresolved launch inputs are forbidden. Catalogue
contains selected-launch inputs plus these three objects, never full slot
table or other slots' source/outcome roots. Reservation overhead is
O(log N) per request: P depth9, W depth7; one O(N) table per campaign.
To avoid also multiplying ordinary immutable input inventories,
Catalogue.base may name ONE immutable base catalogue (whose base=null)
shared by the policy/source view at the fixed immutable path
A/preparation/catalogues/base/<viewSha256>/catalogue.json, where
viewSha256=H({schemaVersion:2,kind:"change0017-g9-tooling-catalogue-v2",
base:null,objects:<exact ordered base rows>}). This directory hash is the
base catalogue's canonical raw SHA, not an ID derived from its own path;
rows' file fields are relative objects/<sha>, so no self-reference exists.
The base Ref.path is preparation/catalogues/base/<viewSha256>/catalogue.json.
Different seed/policy views get different immutable content-addressed bases;
each catalogue JSON is counted once in P-control, never a mutable "current"
base. Its objects directory contains the verified immutable hardlink aliases
defined below, not physical copies of every source/spec for every view.
It contains only common transitive
launch inputs; per-nonce catalogue contains its base Ref and delta rows
(membership trio and genuinely request-local inputs). Resolve
objects/<sha> relative to the catalogue that owns each row. Union must
be disjoint by ref.path: no shadow/override, base chain/cycle, mutable
base or unused effective input. Hash-verify the base under immutable
custody and the delta each request. Common bytes stay one stored object,
not a different full inventory serialization per nonce. Storage is
O(K+N log N), not O(N*K) base copies or O(N squared) slot roots.
Base/delta metadata and proofs remain charged; no input is omitted.

**Immutable input-store and physical identity accounting (r22).** The
single store is A/preparation/input-store/objects/<raw-sha256>. It is not
a sixth authored file, new F member or live mutable catalogue. The parent
imports exact approved immutable inputs, exclusively writes/hashes/fsyncs
each new object, removes every writer handle and seals its inode read-only
before publishing an alias. No transparent decompression is allowed here.
Authoring paths for the five inputs become registered read-only aliases
of their same store inodes after sealing, not retained duplicate copies.
Approved documents imported from control are real new copies and consume
source/snapshot capacity; changing either the approved origin or imported
bytes invalidates currency. Later independent build/source views remain
real physical copies under their original snapshot/dependency limits.

Base and delta row.file stays EXACTLY objects/<row.ref.sha256>, resolved
relative to the catalogue OWNING that row. It must be a regular no-follow
hardlink with the same device/inode/size/hash/mode as the registered
canonical object, or a genuinely new request-local object owned by that
slot. No symlink, "../" escape, absolute fallback or hash-only copy discount.
An unavoidably different-device copy requires its own declared owner charge
before creation; it cannot pass as a free alias. Reuse of already emitted
policies/headers/proofs uses a registered hardlink to their P/W-owned
canonical inode and NEVER relabels those bytes as original source input.
Immutable custody seals file and parent-directory writes between owner
registration, alias creation, dispatch and final verification.

| Canonical byte owner | Hard cap and existing counter | Complete scope |
|---|---|---|
| I-source | 536,870,912 bytes, <=16,000 canonical files; subcaps of snapshotBytes=2,147,483,648 and snapshotPaths=60,000 across all views, not added capacity | immutable original document/test/config/source/history bytes and five approved authored inputs in the store; every additional real source copy also consumes the existing snapshot counters |
| I-dependency | 2,147,483,648 bytes and 100,000 files across store AND all retained dependency materializations, the unchanged dependencyBytes/dependencyFiles ceilings | original pinned tool/compiler/loader/library/header/Python/npm dependency bytes; identical but physically copied files still count again |
| Existing P/W owner | unchanged individual class/shared cap plus emitted-output aggregate | all generated input manifests, source snapshots, catalogue JSON, BudgetSpec, filter/policy/census/provenance, headers/entries/proofs and evidence, including when later read as inputs |

I-source/I-dependency are not additions to the 512 MiB emitted trace
reservation. They are already separately capped original input bytes.
Their use cannot exclude generated observations or buy extra output space.
Any bytes actually embedded into F, inline or sidecar representation must
ALSO pass the existing 512 MiB closure, 320 MiB decoded inline, 46 MiB raw
and 64 MiB immutable-file limits, including duplicate F copies. A Ref
does not exempt a copied payload from these AND constraints.

Known single-store input caps are: design.md <=2,097,152; ADR-0036.md,
CHANGE-0017.md and migration-guide.md <=524,288 each; requirements.md
<=524,288; tracer.c and tracer-bootstrap.py <=65,536 each; BuildSpec and
PolicySpec <=4,194,304 each; FixtureDefinitions <=33,554,432. These ten
raw objects total at most 46,268,416 bytes. Every additional source input
and registry/index byte must have its respective owner; this list is
not a limit on transitive enumeration. The starting r21 four documents
were 891,062/155,209/158,502/146,638 bytes (1,351,411 combined); r22 models
rehash/size the CURRENT four documents and approved requirements, generate
all 9,587 fully populated case definitions, and model full authored-file
caps, rather than a 665-byte skeleton or unspecified base-copy allowance.
Four modeled policy/seed views share those same raw source inodes, while
their distinct catalogue JSON rows and alias bindings still consume
P-control. Actual additional views, dependency closures and path counts
must pass the same caps before sealing; the four-view model is not an
assertion that all future source/tool inventories were measured.
The retained three-view baseline is 905,073,501 source bytes/28,740
paths. Reserving all I-source's 536,870,912 bytes/16,000 canonical files
alongside it gives 1,441,944,413 bytes/44,740 paths before other physical
copies/overlays; each such copy must fit the remaining original counters.
Never multiply the I-source allowance by view or campaign.

Before any alias publication, P-control owns the sealed identity registry
with canonical path, raw hash/size, stable device/inode/mode, owner, origin
(approved-input or generated-output), and exact allowed alias paths.
Subsequent stage extensions are append-only bounded records under P-control,
not retained full-prefix copies; referenced prior records remain immutable.
Generated-output ownership is assigned BEFORE creation and cannot change.
Final verification walks every declared root AND every store/alias path,
no-follow, and builds one global device/inode map. Validate all aliases,
the canonical object and input source/approval reachability, rehash the
actual inode, and require observed link count to equal the complete known
alias-plus-canonical name set. Unknown links or unaccounted open/unlinked
writer files reject; no directory-prefix or hash-equality exclusion.
All root rows retain their logical path/size/hash/identity; chargedBytes
is size exactly at the registered canonical owner's root, 0 only at its
verified aliases. I-source/I-dependency canonical bytes are charged in
their own reconciled input totals, not P/W outputRoots, and their aliases
in a P/W root may be 0 ONLY after those independent totals and immutable
origin bindings verify. Generated P/W objects linked into the input store
remain charged once to their original P/W owner. A same-hash different
inode costs size again; conflicting owners, extra files, detached canonical
objects, mutable aliases, symlinks, unexplained nlink or output-to-input
reclassification reject. Partial/failed output cannot be removed or
exempted by moving/linking it into this store.
The registry and all base/delta JSON remain under their existing explicit
metadata caps. No raw source payload is included in the 2,801,664-byte
P-control metadata partition. Hash each immutable physical input once
under custody and enumerate each alias once; verify only the selected
delta and O(log N) membership per request. K counts all distinct input
bytes plus actual base/view/alias rows, so retained storage/work remains
O(K+N log N), never N copies of K or a quadratic full-slot catalogue.

**Syscall decisions.** The default seccomp action is changed from the old
underspecified allow-default to DENY for unknown numbers, another ABI and
x32; this closes tooling enforcement, not the child program's success
contract. Enumerate every x86-64 number from the pinned headers in the spec.
The allow rows are EXACTLY brk, poll, ppoll, select, pselect6,
rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, rt_sigreturn, rt_sigpending, rt_sigtimedwait,
rt_sigsuspend, sigaltstack, pause, nanosleep, clock_nanosleep, getitimer,
setitimer, alarm, timer_create, timer_settime, timer_gettime, timer_getoverrun,
timer_delete, getpid, getppid, gettid, getuid, geteuid, getgid, getegid,
getgroups, uname, getcwd, getdents, getdents64, gettimeofday, time,
clock_gettime, clock_getres, getrlimit, getrusage, sysinfo, times,
getpriority, sched_getparam, sched_getscheduler, sched_get_priority_max,
sched_get_priority_min, sched_rr_get_interval, sched_yield, getcpu,
sched_getaffinity, futex, futex_waitv, set_tid_address, set_robust_list,
get_robust_list, rseq, restart_syscall and getrandom. capget is admitted as a
routed read-only query (not capset), with target 0/self/owned descendant and
native result retained. These affect no admitted
file/namespace or external process; the pinned libc owns their memory
arguments. No other named syscall is implicitly "harmless".
An operation in the routed set below MUST be trace (unless explicitly
always-denied), never allow.
Trace execve/execveat, fork/vfork/clone/clone3, exit/exit_group,
kill/tkill/tgkill/rt_sigqueueinfo/rt_tgsigqueueinfo, wait4/waitid,
setrlimit/prlimit64, sched_setparam/sched_setscheduler/sched_setaffinity,
setpriority, arch_prctl, umask; open/openat/
openat2/creat, close/close_range, dup/dup2/dup3/fcntl/flock/lseek,
pipe/pipe2/socketpair/eventfd/eventfd2/epoll_create/epoll_create1/epoll_ctl/
epoll_wait/epoll_pwait/epoll_pwait2/inotify_init/inotify_init1/inotify_add_watch/
inotify_rm_watch/timerfd_create/timerfd_settime/timerfd_gettime;
read/pread64/readv/preadv/preadv2 and write/pwrite64/writev/pwritev/pwritev2;
sendfile/splice/tee/vmsplice/copy_file_range; mmap/mprotect/mremap/munmap/
msync/madvise/mincore; stat/lstat/fstat/newfstatat/statx/access/faccessat/faccessat2/readlink/
readlinkat/chdir/fchdir; mkdir/mkdirat/rmdir, link/linkat/symlink/symlinkat,
rename/renameat/renameat2, unlink/unlinkat, truncate/ftruncate, chmod/fchmod/
fchmodat/fchmodat2, chown/fchown/lchown/fchownat, utime/utimes/futimesat/
utimensat, fsync/fdatasync/sync/syncfs/sync_file_range, fallocate;
setxattr/lsetxattr/fsetxattr/removexattr/lremovexattr/fremovexattr, ioctl;
socket/connect/bind/listen/accept/accept4/getsockname/getpeername/sendto/sendmsg/sendmmsg/recvfrom/
recvmsg/recvmmsg/shutdown/getsockopt/setsockopt; pidfd_open/pidfd_getfd/
pidfd_send_signal, process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev, ptrace, seccomp,
prctl, capget/capset, all set*uid/set*gid/setgroups, unshare/setns, mount/umount2/
pivot_root/chroot and new mount API (fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount/fspick/
open_tree/move_mount/mount_setattr), io_uring_setup/enter/register,
open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at, memfd_create, bpf, userfaultfd,
perf_event_open, mknod/mknodat, acct, swapon/swapoff, reboot, kexec*,
init_module/finit_module/delete_module, quotactl and keyctl/add_key/request_key.
Unavailable named numbers are represented by the header inventory and
rejected if called, not assigned guessed numbers. clone3 and io_uring_setup
are the ONLY compatibility actions: skip kernel entry and deliver -ENOSYS
at that SAME thread's matched syscall-exit stop, logging decision ENOSYS,
result -38/errno 38; not a violation or successful allocation. io_uring_enter
and io_uring_register always deny. Deny every other escape/
privilege/device/mount entry and unknown ioctl/fcntl option. For routed self/process operations accept only
pid=0/self or an already registered owned descendant (never negative group
selectors or a host peer); record exact signal/limit/scheduler operation.
umask accepts 0022 and the census-observed read/query pair 0000 -> 0022
from the pinned Node npm pack/npx path (or seed ld). On native umask(0000)
retain prior result 0022 and hold every fs-sharing peer; enter
mask-query-pending. Its next syscall must restore umask(0022), retaining
native prior result 0000; no file operation, fork/exec or resumed sharing
peer is possible between them. Any other next syscall, prior mask or lost
custody aborts. Thus every exec/allocation still runs under 0022; never
synthesize a getumask result or leave a generally permissive mask.
Fixture pack-clean-env/positive checks this actual pair and unchanged
creation modes. arch_prctl accepts only
ARCH_SET_FS/ARCH_GET_FS/ARCH_SET_GS/ARCH_GET_GS with same-process memory;
prctl only PR_SET_NAME, PR_GET_NAME, PR_GET_DUMPABLE, PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS,
PR_GET_SECCOMP and PR_SET_VMA with PR_SET_VMA_ANON_NAME on owned anonymous
memory. Every other prctl/arch_prctl option denies. fcntl accepts only
F_GETFD/F_SETFD (FD_CLOEXEC), F_GETFL/F_SETFL (O_NONBLOCK|O_APPEND changes
only on its admitted fd, allowing unchanged access/status bits such as
the observed O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY argument), F_DUPFD/F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC and F_GETLK/F_SETLK/
F_SETLKW on admitted private files; unknown bits deny. ioctl accepts only
FIONBIO/FIOCLEX/FIONCLEX on owned pipes/socketpairs and read-only
TCGETS/TIOCGWINSZ on owned pipes/socketpairs or an explicitly inventoried
terminal, preserving native ENOTTY or success and exact returned bytes;
never fabricate terminal attributes. Otherwise deny.
R19 adds the missing operand rules, not a blanket socket/fd exemption.
getsockname/getpeername and SOL_SOCKET getsockopt with exactly SO_TYPE,
SO_SNDBUF, SO_RCVBUF or SO_ERROR accept owned pipe endpoints and owned
AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socketpairs. Preserve the native result/output length/
bytes: pipes return ENOTSOCK, not a violation, socketpairs return their
actual local address/options. Bound user buffers to writable owned memory
and sockaddr length <=128 / integer optlen exactly 4; do not synthesize
socket metadata. SOL_SOCKET setsockopt accepts only SO_SNDBUF/SO_RCVBUF,
optlen=4 and positive signed integer <=1,048,576, only on owned socketpairs.
Retain native clamping/doubling and query results; the requested size is
not a promise of the kernel's effective buffer size. shutdown accepts
SHUT_RD=0, SHUT_WR=1 or SHUT_RDWR=2 only on an owned socketpair. Other fd
kinds, option levels/numbers, buffer lengths, oversized/nonpositive values
or shutdown values deny before dispatch. These socketpair query/options
are separate from, and do not broaden, the closed NETLINK protocol below.
fcntl F_GETFD (no flag operand; unused registers are not authority) or
F_SETFD with arg exactly 0/FD_CLOEXEC may address a
nonnegative never-opened or known-closed fd number. With all files-sharing
threads stopped, reconcile /proc/<tid>/fd plus inherited/dup/close ledger:
prove absence before resumption and at matched exit; retain native
-EBADF (result -9/errno 9), create NO fd-ledger entry, and preserve that
absence. An actually open but untracked fd, concurrent allocation, result
other than EBADF on this absence branch, or extra F_SETFD bits is custody
loss/denial, never adoption. No other operation gains an unknown-fd route.
Epoll/eventfd/timerfd/inotify create tracked anonymous descriptors;
inotify watches only admitted read inputs. mmap/msync/mprotect/mremap/
madvise may only manipulate owned anonymous or MAP_PRIVATE memory and
read-only inventoried file mappings; MADV_REMOVE and writable MAP_SHARED
deny. No fd-changing operation bypasses the same provenance ledger.
SyscallDef.handler is determined by the first applicable named group above:
process/enosys, fd, memory, path, network, namespace/deny; read-only queries
use observe. Emit one row per defined pinned-header number, sorted numeric;
every other defined number is action=deny/handler=deny. Unknown numbers
hit the filter default. This fixed classification is not author discretion.
The semantic default-deny is compiled to a TRACE admission stop, not an
unlogged kernel errno: only enumerated allow numbers return RET_ALLOW.
TracePolicy.seccomp.syscalls is the fixed reviewed syscall table, with
requiredSyscalls enforcing all retained rule obligations regardless of
observation. Only the fixed harmless allow rows return RET_ALLOW; every
operand-sensitive or required mutation row is routed and checked by its
writer/source/state handler. In particular fsync/fdatasync cannot vanish
because a startup census did not exercise runtime publication. Unknown
numbers/images/declarations still deny. Empirical image census validates
coverage and operands; it is not intersected into the authorization table.
A
pre-exec trusted child stub is not an arbitrary image exemption: its
exact pre-exec call list is source-bound and admitted separately at the
barrier. Tracee unknown image/shape/call denies before dispatch.
The exact classic-BPF generator is little-endian Linux sock_filter records
(u16 code,u8 jt,u8 jf,u32 k): load seccomp_data.arch, on non-X86_64 return
SECCOMP_RET_TRACE; load nr, on x32 bit return TRACE; for each sorted effective allow
number emit JEQ(number,0,1), RET_ALLOW; finish RET_TRACE. No other branch
returns ALLOW. Source is the hash-bound tracer generator range; program
is the raw generated record array, programSha256=B(program bytes).
Tracer reconstructs and byte-compares it before installation. Denied/
unknown numbers and ABI violations therefore have a recorded pre-kernel
stop; an absent tracer cannot become an allow path. The trace entry handler
uses GET_SYSCALL_INFO's actual architecture and never decodes foreign-ABI
pointer arguments; it skips/denies and kills/reaps instead.
Socket creation is limited to anonymous local socketpair pipes with no
SCM_RIGHTS and the following closed read-only kernel metadata query.
INET/INET6/PACKET, external connect/bind/listen, fd transfer and inherited
sockets are denied and counted. No external network attempt is a pass.
The full npm census also observed libc getifaddrs: AF_NETLINK,
SOCK_RAW|SOCK_CLOEXEC, protocol NETLINK_ROUTE. R17's blanket NETLINK denial
would reject even npm --version. Admit ONLY this namespace-local metadata
protocol (not external networking), preserving r14 deny-inet-v1/zero egress:
bind sockaddr_nl pid=0,groups=0; getsockname reports the assigned owned
port; sendto/sendmsg destination kernel pid=0,groups=0 and exact nlmsg
RTM_GETLINK/RTM_GETADDR, flags NLM_F_REQUEST|NLM_F_DUMP, nlmsg_len=20,
16-byte nlmsghdr plus the observed 4-byte rtgenmsg/padding area, family
AF_UNSPEC and all padding/selector bytes zero (not a full ifinfomsg).
Validate length/alignment/no extra messages, recorded request sequence,
and no ancillary data. recvmsg accepts only replies from kernel pid=0,
matching sequence and owned port, bounded RTM_NEWLINK/RTM_NEWADDR/
NLMSG_DONE/NLMSG_ERROR metadata. Truncation, unexpected type, multicast,
foreign port or any mutation request denies; no route/link/address change
is sent. SOL_SOCKET SO_RCVBUF/SO_SNDBUF (positive <=1 MiB), SO_ERROR/SO_TYPE,
and SOL_NETLINK NETLINK_GET_STRICT_CHK=1 are the only queried/set options
on this descriptor; native unsupported errors are retained. This requires
the proved private NET namespace; a host namespace query is NOT admitted.
Record localMetadataQueries separately from networkAttempts, and reject
unmatched request/reply state. The census itself ran without namespaces
and is evidence of REQUIRED call shape, never authority for host execution.
clone accepts EXACTLY these x86-64 flag words (including low-byte signal):
glibc fork 0x01200011 = CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID|CLONE_CHILD_SETTID|SIGCHLD;
glibc pthread 0x003d0f00 = CLONE_VM|CLONE_FS|CLONE_FILES|CLONE_SIGHAND|
CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_SYSVSEM|CLONE_SETTLS|CLONE_PARENT_SETTID|CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID;
glibc posix_spawn 0x00004111 = CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK|SIGCHLD;
Go/esbuild thread 0x000d0f00 = CLONE_VM|CLONE_FS|CLONE_FILES|CLONE_SIGHAND|
CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_SYSVSEM|CLONE_SETTLS.
Validate stack/TLS/tid addresses in the stopped process's owned memory and
the required ptrace child event/ownership; unknown bits, CLONE_UNTRACED,
namespace bits and any other set deny. Native fork/vfork remain separately
traced. Neither clone3 nor io_uring_setup may synthesize successful handles.

Resource/signal queries in the apparent allow list that accept a pid/tid,
including getpriority/sched_get*/sched_rr_get_interval/get_robust_list,
are routed observe instead of RET_ALLOW: restrict to self/owned descendants.
pid=0 is decoded per syscall (kill(0) targets a process group and DENIES);
getpriority/setpriority require which=PRIO_PROCESS, never PRIO_PGRP/PRIO_USER;
negative selectors always deny. wait4(-1)/waitid(P_ALL) are the sole
negative/all exception, reaping only owned children; they cannot signal or
mutate a host task. pidfd_open may only name a live owned descendant;
pidfd_send_signal validates that recorded fd/task; pidfd_getfd always denies.
Tracee ptrace/process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev always deny. SCM_RIGHTS and
all ancillary fd transfer deny before send/receive; recvmsg/recvmmsg require
msg_control=null and msg_controllen=0 BEFORE dispatch, so an unexpected
rights-bearing peer cannot make the kernel install an untracked fd.
The negative receive fixture supplies a nonzero control buffer and is
denied before blocking; it does not need an untracked inherited socket.
Only owned socketpairs
and the exact kernel-query state above with absent ancillary data use native
I/O. O_PATH/openat2 are admitted only
for no-follow component-checked read-only inventoried inputs, with flags
exactly O_PATH|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW (optionally O_DIRECTORY), or ordinary
already-admitted open flags, open_how size 24 and resolve exactly
RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS. Other resolve/size
bits deny. AT_EMPTY_PATH admits read-only fstatat/statx of an owned
inventoried fd only; linkat/fchownat/execveat empty-path variants deny.
execveat (all variants), memfd_create, open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at,
bpf, userfaultfd, perf_event_open, keyctl/add_key/request_key, mknod/mknodat
always deny for tracees. Driver-only sealed memfd/pivot_root is before the
tracee boundary and cannot be inherited as a tracee capability.

At mutation entry, stop all threads sharing mm/files/fs and read argument
bytes twice under stopped custody. Resolve dirfd/cwd/root and every path
component with pinned identities, no-follow traversal, fd aliases and
link counts; validate all source/destination operands, memory-write sharing
and exact native flags/mode. Keep conflicting peers stopped until matched
exit and identity recheck. Track descriptor inheritance, dup/close reuse,
cloexec, mappings and offsets. unknown open-fd provenance, writable shared
mappings, fd passing, unknown O_PATH/AT_EMPTY_PATH semantics or a race
reject. Read-only inherited fds are explicitly inventoried; tracee stdin is
an owned empty pipe, stdout/stderr are owned output pipes, and no audit,
catalogue, namespace or host-writable descriptor enters the tracee.
Only the exact init symlink leaf can be created, never traversed.
Denial occurs before the kernel mutation: skip syscall, record EACCES and
terminate/reap the owned tree (not a synthesized successful child exit).
Record genuine EEXIST/ENOENT/result unchanged when the admitted syscall
runs. No mkdir/chmod repair, report rewrite or exception remapping.

**Exact tracer argv and streams.** Arrays below are argv grammar, not shell
strings. Angle names denote a SINGLE validated value from the launch input,
except `<arg>*`, which denotes zero or more separate argument strings;
no splitting, expansion, search PATH, shell, eval or response files.
Options occur once in the shown order, long form only, no `--x=y`:

```json
[
 ["<tracer>","--version"],
 ["<tracer>","--help"],
 ["<tracer>","--check-policy","--policy","<policy>","--catalogue","<catalogue>"],
 ["<tracer>","--policy","<policy>","--catalogue","<catalogue>","--audit","<new-audit-directory>","--bootstrap-proof-fd","3","--cwd","<cwd>","--","<executable>","<arg>*"],
 ["<tracer>","--policy","<policy>","--catalogue","<catalogue>","--audit","<new-audit-directory>","--bootstrap-proof-fd","3","--cwd","<cwd>","--fixture","<fixture-id>","--case","<case-id>","--","<fixture-executable>","<arg>*"],
 ["<tracer>","--fixture-child","<fixture-id>","<case-id>"]
]
```

The suffix grammar is `"--","<executable>","<arg>"*`: exactly one absolute
nonempty executable followed by ZERO OR MORE strings; empty strings,
option-looking strings, Unicode and multiple args are valid after `--`,
but NUL is invalid anywhere. An `<arg>*` token is not passed literally. Exact
physical argv/cwd must equal the uniquely selected policy.launches row
after token expansion; logical
argv remains separately bound. Initial child env is EXACTLY launch.environment,
equal to policy.environment, no inherited variables; each exec records the
actual environment digest and applies its pinned ArgvRule/child-env rules
(including npm's frozen PATH algorithm), never initial-env equality to npm
children. Reject NUL, oversized input, empty executable, relative executable,
extra flags and unknown fixture/case before fork. `--check-policy` does not
launch, mount or create an audit. On valid --check-policy: exit 0, empty
stdout and empty stderr; on canonical/schema/ref/semantic failure: exit 65,
empty stdout, Diagnostic JSONL stderr. Invalid option grammar exits 64,
also with empty stdout and Diagnostic JSONL stderr. Read/resolve all
reachable refs and validate policy identity without requiring driver-created
identities or performing namespace/syscall capability probes.
`--fixture-child` is an executable test
target only: it must have the fixture-mode read-only launch capsule on fd 4,
hash/parent/nonce-bound to the traced fixture launch; it is never permitted
by an official/feasibility image argv rule. This is the sole explicit
tracee-fd exception and cannot register or authorize operations. The child
performs the fixed scenario selected by ID; no arbitrary command language.
Version stdout is `change0017-g9-tracer 2 linux-x64-ptrace-v1\n`.
Help is static UTF-8 usage for exactly these forms; both exit 0/no audit.

For run/fixture, tracer stdout is exactly one canonical Terminal after
completion, including pre-dispatch 64/65 errors. Terminal.policySha256 is
null until a complete canonical policy is independently validated; a
parseable unverified field is never an identity. Null is allowed only for
usage/invalid-input, with log/rootStatus null and complete=false; neither
may dispatch. Valid policy prelaunch failures retain its computed hash.
--help/--version/--check-policy are the explicit non-Terminal forms above.
An unrecognized top-level form also emits the nullable usage Terminal/64;
only an argv beginning --check-policy uses its documented empty-stdout
error protocol. Help/version with extra arguments are unrecognized forms.
If output itself cannot be written, stdout may be empty and the parent
records incomplete, not a Terminal. The
stderr is canonical Diagnostic JSONL (first error deterministic by pointer,
then code; no policy secrets or raw environment values). Child stdout/
stderr raw bytes go through supervised pipes into their lossless WireStreams,
never mixed with tracer stdout. EOF, decoded bytes and raw hashes are recorded;
stream truncation is budget failure, not successful truncation. All writes
use the owned audit directory, exclusive/no-follow files, fsync and final
no-replace publication; a missing/unwritable audit fails before child fork.
The driver captures its own stdout/stderr separately and checks terminal
against the published summary bytes. Interrupts kill/reap owned processes;
no output is interpreted as success.

| Tracer exit | terminal class | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | completed | Entire tree closed, child exit 0, zero violations, all invariants. |
| 20 | child-exit | Complete trace; actual root nonzero exit retained verbatim in rootStatus. |
| 21 | child-signal | Complete trace; actual root signal/core status retained. |
| 64 | usage | Invalid argv, no dispatch. |
| 65 | invalid-input | Noncanonical/schema/hash/registration/policy mismatch, no dispatch. |
| 66 | platform | Required ptrace/namespace/filter capability unavailable before dispatch. |
| 70 | denied | Prohibited image/operation stopped before continuation, custody complete. |
| 71 | custody-lost | Lost stop/identity, tracer death or incomplete tree; generationAbandonRequired. |
| 72 | budget | Any event/byte/time/RSS limit reached; kill/reap, no credit. |
| 73 | isolation | Namespace/mount/host conservation drift; no authority. |
| 74 | audit-io | Failed durable log/output/publication; after dispatch also custody-lost disposition. |

These are SUPERVISOR statuses, not rewritten CLI/test statuses. Every
consumer uses rootStatus.rawWaitStatus/exitCode/signal and the class; exit 0
alone is insufficient. If multiple faults occur, disposition is custody-lost
first, isolation second, audit-io third, budget fourth, denied fifth, child
status last. Return the associated wrapper code. Before any terminal can be
durably written, the parent records an observed incomplete outcome with
code 71/74, not a forged tracer terminal or missing fixture "pass".

**Audit wire schema and completeness.**

Schema tagged-union constraints are mandatory: exec iff exec!=null;
syscall/seccomp iff syscall!=null; registration iff registration!=null;
exit iff wait!=null; fork/vfork/clone have child; signal/group-stop have
signal; deny has nonnull violation/ruleId. Every observation retains actual
PID/TID/wait status, not model identities. args are exactly six unsigned
64-bit lowercase hexadecimal words, instructionPointer one such word;
nanoseconds/start ticks serialize losslessly as decimal text where needed.
architecture records the actual kernel AUDIT_ARCH integer even on rejected
ABI/x32 entries; name is the pinned syscall name or literal "unknown".
All other null fields are explicit. Sequence starts 1 and increments in
actual waitpid(-1,__WALL) return order. Related synthetic registration is
written immediately after its triggering entry, before continuation.
Simultaneously ready output pipes drain stdout then stderr; do not sort
events by PID/time or claim byte-identical concurrent runs. Read-only
metadata subrecords sort by operand index then component depth; diagnostic
ties by pointer then code. Content hashes, not time/PID, identify chunks.

Chunk at an event boundary before exceeding 1,048,576 DECODED bytes; one
event may not exceed that cap. R22 preserves every canonical Event byte,
order, operand, signal and decision, but stores sealed chunks losslessly:
Chunk.ref resolves WireObject; WireObject.data resolves the zlib-compressed
bytes with its own raw Ref hash/size. decodedSha256/decodedBytes must equal
the exact original canonical JSONL, not a projection that omits fields.
Use pinned zlib 1.3, deflateInit2(level=6,method=Z_DEFLATED,windowBits=15,
memLevel=8,strategy=Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY=0), no dictionary, one independent
stream per chunk, Z_FINISH, no timestamp/root-dependent header. Same decoded
bytes plus codec pins yield identical stored bytes; concurrent executions
still have different actual observations. No lossy interning or sampling.
Pin /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz.so.1.3 raw SHA
86200da370f20476a2507e9097a789b5ef97269b4ca8d5e164ad82dab9d99892,
/usr/include/zlib.h raw SHA
6f1c7ebe0ac0f0794852b770c20efae041a451f833c91f60f837b599ea81679e,
and /usr/include/zconf.h raw SHA
1800d30368be262886ccaa0b4e0a82240f4b7cd65704f480c988f1ccbf74e14e.
Add exact -lz to the reviewed linker array; inventory resolved loader and
library as build/runtime inputs. Missing/mismatched pins block, not install.

Tooling raw stream/seed-observation refs (BuildRun stdout/stderr/observation,
TraceLog stdout/stderr/registrations, ExecRecord.argv and BootstrapEntry.observations) resolve a canonical
WireObject sequence descriptor for consecutive <=1 MiB byte slices;
its decoded concatenation is the original stream. Use the additional
WireStream type below for these refs. Parent/native JSON proofs, actual
native reports, source and approval Refs remain raw and unchanged; no
transparent compressed fallback for arbitrary Ref types. Record complete
wire/raw hashes and lengths. Readers reject unknown codecs, noncanonical
descriptors, mismatched lengths/hash, trailing concatenated zlib members,
truncation or decoded limits before accepting any event/stream. Verify
canonical encoding by re-encoding with the pinned parameters and derived
exec/registration flush schedule (streams have no intermediate flush),
and compare stored bytes. Counters.traceBytes is stored data/descriptors/
metadata; decodedTraceBytes is decoded event/stream work, tracked separately.
NamespaceProof.mountinfo, ProcMountInventory.mountinfo and FixtureResult.cases
are explicit WireStream consumers: decode exact captured bytes before
parsing/identity comparison. FixtureResult.cases decodes the entire canonical
ordered case array, not a sampled summary. Batch per-case TraceLog/Terminal/
BatchHandoff/actual/comparison objects are the only additional WireObject
consumers; decode their exact closed schema before use. The containing proof/inventory JSON stays raw
canonical. This prevents repeated full mountinfo text from overwhelming
small fixture slots without omitting any mount or observation.
Decode incrementally with <=1 MiB output per chunk, <=64 MiB decoded/call,
<=8 GiB decoded/program, and existing time/RSS caps; never inflate a whole
campaign in memory or persist a hidden uncompressed authority copy.
These additional decoded limits bound streaming work, not new disk/inline
allowances. Stored compressed data + descriptors + all other output bytes
are charged to the slot/P/W ceilings. The wire/decoded cap can fail on
incompressible data: terminate budget/72, never drop the failing decision.
Before resume, compress/durably append exec/registration decisions and
Z_SYNC_FLUSH the open stream, counting emitted bytes; Z_FINISH seals it.
Therefore the stream uses the fixed flush schedule at exactly those
decision boundaries (and final finish), also recorded by event sequence;
no discretionary periodic flush. after sealing reopen/hash. Chunk refs order by
firstSequence with no gaps/overlaps and eventCount equality. TraceLog
chunks+argv+registrations+stdout/stderr+namespace/diagnostics count toward
the selected r22 stored-wire slot caps and 512 MiB whole-program limit
(shared refs counted once per
call, once per full closure); exceeding either blocks success. Immutable
source/spec/binary/provenance inputs are references, not newly emitted
trace bytes: charge their stored bytes once to the existing dependency/
closure/inline budgets, not again to each output reservation. Suite case
indices/results still count toward the 512 MiB aggregate emitted trace
budget and closure caps. This is accounting by artifact kind, not exclusion
of any emitted event or hidden dependency. Do not drop
observations to meet the 100,000-process-event/5,000,000-pack-syscall caps.
Every child/thread needs start/inherited-image or exec identity and actual
terminal status. complete requires started=terminal, live=pendingUnknown=0,
all routed syscall exits closed (or a cancelled record tied to the actual
terminal wait for an in-flight syscall, including exit/exit_group; never a
fabricated successful syscall return), zero unaccounted descriptors/mappings,
both stream EOFs and namespace/post-call checks. A killed descendant's
terminal signal is still retained. Denied fixtures can have complete=true
but never official success. Emit stdout Terminal only after TraceLog fsync;
summary.json contains identical Terminal bytes (no self-reference).
In batch mode the per-case tracer itself emits the five-table transport's
TraceLog/Terminal WireObjects directly and keeps this counted raw summary;
the driver writes BatchHandoff/actual/comparison WireObjects. All event
and stream descriptors remain external files as specified above.
TraceLog's provenance excludes fixtures/audit; the later TracerBuild binds
TraceLog/fixtures in one direction. Final TracerBinding binds TracerBuild,
policy and source/binary, not vice versa.

**Bootstrap driver, fixed CLI and custody handoff.** Author
tooling/tracer-bootstrap.py (<=65,536 bytes, 0644) for pinned
/usr/bin/python3, Python 3.12.3 raw SHA
e50d468e8b0adfb05733f5b87b3cff34829c4a8c1aea50c865aa8bdfe4bb150f.
Inventory its resolved interpreter, standard-library files, extension
modules, libc and loader before execution; `-I -B -S` forbids ambient
PYTHONPATH/user/system site initialization and bytecode writes. Use only pinned standard
library and libc syscalls (ctypes signatures explicitly typed), never
shell/eval, unpinned modules, package installation or downloaded helpers.
It is a deterministic driver, not a musubix5 command or a new runtime test.
The parent may run this exact argv from the approved authoring root:


For namespace runs NamespacePlan additionally has required root:RootPlan
with the same construction algorithm as SeedPlan. `origin=existing` means
non-null StableIdentity measured before policy hashing; compare exactly
device/inode/file-type-and-permission mode/uid/gid at handoff and each
operation. `origin=driver` means identity=null in the policy/SeedPlan,
with an exact NAMESPACE path, creation/mount kind and ownership contract.
AUDIT is always `/__g9_audit`, never the host output path; this literal
token and null identity can be shared across calls/retries. NamespaceProof
binds the actual inode at that fixed mount plus audit.hostPath derived
from its request's nonce. The parent verifies host output fd identity
equals the mounted AUDIT binding. Policy does not contain a request nonce,
host output path, catalogue Ref or NamespaceProof identity.
Require one NamespaceProof.tokens row per plan token, same ordered
names/path/origin, stable observed identity matching existing pins or the
driver's actual created mount/inode. Reject missing/extra/cross-request
bindings, unexpected aliases, owner/mode drift or a non-null driver pin.
NamespaceProof itself and request/policy/nonce are hash-bound in fd3.
FileIdentity.size/nlink/mtimeNs/ctimeNs are observation-only, not frozen
token identity. Recheck stable identity across each operation; volatile
changes must match its actual state-machine transition (including recorded
hard-link publication), not be ignored as a general mutation permission.
R/Q use Registration.parent's stable projection, and native-success
registration stores the resulting stable identity in its observed event;
no prehashed R/Q token or synthetic directory identity is admitted.

files is exactly five source/input files, path-sorted; no output/proof
placeholder. Static checks are optional empty only before performed; they
are not executionEvidence. Actions build/dist-build/npx-bind have a nonnull seedPlan and null
policy/fixtureId/caseId/launch; their seedCommands are exactly the table below.
Fixture has null seedPlan, empty seedCommands and fixture policy. Singles
have both IDs and launch equal the fixture definition, batchIndex=null.
Fixture 21 has caseId/launch/launchIndex=null, fixtureId=ancestor-mkdir and
batchIndex=1..37; the exact contiguous case slice selects launches below.
Run has null seedPlan, empty seedCommands, official/feasibility policy and matching launch, null
IDs/batchIndex. Seed actions require purpose=seed, fixture requires purpose=fixture
or the two fixed purpose=fixture-probe measurement requests;
run requires purpose=diagnostic|feasibility|official. Only official purpose
requires a nonnull runtimeCensusBinding, and it must independently match
the selected policy, source contract and verified post-D1 feasibility/
diagnostic reports. Other purposes require null, never a fake completed
binding. Parent lifecycle guards prohibit official purpose before that
binding/F/replay and actual Red sequence; purpose is not itself native
credit. Diagnostic/feasibility attempt is 0 with retryOf=null; official
attempt 1 uses only the retained operational retry predicates for TDD
ordinals 1..12/15..26. Seed/fixture/probe use P's exact primary/retry pools
and retryOf rules above, not an unconditional attempt=0 restriction.
action=probe requires purpose=probe, probeId exactly 1..8, index=null,
nonnull seedPlan, seedCommands equal its fixed named representative shape,
and policy/fixtureId/caseId/launch/launchIndex/runtimeCensusBinding=null;
it uses the pinned seed observer/codec and no native lifecycle writers.
purpose=fixture-probe uses action=fixture and probeId=1 or 2, selecting
env-hop/positive (batchIndex=null) or ancestor-mkdir/batchIndex=36 respectively.
All other fixture requests have probeId=null. Non-fixture actions have
batchIndex=null. Other actions require probeId=null. Probe 05's seven commands are one
bounded slot in source order, not seven uncharged requests. The slot and
proof must match purpose/target/attempt and cannot be reused after output.
SeedPlan is inventoried actual input data created by the authorized
parent before building, not source-authoring execution evidence. Its mounts
are exactly the read-only inventoried tool paths and selected private source
view, its action-specific writable outputs and separate HOME/TMP mounts;
no control-root source/config/dist/ledger write is possible. Seed command
selection is closed, not a general unaudited execution facility:

| Seed action | Exact logical/physical selection and outputs |
|---|---|
| build | Exactly the two BuildSpec compiler/linker arrays, cwd /build, /build/tooling read-only, only /build/out and private HOME/TMP writable. |
| dist-build | Exactly logical ["npm","run","build"], physical [PINNED_NODE,PINNED_NPM_CLI,"run","build"], in each of two independent materialized source views; inputs are archived-test/runtime-absent control bytes, only each private dist and HOME/TMP writable. Capture subprocess reads/argv through the same pinned seed observer, normalize only the CLI entry to 0755, compare every dist output as the retained BuildProof requires. |
| npx-bind | Exactly logical ["npm","exec","--offline","--package=file:"+C,"--","musubix5","--help"], physical [PINNED_NODE,PINNED_NPM_CLI,"exec","--offline","--package=file:"+C,"--","musubix5","--help"]. C is one validated literal path concatenation, not shell syntax. Fresh verified published dist is read-only; only private npm cache/HOME/TMP outputs. |

PINNED_NODE/PINNED_NPM_CLI are the exact earlier toolchain image/script
paths/hashes, resolved from SeedPlan inventories, not ambient PATH.
dist-build/npx-bind use the earlier closed official initial environment
with private paths mapped to their selected view, no inherited variables;
build uses the exact seven-variable BuildSpec environment. SeedPlan
records the actual read-only view and before/after inventories. The
guarded dist archive/quarantine/publication remains a separately recorded
parent operation under the retained DistReset contract, not a permitted
child mutation of C/dist. npx-bind must yield the actual offline derived
_npx name and .bin/musubix5 resolving to the identical C/dist CLI entry,
bytes AND executable mode. A copied package, registry request, unexpected
install hook or stale link stops preparation, never copy/repair it into a
claimed match. These seed actions precede final policy/fixtures/audit and
have only seed-observer proof; no official ordinal or TracerBuild is needed
to build itself. Final audit covers all seed observations and inputs. Validate request/source snapshot/current exact approval, D0 archive and r25 gap authority
history, executable/library hashes, real uid/gid and every PRE-EXISTING
ancestor before creating anything. Created targets are instead bound at
handoff. Let A be the approved source-authoring root. Request file is exactly
A/preparation/requests/<nonce>.json, catalogue is
A/preparation/catalogues/<nonce>/catalogue.json,
ownedRoot exactly A/preparation/work/<nonce>, and --output exactly the
relative path preparation/observations/<nonce> under cwd=A. `<nonce>` in
both CLI arguments is the request's 64-lowercase-hex nonce, substituted as
one token, not a shell expression. ownedRoot and output are disjoint
same-owner siblings with no existing leaf; they are NEVER independently
caller-selected paths. Validate all ancestors no-follow and claim both
leaves with mkdir(0700) exclusive. AUDIT/OBSERVATIONS is the fixed namespace mount `/__g9_audit` backed by
that output leaf (the two names are this one explicitly allowed alias).
Tracees receive no audit/driver FDs and their operand rules deny access
to the mount; knowing its fixed pathname is not authority to read/write it.
Only the tracer/driver or seed observer may open its output files.
Driver journals request hash/nonce before child spawn.
The parent exclusively creates/seals each catalogue directory and its
objects before publishing the request. BootstrapRequest.catalogue is the
raw Ref {path:"preparation/catalogues/"+nonce+"/catalogue.json",sha256,size};
--catalogue must resolve that exact path and bytes. NamespaceProof.catalogue
must equal the request Ref, and the tracer compares its CLI catalogue
against the proof. No fixed mutable catalogue, nonce reuse, overwrite or
extra/transitively unused objects are permitted. Equal unchanged objects
may use verified immutable same-hash storage; new request catalogues remain
distinct path bindings. The catalogue does not include its own raw Ref.
TracePolicy.launches is the closed ordered set of admitted Launch rows
from the command/fixture definitions; BootstrapRequest.launchIndex selects
exactly one and request.launch must equal that row after the approved
token expansion. Null index/launch is required for seed actions. No argv
wildcard or per-request policy rehash is introduced: the same policy can
serve different allowed calls and fresh-nonce retries. Fixture policies
can share the full case schedule; single request IDs select its unique row,
and batchIndex selects exactly its consecutive slice, not an argv wildcard.
Publish output/outcome.json via exclusive staged file, fsync file, no-replace
rename and fsync parent. Failed/incomplete runs keep both allocated paths
and observations; a retry always uses a NEW request/nonce/ownedRoot/output.
Do not overwrite, rotate in place, reuse a nonce or delete failed evidence.
The same rules apply to every build index, dist view, npx and single/batch fixture request,
so multiple invocations never collide on a fixed outcome path. Request
nonce is parent-generated 32 random bytes, not time/PID-based authority.

Parent retains a supervisor outside the new namespaces; it never mounts.
A forked bootstrap worker unshares USER, waits while the parent writes
setgroups=deny, uid_map=[{inside:0,outside:hostUid,count:1}] and equivalent
gid_map, then unshares MOUNT|NET. Make `/` recursively private first. Outer
mapped root is permitted ONLY during this mount phase and maps to the
same original host owner, not host root. Build a private mount view from an EMPTY tmpfs root, not a read-only host `/`
bind. In the private mount namespace mount tmpfs(nosuid,nodev,mode=0755)
on the exclusively owned ownedRoot/root directory; that is the only host
mountpoint allocation. Construct RootPlan.parents inside this tmpfs,
parent-first, plus every target leaf, using mkdir or O_CREAT|O_EXCL for
an empty regular bind target according to Mount.targetKind/targetMode.
No inferred/optional target is allowed: parents is exactly the sorted
union of proper ancestors of all target paths plus /.old-root. Reject
duplicate/overlapping targets unless an explicit nested mount overrides;
never follow symlinks while creating. Pin source fds before pivot, bind
only inventoried existing files/directories and explicit owned output
directories, remount read-only where declared, with private propagation.
ROOT=/; BUILD=/build; BUILD_OUT=/build/out; PRIVATE=/private; HOME=/private/home;
TMP=/private/tmp for build. SEED_SOURCE is the selected absolute source-view
path, SEED_DIST=SEED_SOURCE/dist; official HOME/TMP paths use the retained
environment table. VARTMP=/var/tmp, TOOL is the inventoried tools path,
AUDIT=OBSERVATIONS=/__g9_audit is the fixed namespace target; its host
backing is selected exclusively from the request. Each path and proper parent
has an explicit target/parent entry even when absent on the host.
Proc is NOT a new `mount -t proc`: that fails in a user/mount namespace
whose unchanged PID namespace is owned by the parent user namespace.
Keep the PID namespace unchanged, use the exact driver-only ProcBindPlan:
the SHARED policy contains ONLY method/source/target paths, recursive
flag, mount_setattr constants and expected relative mount topology.
Expected rows (parent-first) are "/" filesystem proc,
"/sys/fs/binfmt_misc" filesystem binfmt_misc,
"/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/status" filesystem tmpfs; every target requires
flags ["nodev","noexec","nosuid","ro"] sorted by byte. These are the pinned
platform topology from actual probes, not mount IDs/devices/uid/inodes.
Absent/extra/type-changed topology blocks before dispatch and needs review;
do not silently accept a different host layout.

BEFORE EACH dispatch parent pins host /proc's current source identity,
boot ID, PID namespace inode, uid/gid maps, overflow IDs and complete
mountinfo/submount observations in ProcMountInventory(observer=parent).
They are request/nonce-bound NamespaceProof.proc.before, not policy/
SeedPlan/ProcBindPlan bytes. After binding/credential handoff, capture
observer=child in proc.after. Require same boot ID and request, and
after.pidNamespaceInode = before.pidNamespaceInode =
before.parentPidNamespaceInode = after.parentPidNamespaceInode; compare
actual child namespace link to the parent just before dispatch. Across a
later boot the identities may differ while the exact same structural
ProcBindPlan remains valid. Within one request any source/namespace drift
rejects. Never compare to a previous run's boot-specific values.
Make `/` recursively private and bind
`mount("/proc",root+"/proc",null,MS_BIND|MS_REC,null)` onto the precreated
directory. HOST_PROC is held/pinned by the outer parent before unshare;
its per-request host-namespace sourceIdentity is not compared as if its numeric uid/gid
were unchanged inside a user namespace. PROC is driver-origin/null in the
policy, and its actual target TokenBinding is observed after mapping.
For the root and every submount compare device/inode/mode directly and
project each host uid/gid through the recorded one-ID outer/inner maps;
unmapped owners must equal this request's observed overflowUid/overflowGid read from
/proc/sys/kernel/overflowuid and overflowgid. In particular host root-owned
proc normally appears as overflow 65534, not command hostUid. This sole
read-only source-owner projection does not authorize a foreign writable
token or change the same-owner private output rules. Store host and target
identities separately in before/after inventories; do not invent chown or
pin the target's nonexistent inode before the bind. Then call pinned x86-64 mount_setattr(442)
with AT_FDCWD=-100, target path, AT_RECURSIVE=32768 and the 32-byte
mount_attr {attr_set:15,attr_clr:0,propagation:0,userns_fd:0}; 15 means
RDONLY|NOSUID|NODEV|NOEXEC. Require success, never fall back to a writable
or nonrecursive bind. This only adds protections and retains inherited
locked masks/restrictions; no child mount may be unmasked or omitted.
Re-read target mountinfo. Before/after lists must have exactly the same
relative mount paths, device/root/filesystem/source identities and
pre-existing restrictive flags; each target additionally has ro,nosuid,
nodev,noexec and private propagation. Actual target mount IDs are new
observations, not equal to source IDs. Reject a new/disappeared submount,
source drift, writable target, hidden mount or per-request PID namespace
inode mismatch. No boot-specific field enters the shared ProcBindPlan.
Record source/target inventories in NamespaceProof.proc; proof.plan
resolves exactly the NamespacePlan/SeedPlan ProcBindPlan canonical bytes.
The parent retains same-PID /proc identity rules; there is no PID remapping
or new PID namespace. Tracees cannot remount, unshare or write /proc.
At cleanup reap all owned children and release namespace/source fds, detach
only the owned bound subtree with MNT_DETACH (locked inherited submounts
need not permit individual umount), then let its last namespace process
exit. Verify no leaked namespace/process/fd and unchanged host mountinfo;
never attempt to unmount the host /proc or its submounts. The r19 isolated
probe demonstrated recursive bind plus recursive protections; its first
individual recursive-umount attempt failed on locked submounts and is
retained as a failure, not preparation proof.
Bind the
verified host /dev/null character device 1:3 to its precreated file target;
it is the sole nodev=false exception (nosuid/noexec), not permission for
tracee mknod or other devices. All other mounts require nodev=true.
Mask existing denied paths with inaccessible empty tmpfs/regular targets;
absent denied paths remain absent (no mask creates a new host path).
chdir(root), pivot_root(".", ".old-root"), chdir("/"), detach /.old-root,
rmdir it, close every old-root/source fd and verify mountinfo has no old
root or unlisted mount. No host pathname creation except ownedRoot/output
is possible. Root construction fails before command dispatch on any
missing source, unexpected target, mount or pivot failure. Preserve the
absolute C/cwd path by constructing it INSIDE the new root, not by using
the host root as a fallback.
Mount target existence is checked AGAIN after every ancestor mount:
creating a placeholder before a parent bind does not make it survive that
bind. Every directory-bind input must already contain all descendant
mountpoint leaves with the declared kinds. Missing leaves in a read-only
dependency/source view are created only in its independently owned private
materialization BEFORE sealing/binding, with the added placeholders listed
in SeedPlan/NamespacePlan and NamespaceProof.actions. The nearest such
parent is itself an explicit driver-origin bind token (for example the
required privately copied node_modules), never an implicit overlay mount.
Existing C/G authority backing is not copied or modified to manufacture
mountpoints: either the exact narrower target already exists or launch
rejects until a separately authorized, inventoried parent allocation exists.
No host shared dependency may be mkdir/chmod-repaired. `targetToken` and
`sourceToken` use TOKEN plus an optional normalized `/relative/suffix`;
read-only input files may instead use `INPUT:<Source.path>` resolved from
the exhaustive seed inventory. Ambiguous tokens, suffix escapes and
missing source keys reject. RootPlan.parents and the mount list together
exhaust all created paths; no unrecorded `mkdir -p` behavior is implied.
Private /tmp and /var/tmp are two different tmpfs mounts with 01777 roots,
no host backing; TMPDIR points to the owned private TMP subdirectory.
Their namespace-visible existence does not authorize host writes. Mask
/run/WSL, /run/user, /mnt/wslg and nonadmitted npm parent bins exactly as
specified; absent host paths remain absent. Read-only HOME config/npmrc/
globalconfig/templates/tool/compiler/header/dependency/authority views,
private HOME cache/prefix/XDG/tmp and exact narrow control/G/write mounts
follow the retained tables. No wholesale writable C, G, HOME or node_modules.
Read-only mount plus seccomp rules are conjunctive, not alternatives.

To run with the original numeric uid/gid WITHOUT subordinate-ID helpers,
use a second USER namespace after mounts: map inside=hostUid,outside=0,
count=1 and inside=hostGid,outside=0 in the outer namespace; setgroups=deny.
Its parent is outer mapped root, so this one-ID mapping preserves the same
kernel host owner. The worker explicitly verifies setresgid(hostGid) and
setresuid(hostUid), effective/real/saved IDs, unchanged host supplementary
group identities (including their mapped/overflow representations), drops
permitted/effective/inheritable/ambient capabilities, sets no_new_privs=1
and umask 0022. Do not try mapping both inner 0 and hostUid to the same
single outside ID. This two-user-namespace plan replaces r16's impossible
implicit single-map mount-and-nonroot assumption while preserving host
ownership and exact numeric command IDs. A uid/gid/map/drop failure is a
pre-dispatch platform/isolation failure, not permission to run as mapped
root. Record both map levels and namespace IDs (user,mnt,net,pid), with the
unchanged PID namespace explicitly shown; network has loopback DOWN and
no external route/interface. No host mount/network operation is performed. Because setgroups=deny is
irreversible without subordinate-ID helpers, do not claim the launcher
cleared inherited supplementary groups. Capture original kernel group
identities before unshare, require their exact unchanged mapped/overflow
representation at handoff, and admit no new group. All host resources stay
read-only except the same-owner owned/write-set allocations; group
membership is never an additional write rule.

Construct NamespaceProof before exec, canonicalize into a sealed read-only
memfd on inherited fd 3 (F_SEAL_WRITE|GROW|SHRINK|SEAL), and bind its raw Ref
in parent observations, NEVER the already sealed input catalogue. The
fixture-21 batch branch instead puts BatchHandoff on fd3 as specified
below; the underlying shared NamespaceProof is an already sealed output.
Only proof-local generated Refs (namespace/proc/map/action/conservation
observations and prior case terminals) use the output resolver: require
the exact request's preparation/observations/<nonce>/ prefix, strip that
prefix and open relative to the pinned AUDIT fd, no-follow, immutable,
size/hash/type/request-bound. This typed output route cannot resolve or
override a policy/source/launch input or read another nonce. Its objects
are charged to that request; input Refs still require the sealed base/delta
catalogue. No future Ref or mutable catalogue row is inserted. Check /proc identities before and after
the handoff, nonce, FD type/seals, request/source/policy and mount plan.
Its reservation Ref resolves the parent's verified P or W header; P is
required for source/seed/probe/fixture, W for post-D1 purposes. Read only
request.reservationEntry/Proof, verify membership against the header,
then match reservationSlot/stage/target/attempt/case to this request and
enforce that entry's maximumBytes, no larger than policy.limits.traceCallBytes.
Proof.reservation/Entry/Proof must equal the three request Refs. Request
contains no future outcome/proof hash. P is sealed before source/requests;
W references finished P charges only. Neither header references its own
future request/outcome, avoiding a digest cycle. The parent
owns global accounting and verifies prior sealed bytes;
the tracer owns its exact per-call counter, refusing each next event/stream
write that would exceed the smaller reservation. Seed observer output is
also charged and checked by the parent, with failure on any excess; a seed
overflow cannot be sealed/admitted merely because its process exited zero.
Exec the verified tracer with exactly the argv above; inherited fds are only
0/1/2 and 3, and the driver-side audit/output plumbing is inaccessible to
tracees. The tracer verifies fd3, closes it for its child, forks behind its
own barrier, SEIZE/INTERRUPT-stops that child, installs the policy-bound
filter from the child bootstrap stub BEFORE first exec and durably records
the barrier/filter/namespace identities. NamespaceProof covers driver
mounts/credentials; TraceLog covers the subsequent filter and initial-child
custody. Neither may claim to have done the other's work. Never enter
fixture mode or install a weaker filter in an official launch.

Build action uses that SAME driver mount/credential isolation, then the
two pinned build arrays below under the fixed seed observer, not a
nonexistent tracer. Its observations are explicitly non-tracer seed-build
observations, not a TraceLog; read-only tool views, output inventory, actual wait status and
independent byte reproduction plus subsequent audit establish provenance.
This breaks the bootstrap dependency cycle without claiming audited tracer
execution before a binary exists. No official command can use this branch.
Parent detects driver/tracer death, enforces monotonic watchdog/RSS and
kills/reaps only recorded owned PIDs (never process-name killing), verifies
EXITKILL/descendant closure, captures host after-inventory/mountinfo, and
discards namespace views. Host before/after mount table and protected
identities/hash inventories must match; only explicitly owned output/cache
allocations may differ. Audit/private outputs are never copied into host
dependencies. Cleanup removes only inventoried owned allocations after
reaping; preserve sealed evidence and failed observations. Drift, leaked
process/mount/FD, unsuccessful cleanup or missing after-inventory is failure.
Bootstrap stdout is one canonical BootstrapOutcome, byte-identical to its
exclusively published output/outcome.json after file/parent fsync; stderr
is the same Diagnostic JSONL protocol. Missing outcome is incomplete,
never success. Driver --version returns
`change0017-g9-tracer-bootstrap 2\n`; --help prints only the fixed usage;
both exit 0 and perform no namespace/file operation. Bootstrap exits and BootstrapOutcome.driverExit use exactly the tracer
class table, with equality to its exitClass; seed-build child failures
return child-exit/20, actual signals child-signal/21. For fixtures an
expected denial still returns denied/70, NOT success/0. The parent compares
the actual child terminal/outcome to the case and records passed externally.
No expected predicate remaps driver or child statuses. A pre-input CLI
error with no validated request emits empty stdout and Diagnostic stderr,
64 for usage or 65 for input; parent records an incomplete observation,
not a fabricated executionEvidence=true BootstrapOutcome.

**BuildSpec, exact two-command build and evidence.** This deliberately
replaces the single GCC link-driver recipe with an explicit compiler then
linker argv to remove collect2/ld argument ambiguity. Do not use the old
session recipe's combined argv as r22 build authority. Pinned GCC and ld.bfd
hashes/versions remain the earlier exact 13.3.0/2.42 values.

```json
[
 ["/usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc-13","-std=c11","-D_GNU_SOURCE","-O2","-Wall","-Wextra","-Werror","-fno-ident","-frandom-seed=change0017-g9-tracer-v1","-fPIE","-save-temps=obj","-c","-o","./out/tracer.o","./tooling/tracer.c"],
 ["/usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd","--build-id=none","--eh-frame-hdr","-m","elf_x86_64","--hash-style=gnu","--as-needed","-dynamic-linker","/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2","-pie","-z","relro","-z","now","-o","./out/tracer","/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/Scrt1.o","/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/crti.o","/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13/crtbeginS.o","./out/tracer.o","-L/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13","-L/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu","-L/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu","-lgcc","--push-state","--as-needed","-lgcc_s","--pop-state","-lc","-lz","-lgcc","--push-state","--as-needed","-lgcc_s","--pop-state","/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13/crtendS.o","/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/crtn.o"]
]
```

Each clean owned build view has cwd=/build, identical read-only source at
/build/tooling/tracer.c and writable /build/out, separate backing storage
and HOME/TMP. Environment is empty except PATH=/usr/bin, LANG=C.UTF-8,
LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, TZ=UTC, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0, HOME=/private/home,
TMPDIR=/private/tmp; both private paths are namespace mounts, never host
paths. No ambient include/library search bytes are admitted. Inventory the
complete GCC default include/lib/spec/search closures including cc1,
assembler, plugins if loaded, every header (including generated/pinned
syscall constants), specs, crt objects, libc/libgcc/linker scripts/loader,
symlink targets and Python bootstrap closure BEFORE either build. Default
search directories are permitted only as exact read-only inventories; an
unlisted read/dependency or compiler subprocess fails reproducibility.
Capture GCC `-###` plans separately as nonexecuted plans and actual exec
argv/reads from the approved preparation observer; plans are not actual
compiler executions. Never expand a reported string through a shell.
The seed observer is /usr/bin/strace, raw SHA
28f957c227012de0b18d1bd7fff2d396cb693ea60ed8013be68de071e84b5001,
with its entire loader/library closure included in bootstrapInputs. For
clarity this is a NAMESPACE-VISIBLE pinned path, not a claim that host
/usr/bin/strace exists. The retained r14 input is session
g9-design-r14-tools/usr/bin/strace, with those exact raw bytes. Resolve its
immutable input Ref, rehash/inventory dependencies, and materialize only
inside the owned view; never install a host package or search PATH as a
fallback. If the retained input is unavailable, stop before build.
Every seed command uses this EXACT prefix followed by its unaltered
physical command array:
`["/usr/bin/strace","-f","-q","-yy","-s","65536","-v","-e",
"trace=all","-e","inject=io_uring_setup:error=ENOSYS","-e",
"inject=clone3:error=ENOSYS","-o","<observation-file>","--"]`.
Use single -q, never -qq (which suppresses descendant exit records).
These two source-bound observer injections explicitly record INJECTED
-ENOSYS, never pretend to be native kernel returns. They reproduce the
future compatibility path and prevent invisible io_uring submission I/O.
Reject any io_uring_enter/register or successfully allocated ring in seed
observations. This is still strace observation, not tracer custody proof.
No `-c`, filtering out reads, abbreviated strings or sampling is allowed.
`<observation-file>` is one absolute path from the closed table below,
not an independently supplied string:

| Request action/command | Observation file inside request output mount |
|---|---|
| build index 1 or 2 / compile | OBSERVATIONS/compile.strace |
| build index 1 or 2 / link | OBSERVATIONS/link.strace |
| dist-build view 1 | OBSERVATIONS/dist-build-1.strace |
| dist-build view 2 | OBSERVATIONS/dist-build-2.strace |
| npx-bind | OBSERVATIONS/npx-bind.strace |
| probe NN / command JJ | OBSERVATIONS/probe-NN-command-JJ.strace (NN=01..08, JJ=01 except probe05 uses 01..07) |

BootstrapRequest adds index:1|2|null: build/dist-build require 1 or 2,
npx-bind/fixture/run require null. Each independent build/dist view uses
a different request/nonce, not a reused cwd/output directory. For dist
the suffix index equals request.index; build retains both commands in
compile/link order. SeedPlan contains OBSERVATIONS at the fixed namespace path /__g9_audit,
backed by the request's exact host output leaf in every view. RootPlan
creates that namespace target and strace -o resolves ONLY from it;
neither derives a namespace path from the host output pathname. It
never presumes /build exists in dist/
npx views. Only the driver/seed observer owns these log leaves. Under writer
exclusion create each exact log path as a fresh 0600 FIFO (mkfifo, no-follow,
reject any prior leaf), start the pinned driver zlib reader and verify its
read end before spawning strace. strace -o writes that FIFO at the fixed
/__g9_audit path. The reader encodes consecutive <=1 MiB slices directly
to reserved wire objects, counts decoded/stored bytes and drains to EOF;
no uncompressed 10-MiB intermediate file evades a 2-MiB stored cap.
Publish the WireStream descriptor only after observer exit, FIFO EOF and
encoder finish/hash/fsync; remove only the owned drained FIFO. Broken pipe,
reader death, truncated stream or overflow fails the run. Python bootstrap
uses its inventoried zlib extension linked to the same pinned 1.3 library;
this precedes the C tracer and does not require building the tracer first.
No concurrent invocation or tracee may open/write/publish the FIFO or wire
objects; these are trusted seed-observer plumbing, never tracee descriptors.
The source-bound trusted seed children are audited for log mutation; this
observer is NOT an enforcing tracer and cannot prove malicious-seed isolation.
Require complete fork/exec/exit and
unfinished/resumed joins, all byte reads/mapped inputs and fd paths;
unknown, missing or unreconstructable observations invalidate the run.
The fixed string limit may abbreviate read/write buffer DISPLAY only:
admit that abbreviation solely when fd identity, offset and actual returned
length reconstruct every byte from an inventoried immutable input or the
captured owned-output bytes. Hash that exact slice and retain its Source/
Ref; path/argv/environment/exec/sockaddr/control-data truncation, unknown
offset, unaccounted partial write or missing payload always rejects.
This is not omitted I/O evidence or permission to infer bytes from size.
SeedPlan absentPaths explicitly binds failed search probes; virtualReads
admits only the three listed process/device reads, captured as observations,
not invented immutable files. Every other successful tool read resolves an
inventoried input or this build's previous owned output. The observer is a
fixed external trust input inspected by the later audit, not claimed to
enforce the official write policy or substitute for the tracer fixtures.
`-save-temps=obj` keeps intermediates in owned out; no random /tmp fallback.
Pinned tool bytes may differ from their conventional path alias only by
verified internal symlink resolution, never by downloaded replacement.

BuildSpec contains no future output hash, completed audit or successful
fixture claim. Its compiler/linker/interpreter pins are existing inputs,
not evidence they were run. Inventory arrays sort by path and include modes/
raw bytes, toolsetSha256=H({compiler,linker,headers,libraries,bootstrapInputs}).
BuildProvenance has exactly two actual runs [1,2], both commands exit 0,
independent backing identities, equal raw binary bytes/size/100755 mode;
source<=64 KiB, each output<=4 MiB, final TracerBuild<=4 MiB and existing
2 GiB/100,000 dependency budgets. No stripping, timestamp injection,
unrecorded chmod or compare-only-one-build shortcut. Verify ELF64
EM_X86_64, pinned interpreter/library closure, no build-id/root-string
leakage. The audit includes bootstrap source and seed-build observer/trust
boundary, exact filter/syscall tables and absence of shell/plugin loading.
