Policies reference BuildProvenance, not TracerBuild, preventing
binary -> policy -> fixtures -> audit -> build-proof cycles.

**Fixture definitions, order and invocation.** tooling/tracer-fixtures.json
is input, never a result. It transcribes these exact ordered IDs; every
fixture has ordered cases `positive` then its listed adversarial cases,
except deny-only fixtures have no fabricated positive execution.
No expected log bytes/PIDs/timestamps/unknown commit ID are invented.

```text
FixtureDefinitions={schemaVersion:2,kind:"change0017-g9-tracer-fixtures-v2",
 policySpec:Ref,gitOperations:Ref,directoryModel:Ref,gitModel:Ref,
 fixtures:[{id:text,cases:[FixtureCase]}],executionEvidence:false}
FixtureCase={id:text,scenario:text,launch:Launch,inputs:[Ref],
 actors:[{ruleWriter:text,fixtureArgvRule:text,sourceInputs:[Ref]}],
 mutations:[{target:text,field:text,value:string}],
 driverAction:"none"|"kill-tracer"|"drop-stop"|"deny-ptrace"|"omit-proc-ro"|"drop-fd-entry",
 expect:{class:"completed"|"child-exit"|"child-signal"|"usage"|"invalid-input"|
 "platform"|"denied"|"custody-lost"|"budget"|"isolation"|"audit-io",
 supervisorExit:0|20|21|64|65|66|70|71|72|73|74,complete:bool,dispatch:bool,
 decisions:[text],absentWrites:[text],rootExit:uint|null,rootSignal:uint|null,
 treeClosed:bool,hostUnchanged:true,assertions:[text]}}
FixtureCaseResult={id:text,policy:Ref,request:Ref,outcome:Ref,log:Ref|null,
 handoff:Ref|null,terminal:Ref|null,actual:Ref,comparison:Ref,result:"passed"}
FixtureResult={id:text,definition:Ref,cases:Ref,caseCount:pos,result:"passed"}
```

Fixture mutations are fixed literal data edits to that fixture's isolated
inputs, NEVER policy relaxations or arbitrary syscalls/code. Actual/expected
FixtureResult.cases resolves one lossless WireStream decoding a canonical array of FixtureCaseResult in
the exact definition order; caseCount and IDs must match the closed
schedule, with every actual/comparison/log reference verified. This array
is <=33,554,432 decoded bytes; the sum of all 22 decoded arrays is also
<=33,554,432. Their stored bytes/descriptors/indices have P-case-results'
combined 8,388,608 cap, not an unallocated 32 MiB addition.
Keeping the large case arrays content-addressed, rather than inlining them
into TracerBuild, preserves the 4 MiB TracerBuild cap without dropping any
fixture result or changing the 22-ID order. Audit.fixtureResultsSha256 is
H(the ordered 22 FixtureResult rows), transitively binding every case. Actual/expected
comparison is external to the tracer; a tracer "fixture passed" string is
not a result. Case ID/argv must match the definitions, and each expected
assertion below is mandatory; omission is invalid fixture input. Launch
for native scenarios is `[TOOL+"/tracer","--fixture-child",id,caseId]`;
the read-only fd4 capsule contains the exact FixtureCase plus its Ref,
request nonce and known parent ProcessId. Node/Git/esbuild scenarios use
the pinned image and explicit arrays below instead, no sh -c:
`[NODE,"--input-type=module","-e",<inventoried-script-bytes>]`,
`[ESBUILD,"--version"]`, the seven r14 Git argv arrays with expanded Q,
and `[GIT,"maintenance","run","--auto","--quiet"]` only as the commit child.
env-hop uses an inventoried executable fixture script with exact
`#!/usr/bin/env node\n` interpreter hop; its script path is the one-element
command argv, no unknown script admitted. For npm use the exact frozen
pack argv; for Vitest invoke its pinned ResultsCache writer with an
inventoried Node -e fixture program contained in FixtureCase.launch, without
launching the not-yet-implemented runtime tests. Native allocation/blob
scenarios reproduce the exact operation/state predicates with fixture-only
actors; actors explicitly map each ruleWriter to a unique fixtureArgvRule
and pinned sourceInputs. This is a closed synthetic actor substitution in
mode=fixture, never a change to operation/path/flags/mode/order predicates.
Official/feasibility policies reject nonempty fixture actors and fixture
argv rules. Passing those real syscall fixtures proves rule enforcement
under the substituted actor, NOT actual frozen-JS caller attribution.
The post-D1 27-shape/12+12-test diagnostic independently proves that actual
caller attribution; it remains mandatory. This avoids executing absent
runtime code before D1 or claiming modeled writers were observed JS stacks.
Except fixture 21, the driver invokes one case with the fixed
BootstrapRequest action=fixture, fixtureId/id, caseId. Fixture 21 replaces
9,398 per-case requests with 37 batch requests, preserving every case ID,
order and actual assertion. Real namespace tests are required later;
the r14 model is not a substitute.

Each batch creates ONE driver namespace/NamespaceProof/request/delta/
outcome and a monotonically consumed quota. For each of its <=256 cases
the supervisor starts a fresh tracer and fresh owned tracee tree with the
same fixed namespace mounts, a new exclusive cases/<four-digit-index>
audit subdirectory and disjoint owned fixture roots. It cannot reuse a
previous case's allocation/FD/process state. Before continuing, verify
the previous entire tree dead, native cleanup/conservation and baseline
identity/state restoration. A failed comparison, surviving process,
unexpected leftover or custody/isolation/budget failure stops the batch;
it cannot retry an already dispatched prefix or manufacture remaining
results. Intentional expected denials count as passed only after their
native cleanup/assertions pass. Case 21's native operand/state mutations
never alter the shared mount plan or grant a new policy permission.

The batch branch of --bootstrap-proof-fd 3 accepts ONLY sealed BatchHandoff;
singles still accept NamespaceProof. It contains the shared NamespaceProof
Ref, current case/zero-based flattened caseIndex, exact policy, parent/
nonce, previous case's sealed Terminal Ref (null only first), and remaining
metadata/data/decoded quotas derived from the parent's checked ledger.
Validate the request's batchIndex slice, approved FixtureCase and its exact
launch row before spawning; the existing fd4 capsule still binds that case
and parent. TraceLog.namespaceProof points to the ONE batch proof and
handoff.proofSha256 hashes this actual BatchHandoff. Subsequent tracers
cannot replenish quota: subtract every prior case output and check parent
ledger custody before each handoff. Recheck live /proc/mount/credential
invariance per case; unchanged checks are compact actual comparison rows
referencing the batch inventory, not 256 full inventory copies. Drift stops.

Each case retains its full TraceLog, Terminal, BatchHandoff and actual/
comparison objects in typed lossless WireObjects; events/registrations/
argv/stdout/stderr retain their original ordered chunk streams. Per-case
metadata containers AND every external descriptor/filter/raw summary charge
fixture-batch metadata (3,407,872 combined, including the terminal reserve);
their stream data charge its 917,504 data cap. Single case results have
handoff=null and terminal=the actual child Terminal Ref where dispatched.
Batch result rows have nonnull handoff/terminal and their own log/actual/
comparison; request/outcome refer to the one outer batch, never 256
fabricated BootstrapOutcomes. Comparison independently verifies the full
decoded case content and exact slice coverage (no missing/duplicate IDs).
The outer batch BootstrapOutcome.childTerminal is null: no one child
Terminal represents 256 differing native statuses. Its completed/0 means
the driver verified every expected case disposition and cleanup; all
actual case Terminal/rootStatus bytes remain in the case rows. The later
FixtureResult/TracerBuild binds those rows to the already sealed outer
outcome; the outcome cannot point back to an array that contains its own
Ref. Failed/partial batches have non-completed outcomes and no passed
FixtureResult. The independent bootstrap/build verifier checks this
cross-object binding, not a driver aggregate success string.
Final arrays are assembled by streaming case rows in original order, with
all wire hashes/chunk lengths checked, into P-case-results; no huge raw
intermediate escapes the owner caps. Streaming/finalization failures keep
charged partial output and prevent complete/passed publication.
The 64 MiB decoded-call cap applies to the ENTIRE batch (all cases and
streams), not each child; the 8 GiB program and existing event/time/RSS
caps also aggregate across children. This compression/batching is lossless
evidence transport, not sampling or acceptance by a model.

For fixture 21 each index resolves the exact respective preserved model
case's name, inputs and independently asserted result; the fixtures input
must bind those original raw model refs, not just a copied pass count.
Materialize the scenario-specific real syscall sequence from the pinned
registry/model and validate its native outcomes; do not "run" a model then
write a TracerResult. Model `allow`/`EEXIST`/`ENOENT` cases keep the native
outcome, whereas deny cases require stopped-before-mutation. Cases targeting
lost custody are observed by the driver as 71; configuration/identity
corruption caught before launch expects 65/dispatch=false instead of
inventing an exec denial. Case definitions fix the observation boundary:
hash corruption is invalid-input, unapproved but internally hash-consistent
image/rule is denied. Under-capability and event-loss hooks are available
only for their named fixture IDs and cannot be activated through environment.
The case schedule has 9,587 cases (9,398 retained directory/Git cases plus
189 named cases), a definition count only, not executions. R19 adds 38
fixture-16 cases (30 native-success/error-preservation plus eight denial/
custody variants) and four fixture-18 proc-binding cases; fixture 16 now
has 50 cases and fixture 18 has 22. Not all named cases are negative.
The 30 native operand cases preserve actual success/ENOTSOCK/EBADF, complete/0;
the eight invalid-operand variants require denied/70 before mutation except
an actually open untracked fd requires custody-lost/71. No placeholder
fd or socket is entered in the ledger for native EBADF/ENOTSOCK.
The untracked-open case uses the sole named drop-fd-entry hook after an
actually observed owned open; the next reconciliation must detect the
missing ledger entry and stop/71. It is not an inherited arbitrary fd.
proc-rbind-readonly is a driver setup/proof positive followed by the normal
traced no-op child, completed/0; the other three mutate the isolated setup
inputs/observations and require isolation/73 before child dispatch. These
proc-submount-writable uses omit-proc-ro: the isolated fixture driver
omits RDONLY from its actual recursive attr_set, records that fault, then
must detect the writable view and refuse child dispatch. Source-inventory
and PID-drift cases target that request's before/after observations (not
ProcBindPlan pins): change the observed source inode between capture and
handoff, or supply an observed child namespace different from its current
parent, expecting isolation/73 rather than
pretending malformed JSON/hash corruption is a namespace execution.
omit-proc-ro is available ONLY to fixture 18/proc-submount-writable;
drop-fd-entry ONLY to fixture 16/fcntl-untracked-open; every other
case/purpose rejects those actions before setup. No weakened official
mount/ledger or arbitrary fault command is accepted. These are explicit
fixture-18 exceptions to its otherwise deny-only tracee cases,
not permission for a tracee to mount proc or change PID namespace.
Host/process targets in adversarial cases are driver-owned sentinel
processes OUTSIDE the admitted tracee tree, never arbitrary host processes.
Negative/zero process-group selectors are intercepted before dispatch;
the sentinel's independent wait/state/limits prove no mutation.
SCM_RIGHTS cases carry an owned sentinel fd, then assert no transfer; raw
send/recv ancillary buffers and fd inventories are checked independently.
O_PATH/AT_EMPTY_PATH/openat2/execveat/memfd cases assert no path/image escape
or userspace marker. bpf/userfaultfd/perf/keyctl/device cases assert no
kernel resource creation and no host state change. Unknown ioctl/fcntl
use a pinned literal unrecognized request/command, never an arbitrary
dangerous host operation. Each definition names exact numeric syscall,
flags/arguments, actor/image, expected decision/result and observer refs.

**Admission base fields, dependency DAG and stop boundary.** The v2 base keeps
every r16 field/guard and becomes schemaVersion=2,
kind=change0017-g9-recovery-admission-v2. Add these REQUIRED Ref fields:
sourceSnapshot, buildSpec, policySpec, fixtureDefinitions, bootstrapSource,
buildProvenance, bootstrapEvidence, tracerAudit, priorDesignApprovalHistory.
R25 v3 removes that last impossible field and requires historicalEvidenceGap,
recoveryAuthority and retainedDesignHistory instead, under the closed r25
schemas/guards above. This v2 list is a field-list reference, not an accepted
current shape or assertion of retained r16 raw bytes.
R22 requires traceReservation:Ref to W. W.preparation must equal
BootstrapEvidence.reservation (P), and W.preparationCharge must resolve the
rehashed complete P ledger. This one-way P -> finished charge -> W ->
RecoveryAdmission avoids requiring future W before a seed/fixture request.
P alone never authorizes D1; wrong-stage/missing/oversized W rejects.

entries are exactly the 241 successful logical request results: build[1,2],
dist-build[1,2],npx-bind, probes[1..8], fixture-probes[1,2], then the 226
fixture requests in definition order (37 batches replacing fixture 21).

measurement duplicates are never counted as corpus results.

via request.retryOf; no failed primary is overwritten. attempts is the
actual dispatch-order list of all bootstrap requests including failures
and used retries (241 through 265 rows on a completed campaign).
All actual failures and retry usage must also be in PreparationCharge.
author:00/static-check output is separately in that charge, not a fake
BootstrapOutcome. representativeProbes is exactly probes1..8's selected
observed-result refs, with source/argv/codec size checks against PostSourceContract.

must precede the first corpus attempt, and counts derives fixture cases
by expanding/validating each batch slice. Shared P-bootstrap owns every
byte of both arrays and their enclosing object, not just request files.
sequence is contiguous from 1. Each entry's action/index/IDs equal its
decoded request, outcome.request equals entry.request, outcome proof equals
namespaceProof, parent stdout bytes equal canonical outcome and its
driverExit equals decoded parent wait. Build entries have compile/link
observations in that order, dist/npx exactly one each, probes in their exact command order (probe05
seven, all other probes one), fixture none (single TraceLog is in
childTerminal; batch logs/terminals are independently reached through the
exact FixtureResult.cases slice in TracerBuild). No duplicated per-case
log-ref array is inserted into both BootstrapEvidence arrays.
No unrelated observation may be inserted.
No run action or official-call evidence is accepted before D1. A required
missing/invalid outcome is a FAILED preparation entry, not an admissible
BootstrapEvidence. Fixture pre-dispatch platform/invalid-input cases permit
null proof only when that exact case expects dispatch=false; all dispatched
cases require proof. The request must itself be validated even when its
deliberately corrupted child input fails; invalid request/driver CLI never
becomes a successful fixture outcome.
counts is independently derived from entries, never trusted as a summary.
Build entries [1,2] equal BuildProvenance.builds by index, proof, full

Each fixture-21 entry binds one batch's contiguous set of case rows with

Decode parentObservation.hostConservation as HostConservation; independently

tracerAudit resolves canonicalBytes(TracerBuild.audit), exactly byte-equal
to the inline audit after schema validation, with identical source/bootstrap/
binary/provenance and fixture result digest. It has no own/build/admission

Independent admission reconstruction resolves every raw Ref by size/hash,
checks closed schemas, cross-edge equalities, fixture schedule/counts,
namespace origin bindings, class/code mapping, reservations, D0 archive
and current approval/source/native fingerprints. It then constructs ALL
RecoveryAdmission fields from those verified inputs (never spreads a
submitted object), compares canonical bytes to the submitted admission,
and computes H of the reconstructed full object. Compare that digest with
the native operationId. A different but individually valid audit/outcome/
policy chain fails equality before hashing; unknown/omitted keys and
noncanonical bytes reject. R19 RETRACTS the r18 claim that its 61 transport/
8 projection cases independently rebuilt all 37 fields. Their candidate
copies, rehash comparisons and self-exclusion checks are not admission
evidence and are not included in current evidence/model counts.
The exact reconstruction source map is below. It is a consumer algorithm,
not permission to trust a preassembled "independent context" object:

| RecoveryAdmission fields | Independent raw source and derivation |
|---|---|
| schemaVersion, kind, changeId, generation, nonCredit | Closed schema literals and sole-active generation 9 in independently parsed CHANGE ledger; no submitted field is a source. |
| initialDesign, priorDesign | Parse complete pinned native order/CHANGE/journal records; select D0 by change/generation/designOrdinal=1 and currently active design checkpoint independently. Verify raw records, pointer, native source hash, chain and D0 history equality. |
| requirementsCheckpoint, orderTip | Select the active g9 requirements checkpoint and actual final order row from verified native ledgers, not guessed ordinals or candidate Native fields. |
| initialDesignApproval, initialDesignArtifacts | Rehash/decode the read-only D0 archive manifest, its approval object and all 68 approved raw artifacts; reconstruct refs from those bytes. |
| requirementsApproval, designApproval | Independently compute native current manifests from declared stage paths/configuration and compare exact current approval records; a stale record blocks, never becomes a model approval. |
| blockerInputs | Read the closed eight retained blocker paths in the normative table order; raw bytes produce refs, not strings copied from the candidate. |
| documents | Read current design/ADR/CHANGE/guide bytes, validate approved artifact digests and sort paths; derive mode/size/hash from actual files. |
| checkpointFingerprints | Invoke the source-pinned native currentChangeFingerprints over the full six-requirement set; independently validate all seven output domains and source inventory. Never reuse a candidate fingerprint map. |
| archivedTests | Resolve the five ordered archived test bytes through the transition/D0 archive and compare current files at the D1 guard; derive Sources from those bytes. |
| runtimeAbsentPaths | Derive the exact source/script/compiled-output absence set from the approved runtime inventory and verify no profile; do not trust a submitted missing-path list. |
| baselineInputs | Decode the transition manifest's six restored baseline entries, resolve/re-hash their raw objects and compare actual guarded inputs. |
| closure | Parse the approved closed path list and Git-mode exception, require 42 unique paths, compute ordered-array hash and executable literal independently. |
| sourceSnapshot | Decode the independently located sealed authoring snapshot; verify its current approval/doc refs, exact five files and all source bytes/static observations before deriving its raw Ref. |

**R22 interface precedence.** The following r14 implementation rationale's
TracePolicy/TraceLog/TracerBuild/OfficialNamespace v1 shapes and combined
compiler argv are retained historical interface context. Use the complete
r22 schemas, split bootstrap, explicit GCC/ld arrays and 42-file closure
above instead; all process, syscall, writer and allocation safeguards in
the rationale remain mandatory except explicitly replaced r17 interface
details and the r18 read-only namespace-local kernel query clarification.
The tracer owns tracee custody; the driver owns preceding mount setup.

**Exhaustive traced execution, not /proc sampling.** The official supervisor
is the small single-source Linux/x64 ptrace tracer in tooling/tracer.c, built
as tooling/tracer with the closed reproducible proof in tooling/tracer-build.json.
These three output/source paths plus r22's four source/spec additions make F
42 files; no tracer implementation or
binary is created by this design-only action. Before freeze, its actual
source/binary hashes MUST be computed and bound by TracerBinding, BuildProof
and inputs. A placeholder hash, unaudited generated source or unavailable
tracer is a prerequisite failure, never assumed process coverage.

The source implements only this closed supervisor/policy protocol, with no
plugin, downloaded policy or attach-after-exec path. Keep the initial child
behind a tracer-owned pre-exec pipe barrier; PTRACE_SEIZE it with
PTRACE_O_TRACEFORK|TRACEVFORK|TRACECLONE|TRACEEXEC|TRACEEXIT|TRACESECCOMP|
EXITKILL|TRACESYSGOOD, then PTRACE_INTERRUPT and await its event-stop before
releasing the barrier. The child cannot exec before seizure. The trusted
bootstrap creates the namespace/mounts, sets no_new_privs=1 and installs the
hash-bound seccomp filter before first exec. Consume waitpid(-1,...,__WALL).
An early child stop may precede its parent's fork/clone event: retain it in
pendingUnknownTids keyed by tid/startTicks/bootId, never resume it, and join
it only to the exact PTRACE_GETEVENTMSG child identity from a known parent.
Bound this table by processEvents; an unmatched entry at quiescence/exit or
the existing timeout is lost custody. Do not discard or immediately resume
unknown-TID stops. Register every child, including CLONE_THREAD/vfork. At every
PTRACE_EVENT_EXEC, while the tracee is STOPPED, read /proc/<tid>/exe via an
open descriptor, fstat/hash/fstat it, resolve the namespace path, validate its
identity/mode/raw hash against execAllowlist and bind the owned PID/TID/
startTicks/bootId. Record and fsync the ordered exec proof BEFORE PTRACE_CONT.
The initial exec follows the same rule. Handle exec's TID replacement using
PTRACE_GETEVENTMSG; do not drop the former thread identity. Clone-only threads
inherit a verified executable and receive explicit clone/exit records; every
later exec is independently checked. Never PTRACE_DETACH, omit descendants
or infer a short-lived executable from argv. Fork/clone stops are retained
until child registration is durable. No unapproved image executes userspace
instructions after exec-stop admission.
TracePolicy.seccomp={architecture:"AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64",noNewPrivs:true,
source:Ref,program:Ref,programSha256,traceSyscalls:[string],
defaultAction:"allow",clone3Result:"ENOSYS"}. Source/program bytes and the
exact sorted syscall-number/name table are hash-bound before launch; reject
another ABI, x32 entry or filter drift. TRACE routes clone, clone3, ptrace,
setns, unshare, mount/umount, pivot_root/chroot, seccomp, capability-changing
prctl and io_uring entry points to admission stops, plus every file mutation/
descriptor and network operation needed by the declared write/pack policies.
No such operation may be omitted from the prepared table. Deny CLONE_UNTRACED,
namespace/ptrace/filter escape and io_uring bypass. At clone3's seccomp stop,
skip the kernel call and deliver exact -ENOSYS at its syscall-exit stop so
pinned glibc falls back to clone; log that one explicit compatibility action.
It is not success or a lease/test-error remapping. The fallback clone must
be traced and registered normally; its flags are checked before execution.
Use PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO to distinguish seccomp/entry/exit stops; request
PTRACE_SYSCALL only for the matching exit/result or descriptor bookkeeping,
then return to PTRACE_CONT. Claims of syscall coverage apply ONLY to this
filter's routed set, backed by read-only mounts, not to unfiltered syscalls.
Keep shared argument memory stopped where needed until kernel consumption.
Handle exec TID changes, fork/vfork/clone, seccomp, syscall-exit, ptrace
event-stop, signal-delivery, group-stop and terminal wait statuses explicitly.
Pass real signals unchanged; use PTRACE_LISTEN for group-stops and suppress
only identified synthetic interrupt/event/syscall traps. Unrecognized stops
fail custody rather than being swallowed. no_new_privs/filter inheritance
and EXITKILL apply to all descendants.

The tracer sets umask(0022) before first exec and records the prior/current
mask in bootstrap proof. At EVERY exec-stop require /proc/<tid>/status Umask
to equal 0022 and record it; missing/mismatched masks fail isolation. This
is independent of the existing build-mode normalization, not an assumption
that npm or a child kept the inherited mask.

Any unsupported ptrace/namespace capability fails platform BEFORE dispatch.
Any missing/escaped child, lost stop/identity, tracer death, failed log fsync
or unexpected tracer exit after dispatch loses custody: EXITKILL terminates
tracees and classification selects generationAbandonRequired. An unapproved
executable is denied before continuation, recorded as executableIdentity;
if custody remains complete it suspends rather than silently granting credit.
Tracer death cannot be interpreted as CLI success. The supervisor's own
pre-launch ELF identity is verified separately before it creates tracees.
The tracer never rewrites CLI/test exit codes or report bytes.

ProcessProof={pid,tid,parentTid,childTid:null|positive-integer,startTicks,
bootId,sequence,event,role,executablePath:null|string,sha256:null|string,
argv:Ref|null,argvSha256:null|string,exitStatus:null|integer,umask:null|"0022",policySha256}.
event=start|fork|vfork|clone|exec|seccomp|signal|group-stop|exit|deny; sequence is contiguous from 1 in
observed wait order. Exec rows have non-null image/argv identity, clone rows

TracerBinding={source:Ref,binary:Ref,build:Ref,policySha256,abi:"linux-x64-ptrace-v1"}.

They provide neither C/R grammar authority nor publication evidence.

Each fixture verifies stopped-before-continuation and process-tree closure
or its exact fail-closed outcome. These are non-credit tooling checks.
After design approval, provision these tools/tracer BEFORE the pre-D dist
reset, in excluded .musubix/cache/g9-toolchain/<H(TracerBuild)>/ with a sealed
ObjectEntry catalogue. This is diagnostic-tool preparation, not runtime
implementation or a frozen-test edit. BuildProof can therefore bind real
tool hashes before D without depending on D or future F/M. The later F
tooling files are exact copies of those bytes; inputs and build proof refer
to them by hash, with no own-manifest/commit field. Compiler/library bytes
are a versioned external prerequisite, like the pinned installed JS dependency
tree, NOT a new compiler bundle in F. toolsetSha256=H({compiler,linker,headers,
libraries}); Source paths are relative to the private namespace's / root.
Every required installed byte must match this full toolset before copying/
building/reproducing; missing tools fail without a network or host-version
fallback. F binds the manifest and actual build observations, while replay
does not claim it recompiled a binary unless that exact toolset was present.
The source/binary must be audited against this protocol before freeze; this
design action does not pretend that future tool hashes/builds already exist.
Bootstrap order is raw tool/tracer builds, normalized private TS builds and
dist publication and independent isolatedDist inventory, private npx link binding, then final TracePolicy/tracer
fixtures/TracerBuild and assembled BuildProof, ALL before D. Compiler builds
are preparation, not official ordinals. The independent source-range object
can be hashed before BuildProof exists. No final proof is required to build
itself, and no official phase may run with a provisional proof.
Hash-DAG edges point only to earlier objects: raw tools/dist/slices -> policy
-> fixture logs/audit/TracerBuild -> pre-D Toolchain -> BuildProof. The
post-restore dist/slices -> supplement policy; that policy and the post-restore
BuildProof -> supplement. Neither policy contains a BuildProof/Toolchain/
supplement hash; neither dist inventory contains any of those hashes.
Check this dependency graph for cycles before publication, not just its prose.

**Closed official-call namespace.** TracePolicy.namespace is
OfficialNamespace={parentMaps:{uid:Ref,gid:Ref},
uidMap:[{inside,outside,count:1}],
gidMap:[{inside,outside,count:1}],setgroups:"deny",network:"none",
mounts:[{targetToken,sourceToken:null|string,kind:"bind"|"tmpfs"|"mask",
access:"ro"|"rw"}],writeRules:[{id,paths:[string],allocator:null|string}],
dependencyExclusions:["node_modules/.vite-temp","node_modules/.vite/vitest"],distProof:Ref}.
distProof resolves to the canonical isolatedDist array of DistEntry=
{path,mode:"100644"|"100755",size:uint,sha256}, sorted by unique safe
control-relative dist/ paths, using the same inventory encoding as
BuildProof.dist. Only dist/packages/cli/src/main.js has mode "100755";
every other DistEntry has mode "100644". Publish it
before TracePolicy; it contains no BuildProof/Toolchain hash. Require exact
canonical equality with dispatch BuildProof.dist (and its isolatedDist).
parentMaps captures the current tracer parent's exact /proc uid_map/gid_map
before namespace creation. Child inside=outside=current effective uid/gid
in that parent namespace; verify actual child /proc maps after creation;
no remapping to another host owner. Lists sort by targetToken/rule id.
The tracer creates/records ALL mounts before first exec; namespaceProof binds
actual uid/gid maps, namespace identities, mountinfo and effective write rules.
No descendant may change mounts/namespaces. The network namespace has no
interfaces/routes for external traffic; attempted networking is denied.
Mask /run/WSL, /run/user and /mnt/wslg with empty read-only private views
(absent paths stay absent); inherited writable fds/sockets outside the closed
set are closed before launch. All other visible paths are read-only/no-write.
Bind masks and writable-parent views without changing the host mount table.

The following is the complete write-set grammar, not a recursive .musubix
exception. Expand C, Git common root G and selected TEST/ordinal first.
Allocate only through the named pinned writer; register exact realized paths
before admitting their first mutation, reject symlinks/escapes except the
exact transient init tSIX leaf below (never traversal), and retain a
per-call path/op/pid audit. Writable parent mounts do NOT authorize siblings.
The seccomp-routed mutation/descriptor operations enforce these narrower rules:

| Rule | Exact paths or bounded allocator |
|---|---|
| vite-temp | C/node_modules/.vite-temp private tmpfs, empty before AND after the entire tree exits; excluded from dependency inventory only at this exact path. Other .vite paths remain read-only except the exact vitest-results mount below. |
| vitest-results | Private empty tmpfs exactly at C/node_modules/.vite/vitest; exclude exactly this path from dependency inventory. Only the pinned Vitest ResultsCache.writeToCache/VitestCache.resolveCacheDir writer may mkdir <sha1(label)> and write that bucket's results.json; label is its actual projectName or empty string, hash is lowercase SHA-1 hex. Audit then discard the tmpfs at tree exit, never copy it to dependencies/authority. Other .vite paths remain read-only. |
| ancestor-mkdir | For an existing non-symlink directory that is a parent of an admitted path, record an EEXIST no-op; never report synthetic mkdir success. Check component identities under tracer custody through syscall completion. Missing-parent creation is limited to G/musubix5, G/musubix5/leases and G/musubix5/leases/fencing (journal.ts acquireNamedLease/nextFencingToken), the exact runtime parent list below, plus the other rows' explicitly registered bounded directory allocations, not arbitrary prefix descendants. All other required static parents must be provisioned before first exec. Every other mkdir is undeclared/fail-closed; private-path membership alone does not authorize ancestor creation. |
| dist | C/dist admitted BuildProof paths and normalized build outputs only; global-setup and nested Vitest rebuilds may write them, but post-call bytes/modes/path inventory MUST equal the current BuildProof after 0755 entry normalization. No new/unbound dist output. |
| worker-probe | C/.musubix/cache/worker-runtime-probe-<mkdtemp six-character suffix>, allocated by nestedWorker with the per-test bounds in the frozen directory-allocation registry below; only observation.json, worker.test.ts, vitest.config.mjs and native.json inside that exact registered directory. Nested Vitest inherits the same namespace/filter/closure and gets its own separately registered runtime request; the probe is not R. |
| native | C/.musubix/evidence/native/test/<selected TEST-ID>.json only; unlink/recreate is admitted but captured by the retry identity protocol. |
| ledgers | C/.musubix/evidence/{order,tdd,changes}.json and C/.musubix/trace/index.json, with only the actual phase's writer deltas allowed by Facts. |
| journal | C/.musubix/journal/normal/<next 12-digit journal order>.json; bootstrap and prior records stay immutable. |
| runtime | R=C/.musubix/cache/test-runtime/<registered fresh runId> from the registered run-directory inventory, including separate registered nested-run IDs; R/{request.json,dispatch.json,ack.json,worker-acks/<UUID>.json} uses the adopted runtime request/packet schema. For B=C and every registered B=R, only pinned durableBlob may create B/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs/<raw SHA-256> and its exact .<sha>.<UUID>.tmp temporary, mode 0600, create-only/content-verified under the parent/publication grammar below. Outside admitted private TMP, no other blob root or child is admitted; the frozen private-TMP durableBlob roots follow the existing private TMP row plus the registered private-runtime-blobs allocations below, providing neither C/R grammar authority nor publication evidence. |
| source-blobs | C/.musubix/evidence/tdd-source/v1/blobs/<raw SHA-256>, create-only/content-verified; no supersession manifest/approval output is admitted. |
| atomic-temp | Only a registered destination's pinned writer temporary name (including destination.<pid>-<UUID>.tmp), link/rename target and cleanup; bind the exact naming rule/source slice before use. No arbitrary *.tmp permission. |
| external-leases | G/musubix5/leases, resolved from actual Git common root; only the invocation's exact registered CHANGE/projection/append or TDD lease names, owner.json, owner-<UUID>.tmp, fencing/<encoded-name>.json and pinned acquisition/release temporaries. No unrelated lease or common-Git write. |
| private-runtime-blobs | Explicit private-TMP allocations for the frozen EVIDENCE-001 shared helper and BLOB-PLATFORM-001 only: TMP/musubix5-runtime-{evidence,publication,publication-failure}-<six-character suffix> and exactly their .musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs directory chains. Apply the pinned call sites, owners, limits and children in the registry below; ancestor-mkdir checks remain mandatory. Deny TMP/unlisted and every unregistered sibling, including under a registered root. These allocations grant neither C/R authority nor publication evidence. |
| private-frozen-tests | Only the registered private TMP empty probes, child, config and Git/lease fixtures in the frozen directory-allocation registry below, with their exact child sets and pinned writers. No recursive TMP permission, C/G/R alias or authority publication. |
| control-frozen-probes | Only registered C/.musubix/cache/runtime-type-boundary-<six-character suffix> and C/.musubix/cache/runtime-groups-<six-character suffix> from the frozen EVIDENCE-001/AGGREGATE-001 call sites below. The closed authoritative runtime parent grammar has two durableBlob root
categories outside admitted private TMP.
For C, admit C/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime,
C/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1 and C/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs.
R is an exact entry in the registered run-directory inventory at
C/.musubix/cache/test-runtime/<runId>, including each separately registered
nested-run ID; a writable prefix or caller-supplied root is not registration.
For every R, after R and R/worker-acks exist, admit only
R/.musubix, R/.musubix/evidence, R/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime,
R/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1 and R/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs.
Only pinned durableBlob creates either chain, parent-first, mode 0700.
C/.musubix/cache/test-runtime remains an exact parent allocation only for
pinned prepareTestRuntimeProvider, mode 0700; its registered R and R/worker-acks
allocations are unchanged. Require C's evidence/cache ancestors to exist.
Before/after identity/mode checks require absence -> owned non-symlink/0700,
or existing 0700 -> unchanged identity/mode through EEXIST; no chmod repair.
Nonmutating recursive-mkdir ENOENT probes retain the error without advancing
creation order. Hold parent identities stable through each child creation;
reject races, symlinks, wrong actor/order/mode and undeclared children.
At B=C or any registered B=R, only pinned durableBlob may create
B/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs/<raw SHA-256> and its exact temporary
B/.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs/.<sha>.<UUID>.tmp, mode 0600;

exclusively (wx), write/file-fsync/close, then hard-link to the create-only
target; EEXIST is accepted only with exact existing-byte verification.
On POSIX, directory-fsync after publication, unlink that temporary,
directory-fsync again and rehash the target. No replacing rename of a blob
target is admitted; existing transport-file rename semantics stay unchanged.
Bind the temporary, target and cleanup to the same pinned writer/root.
Outside admitted private TMP, no arbitrary root, other filename, sibling
or descendant is authorized by this grammar.

#### G9 closed artifacts, hash graph and immutable closure

All new document kinds below have schemaVersion:1 and the prefix
change0017-g9-recovery- followed by the listed suffix and -v1. Every object is
closed: all listed fields required, no extra keys, no implicit defaults.
H(x)=SHA256(canonicalBytes(x)); B(bytes)=raw SHA256. canonicalBytes uses sorted
object keys, preserved array order, UTF-8 and one LF. Embedded native JSON is
a string: parse/validate it without canonicalizing its native digest input.
SHA values are 64 lowercase hex; orders are positive safe integers; paths are
unique relative POSIX paths without empty/dot/parent components. Nullable
fields below explicitly say null. Lists use the stated order, never locale sort.
Every NEW JSON file (including sidecars and capture graphs) must be byte-equal
to canonicalBytes(JSON.parse(bytes)); reject duplicate keys before parsing,
non-finite/unsafe numeric identities, invalid UTF-8 and trailing data. Raw
approval/native-report/source bytes and embedded native JSON strings are
exceptions: preserve them byte-for-byte and hash with B, not H(parsedValue).
All file Ref.sha256/Source.sha256 values are B(bytes). A new canonical JSON
file therefore has B(bytes)=H(parsedValue); an old raw JSON need not.
Fields named *ObjectSha256, authoritySha256, sourcesSha256, treeSha256 and
aggregateSha256 explicitly use H of the specified value/list, not file bytes.
No normalization of native order/TDD digest inputs is authorized.

Shared closed types:

- Ref={path,sha256,size}; Blob={sha256,size,base64}, with canonical base64 roundtrip,
  exact size/B and no unused entries. sha256 is lowercase SHA-256, size a
  nonnegative safe byte count. A Ref names either an immutable container path
  or a versioned object/ address in an ObjectEntry catalogue, never a live fallback.
  Resolve the full address AND expected B/byte size; equal logical sourcePath
  is not identity. An address cannot be rebound to another version.
  Payload rows sort by sha256 ordinally.
- Range=[start,end] is EXACTLY two nonnegative safe integers, 0<=start<end<=
  source byte length, zero-based half-open UTF-8 with no split multibyte code
  point. All edit/AST/matcher ranges use this type; no third item or line-number
  interpretation. Empty arrays for call chains are allowed only on root TEST
  assertions, not an unknown ownership fallback.
- ObjectEntry={path,sha256,size,storage}; path starts object/ and is unique
  per catalogue. storage is exactly {kind:"git",commit,tree,path,oid,mode} OR
  {kind:"payload",partition}; S catalogues additionally permit
  {kind:"sidecar",path}, with path exactly "objects/"+sha256. The sidecar
  variant is forbidden in F so its closure cannot depend on future S writes.
  Git IDs are 40 lowercase hex (object format sha1);
  git path is tree-relative, mode is 100644|100755, and partition is one of the
  sixteen enumerated payload paths. Require commit^{tree}=tree and that exact
  tree path/mode/blob OID, then recompute both Git blob OID and B(raw bytes).
  No dangling/unreachable loose-object reference or mutable branch name.
  The only object address grammars are:
  object/git/<commit>/<tree-relative-path>;
  object/live/<rawSha256>/<control|shared-git>/<source-relative-path>;
  object/transition/<manifestSha256>/<inventoryIndex>;
  object/archive/<rawSha256>.
  inventoryIndex is canonical nonnegative decimal and selects the exact
  immutable transition manifest.inventory row (including its role/path/hash/
  size); it disambiguates baseline/partial entries with the same source path.
  Git addresses must agree with storage commit/path, live/archive hash
  segments with sha256, and transition rows with the pinned manifest. Equal
  bytes at multiple addresses may share storage; different hashes or sizes
  at any one address reject. Do not strip version segments when resolving.
- Native={sourceRoot,sourcePath,sourceSha256,source:Ref,pointer,recordJson};
  sourceRoot is control|sharedGit. The exact bijection to the live-address
  namespace is control -> control and sharedGit -> shared-git; its inverse
  is control -> control and shared-git -> sharedGit. Never accept shared-git
  as a Native.sourceRoot or sharedGit as an object/live address segment.
  Apply this mapping before comparing logical origins in every F/S catalogue,
  Native/Ref resolver and replay materializer; it does not rewrite native bytes.
  sourcePath is relative to control for
  control sources, or the captured Git common directory for sharedGit sources.
  It NEVER has an artificial control/ prefix. source.path is a versioned
  address of the required Git/live/transition/archive version, not a
  sourcePath-only alias. Verify the catalogue's Git tree path, live namespace/
  path or selected archive inventory origin against the logical source.
  source.sha256=sourceSha256 and source.size is the expected raw byte count.
  pointer is a canonical
  RFC 6901 pointer (empty only for the source root). Resolve it in the
  hash-verified source and require JSON.stringify(selectedValue)=recordJson.
  Never reopen sourcePath directly on replay. The native order-prefix
  descriptor's sourcePath remains EXACTLY ".musubix/evidence/order.json";
  validate it separately, without rewriting it to a storage alias.
  recordJson roundtrips via JSON.stringify after parse and passes native
  schema/hash checks; raw source resolves through source, not an ambient file.
- Authority={repositoryId,changeId,generation,requirementIds,serialIds,
  requirementsApproval,designApproval,requirementsCheckpoint,designCheckpoint,
  orderPrefix,scopeId}; changeId/generation are CHANGE-0017/9, six IDs are CHANGE order,
  serialIds=[REQ-M5-COMPAT-013,REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006]. Approval entries are
  {source:Ref,artifactSha256,identity}; require H(identity)=artifactSha256 and
  exact equality with the raw approval's identity fields. Checkpoint entries
  are {phase:Native,order:Native,journal:Native|null}; null is permitted only
  for an existing singular phase format with no journal field, never for batch
  checkpoints. orderPrefix uses the existing evidence-order-native-strings-v1
  closed descriptor, with exact native recordJson strings through D, its
  extraction SHA and source bytes. No g8 context is an alternative authority.
- Source={path,mode,size,sha256}, where mode is the JSON string `"100644"` or
  an explicitly captured baseline `"100755"` for ordinary source snapshots.
  F has 41 files at `"100644"` and exactly tooling/tracer at `"100755"`;
  r22's other 41 closure files are `"100644"` and no
  other executable/mode exception is allowed.
- Assignment={testId,requirementId,testPath,commandName}; all are nonempty
  strings and exactly equal to the twelve-row table, commandName="test".
  No test aliases, extra fields, duplicate IDs or alternate path spelling.
- Scope={changeId:"CHANGE-0017",generation:9,requirementIds,scopeId};
  requirementIds is EXACTLY ["REQ-M5-COMPAT-013","REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006"] and
  scopeId equals the official nextBatchScopeId result on the captured g9
  batches, checked again at each intent.
- PreparedTests={files:[Source],traceNodes:[{id,path,line}],before:{current,
  workspace},after:{current,workspace},changedPaths}; files are the five
  paths in lexical order, traceNodes the twelve IDs in assignment order with
  positive safe 1-based lines. Fingerprint values are SHA-256; changedPaths
  is exactly ["tests/test-runtime-worker.test.ts"]. Both before/after pairs
  are outputs of the named official calculators, not synthetic values.
- LeaseWindow={source:Ref,retryMs:25,attempts:400,ttlMs:30000,
  deadline:{clock:"performance.now",expression:"performance.now() + leaseAttempts * leaseRetryMs"},
  attemptGuard:{attempts:"wait ? leaseAttempts : 3",condition:"attempt < attempts"},
  deadlineGuard:{condition:"performance.now() >= deadline",action:"break"},
  ownerless:{condition:"ownerlessCreatedAt !== null && ownerlessCreatedAt + leaseTtlMs > Date.now()",
  action:"wait"},delay:{call:"delay",argument:"leaseRetryMs"},
  timeout:{module:"../packages/analysis/src/journal.js",class:"LeaseAcquisitionTimeout",
  code:"LEASE_ACQUISITION_TIMEOUT",leaseKind:"change",leaseName:"change-CHANGE-0017",
  message:"Timed out acquiring change lease change-CHANGE-0017."},
  watchdog:{milliseconds:60000,role:"runner-only"}}. All values are literals;
  parse/verify the source AST and the pinned raw journal SHA, not whitespace
  regex matching. The no-wait return branch remains unchanged.
- GitFile={path,mode,oid,size,sha256}. Snapshot={git:{objectFormat:"sha1",
  commit,tree,entries:[GitFile],entriesSha256},overlays:[Overlay],
  sourcePaths,sourceInventorySha256,changeDocument,nonCalculatorInputs}.
  changeDocument={path:".musubix/changes/CHANGE-0017.md",source:Ref,
  designImpactFingerprint}; nonCalculatorInputs is exactly
  [{path:".musubix/trace/index.json",role:"generated-trace",source:Ref},
  {path:"docs/migration-guide.md",role:"migration-guide",source:Ref}].
  designImpactFingerprint is D.fingerprints.impact, not the original 3819
  impact checkpoint and not the raw file hash. Recompute that existing
  official fingerprint on the materialized CHANGE document; it must agree.
  entries is the complete git ls-tree -r
  inventory, sorted by path, with entriesSha256=H(entries). sourcePaths is
  the closed sorted selected materialization list, no globs. Overlay={path,
  role,operation,beforeSha256,after:Source|null,content:Ref|null}; role is
  baseline|authority|change|host|partial|completed, operation is put|delete.
  beforeSha256 is the exact preceding-view B or null for absence. put requires
  after.path=Overlay.path and equal after/content raw hash/size; content.path
  is its versioned catalogue address, NOT the logical overlay path. Resolve
  that address and verify its bound logical origin. delete requires both null. Each
  role/path is unique; apply roles in the listed order, paths ordinally.
  change has exactly the CHANGE-0017.md put row, equal to changeDocument.source.
  View baseline applies baseline+authority+change+host, partial additionally partial,
  completed applies completed INSTEAD OF partial to that baseline. Deleted
  files cannot remain in sourcePaths. Non-calculator rows materialize
  separately, read-only, and are not fed to the two fingerprint calculators.
  They count toward materialization bytes and have their own immutable
  versioned Refs. Never copy an unlisted dirty file implicitly.
- RestorePaths and RemovalPaths are sorted unique arrays of exact paths,
  never globs/directories. RestorePaths equals the completed-vs-baseline
  changed path set; RemovalPaths is precisely its baseline-absent subset.
  BaselineRow={path,source:Source|null}, one row per RestorePaths entry.
  Every restored path is within the existing 21-file runtime input list.
  Existing unrelated dirty baseline files are immutable input, not restore
  permission. HOST belongs only to the host overlay and is never a runtime
  restore/removal path.
- CapturedGraph={schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-captured-graph-v1",
  root:CapturedValue,nodes:[CapturedNode]}. CapturedValue is a closed union:
  {tag:"null"}|{tag:"undefined"}|{tag:"boolean",value:boolean}|
  {tag:"string",value:string}|{tag:"number",lexeme:string}|{tag:"ref",index}.
  Number lexeme is JSON.stringify(Number(lexeme)), except "-0" explicitly
  preserves negative zero; nonfinite numbers reject. Ref index is a valid
  nonnegative safe node index. CapturedNode is
  {kind:"object",prototype:"object"|"null",extensible,properties:[CapturedProperty]} OR
  {kind:"array",length,lengthWritable,extensible,properties:[CapturedProperty]} OR
  {kind:"regexp",source,flags,lastIndex,lastIndexWritable,extensible}.
  CapturedProperty={key,value:CapturedValue,enumerable,writable,configurable};
  booleans are actual descriptors. Assign node indices on first DFS visit
  in Reflect.ownKeys order, preserving later aliases. Arrays are dense,
  index properties only, with length separately represented. Reject symbols,
  accessors, cycles, functions, exotic prototypes other than the explicit
  native RegExp case, or holes instead of dropping
  them. Reconstruct descriptors/prototypes and re-encode to byte-identical
  canonical graph. Thus own undefined and insertion order survive, even
  though the transport itself is canonical JSON.
  extensible is the observed boolean; apply preventExtensions after defining
  properties when false. Never silently make a sealed input extensible.
  RegExp permits only its native prototype and lastIndex own property;
  flags must equal new RegExp(source,flags).flags, lastIndex is a nonnegative
  safe integer. This handles serializedConfig.testNamePattern without losing
  matcher semantics; captured historical arguments are still required to
  match their actually observed graphs, not arbitrarily added regexp values.
- Property={present,value}; absent means present=false,value=null; a present
  null remains distinguishable. ErrorContract={constructor:{module,export,
  realm},code:Property,fields:[{name,property:Property}],message:{template,
  operands,text},throwSite:Ref}. Fields sort by name; template is literal,
  source-expression or native-clone-v1, operands a closed source-derived
  name/value list, and text the complete expected message. Source-expression
  permits only the pinned throw-site string concatenation/template over
  fixture inputs and literal reason/detail, not arbitrary code or regex.
- Matcher={testId,path,callChain,range,syntaxSha256,syntax,classification,cases};
  classification=diagnostic|non-diagnostic, callChain is an ordered list of
  closed {path,start,end,sha256} source ranges,
  range=[start,end], cases=[{caseId,contract:ErrorContract}] in source/loop order.
  Non-diagnostic cases are []; diagnostic cases cannot be empty. Case IDs are
  ordinal source-call-chain/fixture-index tuples, not random names.
- Run={testId,variant,argv,cwdToken,environment,toolchain,exitCode,nativeReport,
  stdout,stderr,observations}; variant=plain|observed; file outputs are Refs
  resolving payload bytes, cwdToken=scratch|control; F's 24 diagnostic runs
  require scratch, supplement.currentFocusedRuns requires control.
  environment is the closed
  runtime/observer variable allowlist from the invocation contract (no secrets).
  toolchain={node,vitest,typescript,platform,arch,lockSha256}; observations are
  [{caseId,invocation,actual:{constructor,code,fields,message,raw:Ref},constructorMatches,matcherAccepted,
  throwSiteMatches}], in case/invocation order, all three booleans true.
  actual.constructor/code/fields use the corresponding ErrorContract shapes,
  but actual.message is the observed string, not an expected template. raw
  binds captured error/report bytes including producer-side identity
  observations. Plain runs have observations=[]; observed runs cover all
  diagnostic cases. Environment entries are closed {name,value} pairs in
  ordinal name order; operands likewise use closed {name,value} pairs.
  Report source records retain raw native bytes, not reserialized JSON.
- PackageBinding={name,version,packageJson:Source,entries:[Source]} uses exact
  versions/pins from the table. DependencyEntry={path,kind,size,sha256,target};
  kind=file|internal-link, target=null for files and a relative private target
  for links, with size/B over raw file or UTF-8 link-target bytes respectively.
  Toolchain={node:{version,platform,arch,pathToken,sha256},lockSha256,
  typescript:PackageBinding,loader:PackageBinding,vite:PackageBinding,
  vitest:PackageBinding,esbuild:PackageBinding,dependencyTree:[DependencyEntry],
  dependencyTreeSha256,offlinePackages:[{name,version,integrity}],
  launchers:[{name,version,files:[Source]}],official,argvTemplate,
  environment:[{name,value}],resolution:{kind:"vite-node-private-v1",
  conditions:"node24-default",aliases:[],configFile:false,network:false}}.
  Launchers are npm,npx,git,sh in that order; their complete resolved input
  files are privately provisioned and hashed, not merely a PATH name.
  dependencyTreeSha256=H(dependencyTree), paths unique and lexical.
  offlinePackages is exactly the resolved lockfile dependency tarballs needed
  by the existing isolated consumer tests, sorted name/version; integrity is
  the exact lockfile SRI string, verified before copying into the private cache.
  Parent argv/environment must equal the literal token templates above.
- BuildProof={schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-build-v1",
  toolchainSha256,sourceViewSha256,inputs:[Source],buildScript:"tsc -p tsconfig.build.json",
  argv:["npm","run","build"],exitCode:0,stdout:Ref,stderr:Ref,dist:[DistEntry],
  isolatedDist:[DistEntry],distSha256,distReset:Ref,entry:{path:"dist/packages/cli/src/main.js",
  sha256},npxResolution:{package:"musubix5",binPath,binSha256,cache:NpxBinding},
  umask:"0022",normalizedMode:{path:"dist/packages/cli/src/main.js",mode:"100755"},
  retrySourceContract:{ranges:[{id,path,range:Range,sha256}]}}.
  dist=isolatedDist byte inventories, distSha256=H(dist), and the entry/bin
  raw hashes must equal the inventory member; no path outside local dist.
  Ordered input/output lists are closed by the pinned compiler's complete
  input/output manifest; extra output is failure, not ignored stale code.
- ObserverOverlay={observer:Ref,config:Ref,plainArgv,observedArgv,
  plainResolvedConfig:Ref,observedResolvedConfig:Ref,logicalCommandSha256,
  observedCommandSha256,projectionSha256,
  differences:[{pointer,before,after}],
  loaderMetadata:{before:{configFile,configFileDependencies},
  after:{configFile,configFileDependencies}},
  bootstrap:{profileSha256,inputsSha256,
  bootstrapSha256,setupFiles,preloadCount:1},restored:true}.
  Differences are exactly the --config argument slot and appended setupFiles
  entry; before/after values are typed JSON values verified against the raw
  configs/argv. No other property is optional or excluded from comparison.
  The resolved-config Refs contain canonical CapturedGraph snapshots of the
  complete pinned serializedConfig, not server internals. configFile is a
  private-root path token; dependencies are sorted unique path-token arrays
  with exactly the overlay addition specified above.
  logicalCommandSha256 and observedCommandSha256 use the existing
  digest(JSON.stringify([command,logicalArgs])) of each run's validated
  executionBinding.logicalInvocation, BEFORE runtime augmentation.
  projectionSha256 applies that same encoding after removing exactly the
  diagnostic --config pair from observed logicalArgs; it must equal
  logicalCommandSha256. Revalidate each binding's augmentation against its
  own effective argv; never strip unknown effective-argv tokens to guess it.

The closed containers are:

| Suffix/file | Required fields in addition to schemaVersion/kind |
|---|---|
| history / history/g8.json | archiveManifest:Ref, transitionResult:Ref, blockedResult:Ref, freezeManifest:Ref, freezeCommit, checkpoint3805:Native, orders:[Native], receipts:[Ref], reports:[Ref], orphanIntent:Ref, sources:[ObjectEntry], payloads:[Ref] |

| results / diagnostic/results.json | inputs:{sourcesSha256,matchersSha256,implementationSha256,historySha256,toolchainSha256}, runs:[Run], historicalCalls:[HistoricalCall], observerOverlays:[ObserverOverlay], feasibility:Ref, allTwelvePlainPassed, allTwelveObservedPassed, allContractsMatched, observerRemoved, controlRuntimeAbsent |
