| preflight / preflight.json | recipe:"g9-recovery-preflight-v1", inputsSha256, executorSha256, checksSha256, authoritySha256, sourceFilesSha256, diagnosticResultsSha256, implementationSha256, fingerprintsSha256, historySha256, lineageSeedSha256, exitCode:0 |
| manifest / manifest.json | authoritySha256, inputsSha256, preflightSha256, orderedPathsSha256, predecessor:{manifestSha256,sealSha256}|null, files:[Source] |

HistoricalCall={caseId,ordinal,graph:Ref,graphObjectSha256,
outcome:{valid,diagnostic},unchanged:true}; ordinal is 1..47, graphObjectSha256
=H(decoded transport CapturedGraph), NOT H(the reconstructed JS candidate).
valid is boolean; diagnostic is null exactly for the first call, otherwise
"phase-runtime-transition". The graph Ref contains the captured codec, not
a replayed factory output. observerOverlays has twelve entries in assignment
order. No arbitrary success/status fields are inferred from runner exit 0.

Budgets is exactly {snapshotPaths:60000,snapshotBytes:2147483648,
dependencyFiles:100000,dependencyBytes:2147483648,rawFileBytes:48234496,
immutableFileBytes:67108864,inlineBytes:335544320,closureBytes:536870912,
graphNodes:2000000,graphDepth:256,operationUnits:500000000,replayMs:300000,
diagnosticMs:10800000,buildMs:120000,commandMs:180000,
processTreeRssBytes:8589934592,nodeHeapMiB:2048,tracerSourceBytes:65536,
tracerBinaryBytes:4194304,tracerBuildBytes:4194304,traceCallBytes:67108864,
traceTotalBytes:536870912,traceDecodedCallBytes:67108864,
traceDecodedTotalBytes:8589934592,processEvents:100000,packSyscallEvents:5000000}.
Fields are integer literals,
not user-tunable limits. rawFileBytes applies ONLY to inline rows and new
raw sidecar objects, never to Git-backed historical blobs. Count all physical
source materializations, including all three views and private Git metadata,
against BOTH aggregate snapshotPaths and snapshotBytes, as specified above.

All SHA fields in these containers are lowercase 64-hex; IDs/paths/strings
are nonempty unless an explicit exception permits "". Boolean fields are
booleans, never truthy values. sourceFiles is exactly the five complete files
in lexical path order. scope/checkpoint/order identity strings are checked
by native validators. requirements in fingerprints is exactly the two serial
IDs in order; applicable/changed are booleans, before/after are both present
when applicable, and absence must match the native predicate and source
evidence rather than serve as a skipped comparison.
archivedTestOutputs, baselineOutputs and completedOutputs are each exactly currentChangeFingerprints,
then workspaceChangeFingerprints raw returned JSON files; compare their
existing encodings, not a hand-normalized substitute.
The archived-test current calculator uses Authority.requirementIds, the full
six IDs in their declared order, verified against D's enclosing generation/
CHANGE requirement set; baseline/completed use Scope's two serial IDs.
The native ChangePhaseEvidence D has NO requirementIds member; do not invent
one or interpret its absence as missing approval. Resolve the enclosing
record from the same hash-verified native source/pointer binding.
The archived-test workspace calculator uses the serial IDs for the existing
test-delta comparison. Preserve the D-time TDD ledger and all D-bound source
bytes in archived-test; replacing them with later live data is not allowed.
Parse the hash-verified Authority.designCheckpoint.phase.recordJson as D.
Require that currentChangeFingerprints(archivedTestRoot,"CHANGE-0017",
inputs.authority.requirementIds) has exactly the same impact, requirements, design, tests,
implementation, requirementImplementations and tdd fields as D.fingerprints.
Compare each field's JSON value with exact presence, object members and
array order (canonicalBytes equality); no selected-map projection, missing
field default or synthesized hash. This uses the official read-only export,
not a new calculator or observed-read instrumentation.
The resolved output is materialization.calculatorOutputs[0].value; on
mismatch use /materialization/calculatorOutputs/0/value/<field>, appending
the first differing RFC 6901 field/index if nested. The counterpart is the
same field of JSON.parse(inputs.authority.designCheckpoint.phase.recordJson)
.fingerprints, NOT a pointer through the recordJson string. A missing/invalid
native D uses /inputs/authority/designCheckpoint/phase/recordJson.
This exact seven-field equality is mandatory before any g9 Red and does not
replace the baseline/completed implementation deltas.

sourcesSha256=H(the sorted complete Source inventory of Snapshot's COMPLETED
materialized sourcePaths view). sourceInventorySha256 similarly binds its
BASELINE view. controlBaselineSha256 and restoredBaselineSha256 each equal
H(the same sorted Source inventory of runtime restore paths, with
{path,source:null} for absent paths); equality proves exact removal/restoration,
not whole-repo cleanliness. sourceFilesSha256=H(the five Source rows);
authoritySha256=H(Authority); toolchainSha256=H(Toolchain).
All other *Sha256 referring to a named JSON file are B(that file's required
canonical bytes). Fingerprint strings remain the existing official hashes.

assignments is exactly the twelve-row TEST/requirement/path table below in
that order, commandName="test" for every row, with no additional entries.
The history container includes the raw archive manifest/result/blocked result,
all archive blobs, preserved g8 freeze/approval/source/call/report bytes,
native g7/g8 order and checkpoint sources, and abandonment/transition facts.
Validate every referenced member and each g8 receipt n against its actual
order/phase, archived report and predecessor; intent 14 has NO matching
receipt/checkpoint/Green. No success field in a historical report substitutes
for revalidation. sources is the sorted ObjectEntry catalogue of those bytes.
Prefer a git storage reference only when exact bytes have a verified tree
path in the pinned HEAD or g8 freeze commit; otherwise use bounded payload
storage. Verify all 1,034 archive members from those sources; do not embed a
second base64 copy of tracked files. Git objects are read by immutable OID
and verified against commit/tree/path plus B, never by mutable worktree path.

The source snapshot is Git HEAD commit/tree/object identities plus a CLOSED
overlay inventory, not a base64 dump of the worktree. Before materialization,
enumerate every dirty/untracked source/test/config input needed by the runners
and calculators. Baseline overlay hashes must equal the preserved transition
inventory (using its six restored-baseline overrides and four absent paths).
Unrelated baseline graph/other dirty sources are read-only, not new edit
permission. Authority overlay may contain only current approval-listed
requirements/design/constitution documents and the explicitly captured native
authority records. HOST overlay is the one pinned replacement. Partial and
completed overlays may contain only enumerated approved runtime paths.
The change overlay is the current CHANGE document bound to D's impact
fingerprint, since both official calculators read it. Migration guide and
generated trace have the exact read-only non-calculator rows above. Capturing
them is not permission to edit them, or to use persisted trace as calculator
input instead of buildTrace(...,false).
The fail-closed changed-file rule applies to the declared runner/calculator
dependency closure: any unlisted dirty/untracked member, omitted dependency,
oversized inline input or stale baseline blocks. Other dirty repository files
are preserved and inventoried for conservation but are NOT silently copied
or considered inputs. Recompute the exact archived-test/D output comparison
instead of claiming an observed-read detector. An inventory/output mismatch
blocks preparation; no file is promoted automatically. The non-calculator trace row is an
as-of-snapshot observation; later official trace regeneration gets a new
versioned address and is checked normally, never overwrites F's old row.
The exact overlay rows are sealed before use, with before hashes checked;
a missing file is an explicit delete/null, not a silent default.
Materialize tracked base from git cat-file verified blobs, then only those
rows. Do not copy a writable working tree, .git alternates, caches, node_modules
or dist into the snapshot. Private Git metadata retains the pinned HEAD/tree.
Current g9 freezes and generated outputs are excluded to avoid recursion.

Payload storage is now sixteen fixed partitions: history/payloads-0.json
through -7.json and diagnostic/payloads-0.json through -7.json. The diagnostic
catalogue contains only non-Git overlays, tool/observer sources, raw run
reports, fingerprint outputs and the 47 captured graphs; no node_modules.
For each group deduplicate by B, sort by sha256 and greedily append complete
Blob rows to the lowest current partition while its EXACT canonical envelope
would remain <=64 MiB. Otherwise advance once to the next partition. No row
splitting, hash-prefix bucketing or backtracking. An empty partition is a
canonical payloads container with blobs:[], and all sixteen files always
exist. Exhausting eight partitions, an inline raw row >46 MiB, total decoded inline
bytes >320 MiB or total F bytes >512 MiB fails before publication. Thus every
GitHub blob is <=64 MiB, strictly below 100 MB. Git-backed bytes count toward
source materialization budgets but not inline payload size.
Each raw content hash is stored once per group; cross-group aliases reuse
the history catalogue rather than duplicate data. Reject unreferenced payload
rows and catalogue conflicts. Missing Git objects are an explicit prerequisite
failure, never a network fetch or mutable-cache fallback.
Arrays with source paths sort ordinally except explicitly ordered test/run
and closure lists. results has exactly 24 runs, plain twelve then observed
twelve in assignment order; report selection must contain the intended one
passing test with no skipped/missing selected result or bootstrap error.
Booleans are derived by replay, never accepted as assertions.

Preparation hash graph is acyclic: capture source/implementation/matcher/
history data and actual runs first; seal diagnostic outputs and fingerprint
proof; resolve Authority from existing approval/checkpoint bytes; construct
seed and inputs; I=H(inputs) addresses
.musubix/cache/g9-recovery-v1/I/. The generic executor bytes contain no I,
future manifest/hash or commit. Inputs bind its raw SHA. Execute the sealed
cache twice by materializing separate R mirrors and executing the ONE argv/
cwd/environment template above, including --max-old-space-size=2048 and
./preflight paths. The cache is an F-layout mirror, not flat executor.mjs/
inputs.json aliases. Each R/out is empty initially. Committed replay uses
the identical template and layout, with input bytes read from committed F.
The executor writes only deterministic successful checks/preflight, with
fixed case order and no timestamps, random IDs or current clock observations.
Both runs must be byte-identical. Real diagnostic runs are captured once and
replayed as immutable observations, not rerun to fake identical native reports.
Failures emit deterministic stderr and write neither new checks nor preflight;
existing outputs are never overwritten or treated as a fallback.

The ordered checks registry is exactly: authority, history, source-edit,
lease-window, discovery, test-delta, matcher-inventory, matcher-contracts,
diagnostic-runs, implementation-delta, runtime-absent, historical-activation,
current-activation, activation-negatives, lineage, closure. First failure is
registry order then ordinal JSON Pointer order; emit
G9_RECOVERY_INVALID:<checkId>:<pointer>. Missing/incomplete observations block
admission; a regex/bare matcher by itself never fails matcher-contracts.
The pointer bases refer to the following closed validation view, not arbitrary
filesystem names: {inputs,history,edit,matchers,results,implementation,
fingerprints,lineage,fixtures,closure,budgets,toolchain,materialization,
observerOverlay}. Resolve its members only from the bound containers. Append
canonical RFC 6901 segments for the first failing field/array index; compare
pointer strings ordinally for ties AFTER registry order. JSON/schema failure
uses that container's check and exact field pointer, including the parent
pointer for an absent whole container. Operational budget/toolchain/isolation/
observer errors use the separately declared operational IDs, before semantic
checks; success contains only the sixteen registry rows.

The validation view is an in-memory, closed object, not another immutable
file. inputs/history/edit/matchers/results/implementation/fingerprints/lineage
are their named decoded containers; budgets/toolchain are inputs' exact
members. The remaining shapes are:

- materialization={layout:"g9-mirror-v1",views:[MaterializedView],
  dependencies:{inventorySha256,fileCount,bytes,private:true},
  snapshotTotals:{paths,bytes},
  terminalCases:[{id,inputSha256,field:null|string,action}],
  distResets:[Ref],calculatorCharges:[CalculatorCharge],
  calculatorOutputs:[{view,name,source:Ref,value}]}.
  MaterializedView={name,rootToken,gitCommit,gitTree,overlayIndices,
  sourceInventorySha256,nonCalculatorInputsSha256,fileCount,bytes};
  name order is archived-test,baseline,completed, with rootToken respectively
  "private/archived-test","private/baseline","private/completed".
  overlayIndices is a sorted unique array of valid Snapshot.overlays indices;
  archived-test omits host/partial/completed, baseline omits partial/completed,
  completed omits partial. Non-calculator rows have their separate H(list).
  Counters are nonnegative safe integers measured from the bounded inventory.
  snapshotTotals sums the three physical source-view inventories plus private
  Git metadata/object files and any additional source copies, without counting
  a physical file twice within one view. Separate view copies count separately.
  Enforce paths<=60000 and bytes<=2147483648 before invoking calculators.
  terminalCases is the exact 66-row derived classifier fixture array specified
  below and copied to checks.terminalCases, not a new input authority.
  distResets resolves completed records, never a guessed absent-output flag.
  calculatorOutputs has exactly six rows in the same order as calculatorCharges;
  view/name equal their charge, source is the corresponding archivedTestOutputs,
  baselineOutputs or completedOutputs Ref, and value is the exact parsed raw
  output of that pinned official export, with its native return schema.
  For currentChangeFingerprints the closed value fields are impact,
  requirements, design, implementation, tests, tdd and requirementImplementations,
  using the existing ChangeFingerprints types without coercion. Workspace
  values use that export's existing return schema. Ref hashes bind the raw
  output; this view adds no alternate serialization or persisted file.
- fixtures is an EXACT 60-element array, in the case order below, of
  {caseId,candidateGraph:CapturedGraph,inputSha256,structuralValid,
  currentContextValid,structuralDiagnostic,currentDiagnostic}.
  inputSha256=H(candidateGraph); decode it for validation without replacing
  native object order/undefined fields. This gives the same transport meaning
  to historical and generated case hashes. checks.fixtureCases is the exact
  projection of these rows without candidateGraph.
- closure={phase:"cache-plan",paths:[string],files:[Source],
  prospective:{checks,preflight,manifest},partitionSizes:[{path,bytes}],
  totalBytes}. paths/files are exactly the ordered 42-file list, files includes
  the prospective manifest; prospective members have their named closed
  schemas. partitionSizes lists the sixteen partitions in closure order.
  totalBytes sums the 42 raw file sizes. This view is constructed only after
  the first fifteen checks, never hashed back into checks/preflight/manifest.
- observerOverlay={runs:[ObserverOverlay]}; runs has exactly twelve rows in
  assignment order and equals results.observerOverlays.

All view arrays use zero-based numeric JSON Pointer indices. In particular
g9-positive is fixtures[47], g7-foreign fixtures[58], g8-foreign fixtures[59];
never address /fixtures/g9-positive. A case-ID lookup must first find the
unique expected array index and verify that row.caseId; no implicit map shape.
Observer failures use /observerOverlay/runs/<assignmentIndex>/<field>;
run observations use /results/runs/<0..23>/observations/<index>.
Charges have exactly six rows: each view in the above order, then current
calculator followed by workspace calculator. /materialization/views/0 names
archived-test, not a dynamically keyed property. Missing whole members use
the member pointer; a missing expected row uses its numeric index. No new
successful view property may be invented solely to fit an error pointer.

| Check ID | Exact acceptance predicate | Pointer base |
|---|---|---|
| authority | Current g9 3820/D approvals, six IDs, serial Scope, source bytes/native hashes and complete order prefix all verify; latest live authority matches; archived-test current output equals all seven persisted D fingerprint fields | /inputs/authority; output mismatches use /materialization/calculatorOutputs/0/value |
| history | All pinned g7/g8/archive objects, Git bindings, 13 receipt/report chains and orphan-14 absence verify without credit transfer | /history |
| source-edit | Raw old/new hunk, prefix/suffix, getStart(sf) AST ranges and all five file hashes equal the pinned values; no other diff | /edit |
| lease-window | Every LeaseWindow literal, source AST predicate/delay/guard and pinned journal SHA agrees | /edit/leaseWindow |
| discovery | Recomputed exact twelve node/path/line assignments and whole traced-test path inventories match recorded discovery; no helper-only change | /edit/discovery |
| test-delta | Both official before/after tests hashes differ with changedPaths exactly worker, and actual D baseline agrees | /fingerprints/preparedTests |
| matcher-inventory | Source-reachable assertion/case set is exactly the closed inventory; no unknown/missing/extra cases or altered frozen syntax | /matchers |
| matcher-contracts | Each captured actual constructor/code/fields/message/producer and delegated matcher acceptance matches the prebound contract; bare failures are intended diagnostics | /results/runs |
| diagnostic-runs | Exactly 24 fresh selected-only plain/observed passes, complete raw reports/toolchain/overlay/bootstrap bindings and all required captures; no skip/error | /results |
| implementation-delta | Recomputed current/workspace outputs match archived outputs for the same views; both implementation hashes and every applicable serial map differ | /fingerprints |
| runtime-absent | Completed comparison restore set removed to exact BaselineRows, control restore-path hash equals baseline, runtime source/profile AND compiled outputs absent after verified dist reset; unrelated baseline inputs unchanged | /materialization |
| historical-activation | Decode/re-encode and revalidate the exact ordered 47 stored candidates; outcomes equal observed results, with unchanged graphs and no factory invocation | /results/historicalCalls |
| current-activation | Independently constructed g9-positive passes structural and current-context checks against bound g9 fixture authority | /fixtures/47 |
| activation-negatives | All specified negatives give their exact expected outcomes; g7/g8 foreign contexts are structurally valid and rejected only by current binding | /fixtures |
| lineage | Seed predecessor chain/seals/Git ancestry are exact, unique-tip, current D-bound; no predecessor intent or orphan partial root permits replacement | /lineage |
| closure | The prospective 42-file cache plan, including tracer source/build/binary and their toolchain closure, canonical schemas, raw hashes, Git dependencies, partition algorithm and byte caps all verify, with no self-reference or missing dependency | /closure |

closure is explicitly PRE-MANIFEST validation, not a claim of Git publication.
After the first fifteen checks, construct prospective checks bytes with the
closure row true, then prospective preflight and manifest bytes in memory.
Their sizes/hashes and the other staged files determine the closed 42-file
plan. Verify all limits/schemas and dependency references before writing any
of the three files. No manifest hash is stored in checks or preflight. A
failure writes none; success recomputes the same bytes. Actual file modes,
introducing commit, HEAD/index/live equality, fsync and committed replay are
later mandatory publication/seal checks, reported under
G9_RECOVERY_INVALID:publication:/publication/<field>, not fabricated in
checks.closure. Sidecar failures use ONLY the closed field enum and precedence below; the
notation G9_RECOVERY_INVALID:sidecar:/sidecar/<field> is not an extension point.
Fixture case order is g8-historical-positive, its 23 source-index mutations
in plain/reconstructed order, g9-positive, six missing-conjunct cases,
unchanged-tests, unchanged-implementation, unchanged-COMPAT-map,
unchanged-LIFECYCLE-map, g7-foreign, g8-foreign. G8 runtime cases must actually
execute against completed scratch implementation, not deferred registry rows.
currentContextValid=false for every historical case; valid historical
positives still have structuralValid=true. Foreign cases are constructed
internally valid before current-context rejection. This is a new registry,
not the g8 twenty-evaluator or 23-mutation hashes relabeled as g9 evidence.
There are exactly 60 unique case IDs: g8-historical-positive;
g8-mutation-00-plain, g8-mutation-00-reconstructed through index 22 in that
interleaved order; g9-positive; g9-missing-conjunct-1 through -6;
g9-unchanged-tests, g9-unchanged-implementation, g9-unchanged-COMPAT-map,
g9-unchanged-LIFECYCLE-map; g7-foreign; g8-foreign.
The six new negatives respectively set legacy Red.testRuntime=null, remove
the implementation checkpoint, substitute SESSION for the candidate TEST,
change the candidate Green logical command hash, remove Green runtime runs,
and change the activation's design approval SHA. Recompute dependent native
envelopes/chains so an unrelated stale hash cannot stand in for the targeted
failure. The four unchanged cases copy only the tested predecessor
fingerprint/map into its successor, rehashing dependencies consistently.
Expected diagnostics are phase-runtime-transition for malformed activation
and foreign current context; positives have no structural diagnostic.
All 46 historical mutation variants and all ten g9 mutation cases MUST have
structuralValid=false with phase-runtime-transition, not merely fail current
context. Both foreign cases have structuralValid=true and currentContextValid=false.
Only g9-positive has currentContextValid=true. Native-order validation independently checks the entire
prefix/suffix, not merely a final tip string.

For EVERY case define currentContextValid = structuralValid &&
currentGenerationBindingPasses. Invoke the current-binding predicate only
after structural success, checking generation before the other current
identity bindings. On structural failure propagate its exact diagnostic to
currentDiagnostic (the AND short-circuited; no generation rejection is claimed).
On structural success, structuralDiagnostic=null, and currentDiagnostic is
null iff current binding succeeds. The complete expected outcomes are:

| Fixture indices | structuralValid | currentContextValid | structuralDiagnostic | currentDiagnostic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (g8 historical positive) | true | false | null | phase-runtime-transition |
| 1-46 (historical mutations) | false | false | phase-runtime-transition | phase-runtime-transition |
| 47 (g9-positive) | true | true | null | null |
| 48-57 (g9 negatives) | false | false | phase-runtime-transition | phase-runtime-transition |
| 58-59 (g7/g8 foreign) | true | false | null | phase-runtime-transition |

No blanket foreign/current diagnostic is attached to the successful
g9-positive. An unexpected diagnostic is a failed evaluator, not normalized
into this table. Both diagnostic fields are required even when null.

Let K=H(checks), P=H(preflight); K is not the control-root token ${C}.
The manifest binds the other 41 immutable
files' raw hashes, modes and sizes, not itself; M=H(manifest) is the directory
name. The fixed ordered list (including manifest first) is:

preflight.json
preflight/inputs.json
preflight/executor.mjs
preflight/checks.json
approvals/requirements.json
approvals/design.json
sources/tests/candidate-gate-trust.test.ts
sources/tests/test-runtime-evidence.test.ts
sources/tests/test-runtime-gate.test.ts
sources/tests/test-runtime-timers.test.ts
sources/tests/test-runtime-worker.test.ts
history/g8.json
history/payloads-0.json
history/payloads-1.json
history/payloads-2.json
history/payloads-3.json
history/payloads-4.json
history/payloads-5.json
history/payloads-6.json
history/payloads-7.json

diagnostic/matchers.json
diagnostic/results.json
diagnostic/implementation.json
diagnostic/payloads-0.json
diagnostic/payloads-1.json
diagnostic/payloads-2.json
diagnostic/payloads-3.json
diagnostic/payloads-4.json
diagnostic/payloads-5.json
diagnostic/payloads-6.json
diagnostic/payloads-7.json

lineage/seed.json
tooling/tracer.c
tooling/tracer-build.json
tooling/tracer
tooling/tracer-build-spec.json

H(the JSON array of these strings) =
8d20cbff579b61377acce5efd7a9579333f6713856205762ec4c01bac227196d.
The g9 closure is therefore **42 files**, replacing the unpublished 38-file
proposal; neither its old list hash nor g8's twelve-file list is g9 authority. F is
.musubix/evidence/test-file-freeze/CHANGE-0017/g9/M. Every immutable file is a
normal Git blob: 41 are 100644, and tooling/tracer alone is 100755.
POSIX files/directories are 0644/0755, with tracer 0755, owned by the executing user; reject
symlinks, non-regular files, wrong ownership, unsafe ancestors or unaccounted
hard links. Final link count is one. Use exclusive same-directory temporary
files, file fsync, no-replace publication, parent fsync and no-follow reopen/
rehash; only a verified publication temp may temporarily be the second link.
Win32 reports missing directory-fsync capability explicitly while retaining
file flush/atomic no-replace/reopen checks. Never chmod or clean unrelated files.

Write the 41 non-manifest files in listed order, manifest last, from the sealed
cache. Partial recovery is allowed only for an exact publication prefix with
no call intent: revalidate all present bytes and complete only missing suffix
files from that same sealed cache. A temp is recoverable only when its recorded
destination/bytes/link identity matches; never rewrite a linked temp. States
are empty, exact-prefix, ready-41, complete-uncommitted, committed-unsealed,
sealed. Extra/torn/different files are not reclassified into another state.
No cleanup, alternate cache fallback or inferred successful publication.

Commit only the exact closure; identify the introducing commit from Git
objects, verifying all 42 normal blobs and exact modes, parent absence of F, index/HEAD/live
equality and no symlink/submodule/mode substitution. Reexecute sealed preflight
from committed bytes with no cache access and require exact K/P; reconstruct
history/diagnostic inputs from pinned Git objects plus bounded payloads in an
excluded replay directory with the separately verified private dependencies.
Only then publish an external seal, so no manifest contains its own commit.
Seal/intent/receipt files live in the separate append-only
.musubix/evidence/runtime-recovery-calls/CHANGE-0017/g9/M/ directory S,
never in the 42-file immutable Git closure.

Seal has kind change0017-g9-recovery-seal-v1 and closed fields schemaVersion,
kind, manifestSha256, commit, orderedPathsSha256, files:[Source],
aggregateSha256, preflightSha256, committedReplaySha256, predecessorSealSha256.
Here files is the full ordered 42 including manifest; aggregateSha256=H(files);
committedReplaySha256=H({checksSha256:K,preflightSha256:P}); predecessor is null
only for the first g9 root. Seal itself is H(seal), not self-referential.
After any unrelated descendant commit, recheck the introducing commit and
current HEAD/index/live equality of the closure, not HEAD==introducing commit.
The global guard validates every g9 manifest/seed/seal as a single acyclic
predecessor chain with one tip and no branch/unexplained root. A replacement
tip is allowed only before ANY intent on its predecessor and with fresh
current diagnostics/authority; old roots/seals remain immutable. An orphan
partial publication must be resolved exactly before creating another root.
Ancestor roots validate against their archived authority, not today's
approval; only the tip must match the current latest design. Require each
predecessor introducing commit to be an ancestor of the successor commit,
and exact predecessor manifest/seal hashes in both seed and manifest.
Never search the g8 directory to select g9 authority.

F has the introducing Git commit as its immutable commit point. S instead uses
file/directory fsync PLUS external durability seals, not a Git commit per call.
Before accepting S/seal.json, an intent, dispatch, attempt, retry or receipt,
publish its entire referenced immutable S closure with exclusive/no-replace
files, fsync each file and parent, reopen/rehash, then publish/fsync/reopen
S/durability/<H(durability)>.json. Durability is exactly
{schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-durability-v1",manifestSha256,
ordinal,event,target:Ref,files:[Ref],previousSha256}.
event is freeze|intent|dispatch|attempt|retry|receipt, ordinal 0 only for freeze;
files is the complete unique referenced S file set sorted by path, including
target. previousSha256 is null only for the first freeze event, otherwise the
previous durability seal hash in this S. The fsync/reopen of this external
record and its parent is the commit point; it needs no recursively self-
referential seal. It is not authority before that point.
Validate a single unbroken event chain and fixed ordinal/attempt state machine,
with no mutable HEAD/tip pointer. BuildProof/log/object/supplement files are
durable dependencies of the dispatch/receipt seals that consume them.

All readers verify the durability chain, target and complete dependency set.
An exact target stranded before its durability seal permits completion of
THAT seal only if it is the sole valid next state and no later target/event/
call exists; missing bytes, conflicting targets or uncertain execution stop.
Do not replay an official command to reconstruct a seal. g9 execution is
linux/x64, so directory fsync is REQUIRED here; the older runtime's win32 blob
contract is unchanged, not an exemption for S. Every S file is <=64 MiB,
all S content <=2 GiB, and the same no-follow/owner/mode/link checks apply.
Commit the complete S history with the serial Green base before parallel
handoff; its introducing commit is separate from F's introducing commit and
does not alter F. Root-to-root lineage still uses predecessor manifest/seal
hashes and Git ancestry, never a mutable publication marker.

#### G9 calls, receipts and crash boundaries

This is an executor guard, not a claim that the current CLI already implements
the new freeze gate. Before/after each official call, validate F/seal/lineage,
live five-file hashes, current approvals/D, actual order/journal/TDD histories
and predecessor receipts. Never hold shared CHANGE/projection/append leases
while runners or large capsule replay execute. Existing writers acquire only
short CHANGE -> projection -> append reload/recheck/merge critical sections.
From dispatch publication through its attempt seal and any immediate retry
classification/dispatch, no OTHER musubix5 process that can
acquire any relevant CHANGE/projection/append/TDD lease may run. This includes
read-like CLI commands whose implementation acquires those leases. Enforce
sole-coordinator launch exclusion, without holding any shared lease across
the runner. Verify no such process is already active before release; inability
to establish exclusion blocks dispatch. Do not start status/validation calls
concurrently as a liveness probe. Unknown competing activity is ambiguity,
not permission to retry.
Guards inside this interval use captured bytes and lease-free pure validators,
not another musubix5 CLI command or a helper that acquires those leases.

Ordinals are closed: 1-12 fresh Reds in assignment order; 13 serial batch Red;
14 implementation intent, restore/implementation, then implementation batch
checkpoint; 15-26 the same twelve Greens; 27 serial batch Green.
For TDD use exactly `npx musubix5 tdd red|green <TEST-ID> --requirement
<mapped-ID> --command test --json`. For batch phases use exactly
`npx musubix5 change-record CHANGE-0017 red|implementation|green --requirement
REQ-M5-COMPAT-013 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 --workspace . --json`, from control,
preserving recordChangePhaseFromWorkspace's journal-first routing. The CLI
requires this explicit --workspace even when source and control are the same
directory; do not use the non-workspace route and backfill a journal later.
Its current contract does not permit --dry-run with --workspace. Initial and
superseding singular design checkpoints use their existing non-workspace CLI
route, full six IDs and fresh operation identity where supersession requires
one; they are not batch calls or part of the 27 ordinals.
Require actual D < each Red < batch Red <
implementation checkpoint < each Green < batch Green; ordinals are not
predicted global order numbers. No unrecorded phase or synthetic order suffix
may fill a gap. Every Red must be the expected native assertion failure
(provider/marker absence, or TRUST/GATE missing policy digest), not missing
module, setup, watchdog, lease or observer/tooling error.

Publish S/intents/NN.json before its call. Intent closed schema is
{schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-intent-v1",manifestSha256,
sealSha256,authoritySha256,ordinal,phase,testId,requirementId,scopeId,
commandName,predecessorReceiptSha256,preCallOrderTipSha256,buildProofSha256}.
buildProofSha256 names S/builds/<hash>.json, a canonical BuildProof.
NN is two-digit 01-27; phase is red|batch-red|implementation|green|batch-green.
TEST/requirement/commandName are null for batch calls; commandName otherwise
test. scopeId is the existing nextBatchScopeId calculation over actual current
batches, bound once at preparation and rechecked (no predicted order).
Only ordinal 1 has null predecessor. Intent 14 precedes ANY control runtime
restore; no Green intent may precede its verified checkpoint receipt.

Each invocation also has S/dispatches/NN-AA.json, committed by its durability
seal BEFORE the npx command is released through an owned launcher barrier.
AA is 00, or 01 for the single authorized TDD operational retry.
Batch ordinals 13/14/27 permit ONLY AA=00.
Dispatch={schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-dispatch-v1",
ordinal,attempt,intentSha256,buildProofSha256,supplementSha256,
argv,environment:[{name,value}],environmentSha256,owner:{pid,startTicks,bootId},
launcherProof:ProcessProof,preCallFactsSha256,
nativeTarget:{path,before:Source|null,identity:TargetIdentity|null}}.
pid is a positive safe integer, startTicks a canonical unsigned decimal Linux
/proc start-time string, bootId a UUID; only this registered owned process
tree may execute/terminate the command. argv is the exact CLI vector above,
environment is exactly Toolchain.official.environment (unexpanded, sorted),
environmentSha256=H(environment), and preCallFactsSha256
hashes the current native order/journal/TDD/phase snapshot plus live guard
hashes. Supplement is null except at ordinal 14. All dispatched builds must
match intent.buildProofSha256 except ordinal 14's deliberate post-restore
build, which MUST match its completed supplement. A crash before registration/
barrier proof is not evidence that no command executed.
For ordinals 14..27 (including retries), the tracer verifies
supplement.tracePolicy; 1..13 use pre-D TracePolicy. At 15..27 resolve the
same supplement through receipt 14, without changing the null Dispatch
supplement field. Toolchain and toolchainSha256 remain the pre-D values.
Dispatch/process proof policySha256 is H(the selected policy); do not
rewrite the pre-D Toolchain's TracerBinding to select the supplement policy.
For TDD, nativeTarget.path is the exact safe control-relative native report
target resolved from the bound configured command/adapter for this TEST.
Before releasing the command, archive its existing bytes and verify an
ObjectEntry at object/live/<B>/control/<nativeTarget.path>. before is a
Source whose path is THAT immutable address, mode=100644, size is the exact
raw byte length and sha256=B(bytes); its catalogue/storage must already be
durable within the dispatch closure. It is not a second logical source path
or an alias to the mutable native target. Every g9 TDD call REQUIRES before
non-null: all twelve targets already exist. Missing targets block admission;
do not create placeholders. Refuse symlinks, unsafe ownership or a changing
target. Pre-existing g8/earlier g9 reports are historical bytes, not output
or credit for the new attempt. Recheck equality immediately before release.
For batch ordinals nativeTarget is exactly {path:null,before:null,identity:null}, since
change-record has no native test-report target; never invent a target.
For TDD path and identity are non-null. TargetIdentity={device,inode,ctimeNs,
size,sha256}; device/inode/ctimeNs/size are canonical unsigned decimal strings
from bigint stat, never rounded Number values; sha256 is B(raw bytes).
size must equal String(before.size). Use no-follow open, bigint fstat before/
after hashing, and lstat of the named target; require matching identity and
one regular owned file with link count one. Recheck immediately before
release and after owner death. ctimeNs is native nanoseconds, not ctimeMs
multiplied by 1e6. Any unstable/unmeasurable sample fails closed.
Facts={schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-facts-v1",order:Native,
tdd:Ref,changes:Ref,journalTips:[{stream,record:Native|null}],
manifestSha256,sealSha256,authoritySha256,liveFiles:[Source],
buildProofSha256}. journalTips is exactly normal,bootstrap order; null means
an actually empty verified stream. Native/file snapshots are exact bytes,
referenced by immutable content addresses, NOT copied into each ordinal
Facts file. Facts.order points only to the final native order record via its
pointer, backed by the complete immutable ledger Ref, never embeds the whole
order ledger in recordJson. liveFiles is the five-file ordered inventory.
Hash the canonical Facts file and store it at S/facts/<hash>.json before
dispatch. After termination publish the exact post-call Facts and durable
Attempt BEFORE classifying outcome/retry. Unchanged facts deduplicate to the
pre-call object. This supersedes the unpublished no-Attempt-before-retry rule:
a sealed failure Attempt is non-credit observation, not native phase evidence.
It is necessary to classify a real durable outcome without inventing one.
Mutable native report/lease observations
are NOT in Facts equality: keep reports in Attempt and independently inspect
lease ownership using existing APIs. No phase/order/journal delta may be
hidden by excluding it from this snapshot.

**Deduplicated facts storage:** resolve each ledger Ref by versioned address,
expected B and size. Prefer an exact pinned Git object or existing F payload;
otherwise publish raw bytes ONCE at S/objects/<B>. Every before/after/ordinal
reference to the same byte version reuses that object, even if its logical
origin address differs. Do not serialize the 36 MB changes ledger into a
Facts file, durability record, per-ordinal folder or new base64 wrapper.
Different hashes retain distinct immutable objects; this is not destructive
replacement, a normalized JSON digest or a delta that requires mutable state.
Every fact is reconstructable from its native pointer, versioned Ref and
the immutable Git/F/S object closure.

A closed capacity proof for the normal 27-ordinal protocol is enforced:
initial plus three batch checkpoints gives at most FOUR distinct changes
ledgers, <=46 MiB each; initial plus 24 successful TDD phases gives at most
25 TDD ledgers, <=16 MiB each; initial plus 27 appends gives at most 28 order
ledgers, <=4 MiB each. At most 108 unique pre/post Facts files (two snapshots
for each of at most 54 dispatches) are <=1 MiB each; at most five distinct
journal-tip records (two initial stream tips plus three batch records) are
<=8 MiB each. Reserve these limits before dispatch. This sums to
4*46 + 25*16 + 28*4 + 108*1 + 5*8 = 844 MiB; all OTHER S objects, supplements,
reports, build/reset proofs and durability files together are capped at
1,024 MiB. Thus total S <=1,868 MiB, leaving 180 MiB below its 2 GiB cap.
Count physical unique B-addressed bytes once and metadata files by actual
size; Git/F references consume only reference metadata in S. Unexpected
ledger versions, oversized records or unrelated writes invalidate this
proof and stop; never discard old facts or silently reserve a 28th full
changes.json copy. Append-only native facts and receipts still verify normally.

Attempt={schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-attempt-v1",ordinal,attempt,
dispatchSha256,state,outcome,exitCode,signal,stdout:Ref,stderr:Ref,nativeReport:Ref|null,
nativeTargetAfter:Source|null,targetIdentityAfter:TargetIdentity|null,
processProofs:Ref,postCallFactsSha256,ownerDead:true}.
Publish S/attempts/NN-AA.json with its durability seal after exit, before the
classifier. outcome is EXACTLY success|failed|interrupted: success requires
state=exited, exitCode=0 and signal=null; failed requires state=exited,
observed nonzero integer exitCode and signal=null; every proven interruption/
signal termination or unknown exit is interrupted, never default success.
This is the outer official CLI outcome (Red's runner may fail as expected).
state=exited|interrupted-proven-dead, exitCode is
an observed integer or null only for interruption, signal is a nonempty
observed string or null. Owner death requires the recorded PID/start/boot
identity; never infer it from a missing lease directory alone. Unknown exit
is not zero. An unpersisted native report is saved as attempt output, not
under S/reports and never as TDD evidence.
nativeTargetAfter is an immutable addressed Source with the same raw
size/hash/mode semantics as Dispatch.nativeTarget.before, or null for absence.
Compare the archived before bytes with the after bytes, not mtime or mere
file existence. Set Attempt.nativeReport to the Ref for after bytes ONLY
when present and byte-different from before (including creation from absence).
Otherwise nativeReport=null. Byte-identical historical output is not a report
produced by this attempt. Before absence is forbidden for TDD; removal of an existing
target is NOT unchanged and is terminal incomplete output. For batches both
nativeTargetAfter and nativeReport, plus targetIdentityAfter, are null.
An unmeasurable after identity is null and terminal, not evidence of absence;
retain the actual stat error in stderr. A changed malformed report is
still archived as the attempt's raw output, then rejected, never ignored.
Identical bytes alone do not prove pre-run failure: the full identity proof
below must also match. Changed valid reports remain eligible for normal
successful persistence/receipt, but never for retry; identity change by itself
does not turn successful execution into a failure.
Sidecar Ref paths use explicit freeze/<F-relative-path> or
sidecar/<S-relative-path> namespaces, or the versioned object/ addresses.
For a new object address, its canonical ObjectEntry is stored at
S/catalogue/<B(UTF8(address))>.json; verify entry.path equals the entire address,
its expected SHA/size and its storage before reading. That exact catalogue
file and any S raw bytes join the consuming durability closure. An existing
F catalogue entry may be reused only with identical full address/SHA/size.
No per-ordinal mutable catalogue, directory guessing or sourcePath alias.
Raw logs/attempt objects are published
at S/objects/<B(bytes)>. Ref resolution never falls back to a live report.
BuildProof stdout/stderr and other sidecar-native Refs follow this same rule.

Archive each fresh TDD report's exact lossless UTF-8 bytes at
S/reports/<phase.reportSha256>, then derive S/receipts/NN.json ONLY from
persisted native phase/chain/order or batch checkpoint/journal facts.
TDD receipt admission additionally requires the dispatch-bound changed
report (Attempt.nativeReport non-null) and its exact native phase report SHA.
Matching a historical before report SHA is insufficient, even if native facts
exist. Crash recovery must establish this same before/after byte delta;
otherwise it is terminal, not a historical report relabeled as fresh output.
Receipt schema is {schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-receipt-v1",
manifestSha256,sealSha256,authoritySha256,ordinal,intentSha256,
predecessorReceiptSha256,sourceFilesSha256,completion,evidence}.
completion is null except for ordinal 14, where its closed fields are
{supplementSha256}. It resolves ONLY to
S/implementation/<supplementSha256>.json, whose exact closed schema is:
{schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g9-recovery-implementation-supplement-v1",
manifestSha256,authoritySha256,ordinal:14,intentSha256,
predecessorReceiptSha256,implementation:Ref,results:Ref,fingerprints:Ref,
payloads:[Ref],buildProofSha256,sourceViewSha256,currentFocusedRuns:[Run],
retrySourceContract:{ranges:[{id,path,range:Range,sha256}]},tracePolicy:Ref}.
Its address is H(the entire canonical object), with no own-hash field.
It is always required, including an unchanged exact archive restore.
Its retrySourceContract is the post-restore build's recomputed seven slices;
tracePolicy is pre-D TracePolicy with exactly two replacement fields:
/retrySourceContractSha256 and /namespace/distProof. They bind current slices
and the independently published post-restore isolatedDist inventory; all
other canonical bytes MUST equal pre-D policy. Compare canonical objects
with only these two leaves removed, and separately validate both replacement
values against dispatch BuildProof. Neither replacement must differ if its
inventory is unchanged; no other field may differ. Toolchain/toolchainSha256
remain pre-D; policy selection for ordinals 14..27 is explicit above.
The original policy and proof remain immutable; no slice-byte/order waiver.
predecessorReceiptSha256 equals receipt 13 and intentSha256 equals intent 14.
The three document Refs use their existing closed container schemas; either
freeze/diagnostic/... for unchanged bindings or sidecar/implementation/objects/
<hash>.json for newly validated versions, never both/fallback. payloads has
exactly sixteen Refs in fixed partition order; the eight history partitions
MUST reference F. Every Ref is rehashed, schema-checked and resolved before
acceptance; no implicit directory scanning. New diagnostic partitions follow
the same deterministic packing/caps and address grammar as the other objects.
currentFocusedRuns is exactly twelve plain current runs in assignment order,
all passed on the final implementation; it is not optional archive reuse.
Changed implementation additionally requires fresh 24-run results, 47 captures
and recomputed delta proof. sourceViewSha256 equals H(BuildProof.inputs), and
the dispatch/checkpoint source must match those inputs and final restore
inventory. BuildProof.inputs excludes mutable lifecycle ledgers; they remain
separately checked phase facts, not compiler inputs.
The evidence union retains exactly the TDD/checkpoint fields specified in the
historical receipt subsection below, but changeId/generation/context must be
g9 and archive paths resolve in S. Native phase labels/digest algorithms are
unchanged. Batch Red includes twelve Red receipt hashes; implementation
includes receipt 13; batch Green includes receipt 14 and twelve Green receipts.
No CLI exit field is invented for checkpoints. TDD runnerExitCode comes from
the persisted phase, not the successful outer `tdd red` exit.

Receipt 13 must verify before intent 14. Restore exactly the completed
diagnostic implementation allowlist, with expected absent/baseline hashes,
no blanket checkout, no changes to frozen tests or unrelated dirty work.
If completion needs new bytes, update implementation only and rerun focused
validation; preserve the original diagnostic archive and bind the final exact
inventory/deltas in the implementation checkpoint's source evidence and a
content-addressed implementation-supplement just specified. It cannot replace
F or claim its prior reports tested new bytes. Receipt 14 binds its one hash
through completion and must resolve the final inventory
before any Green. If bytes changed, repeat the twelve plain/observed diagnostics
and actual delta proof before checkpoint 14; unchanged bytes may reuse the
archived diagnostic bindings, but still need focused current validation.
After checkpoint 14 the final implementation inventory is also rechecked
before each Green; unexpected drift stops rather than silently changing it.
A changed
policy, authority, test source or inability to preserve the proven checkpoint
deltas is a protocol blocker, not permission to relax the gate.

After a crash, no later intent is permitted before the preceding receipt.
With persisted exact matching phase facts and report bytes, recover only
that receipt/archive, byte-identically and without rerunning its test.
Never obtain a missing historical report by running again.
**Mechanical pre-run proof (option a, existing targets only).**
BuildProof.retrySourceContract binds ONLY the seven ordered AST/source slices
below, not whole-file equality across implementation. Full-file hashes remain
ordinary per-build provenance, not post-restore pins. Legitimate runtime/TDD
integration elsewhere in tdd.ts/adapters.ts remains permitted.
Each build locates the unique AST owners/statements with pinned TypeScript,
recomputes half-open UTF-8 ranges and exact slice hashes, and proves the call
order. Offsets below are pre-authority measurements, not frozen offsets:

| id | File | Range | Slice SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| lease-wrapper | tdd.ts | [108753,111125) | b0238b062ade1c1253efdd4a390eff4b1afd86c81ce8ce92ad7ac0edb8a3dd86 |
| pre-run-lease | tdd.ts | [116916,117296) | ab8436cee63efebe96c7fda446b2bb7c223163401917dc9beb12d2994bf511e2 |
| clear-call | tdd.ts | [117296,117735) | 56eb30b3ce6dc882ea56e7d02ba5b78f2b09c9dc8f5d0fde8f12256540359d63 |

Range.path uses the full source path, not the abbreviated table filename.
Selectors are: withTddEvidenceWrite's declaration; runTddPhase's pre-run
await-withTddEvidenceWrite statement; its adapter/reportPath/reportAbsolute/
clear-if statement group; its runner execution declaration; reportPath's
declaration; adapterInvocation's declaration prefix through the vitest if;
and clearAdapterOutput's declaration. Use lineStart(getStart(sf)), excluding
JSDoc; end at the selected node/group end plus its existing one LF, or two
LF for the three complete declarations. Reject duplicate/missing selectors.
The seven IDs/hashes and their order remain exact; source offsets may move.
Preserve pre-run lease -> clear/unlink -> runner and file-adapter semantics.
Before F/seal/intent authority, the completed-implementation scratch proof
must compare baseline/completed slice inventories and prove all seven
hashes/order/AST relationships unchanged, even when file hashes/ranges differ.
Store SliceProof={baseline:[Slice],completed:[Slice],builds:[Ref],preserved:true}
in the bound feasibility artifact; Slice is the range-row schema above.
Pre-D TracePolicy uses the baseline digest; supplement 14 binds current
post-restore ranges/digest. Any slice change blocks, not unrelated file edits.
The configured test command must select the file-based vitest adapter and
.musubix/evidence/native/test/<TEST-ID>.json with no tddReport override.
For this pinned CLI, the awaited pre-run lease check precedes target clearing,
clearAdapterOutput unlinks an existing file, and only afterward can the
selected runner launch. BuildProof's clean compiled closure must derive from
these bytes; a matching source alongside stale dist does not prove ordering.
Under exclusive writer/launch custody, a before-existing target whose
device/inode/ctimeNs/size/sha256 tuple is EXACTLY unchanged after failure
proves the unlink/selected runner was not reached. There is no absent-file
branch, code-only inference, output-range proof or fabricated launch marker.
Changed identity, removal/reappearance (even identical bytes), or inability
to measure precisely defeats the proof. Preserve a custody violation as

#### G9 closed terminal classification and fixtures

All sidecar errors have the exact form
G9_RECOVERY_INVALID:sidecar:/sidecar/<field>, with NO suffix segments or new
field names. Evaluate all available predicates before selecting a diagnostic;
do not let an earlier low-level error hide native persistence ambiguity.
The total field precedence and action are the row order below. The first
three also outrank every other G9 operational/semantic validation error;
remaining sidecar fields precede the existing operational IDs in their
declared order, then the sixteen-check registry and ordinal pointer ties.
Preserve lower-ranked diagnostics as non-authoritative detail, not alternative
actions. An unreadable post-dispatch native snapshot is itself ambiguity.

Actions: A=stop all g9 calls and require official generation abandonment
through the existing approver/confirmation contract; no self-approved action.
M=suspend for manual investigation, with NO mutation, retry, continuation or
new intent. P=deterministic preparation failure; only before any F/S authority
publication or intent may the same approved preparation be retried after
resolving the prerequisite, without creating evidence. P becomes M once
authority was published; changing approved inputs still requires the existing
design/approval sequence. No terminal action automatically cleans artifacts.

| Rank / field | Exact trigger | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 generationAbandonRequired | dispatched AND (persistenceAmbiguity OR custody lost OR lease failure without the unchanged-identity pre-run proof) | A |
| 2 batchPending | dispatched AND kind=batch AND (known pending native tuple OR failed/interrupted outcome without complete facts), unless rank 1 | M |
| 3 resumeCapability | changed expected TDD report with clean native tuple and no actual native no-run continuation | M |
| 4 platform | not Linux/x64, unavailable /proc proof capability or exact bigint nanosecond stat | P/M |
| 5 environment | official environment keys/order/literals/hash/expansion differ | P/M |
| 6 executableIdentity | missing, wrong or unbound executable/PID/start/boot proof | P/M |
| 7 isolation | unsafe path/ownership/link, mutable/shared dependency or cache escape | P/M |
| 8 sourceContract | seven ordered slice hashes/AST relationships or current per-build ranges/compiled provenance differ | P/M |
| 9 targetIdentity | missing before target; after target missing/unmeasurable; or changed target with no report on a failed/interrupted call, unless higher rank | P/M |
| 10 nativeReport | changed report malformed, incomplete, unexpected selection/result/binding; or receipt tries to credit unchanged historical bytes | P/M |
| 11 retryConsumed | AA=01 outcome is failed/interrupted, or another retry is requested after AA=01 | M |
| 12 retryEligibility | TDD AA=00 failed/interrupted, native clean, target unchanged, report none and retryReason non-null, but any closed retry guard false | M |
| 13 ownership | owner death/exclusion cannot be proven, with no established dispatched custody loss | M |
| 14 facts | invalid native baseline before dispatch, or non-ambiguous receipt/fact binding mismatch | P/M |
| 15 authority | stale/mismatched current approval/D/test/build/manifest binding at sidecar admission | P/M |
| 16 lineage | invalid predecessor/ordinal/receipt chain or later intent prevents recovery | M |
| 17 durability | missing/torn/conflicting sidecar record or seal/flush/publication proof | P/M |
| 18 capacity | sidecar versions/bytes/reservations exceed the closed limits | P/M |
| 19 callFailed | dispatched outcome failed, with no admissible retry or higher-ranked condition | M |
| 20 callInterrupted | dispatched outcome interrupted, with no admissible retry or higher-ranked condition | M |
| 21 missingPersistence | dispatched outcome success but native state clean; every official ordinal requires a phase/checkpoint delta | M |
| 22 admission | remaining sidecar schema/argv/I/O failure not matching an earlier row | P/M |

The enum is EXACTLY those 22 fields. Generic caught I/O/schema failures map
to admission with the original error retained, never a dynamically generated
field or success fallback. lease failure means the captured LEASE_FENCED,
TDD_EVIDENCE_LEASE_BUSY or CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY outcome, or positive
owned-lease fencing/loss evidence. Historical g8 diagnostics do not set it.
Dispatched means the launch barrier was released OR release cannot be ruled
out after a durable dispatch; a proven unreleased barrier remains preparation.
Custody lost means another relevant writer ran or process/file custody cannot
be established for the dispatched interval. Ordinary inability to establish
exclusion BEFORE release is ownership, not a claim of executed corruption.

**Closed persistenceAmbiguity predicate:** take stable before/after snapshots
of native order, BOTH journal streams, tdd.json and changes.json under the
sole-writer boundary, resolving raw hashes AND parsed native records.
Compare O,J,T,P in that order. Each component is U (raw bytes unchanged),
E (the one exact expected native delta below, with valid digests/linkage and
all prior/unrelated records unchanged), or X (anything else, including
unreadable/missing/torn data, unknown extra records, truncation or raw-only
rewrites). A previous journal tip alone is insufficient: verify both entire
prefixes and exact suffixes from the captured immutable sources.

For TDD, E(O) is exactly one native order append for this execution's
cycle/phase; E(T) is exactly its one new phase and chain append, with a new
cycle only for Red, matching that order, selected TEST/requirement/command,
report hash and execution binding. J and P MUST remain U. For batch, E(J)
is exactly one valid normal-stream change-batch-checkpoint record matching
this scope/phase/predecessor; bootstrap stays unchanged. E(O) is its unique
matching order append. E(P) is precisely that checkpoint's native projection
with all other changes/generations/batches unchanged. T MUST remain U.
Validate native encodings/digests using the pinned existing validators and
writer serialization; do not normalize changed JSON into U or invent deltas.

| Kind | O,J,T,P | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| TDD or batch | U,U,U,U | clean |
| TDD | E,U,E,U | complete |
| batch | U,E,U,U or E,E,U,U | known journaled pending |
| batch | E,E,U,E | complete |
| either | every other combination, including any X | ambiguous |

persistenceAmbiguity is exactly dispatched AND classification=ambiguous.
It is not inferred from exit code or report existence. Thus order-only TDD,
projection-without-journal batch, extra foreign writes and unknown snapshot
state all require A. Valid journal-first batch prefixes are known pending,
not silently successful and not conflated with ambiguous corruption; they
still terminate at batchPending. Missing post-call snapshots cannot choose
the cleaner state. Complete facts permit receipt recovery only after all
higher-ranked predicates and changed-report/process proofs pass.
The durable Attempt outcome must also be success. Failed/interrupted complete
facts suspend at callFailed/callInterrupted unless a higher-ranked condition
applies; they are not converted to success by native persistence alone.
Lease failure with changed/unmeasurable target identity requires A even if
O,J,T,P are clean; identical bytes with a different inode/ctime never qualify.
A changed target with no lease failure and clean facts is not, by itself,
persistenceAmbiguity: an expected report goes to resumeCapability, otherwise
targetIdentity/nativeReport wins by the listed precedence.
