tree(n) is `{kind:n.kind,children:n.getChildren(sourceFile).map(tree)}` when
children exist, otherwise `{kind:n.kind,text:n.getText(sourceFile)}`. This
includes tokens/SyntaxList, not positions or trivia; the raw SHA separately
binds whitespace/comments. No AST printer or implementation-discovered
allowlist may normalize away a difference. Read-only proof rejected 17
in-memory base/name/subtree mutations, including a four-argument inputs join,
and confirmed an after-inputs decoder edit leaves this descriptor unchanged.
These are dependency probes, not additions to the 23 TDD mutation rows.

closed-consumer-effects-v1 permits local declarations, pure expressions,
conditionals/throw, immediate/local arrow functions and calls to the supplied
capabilities or pure JSON/string/array/Set operations used by this decoder.
Intrinsic static methods are limited to JSON.parse/stringify (one argument,
no reviver/replacer), Object.keys/entries/fromEntries, Array.isArray,
Number.isSafeInteger and Buffer.from/isBuffer. Permitted instance operations
are array map/flatMap/filter/every/includes/join/slice and sort on a fresh local
key array, Set.has, string slice/includes/startsWith/endsWith, Buffer.toString
with utf8, and non-global/non-sticky literal RegExp.test. Only Error and Set
construction is allowed; local bindings may be assigned, but not external
bindings or properties/prototypes of input/capability objects.
Reject imports (including dynamic imports), require, process, globalThis,
eval/Function, timers/Date/randomness, reflection, getters/setters, prototype/
constructor access, arbitrary computed member access, recursion, loops and
unlisted calls/effects. Async/generator functions, await/yield and tagged
template calls are also forbidden; no deferred work may escape accounting.
Computed reads are limited to numeric array indices,
the two fixed requirement IDs on implementation maps, or the descriptor's
closed literal field names. Disable VM string/Wasm code generation. Freeze
capabilities and input views; no writes, network or real filesystem operations.
Unexpected dependencies/effects or deterministic budget exhaustion reject;
wall-clock expiry is NOT a semantic rejection. Never inject a missing
dependency or widen this allowlist to make a candidate pass.

The following deterministic capabilities are the ONLY environmental stubs:
- root is the logical string @consumer-root; join is a pure POSIX path join
  restricted to that logical namespace, with no parent traversal. The view's
  base is root/.musubix/evidence/test-file-freeze/CHANGE-0017/g8 and its sole
  entry is prepared-root. These are virtual names, never physical directories,
  actual manifest hashes or inputs to the UUID generator.
- readdirSync accepts only that base with no options and returns a fresh
  one-element array ["prepared-root"]. readFileSync accepts only the two
  paths below with encoding exactly "utf8"; all other accesses reject.
  F/preflight/inputs.json maps to the COMPLETE original canonical inputs bytes,
  not a reconstructed object or a decoder-patched copy. Before F exists these
  are the finalized staged bytes, required byte-identical on publication.
  F/manifest.json maps to a discovery-only canonical view
  `{predecessorFreeze:inputs.manifestCore.predecessorFreeze}`; only that
  manifest property may be observed, with nested manifestSha256 where present.
  Track the provenance of that parse result: a read-monitor permits only
  get(predecessorFreeze) on the discovery object and get(manifestSha256) on its
  non-null predecessor object. All other gets, enumeration (including
  Object.keys/entries and spread), prototype inspection, writes or descriptor
  access reject, even though those methods may be permitted on other data.
  The monitor preserves actual values/null and cannot manufacture missing
  properties. Thus a consumer cannot silently depend on fields or key counts
  omitted from this deliberately partial discovery view.
  This explicit stub tests consumer decoding, not lineage discovery or final
  manifest validation. The mode-appropriate structural guard remains separate
  and mandatory (bounded eleven-file guard at step 3, full committed lineage
  at step 4). No unknown final manifest address/preflightSha is injected.
- record is the existing Node-assert object guard; expect supports ONLY
  toHaveLength using a real assertion, never a no-op. Non-JSON intrinsics
  retain the specified native operations; JSON uses the versioned capability
  below, not an unmodified global JSON object. Buffer/hash capabilities are the existing
  approved helpers, not a replacement order validator.
- value is exactly the frozen synthetic
  `{provenance:inputs.fixtureBindings.synthetic.provenance,
  executionBinding:{logicalCommandSha256:inputs.fixtureBindings.synthetic.logicalCommandSha256}}`.
  activationFixture is a capture stub, NOT the extracted factory. Require one
  call, identity equality of the first two arguments to these supplied values,
  and capture/freeze the third argument without reordering its keys. Return a
  unique frozen capture token; the initializer's result must be that token.
  No factory execution, runtime validator, provider, test body or UUID draw
  occurs in this context. The independently captured binding is the consumer
  result being checked, not a fabricated fixture acceptance result.

**JSON capability frozen-native-json-v1:** Supply a frozen object exposing
only parse and stringify, each frozen and accepting exactly one argument.
Capture native JSON functions from the isolated VM realm before user code;
never replace/freeze the host process's shared primordials. parse requires a
string, delegates grammar/value creation to native JSON.parse, then deep-freezes
EVERY returned object/array, recursively including nested values. Primitives
remain native primitives. Freezing visits own JSON data values without sorting
or changing property insertion order. No reviver, replacer, extra argument,
property injection, normalization or decoder-specific patch is allowed.

For text byte-identical to the single delivered discovery-view text only,
return the monitored read-only view of those actual parsed values; for all
other text return the normal deeply frozen native result. Construct any nested
monitored predecessor before freezing its containing target, so a nonconfigurable
property's get returns the actual stored referent and satisfies Proxy invariants.
The capability must not report a native parsing result while returning different
data. The monitor logs every get or rejected trap as
`{ordinal,path,operation,key,allowed}`, with zero-based contiguous ordinal,
JSON Pointer paths, string key or null, and no time/random fields. Only the
previously declared predecessorFreeze/manifestSha256 reads are allowed.
Enumeration, descriptor/prototype inspection, writes and other gets reject.
Logs must be identical across CLI/import/replays for the same inputs.

stringify delegates native JSON.stringify on permitted values with no replacer/
space, retaining native key ordering; attempts to stringify the monitored
discovery object encounter and fail its forbidden-read trap rather than
bypassing monitoring. Freeze VM-realm primordials and reject prototype access/
mutation under the AST policy; normal JSON data has no executable getters or
functions. No mutation/prototype escape or access to hidden native delegates.

Before consumer execution run the fixed twelve capability probes named in
jsonCapabilityProbes, in that order, in disposable isolated capability contexts.
Use ordinary fixtures `{"outer":{"n":1}}` and `[{"n":1}]`, and discovery
fixtures `{predecessorFreeze:null}` and `{predecessorFreeze:{manifestSha256:
"a".repeat(64)}}` serialized by canonicalBytes as their respective delivered
texts. Both discovery variants must enforce the same access policy.
Verify deep freeze, strict nested/array writes, unknown discovery read,
enumeration/write, setPrototypeOf, capability replacement, malformed JSON
and native stringify equality; rejection probes must actually throw and
positive probes must produce the expected native values. Record ordered
`{id,expected,observed}` outcomes; wrong or missing outcomes fail capability.
Probe work/logs are separate from consumer execution counters/access log;
never pre-populate a passing result or count a probe as TDD/runtime evidence.

**Deterministic budget, not a semantic timeout:** Every step-2 CLI/import and
step-3/4 replay uses consumer-operation-budget-v1 with exactly 100000000 units.
No vm.runInContext timeout or elapsed-time threshold may choose its outcome.
ts-statement-call-arrow-v1 instruments ONLY the extracted initializer before
locked ES2022 transpilation: add one statement charge before each executed
non-Block statement, one call charge before evaluation of each source
CallExpression/NewExpression, and one arrowEntries charge on entering each
source arrow body (after parameter binding). Calls use a comma expression
around the whole original call/new, never around its callee/receiver, preserving
this/evaluation/short-circuit semantics. Expression-bodied arrows become a
charged body returning the original expression. Exclude generated charging
nodes, type-only nodes and wrapper/host/helper code; no duplicate charging.
Use source kind/startByte/endByte as site identity and deterministic source
preorder for instrumentation. No instrumentation edits to authoritative tests.

The JSON capability additionally charges parseBytes = UTF-8 input length
before native parse, stringifyBytes = UTF-8 native result length before
returning a string (zero for native undefined), and freezeNodes once per
returned JSON node including primitives, in preorder: array indices ascending,
object own keys in native insertion order. Each parse is a new tree/charge;
monitor-wrapper construction is not another parse/freeze. Counter categories
are exactly the recipe's ordered six fields; total is their sum. A single
private host debit is atomic: before incrementing, if total+amount exceeds
100000000, emit execution-stage reason operation-budget-exhausted with site,
counter, attempted amount and consumed counters; no attempted operation is
performed/returned. The private debit cannot be referenced, shadowed, reset or
caught by source (try/catch and instrumentation-name references reject).
Counters are safe integers, start at zero once per invocation, and never use
clock, CPU speed or engine instruction guesses. Native work not represented
by these explicit units is not claimed to be an instruction/CPU-time measure.

Bind instrumentation version and generated-initializer byte SHA, budget limit,
all six observed counters and total in consumerDecoder.executionBudget.
Require canonical equality of counters, JSON access logs and result across
CLI/import/archived replays. During read-only consumer execution, a separate
host watchdog may stop a hung process
but yields INCOMPLETE, not a persisted semantic pass/fail, timeout diagnostic,
budget-exhausted result, failed receipt or terminal generation decision.
Keep any notice transient; never write a completed preflight from that exit.
Only an observed deterministic completed result can advance publication.
These rules concern the consumer diagnostic, not native TDD command timeouts.
They do not exempt persisted write-window crash states from the portable
publication crash boundary and A/B/C classifier below.

Require the read trace to be exactly one base-directory listing, one discovery
manifest read and one inputs read in that order. Bind logical paths and their
byte hashes; never include the unknown physical F in upstream output hashes.
For COMMITTED step-4 replay the executor first verifies the real F/manifest,
complete twelve-file closure, committed tip and full lineage. The sole
PARTIAL step-3 exception instead verifies the eleven-file publication and
prospective-manifest address as specified below, WITHOUT a real-manifest,
committed-tip or full-lineage guard at that replay boundary. Both then supply
the same discovery view and bytes read ONLY from F/preflight/inputs.json.
The capability view cannot select a different freeze or fall back to live/cache
inputs after publication. Static/data-access checks reject observing other
manifest properties, so the discovery stub cannot mask such dependencies.

Independently decode a SEPARATELY parsed copy of those same inputs in the host
using the native-string recipe above, not the extracted consumer or its output.
Do not share decoded arrays/records or decoder code with the consumer. Compare
the capture's orderPrefix.records against that independent result AND directly
against fixtureBindings.g8.orderPrefix.recordJson: JSON.stringify each captured
record must equal the corresponding pinned string byte-for-byte, in exact
array order, with exact length/tip/aggregate. Validate schemaVersion=1 on the
bound descriptor and reconstructed log, exact sourcePath/sourceByteSha256/
algorithm/version/extraction bindings, and call UNCHANGED validateEvidenceOrderLog
on both independently reconstructed logs, requiring valid=true/diagnostics=[].
The capture's existing factory argument shape remains {orderPrefix:{records}},
not an invented schemaVersion field on that argument. Check its repositoryId,
COMPAT/LIFECYCLE implementation path arrays, complete requirements/design
approval objects and complete phase objects against verified g8 inputs and
current manifestCore approval/checkpoint references (including g8:design:2 at D).
Hashing two wrong decoders identically is insufficient: direct string equality,
externally pinned prefix digests, native validation and approval/phase checks
must ALL pass independently.

checks.json and preflight.json add the closed consumerDecoder record
`{extractionSha256,astIdentitySha256,sourceSha256,inputsSha256,recipeSha256,
invocationCount:1,factoryStubCallCount:1,uuidDrawCount:0,
reads:[{operation,path,sha256}],
discoveryDescriptorSha256,
jsonCapability:{version,probes:[{id,expected,observed}],accessLog},
executionBudget:{kind,limit,instrumentation,instrumentedInitializerSha256,
counters:{statements,calls,arrowEntries,parseBytes,stringifyBytes,freezeNodes},total},
consumerResultSha256,independentResultSha256,
binding:{repositoryId,requirementsApprovalSha256,designApprovalSha256,
requirementsPhaseSha256,designPhaseSha256,requirementsCheckpointOrder,
designCheckpointOrder,prefixDescriptorSha256,recordCount,tipSequence,
tipRecordSha256,recordStringsSha256,implementationPathsSha256},
match:true,nativeDiagnostics:[]}`.
Both result hashes are H of independently obtained complete factory-binding
arguments and must match; string aggregate comparison additionally preserves
key-order sensitivity. astIdentitySha256=H(the literal AST identity string),
recipeSha256=H(consumerDecoderRecipe), prefixDescriptorSha256=H(g8.orderPrefix);
phase/path hashes use H of their complete respective values. reads operations
are exactly readdirSync, readFileSync, readFileSync, in that order, and use paths
"B", "F/manifest.json#discovery-view", "F/preflight/inputs.json"; directory
listing hash is H(["prepared-root"]), file hashes cover delivered raw bytes.
Report structuralChecks entry
`{id:"consumer-decoder-binding",expected:true,observed:true,diagnostic:null}`
only on full success. A failure uses
`PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:consumer-decoder-binding` with stage
extraction/dependency/effect/capability/execution/transport/binding/
decoder-disagreement/publication-drift and first failing source position or
record index. The explicit semantic precedence below applies. This is not a
mutation-table row, expected g7 failure or proof of runtime-only checks.

**Semantic execution/diagnostic precedence:** After the applicable structural
guard, run structural transport checks (canonical input envelope/hash, recipe,
source/helper/tooling identity and historical approval/phase prerequisites),
then native-order-prefix-binding for g7, then g8, then consumer-decoder-binding,
then factory/mutation evaluation. No consumer VM or factory executes while
either native prefix is invalid. Initial execution and consumer-only replay
use this SAME prefix-before-consumer order; replays stop after the consumer
comparison and never rerun factory/mutation evaluation.
Lineage entry/root/graph ranks below remain first; step 3 substitutes only
its explicitly bounded eleven-file structural guard, not a committed guard.
Structural transport prerequisites use this fixed kind order: canonical-input-
envelope/hash, recipe-binding, source-byte-binding, helper/tooling-binding,
historical-approval-source/object, historical-phase-schema. The first four use
`PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:preflight-structural-transport` with that kind;
the latter two retain g7-approval-source-binding and g7-phase-container-schema.
Within one kind use ordinal UTF-8 JSON Pointer/path ties (requirements before
design for historical stage objects). Synthetic phase checks need constructed
fixtures and remain in the later factory evaluation, not this prerequisite.
Wrong/unverified repositoryRoot uses the earlier lineage root-context-mismatch
diagnostic, not consumer dependency. All these diagnostics remain outside the
fixed 20 evaluator checks and 23 mutation rows.
Within each native prefix check use descriptor/schema and external binding,
then string grammar/round-trip by increasing index, then aggregate/extraction
hash, then length/tip/checkpoint bindings, then native validator diagnostics
in its returned order. Finish g7 before starting g8 regardless of index.
Within the consumer use exactly the stage order extraction, dependency,
effect, capability, execution, transport, binding, decoder-disagreement,
publication-drift. Within an AST stage choose smallest authoritative UTF-8
start byte, then end byte, then reason in ordinal UTF-8 order; missing required
nodes/bindings use the initializer start. Other ties use record index, then
JSON Pointer/path in ordinal UTF-8 order (non-indexed checks precede index 0).
The first violation by these ranks determines the primary diagnostic; never
race validators or use exception arrival order. g7's expected two identity
failures belong only to later factory evaluation, not these prerequisites.

Choose this ONE non-circular sequence (no mandatory speculative F1):
1. After D and the authorized consumer edit, finalize five live source hashes,
   the source-copy bytes and all four extraction descriptors. Build canonical
   inputs including consumerDecoderRecipe; determine preparationSha256 and
   stage the byte-identical source/inputs under its cache directory.
2. STAGING, before any F publication: apply structural/transport prerequisites,
   both native-prefix checks, consumer verification, then the existing
   factory/mutation preflight in that order. The normal CLI execution writes
   checks.json including consumerDecoder. Also IMPORT the identical staged
   harness module and call its exported verifyConsumerDecoder with the same
   explicit verified repository root and staged buffers. Revalidate both
   prefixes first and compare canonical consumerDecoder AND its structural
   result byte-identically to the CLI's corresponding results. This is a
   consumer-only comparison, not a second factory/mutation execution. Any
   mismatch rejects at decoder-disagreement with mode=cli-import; do not
   publish or rewrite the CLI result to match. Only after equality and the
   observed CLI exit pass may the parent write preflight.json, then derive
   prospective manifest bytes and F. Keep those exact bytes in the current
   preparation context. No F/final manifest hash/preflightSha enters consumer
   results. The old fixture remains unchanged until approval/D.
3. PARTIAL-PUBLICATION SOLE EXCEPTION: apply the existing preparation and
   permission guards during publication. Publish the eleven
   NON-manifest closure files, including exact staged inputs, checks, preflight,
   harness, sources and raw approval archives, with the existing atomic rules.
   Only AFTER ALL eleven (exact immutable list excluding manifest.json) have
   completed file/directory fsync, reopen, rehash and byte equality to staged
   copies, establish the content-derived ready-eleven seal below and allow
   consumer-only replay, including fresh-process re-execution after interruption.
   Require exactly state A, B or C from the shared classifier below, no other
   temp/unrecognized entry, the
   initial publication capability still current OR a freshly verified
   read-only ready-eleven context (never a restored creation capability), and
   basename(F)=sha256(prospectiveManifestBytes)=H(prospectiveManifestObject)
   from step 2. This replay's structural guard checks precisely those eleven
   files, the classified manifest/temp state, ownership/modes/durability,
   capability and address. In C it verifies the existing manifest's exact bytes;
   it does NOT require a candidate committed-tip/full-lineage claim for unfinished F;
   preceding ordinary preparation guards are not removed.
   Each invocation starts its deterministic counters at zero and reads the
   same immutable bytes. An interrupted invocation yields no result and can
   be re-executed after rechecking the seal; never persist partial counters.
   Import the verified archived harness with the SAME explicit repositoryRoot,
   re-extract from F/sources/tests/test-runtime-evidence.test.ts, validate
   archived transport/prefixes, then verify the consumer with F/preflight/inputs.json.
   Require exact descriptor and canonical result equality to published checks.
   The replay writes NOTHING, allocates no evidence and cannot publish the
   manifest, repair bytes or recompute F. A missing/drifted one of eleven,
   wrong address, unverified seal or ANY other partial rerun is a structural
   g8-freeze-lineage-binding failure; ordered file-list/path ties apply. Semantic
   failure retains its primary diagnostic and requires abandon/reopen because
   publication has begun, but ONLY for a completed deterministic rejection,
   never a watchdog/elapsed-time exit. No incomplete archive publication is
   resumed by the read-only seal.
4. COMMITTED: publish manifest LAST, commit and verify all twelve Git closure
   files, then apply real F/manifest.json, the complete closure, committed-tip
   and full lineage guards. Before first Red perform the full COMMITTED
   verification sequence: structural transport, g7/g8 native prefixes, then
   archived consumer comparison with the SAME explicit repositoryRoot.
   "Full" here means all committed guards, not a second factory/mutation run.
   Any result drift blocks Red. The phrase
   "after freeze published" means checking finalized source/input copies before
   manifest publication/commit as in step 3, plus this committed replay, NOT
   adding a new result to the manifest after its hash has been fixed.

**Restartable read-only replay and result persistence:** The ready-eleven
seal is derived, not a new persisted marker/file or a serialized process lease.
On every original/fresh-process step-3 invocation, independently verify exactly
the eleven immutable paths and raw hashes, canonical archived inputs/checks/
preflight cross-bindings, the generated harness/tooling/source/approval identities,
one admissible A/B/C state (no other temp/unrecognized entry), unchanged live
five-file hashes and all existing
owner/mode/no-follow/durability rules. Reopen/rehash and reassert file/directory
fsync if required; never change file bytes. Reconstruct prospective manifest
bytes as canonicalBytes({...inputs.manifestCore,preflightSha256:
sha256(archivedPreflightBytes)}); require the same F final segment. This is
the exact step-2 object, not a new manifest candidate or changed result.
Check the requirements approval and checkpoint-3805 design approval/scope
bindings preserved in inputs/manifest, never the replaced live design approval
file, plus absence of official attempts under EVERY g8 root, the unique
candidate ready-eleven root and its exact committed
predecessor chain. Other unfinished/competing roots still reject. Do not
require a candidate manifest in A/B or a candidate commit/tip in any of A/B/C;
in C the existing manifest must verify byte-identically. Committed predecessors
retain their normal verification. Capture fresh stable metadata for the read,
not the old dev+inode/nonce as a resurrected creation lease.

Step 3 is the SOLE partial consumer-replay exception and is REPEATABLE read-only
in fresh processes; it is not once-only. The content-derived A/B/C context
replaces any conflicting same-process/crash-terminal rule only for verification
of a complete valid ready-eleven seal. It grants no
authority to create/repair any of those eleven files, accept a partial set,
change source, select another root, publish an intent or run Red.
A process/watchdog interruption during this replay leaves it incomplete;
a fresh process must recheck the same seal, rerun the same consumer with the
same budget and match the already archived expected result/counters/logs.
Step 4 likewise permits fresh-process committed replay after the complete
twelve-file/commit/lineage guard. No elapsed duration or watchdog exit can
itself produce an abandon decision during read-only consumer execution in
steps 2/3/4; the persisted-state classifier still applies after a write-window
crash. Invalid immutable bytes or an
observed deterministic semantic/budget rejection remain genuine failures.

**Shared manifest-only finalization state classifier:** Step-3 admission,
ready-eleven seal validation, fresh-process recovery and diagnostic selection
MUST use the same classifier over one stable no-follow filesystem snapshot.
First collect the eleven-file/ownership/hash facts and independently reconstruct
the prospective manifest bytes/address as above. Then classify exactly ONE
of these states for the sole candidate F; classification itself writes nothing:

| State | manifest.json | Temps | Admission and subsequent action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Absent (ENOENT only) | None | Reverify eleven files and replay consumer; only after deterministic success may normal atomic publication of the fixed manifest begin. |
| B | Absent (ENOENT only) | Exactly one manifest temp in F's own directory | Require fixed destination-derived filename grammar, target exactly manifest.json, no-follow regular/euid/0600 metadata, link count 1, stable identity and all existing parent/target checks. Reverify eleven files and replay consumer read-only; only after deterministic success may the bounded alias-safe manifest operation complete. |
| C | Present as a verified regular/euid/0600 single-link file byte-equal to the independently reconstructed prospective manifest | None | The twelve-file closure is still uncommitted. Reverify eleven files AND manifest, then replay consumer read-only; only after deterministic success may manifest durability/commit verification and commit of these same twelve bytes complete. Never rewrite the manifest. |

All states require the unchanged seal, checkpoint-3805 approval/scope/source
bindings from preserved inputs/manifest, no official attempts and verified
committed predecessors; none re-read the live design approval as fixture
lineage. An already committed
complete root belongs to step 4, not state C. Lookup errors other than ENOENT
are failures, not absence. B's temp bytes are NOT evidence or authority; a
partial temp may be rewritten only after consumer success and fresh single-link
descriptor checks, using independently reconstructed manifest bytes.
No other temp, publication target/context, unrecognized entry, missing/drifted
one of eleven, or fourth recovery state is admitted. B/C are narrowly bounded
manifest finalization, not generic partial-closure recovery or a revived
arbitrary-file creation lease.

In EVERY A/B/C fresh process, validate the snapshot/seal and rerun the consumer
with the same immutable source/inputs, JSON capability, root binding and
deterministic operation budget. Previously persisted expected results are only
comparison inputs, not permission to skip replay. No temp open-for-write,
truncate, unlink, publication, manifest durability completion or commit may
occur before deterministic success. During read-only replay or before the
first write, watchdog/interruption leaves the phase incomplete and repeatable
under the approved state classifier:
leave all names/bytes untouched and classify/replay again in a fresh process.
After success, recheck the eleven-file seal and current metadata before writes;
a changed entry snapshot cannot inherit the prior success blindly.

For B, destination absence uses the existing no-follow/single-link branch:
open the verified temp without O_TRUNC, fstat/recheck, then rewrite only from
the reconstructed bytes, fsync and publish no-replace. If the target is found
existing during that ALREADY AUTHORIZED operation (including after its own
hard-link publication or an EEXIST), use the existing destination-exists branch:
NEVER open/write/truncate the temp, verify target bytes/hash and identity/link
counts, finish durability, unlink only that temp, fsync and rehash the target.
An unprovable identity/race or different target rejects. This transient
target-plus-temp condition is handled only inside the already authorized
atomic operation; it is NOT a fourth fresh-process admission state. A new
entry scan seeing both manifest and temp rejects even if they alias/equal.
Thus the three-state restart contract does not silently expand the alias-safe
procedure's authority. A/B completion reaches C; only verified commit reaches
step 4. C never creates a temp or switches to another publication context.

**Portable publication crash boundary:** The contract deliberately uses
portable no-replace hard-link publication, not a new renameat2 or Windows API
dependency. It prefers fail-closed evidence integrity over guaranteeing crash
recovery for every write window. Once any of the eleven-file publication
writes begins, or during B's manifest temp/write/link/unlink/durability steps
(and the same normal publication steps begun from A), a crash may leave a
persisted snapshot outside A/B/C, including manifest-plus-temp. Such a snapshot
is terminal PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g8-freeze-lineage-binding and requires
abandon/reopen, even when interruption was the only cause. No automatic
deletion, backfill or reclassification may turn a non-A/B/C persisted snapshot
into a recoverable state. In-operation alias-safe temp cleanup is authorized
only inside the already admitted uninterrupted operation; it is not startup
cleanup. A fresh process must classify before any write and may replay only
an independently verified A/B/C seal (or step 4's committed closure).
Losing the first-preparation creation capability never permits reuse of an
incomplete eleven-file set, even if every surviving byte matches staging.

Use the existing diagnostic priority, not a separate recovery validator:
entry/name/type/owner/mode/link/temp violations first; invalid temp grammar,
multiple temps, unrecognized entries and wrong-target/temp-with-manifest
combinations keep their existing entry kinds (the latter is temp-context-mismatch).
Missing/drifted eleven-file bytes and a different existing manifest use the
existing root missing-closure-destination/closure-byte-hash-mismatch kinds.
Only fully admitted A/B suppress the candidate's missing-manifest rejection;
only A/B/C suppress its uncommitted-closure rejection/committed-graph membership.
No non-manifest file absence is excused. Other roots and all preceding entry
errors retain normal ranks. Within each stage use the existing root/path/kind
ordering. Invalid states fail terminally with
PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g8-freeze-lineage-binding before semantic/consumer
checks; a watchdog is not an invalid-state diagnosis.

Only after a deterministic step-3 match may the executor enter a DISTINCT
manifest-only finalization context: recheck the seal and global predecessor/
no-call rules, publish ONLY those already derived manifest bytes using atomic
no-replace rules, commit the fixed twelve-file closure, then pass step 4.
This permits completion after a fresh-process verification without reviving
the old arbitrary-file creation capability. The replay itself still writes
nothing. If interrupted after a completed/persisted result, revalidate its
complete hash/input binding, never infer completion from an exit or partial
output. Existing byte-identical results/destinations are reused, not appended
or rewritten; partial/different results give no credit.
An interrupted manifest-only publication must first be admitted by the SAME
A/B/C classifier and pass read-only replay in the new process. Only then may
the existing alias-safe, byte-idempotent branches operate on manifest.json
and B's one exact temp, with bytes independently reconstructed above.
The other eleven must already verify and remain untouched; absent/different/
extra closure files do not authorize backfilling. A full manifest but missing
commit is exactly C and permits only durability/verification/commit of those
twelve bytes after fresh consumer success; no changed manifest or source.
Fresh-process A/B/C replay is mandatory even if an earlier result was persisted.
For that recovery only, its single manifest temp is allowed by the original
no-follow/link-safety checks, not an unrestricted partial-root exception.

Step 2 before F publication may re-execute the same staged CLI/import work
after an incomplete watchdog stop; no partial checks count as a result.
Completed checks/preflight may be reused only byte-identically after full
binding verification; if the parent did not observe complete CLI/import
success, rerun and observe it rather than fabricate an exit. There is no new
closure file, timeout-failure record, human approval or TDD credit. Existing
fail-closed rules remain for incomplete file publication outside the sealed
eleven-file/manifest-only states. A read-only consumer interruption is
incomplete, not a semantic failure or authority for source changes; a
write-window crash is governed by the portable publication crash boundary.

**Location-independent harness/root contract:** The exact hashed harness exports
the read-only root-explicit host entry
`verifyConsumerDecoder({repositoryRoot,sourceBytes,inputsBytes})`.
repositoryRoot is a required absolute, verified control-worktree root, distinct
from the VM's logical root. Verify repository/workspace identity against inputs
and the existing control context; reject absence/mismatch, never infer a root.
The CLI obtains this parameter only by verifying process.cwd() as that root;
imported callers supply the SAME verified root explicitly at steps 2/3/4.
Resolve locked TypeScript, exact musubix5 distribution and approved helper
paths solely from repositoryRoot using standard Node resolution; never from
import.meta.url, dirname of the harness, relative parent walking or a staged/
archived module's location. No custom loader or future runtime dependency.
Module import is inert except Node built-ins/declarations: repository-dependent
imports are deferred until root verification. import.meta.url may only distinguish
CLI entry from import, not locate the repository or any dependency.
Host root/tooling/helper verification may read their approved files; it and
consumer verification perform NO writes. VM real-FS access remains forbidden.
All modes must verify the same tooling/helper identities; their paths of
module loading and the physical root never affect canonical consumer results.
The step-2 CLI/import byte comparison is mandatory before preflight publication;
step-3/4 archive replays repeat the same root contract, not a new lookup base.
Root/location violations are structural prerequisites, before native-prefix
or consumer execution; an unverified imported root cannot use a cached valid
root from an earlier call. The export returns consumerDecoder and its structural
result and never executes full preflight on module import. Each call creates a fresh consumer-only VM and
one capture-stub invocation, with zero draws and no rerun of either factory/
mutation context. Replay outputs are compared in memory, not new closure files.
The descriptors are bound by inputsSha256, results by checksSha256 and
preflightSha256, then manifest/immutableClosureSha256: all existing twelve
paths and the fixed path-list digest remain unchanged.

Before any root exists, failure blocks preparation. If a completed F1 exists,
any permitted pre-Red consumer correction requires the existing all-root
no-call-intent/receipt/temp guard and a NEW F2 preflight/closure with archive-only
approval-source copying; never repair F1 in place or backfill a check.
Incomplete/corrupt publication outside the ready-eleven/manifest-only states
retains the existing fail-closed rule. The restartable step-3 sealed read
verification and bounded manifest-only finalization are the SOLE partial-root
exceptions; no other partial preflight, consumer or harness replay is admitted.
A watchdog/interruption during read-only consumer replay or before the first
write is incomplete and repeatable under the approved state classifier, not
evidence. Write-window crashes may leave terminal non-A/B/C snapshots as
specified by the portable publication crash boundary.
After first Red NO consumer/test correction, supersession or rebaseline is
allowed. All native-string aggregate pins and the 23-mutation registry remain
unchanged.

##### Factory-only UUID accounting (unchanged)

Supply Buffer, structuredClone, the existing hashing/checkpoint helpers and
a Node assert-based object guard for the factory's `record` dependency.
Supply randomUUID as a deterministic fixture-only function: hash canonical
`["g8-freeze-fixture",preparationSha256,caseId,counter]`, take the first 16
bytes, set RFC-4122 version-4/variant bits and format lowercase UUID text;
caseId here means the execution context ID, not a mutation row or reporting
label. The counter starts at zero once per context, uses its current value
for each draw and increments once after each draw. It continues across
factory, changed declaration and full array construction without resetting.
The independent g7-foreign context has its own counter initialized once at
zero; it never shares or changes g8-mutations counter state.
This does not patch production crypto.
Use fixed literal fixture dates; no wall-clock reads or random reseeding.
Run the g8-positive checks on valid, construct the mutations once, verify the
UUID guard below, then handle every mutation in source order by its registry
disposition. Evaluate the independent g7-foreign scenario in its isolated
context; serialize cases in the fixed g8-positive/g7-foreign order.
Construct g7-foreign from that context's SINGLE extracted-factory output,
using only the ordered rewrite below. Its two expected evaluator failures
are generation-eight and design-approval-reference, with otherwise passing
structural/order/fingerprint predicates. Original g7 records and frozen
sources are never rewritten.

Record `uuidContexts` in checks.json and preflight.json, in the recipe's
context order. Each entry is
`{caseId,initialCounter,factoryCallCount,mutationArrayEvaluationCount,
factoryEndCounter,draws:[{counter,uuid}],finalCounter}`.
Require initialCounter=0 and factoryCallCount=1 for both contexts.
For g8-mutations require mutationArrayEvaluationCount=1, contiguous draw
counters, and finalCounter=factoryEndCounter+1: the unchanged array makes
exactly one UUID draw, at source index 14. For g7-foreign require
mutationArrayEvaluationCount=0 and finalCounter===factoryEndCounter: the
rewrite consumes NO UUID draws. All draws remain local to that scenario.
Audit each UUID against the existing deterministic hash/format rule.
Do not evaluate the factory/array a second time merely to produce the audit.
The generated sequence/count belongs to output recipe evidence, not inputs,
avoiding a cycle through preparationSha256, which seeds the UUID function.
Require mutations[14].cycle.cycleId !== valid.cycle.cycleId. Equality,
counter resets, missing/extra draws or incorrect context/count/UUID replay
reject BEFORE Red with `PREFLIGHT_MUTATION_REGISTRY_MISMATCH`; never reseed
or retry the row to force a difference.

**Mechanical post-step-7 identity closure:** Traverse the resulting candidate
`c` before step 8's other checks. Use JSON-tree depth-first preorder, object
own enumerable string keys sorted by ECMAScript ordinal `.sort()` (not locale),
and array indices in ascending numeric order. Paths are RFC 6901 JSON Pointers
relative to c (root `""`, escape `~` as `~0` and `/` as `~1`); arrays use
zero-based decimal indices without leading zeros. Visit aliases at every path,
so `/cycle` is visited independently of its selected `/tddEvidence/cycles/i`;
do not deduplicate by object identity. Require ordinary JSON data, no cycles,
accessors, symbol/non-enumerable own properties or extra array properties.

prefix through sequence 3788), `/approvals/requirements`, `/approvals/design`,
and the separately validated phase-value containers `/phases/requirements`,
`/phases/design`, `/batch/red`, `/batch/implementation`. Skip only after their
exact prefix/approval-byte bindings and the pinned g7-phase-container-schema
key sets, values and hashes, checkpoint
identities and fingerprint/reference checks have passed; skips are not
wildcards and cannot hide extra sibling properties. Do not skip legacy TDD
phases, journal payloads, runtime provenance or activation. A skipped phase
container's schema must reject added identity fields rather than ignoring them.

For EVERY visited string matching `/^g\d+:/`, require prefix `g7:` and exact

`/orders/3800/phase`, `/orders/3801/phase` (the rebuilt batch Red/implementation
events at sequences 3801/3802), `/journal/j/payload/semanticPhaseKey` and
`/journal/j/payload/orderPhaseKey` for j=0,1, and

Additionally require `/journal/0/idempotencyKey` and `/journal/1/idempotencyKey`

Use one pure evaluator/dispatcher of the following 20 predicates, with the
same function instances and pinned bindings for valid and every mutated
candidate, including g7-foreign; the evaluator bindings remain the g8
manifestCore even after that candidate's identities are rewritten to g7.
Only candidate/checkId vary; the evaluator must not branch on

consume UUIDs. No separate positive implementation or hard-coded result.
The cases entry with caseId="g8-positive" MUST have checks containing exactly
evaluationRecipe.positiveCheckIds in registry order, with no missing, extra
or duplicate IDs. Each result is `{id,expected:true,observed:true,diagnostic:null}`,
computed by that identical evaluator on the g8-mutations context's valid.
Validate ID shape/order and expected=true before interpreting results:
any mismatch uses `PREFLIGHT_MUTATION_REGISTRY_MISMATCH`. An observed false
must report `PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:<checkId>` and fail preflight;
exceptions or nonboolean outcomes also fail, never become positive results.
Only after all 20 positive results succeed may the same evaluator satisfy
the 20 mutation rejection rows. Thus an always-false evaluator cannot pass.
Preserve the other generic journal/order/checkpoint and binding prerequisites
as separate `structuralChecks` in checks.json/preflight.json; they still must
satisfy their expected outcomes, but cannot add IDs to or replace any of the
exact 20 cases[g8-positive].checks.

| red-checkpoint-reference-present | a has an own redCheckpoint property whose value is a non-null, non-array object |
| implementation-journal-reference | a.implementationCheckpoint.journalRecordSha256 equals the recordSha256 of the already generic-validated same-scope implementation journal record |
| implementation-before-green | c.batch.implementation.order < c.green.order |

phase intent, atomically publish both original raw byte buffers at
`F/preflight/approval-sources/<byteSha256>` using the no-replace/file-fsync/
directory-fsync/reopen/rehash rules below. Do not serialize parsed approvals.
Verify each archive's byte SHA equals BOTH its byteSha256 and archiveSha256,
and byte-compare to the original verified buffer at initial publication.
Then archive inputs/harness/checks/preflight/source copies, validate the whole
closure, publish manifest last, and commit the complete F evidence closure
before first Red. No new approval act or historical TDD credit is implied.
Do not archive a duplicate full changes projection: the phase objects and
their pinned descriptors/hashes are durably embedded in archived inputs.

This order avoids a hash cycle: manifest/inputs bind EXPECTED archive digests
and F-relative paths, never F's hash or an output of archive publication.
The initial preflight does not claim the future archives already exist.
Once publication starts, existing archive destinations must be checked rather
than bypassed. No preflight/harness rerun is permitted during partial archive
publication EXCEPT the restartable step-3 consumer replay AFTER all eleven
non-manifest closure files are durably complete, rehashed and byte-identical
to staging, with the prospective-manifest address verified. That replay is
read-only, uses archives only and does not demand the not-yet-published real
manifest or a committed-tip/full-lineage guard. All other partial reruns are
inadmissible; the explicit ready-eleven/manifest-only recovery rules, not a
wall-clock exit, determine handling. Full committed validation requires twelve
files at step 4; a read-only consumer watchdog stop leaves the phase incomplete.
Write-window crashes still require the portable publication state classification.
During uninterrupted initial publication, exact missing destinations may be
created from the still verified original bytes before manifest publication/
any phase intent; this does not authorize recovery of an unfinished root
at a global guard boundary.
an existing byte-identical destination still requires all durability checks.
After manifest publication, every later preflight/replay, pre-call guard,
receipt publication/recovery and batch acceptance reads/reopens/rehashes the
ARCHIVES ONLY, parses those raw bytes and rechecks the pinned full approval
objects/artifact digests. Neither ignored cache nor live approval files are
a fallback. Preserve archive source paths as metadata, not lookup candidates.
Each receipt copies historicalApprovalSources verbatim only after both
archive rehashes pass; its archiveSha256 values are thus rechecked persisted
facts, not remembered publication outcomes. Committed evidence travels with
the freeze closure, so cache deletion cannot remove the historical approvals.

**Pre-Red replacement freeze source (F1 -> F2):** A preparation change may
supersede an already published freeze root ONLY before the generation's first
Red call/intent or recorded Red. Before preparing ANY F2, run the global
lineage guard below and verify absence of call intents AND receipts under
EVERY root in `.musubix/evidence/test-file-freeze/CHANGE-0017/g8/`, not only
the proposed F1/F2. Also verify absence of g8 official calls from persisted
phase/order/journal evidence; after that boundary the
existing generation-immutability/abandonment rules apply. Preserve F1 unchanged.
F1 must be the unique latest fully published, committed root for the same
repository/CHANGE-0017/g8 in the explicit predecessor chain. Verify canonical
manifest hashes and chain links, with no cycles, competing tips or unfinished
replacement publication; never select by directory order, mtime or guesswork.

Every manifestCore/final manifest has predecessorFreeze: null for the initial
root, otherwise exactly
`{root,manifestSha256,commit,approvalArchives:[{stage,sourceArchivePath,
byteSha256,archivePath,archiveSha256}]}`.
root is F1's exact repository-relative root, whose final segment equals
manifestSha256; commit is the full Git commit ID containing F1's complete
verified twelve-file immutable Git closure, including manifest.json and both
raw approval archives, under the identifying-commit verification rules below.
approvalArchives has exactly two entries in
requirements/design order. sourceArchivePath is the full repository-relative
`F1/preflight/approval-sources/<byteSha256>`; archivePath is F2-relative
`preflight/approval-sources/<byteSha256>`. Both digest fields equal that stage's
bound historical raw-byte hash. Cross-check all entries against F1's manifest
and F2's historicalApprovalSources. inputs.json binds this object through
manifestCore; F2's final manifest copies it unchanged. The existing predecessor
hash is safe to include, but do not include F2's own root/hash in its inputs.
Receipts bind this lineage through their verified F2 manifest hash.

F2 obtains BOTH raw approval buffers exclusively by reopening F1's committed
archive paths, rehashing against F1's bound byteSha256/archiveSha256 and
byte-comparing to their blobs in the pinned commit. Validate F1's manifest
bytes against that commit too. Use those verified buffers for F2 preparation/
preflight; do not reconstruct JSON or reread cache/live approval paths after
F1 manifest publication, even if they still contain matching hashes.
Once F2's prospective address is known, atomically publish byte-identical
copies at F2/archivePath with the same no-replace, file/directory fsync,
reopen/rehash and full-byte comparison rules. Complete/verify the F2 closure,
publish its manifest last, and commit before any Red. All subsequent F2
checks read F2's archives only; a later F3 must repeat this rule using F2,
not reach back to cache or silently bypass its immediate predecessor.

Missing/drifted approval-source data or non-byte-identical copies rejects with
`PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g7-approval-source-binding` and requires the
documented terminal abandon/reopen behavior, preserving F1/F2 and all evidence.
Uncommitted/incomplete roots outside the bound uninterrupted construction,
ambiguous lineage and failed/interrupted partial replacement publication
instead use the global lineage diagnostic below.
For replacement roots this is stricter than the initial-root missing-destination
completion rule: no completion/backfill/retry of a partial replacement, no
fallback to an older root, and no replacement-baseline changes after Red.
The same sealed step-3 verification after eleven durable files and the
prospective address verify may be re-executed in a fresh process for F2;
only its explicit manifest-only finalization exception may subsequently write.
No other partial-file completion or source repair is permitted.
This is a preparation-source rule, not an approval act or historical credit.

Missing/corrupt archives after manifest publication, different-byte collision,
torn destination or unprovable durability rejects with
PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g7-approval-source-binding. Do not overwrite,
reconstruct, silently choose a new path or fall back to cache. A conflicting
immutable destination or loss of an already-published freeze closure is
terminal g8 abandonment/reopen under the recovery rule below, including
before first Red; preserve all artifacts. An initial missing cache source or
failure before ANY entry/root under B has been created merely blocks
preparation until the same exact prerequisites are available. Once any root
directory, temp or final destination exists under B, a verified invalid first
preparation outside the ready-eleven/manifest-only exception is terminal
PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g8-freeze-lineage-binding: abandon/reopen, preserve
all artifacts, and never retry by reusing that root. A missing final manifest
does not restore retry permission. This boundary concerns initial preparation;
replacement-root failures retain their already specified terminal rules.
Authorized ordinary recovery below is for official phase publication after a
committed closure. The additional narrow ready-eleven read replay and
manifest-only finalization rules above permit fresh-process completion without
restoring arbitrary preparation authority. A read-only consumer watchdog stop
records no semantic failure/abandonment; write-window crashes can leave terminal
non-A/B/C snapshots. Incomplete sets of the eleven files cannot be backfilled.
No publication
or commit is performed during this design-only review.

##### Global freeze-root lineage and active-root guard

Define the generation base B as
`.musubix/evidence/test-file-freeze/CHANGE-0017/g8`.
**Filesystem ownership and creation:** Anchor traversal at the verified control
repository directory. Every traversed repository ancestor from that anchor
through B's parent must be a no-symlink directory owned by the effective uid
with no group/other write bits (`mode & 0022 === 0`); existing ancestors need
not be mode 0700. Never repair their owner/mode to pass. Resolve each component
relative to its verified parent without following links; compare no-follow
path metadata and opened directory identities before using that parent.

B and EVERY executor-created directory at or below B, including each root
and every closure/calls/receipts/reports descendant, must have requested AND
effective mode 0700, effective-uid ownership and no special permission bits.
Create one level at a time with non-recursive mkdir(mode=0700), never recursive
mkdir or a create-parents fallback. Immediately no-follow lstat/fstat and
require a directory, uid===effective uid and `(mode & 07777) === 0700`,
with matching stable device/inode identity. Fsync its parent before creating
any child. The chosen umask policy is fail-closed, not chmod: before creation
require the observed process umask not to mask any requested owner bit, then
verify effective bits immediately regardless of umask/ACL inheritance.
Do not change umask to create an exception or chmod/chown an existing/new
entry into compliance. Mode/owner mismatch after creation is terminal.
Any needed missing ancestor between the repository and B is created similarly,
one level at a time with mode 0700 and verified before continuing; existing
ancestors retain the less restrictive no-group/other-write rule above.

Every temp is created with exclusive/no-follow semantics
O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, requested mode 0600, without opening an existing
name. Immediately fstat and compare no-follow path metadata: require regular
file, effective-uid ownership, `(mode & 07777) === 0600`, link count 1 and
stable identity before writing. Every published destination must remain a
regular effective-uid-owned mode-0600 file; each directory remains mode 0700.
The alias-safe publication/recovery rules govern the only permitted transient
link count 2; after temp removal require destination link count 1. Recheck
owner/mode/type during every scan/reopen, not just creation. Git does not
preserve uid or private permission bits, so Git byte verification does not
substitute for these live checks; a checkout with broader modes is not repaired.
If the filesystem/platform cannot prove these invariants, no-follow identity,
exclusive creation or required durability, fail before Red. There is no
assumed uid, synthetic mode value or permissive platform fallback; the existing
explicit win32 directory-fsync limitation does not waive ownership/mode proof.
Use terminal PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g8-freeze-lineage-binding (entry kind
filesystem-ownership-mode for these checks), subject to the creation boundary
below when no root/entry under B yet exists.

At every guard boundary, enumerate ALL direct children of B, including hidden
entries, in ordinal UTF-8 byte order of repository-relative paths (no locale
sorting). Require each to be a real directory named by a lowercase 64-hex
manifest SHA; reject links, unexpected files/names and unreadable entries.
Within every root, recursively enumerate paths in the same order without
following links. Inspect all entries under calls/ and receipts/, not merely
valid-looking JSON filenames: any entry denotes an attempt/receipt for the
pre-supersession absence check; malformed, misplaced or partial official
records are never silently ignored. No root may be excluded as "old",
"superseded", untracked, ignored, empty or a cache.

**Closed entries and temporary artifacts:** The only final file destinations
are manifest.json, preflight.json, preflight/inputs.json,
preflight/preflight.mjs, preflight/checks.json, the two hash-named
preflight/approval-sources files, the five sources/<authoritative-path> copies,
calls/<ordinal>.json for ordinals 1-27, receipts/<phase>-<evidenceOrder>.json,
and reports/<reportSha256>. Validate dynamic names against the fixed call
mapping and persisted phase/order/report facts, or the single bound current
publication context below, not merely a filename regex. Directories must be
exact ancestors of those permitted destinations. Any other entry, symlink,
special file, malformed final name or unrecognized directory is invalid.

Use exactly `.<destinationBasename>.tmp-<uuid>` in the destination's own
directory for ALL atomic publications, including reports, calls, receipts,
preflight/approval-sources, sources, manifests and other preflight files.
The exact basename grammar is
`^\.([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)\.tmp-([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12})$`.
UUIDs are lowercase canonical version-4 UUIDs; no alternative spelling.
Derive the target from the first capture in that same directory, without
case folding, normalization, timestamp selection or searching for a similar
destination. Require that derived target to be one exact allowed final path.
A temp is NEVER evidence: its presence/content/hash cannot satisfy any
destination, manifest, intent, receipt, report or committed-closure check.
In particular ANY matching temp under calls/ counts as an attempted official
call in the all-root F2-supersession absence check even without a final intent.

To request the sole temp exception, the caller must bind one current context
BEFORE the scan (ordinary scans without a temp exception need no context):
`{mode,root,manifestSha256,activeFreezeRoot,lineageSha256,operation,
ordinal,targetPath,expectedByteSha256}`.
mode is preparation/publication/recovery/consumer-finalization; operation is closure/intent/report/
receipt. targetPath is the exact root-relative final destination, never a
temp-derived choice. For intent/report/receipt ordinal is 1-27 and is derived
from the fixed mapping, verified predecessor receipts and persisted phase/
order/journal/report facts. Reconstruct exact intended bytes independently
of the temp and hash them to expectedByteSha256; no remembered output/exit or
temp content supplies authority. Recovery of a missing intent requires the
unique next ordinal from those facts and proof no corresponding/later call
has executed; recovery of a receipt/report requires its persisted native
facts and the existing no-later-call rule. If these facts do not determine
one context, recovery is forbidden. Context is an executor check input, not
new evidence or an exemption from the global lineage scan.
consumer-finalization is the sole uncommitted temp-recovery exception above:
root/manifestSha256/expectedByteSha256 bind the independently reconstructed F
manifest; operation=closure, ordinal=null, targetPath=manifest.json only.
activeFreezeRoot/lineageSha256 bind the verified committed predecessor tip/
chain (null tip for genesis), never claim F is already committed. Eleven
unchanged files must verify first; only one exact manifest temp may exist.
Classify A/B/C before granting this context: B alone admits that temp, C admits
only the exact manifest with no temp. No other file or temp can acquire this exception. Read-only consumer replay
itself grants no temp/publication authority.

For a committed complete root, tolerate at most ONE temp across the entire
generation base, ONLY under the unique active tip and ONLY when its derived
target equals the context's single destination and its operation/ordinal/
root/lineage binding passes. Zero temps is normal; multiple temps, another
ordinal/destination, invalid name/UUID, orphan target, non-tip temp or an
unprovable/missing context is terminal. A temp outside this exception makes
even an otherwise committed complete root unfinished/invalid.
The exception does not excuse missing immutable closure files or a wrong
final destination hash. Final intent/receipt/report targets may be absent
only when their permitted current recovery context independently reconstructs
them; the temp never fills that absence. If a target already exists it must
be byte-identical to the independently reconstructed bytes.

Before manifest commit, an expected single current-publication temp is allowed
ONLY during uninterrupted preparation OR as B's single manifest.json temp in
bounded manifest-only finalization recovery, with operation=closure and ordinal=null.
Bind root/manifestSha256 to the prospective approved preparation manifest,
activeFreezeRoot/lineageSha256 to the verified committed predecessor scan
(both null only for the first root), targetPath to its closure inventory,
and expectedByteSha256 to the independently prepared bytes. No intents or
receipts may exist anywhere. The prospective root is the sole in-progress
successor, not an active root for official calls. This permits its ordinary
atomic construction only, not recovery of an interrupted incomplete freeze:
no official call/intent/receipt may accept an uncommitted root. The separate
A/B/C finalization guard admits only its bounded states after eleven-file
verification and mandatory read-only replay; all other roots must already
satisfy global lineage validation.

**One-process preparation admission and terminal boundary:** At the start of
EVERY preparation attempt, run the ordinary generation-wide guard with NO
excluded root and NO restored preparation exception. It must accept all
existing committed roots and prove no call intent/receipt/attempt under any
root. For genesis, require B absent or an already empty, verified-safe
effective-uid-owned mode-0700 B. An existing nonempty B is never treated as
genesis or cleared for a retry. For replacement, the guard must establish the
unique committed predecessor tip before any creation.

After independently computing the prospective manifest/closure bytes, require
no-follow lstat(context.root) to return ENOENT; any other result, including
an existing byte-identical complete root, is terminal. Verify/create missing
safe repository ancestors first, then B if absent, then context.root, in
that exact order. B creation is part of preparation and uses the one-level
verified mode-0700 sequence above. A crash after only safe ancestors/B were
created, with B still empty and no entry ever created under it, may restart
from the ordinary guard; the verified empty B is an unambiguous infrastructure
state, not a prospective root or evidence. Failure before any entry under B
exists only blocks initial preparation; unsafe existing entries still fail
the ordinary guard and are never repaired or removed.

Create context.root with exclusive non-recursive mkdir(mode=0700); EEXIST
or any other mkdir failure is terminal, not permission to reuse a root.
After successful mkdir immediately verify/fsync as above and bind an
unforgeable in-process capability to its verified dev+inode (platform-stable
file identity), root path, prospective manifest SHA and fresh preparation nonce.
This capability lives ONLY in that process's volatile memory: never serialize,
restore, infer from matching bytes, or pass it to a new process to resume
preparation. No child inherits authority to establish it. Recheck the
capability and no-follow dev+inode/uid/mode at EVERY preparation guard and
before each publication; replacement/disappearance/recreation rejects.
The exception starts only after this exclusive creation/verification.
Its nonce is not evidence and is not included in canonical hashes.

Root-directory creation is the terminal boundary, even before a temp or final
file exists. Except for the content-verified ready-eleven/manifest-only states,
any subsequent failed/interrupted preparation, including a crash
after all bytes happen to match, requires abandon/reopen; a new process cannot
reestablish the exception or reuse the directory. Preserve it for diagnosis.
The exception ends after the complete closure is committed, verified and the
ordinary no-exclusion guard succeeds. Later official phase recovery may use
that successfully completed committed closure, never a preparation capability.

**Prospective preparation-root exception:** During this one uninterrupted,
capability-bound
mode=preparation operation, exactly context.root is excluded from stage-2
missing-manifest, missing-closure-destination and uncommitted-closure failures,
and from stage-3 committed graph membership while it is being built.
It remains subject to stage 1 and ALL other stage-2 checks. Bind its complete
independently prepared closure inventory/bytes before creating the root;
every final file already present must equal those exact expected bytes/hash,
otherwise report closure-byte-hash-mismatch. Temps never count as final files.
The prospective manifest and directory SHA must agree with that inventory.
Do NOT compare prospective predecessorFreeze in stage 2. First validate the
remaining committed graph fully in stage 3, then apply the final
prospective-predecessor-mismatch check below to the prepared manifestCore,
even before manifest.json exists. Stage-1 prospective temp ownership uses
the volatile root capability, not an assumed-valid predecessor binding.
Do not derive the expected predecessor or closure bytes from existing files
in context.root. Every other manifest-less/unfinished root is terminal.
Stage 3 validates the remaining committed roots normally; an empty remaining
graph is permitted only for the first prospective root. The prospective root
is never an active F for calls. Once its whole closure is committed, end the
preparation exception and run the ordinary all-root guard to select the new
tip before any official publication/call. An interruption loses the exception:
neither a new creation context nor mode=recovery may resume arbitrary file
preparation. The explicitly content-derived ready-eleven replay/manifest-only
finalization exception does not restore this creation capability. Read-only
consumer watchdog expiry leaves an incomplete phase; a write-window crash may
leave a terminal non-A/B/C snapshot, never permission to reuse partial preparation.

**Alias-safe publication temp recovery:** Ordinary use requires a committed
complete active tip with its independently bound intent/report/receipt context.
The sole precommit use is manifest-only finalization after A/B/C admission and
deterministic consumer success, restricted to manifest.json and B's temp.
Apply the exact ancestor/directory/file uid/mode and
no-follow rules above; existing repository ancestors are not required 0700,
but B and descendants are. If these properties cannot be established,
fail terminally rather than use a weaker platform fallback. Do not fix owner,
permissions or links in place to admit an otherwise invalid artifact.

Branch using no-follow destination metadata, with absence meaning ENOENT
only; other lookup errors reject. Revalidate metadata/identity against
opened descriptors and immediately before each destructive temp operation.

- **Destination exists:** NEVER open, write or truncate the temp. Inspect its
  name with no-follow metadata only. Open the destination no-follow, without
  truncation or content writes; require a regular file with expected ownership/
  mode, exact independently reconstructed bytes and expectedByteSha256.
  Require stable file identity across path metadata and descriptor checks.
  If temp and destination share the same device/inode (equivalent stable
  file ID on win32), require link count exactly 2 and that the two names are
  the verified temp and destination. If they are distinct, require each
  regular file to have link count exactly 1 and the expected owner/mode;
  this permits a separately created temp when a byte-identical destination
  already existed, never an unexplained additional alias. The temp supplies
  no content authority. Any identity/link/metadata anomaly rejects.
  Fsync the verified destination file and containing directory, unlink only
  the verified temp name after rechecking its identity, fsync the directory
  again, then reopen/rehash the destination and require unchanged identity,
  exact bytes and link count 1. No content or metadata repair of the published
  destination is permitted.
- **Destination absent:** Before ANY rewrite/truncation, lstat the temp with
  no-follow semantics and require a regular executor-owned mode-0600 file,
  link count exactly 1, no symlink and an approved parent directory.
  Open it with no-follow read/write semantics WITHOUT O_TRUNC; fstat must
  match the lstat identity/owner/mode and link count 1. Recheck destination
  absence and temp identity/link count before truncating through that verified
  descriptor. Only then write the independently reconstructed bytes, fsync,
  and verify them. Publish without replacement, directory-fsync, and
  reopen/rehash the destination. A destination appearing before truncate
  requires closing the temp descriptor without modification and restarting
  the destination-exists branch. No-replace EEXIST after writing also uses
  that branch; never overwrite the destination. After successful hard-link
  publication the temp may now alias the target: use the destination-exists
  branch to finish durability/unlink/rehash, NEVER rewrite the temp again.

All mismatch/link/owner/mode/no-follow failures are terminal
PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g8-freeze-lineage-binding (entry kind
temp-link-safety for temp metadata/alias violations); retain artifacts for
diagnosis. During normal publication apply the same no-follow/ownership and
no-replace checks. After target publication, remove ONLY the exact authorized
temp after target verification and file/directory durability, then fsync
removal and rehash the destination (with the existing explicit win32 directory
fsync limitation). No broad cleanup or renaming to another operation.
A second crash in ordinary committed phase publication is evaluated from
persisted names and identities again:
target absent permits only the verified single-link branch; target present
permits only the non-writing branch; target present/temp absent permits
reverification and completion of directory durability without creating a
new alias. Unprovable facts are terminal. No crash point authorizes mutation
of a published destination. UUID choice affects only the temp name, never
evidence identity or diagnostic ordering. Manifest-only restart instead FIRST
requires A/B/C: target-plus-temp at fresh entry is invalid, even though the
destination-exists branch may finish that transient within an already authorized
atomic publication. Never use ordinary phase recovery to bypass the classifier.

Capture control HEAD at scan start. A complete committed root has its canonical
manifest bytes hashed to its directory name and its entire required immutable
Git closure of exactly the twelve enumerated paths above, explicitly including
manifest.json AND preflight.json, present, verified and byte-identical to
tracked blobs at that HEAD. Verify the manifest's ordered closure descriptor
and recompute its full immutableClosureSha256, without excluding either file.
The growing calls/receipts/reports are separately validated persisted evidence,
not prerequisites for committing the original freeze closure. Require the
same repository/change/generation on all roots; cross-check every predecessor
root/hash/commit and approval-source link. A predecessor's pinned commit must
be a control HEAD ancestor containing its verified closure, using the exact
Git verification below rather than equality to current HEAD. Missing manifests,
uncommitted closure bytes or partially published roots are unfinished, not
candidates to ignore, except for the exact prospective preparation-root
exclusions above. Re-enumerate names, rehash manifests and recheck HEAD
before accepting the scan; any observed change fails instead of using a mixed
snapshot. This is a sole-writer, runner-free guard, not a shared lease held
across execution.

**Identifying commits and Git closure verification:** A committed tip must
have an identifying full commit object ID: the recorded predecessor commit
when validating that reference, or the captured HEAD as the witness for a
current tip not yet referenced by a successor. Resolve/verify the object as
a commit, require it is an ancestor of or equal to captured control HEAD,
and inspect its tree at EVERY one of the twelve enumerated immutable paths,
including F/manifest.json and F/preflight.json. Require normal
non-executable blob entries (Git mode 100644), not symlinks/gitlinks; extract
raw blob bytes and compare them byte-for-byte and by SHA-256 with the verified
manifest/closure bytes. Do not compare Git blob IDs directly to SHA-256 content
digests. Recompute the full ordered twelve-file aggregate from those Git blob
bytes and require equality to the independently verified live aggregate.
Verify the same closure at captured HEAD and require its index entries
and working-tree bytes match that committed tree; staged or unstaged changes,
missing/untracked closure files or executable-mode changes make the root
uncommitted/dirty and terminal. Unrelated working-tree changes and growing
call/receipt/report evidence outside the immutable closure do not invalidate
this test. Separately enforce live uid/0600/0700 rules, which Git cannot prove.
No identifying commit means no published committed tip. A recorded older
ancestor commit containing the exact closure remains valid after later
commits; never require its ID to equal HEAD or another equally valid witness.

Build the complete predecessor graph from the verified manifests. Require
exactly one genesis root (predecessorFreeze=null), one predecessor for each
other root, at most one successor per root, and exactly one tip. Every root
must be visited exactly once by following successors from genesis to that
tip; equivalently every root's successor path ends at the same F. The active F
is that unique committed/complete tip, not named as predecessorFreeze by ANY
other complete root. Reject competing tips/branches, orphaned-complete roots,
missing predecessors, cycles, ambiguous links or ANY unfinished root.
The sole matching-temp exception above does not change final-file completeness.
Zero committed roots is also permitted during uninterrupted first-root
preparation after excluding its sole prospective context.root. Otherwise
zero roots is permitted only before first-root preparation, never for F2
preparation or an official call/intent/receipt/recovery.

Compute lineageSha256=H of exactly
`{schemaVersion:1,kind:"change0017-g8-freeze-lineage-v1",
repositoryId,changeId:"CHANGE-0017",generation:8,
roots:[{root,manifestSha256,predecessorRoot,predecessorManifestSha256,
predecessorCommit,immutableClosureSha256}]}`.
roots is the complete genesis-to-tip sequence, not directory order;
the three predecessor fields are null only for genesis and otherwise equal
the manifest's predecessorFreeze fields. root is the exact repository-relative
path. Each immutableClosureSha256 is the verified full twelve-file aggregate,
computed from that root's exact manifest-bound list and its identifying commit
and live bytes; a mismatch rejects as closure-byte-hash-mismatch before
accepting lineage. Do not include current HEAD, intents, receipts or timestamps in this
digest: later commits and phase evidence must not change a fixed lineage.
The committed manifests and their twelve-file closures reconstruct every
digest input; it is not a transient
scan claim. Each intent and receipt contains activeFreezeRoot=F and this
lineageSha256 in addition to its matching manifestSha256. Require all existing
intents/receipts to have these exact bindings when verifying them.

Run this global guard before F2 preparation, before EVERY official phase call,
immediately before publishing EVERY intent or receipt, and before any recovery,
identical-byte reuse or republication, for ALL ordinals 1-27.
The publication guard runs before starting the atomic publication operation
(before its unique temporary file is created), not midway through that
operation's own uninterrupted writes.
For F2 preparation,
require no call intent/receipt anywhere under B, even under an ancestor root;
including calls/ temps, any such entry forbids supersession. For calls/publication/recovery require
the chosen F equals the computed tip, with no intent/receipt under ANY other
root and no persisted official g8 call attributable to a non-tip root.
Validate the chosen intent's bindings again before invoking its CLI call.
Never validate an older root in isolation or accept its once-valid digest
against an obsolete subset of roots. Once ordinal 1 exists, every later
operation must retain the same F and complete lineageSha256. No post-Red
supersession or rebaselining is permitted.

Any violation rejects terminally with
`PREFLIGHT_ASSERTION_FAILED:g8-freeze-lineage-binding`, including a call,
intent or receipt under a superseded/non-tip root, unexpected lineage digest,
any competing/unfinished root or an intent/receipt discovered during F2
preparation. Select the first violation using the exact precedence below and
report its stage, kind, offending root/path and observed/expected binding. Preserve all
roots and use the documented generation abandon/reopen protocol; do not delete
an offending root, complete/backfill an unfinished root at a guard boundary,
or choose another tip to continue. This diagnostic takes precedence over
approval-source-binding when the failure is lineage/active-root related.
It is a specified executor preflight diagnostic, not a claim of an existing
production CLI validator or a new member of the fixed 20 evaluator checks.
Publication's ordinary transient construction is not itself a phase call.
After interruption the global recovery guard admits only a committed complete
active tip with the single context-bound temp exception; it admits no unfinished
freeze closure. Earlier completion wording cannot bypass this guard. The
step-3 consumer replay uses its bounded ready-eleven/address guard instead
of this committed guard, including a freshly reverified process after an
incomplete watchdog/interruption. Only its bounded manifest-only finalization
may follow; no official call or arbitrary partial-file repair receives that
exception. Read-only consumer watchdog expiry leaves the phase incomplete;
write-window crashes remain subject to the portable publication crash boundary,
including terminal manifest-plus-temp snapshots at fresh entry.

**Global diagnostic precedence:** Collect facts without accepting a root or
executing semantic checks, then evaluate these stages in this exact order.
All path comparisons are ordinal UTF-8 byte comparisons, never locale or mtime.
Preliminary manifest/graph parsing needed to classify temp ownership does not
change precedence: if it cannot prove the temp exception, record an entry-stage
context failure rather than assuming a tip.
For step 3/seal/manifest-only recovery, the shared A/B/C classifier supplies
these same facts and exception decisions. B is the sole restarted precommit
temp exception; C verifies present manifest bytes without claiming a commit.
No caller-specific absent-manifest/no-temp rule may override this classifier.

1. **entry:** Entry/name/type/temp violations across ALL roots, ordered by
   `(rootPath,relativePath,kindRank)`. The fixed kind rank is unreadable-entry,
   forbidden-entry-type, invalid-root-name, unrecognized-entry, invalid-temp-name,
