The legacy Red stores sourceFingerprint, not a per-path config snapshot.
Absence of runtime config is an explicitly bounded INFERENCE from verified
legacy provenance-field absence, persisted pre-activation order and the closed
TEST set, together with all six conditions. Do not claim direct observation of
old config bytes. Git/worktree/config raw reconstruction is neither required
nor permitted as admission proof; never manufacture old snapshots or acks.
Missing any condition rejects phase-runtime-transition (without suppressing
existing chain/order/command errors). All requirements apply conjunctively.

Only the new Green testRuntime provenance adds an optional `activation`
object, present exactly for this transition:
`{schemaVersion:1,kind:"legacy-red-runtime-activation-v1",changeId,generation,
scopeId,cycleId,requirementId,testId,commandName,redOrder,redPhaseEvidenceSha256,
requirementsApprovalSha256,designApprovalSha256,requirementsCheckpointOrder,
designCheckpointOrder,redCheckpoint:{order,orderPhaseKey,journalRecordSha256,tddEvidenceSha256},
implementationCheckpoint:{order,orderPhaseKey,journalRecordSha256,tddEvidenceSha256}}`.
Its approval aliases refer to the existing approvalManifestSha256/artifactSha256,
and journalRecordSha256 refers to JournalRecord.recordSha256. Validate every
reference, not just hash syntax. The enclosing Green phase digest/hash-chain
and journal bind activation with all runtime blob references. No old phase,
checkpoint or approval schema is rewritten; this is admission metadata, not
new credit or human source approval. At execution validate existing predecessors;
at append recheck them and allocate Green's strictly later official order,
then validate the completed ordering. No predicted order becomes evidence.
This is an evidence schema extension, not a new policy JSON field/input.

Once active, the same descriptor/profile is required; disabling,
changing profile, unexpected augmentation, Green-to-Refactor transition, or an
absent-to-present change outside this single batch rejects. Schema-bound fresh
run IDs/anchors/locations and implementation input snapshots are observations,
not permission to change structural augmentation. All other TDD ordering,
frozen test fingerprints and unchanged native command checks remain mandatory.

This identity/transition implementation is itself fresh g8 TDD work, not a
pre-Red patch. EVIDENCE-001 and AGGREGATE-001 must assert it through existing
config/runner hooks: genuine collected failures under profile-absent old code,
then unchanged tests against profile-present implementation. Their fixtures
prove old/new logical hashes equal, phase-local legacy Red validation without
retroactive ack, complete Green provenance, equal canonical augmentation digest
across distinct absolute roots, and rejection of missing/unknown additions,
changed native selection/args and every unauthorized transition. Never accept
a test only because logical hashes match while its execution binding is absent
or altered. EVIDENCE-001 includes a positive legacy-schema Red plus complete
Green satisfying all six conditions, with no config snapshot. Independently
omit/tamper each conjunct: null/partial runtime fields or unknown schema;
missing/equal/reversed/foreign checkpoint orders; nonmember TEST ID; changed
logical hash; wrong/missing profile/blob/ack/augmentation; wrong approval SHA,
cycle/batch/change/generation/repository or chain binding. Each must reject.
A supplied raw-config/Git reconstruction cannot rescue rejection. Missing-module/
setup failures are not Red.

For a multi-invocation wrapper such as scripts/run-codegraph-tests.mjs, include
that wrapper in inputs and declare its ordered groups before dispatch. The
parent runner/coordinator exclusively writes dispatch.json beneath a fresh
command-run directory: `{schemaVersion:1,kind:"test-runtime-dispatch-v1",commandRunId,commandSha256,
profileSha256,inputsSha256,invocations:[{ordinal,runId,argv,selectedTestIds,
selectedFiles,executionBinding}]}`. executionBinding is the closed binding above;
for TDD, commandSha256 equals logicalCommandSha256. Each ordinal has a unique issued runId and immutable request;
use exactly one entry for an ordinary single Vitest execution. The wrapper
passes the corresponding request to each child, never one reusable request to
all groups. Reconcile every dispatched group with its native result and ack;
missing/extra groups reject rather than silently reducing coverage.

For every declared execution the command runner allocates a fresh unpredictable
runId and an exclusively created .musubix/cache/test-runtime/<runId>/ directory,
then passes its request (command name/argv hash, selected test/file identity,
profileSha256, inputsSha256, runId) through a scoped environment binding.
Configured argv/timeouts do not change; effective argv is composed above.
The one-use runner request is not inherited by
worker-spawned children; only the clock binding is. A nested Vitest execution
allocates its own request/run directory while retaining the incoming clock
anchor. anchor.runId identifies that clock's origin, not necessarily the
nested execution's runId. A direct Vitest invocation uses the same
coordinator protocol with a fresh standalone request but cannot masquerade as
a runner-issued command. These requests are execution metadata, not approvals.
The coordinator is the sole writer of the fixed relative `ack.json` path
in that run directory, using canonical JSON and atomic replace after each event.
For worker-to-coordinator transport, setup writes an exclusive per-worker/module
worker-acks/<UUID>.json packet in that run directory before evaluating the
test module; it never writes ack.json. Packets contain runId, requestSha256,
selected testPath and the worker entry below; workerId is the unique packet
UUID, with pool identifying the actual Vitest pool. Native reporter
onTestRunStart, onTestModuleQueued, onTestModuleCollected, onTestModuleStart,
onTestModuleEnd and onTestRunEnd events supply the
expected file inventory. The coordinator ingests packets, checks selection
and request/hash bindings, rejects duplicate file/realm registration and unsafe
paths/symlinks, and alone publishes aggregate ack.json. While a run is active,
a native 250 ms coordinator polling interval also ingests new packets and
publishes partial inventory, including during module evaluation; clear it on
completion. This does not patch timers or extend any command/test timeout.
These temporary packets
are transport observations, not independent evidence authority. A fresh
directory prevents old acknowledgment reuse; packet inputs and final aggregate
must agree at completed-run validation.

Closed `test-runtime-ack-v1` schema:
`{schemaVersion:1,kind:"test-runtime-ack-v1",runId,requestSha256,profileSha256,
inputsSha256,nodeVersion,platform,anchor,anchorSha256,workers,files,
workerSha256s,reporterRegistration,reportedFailed,bootstrapErrors,complete}`.
`reporterRegistration` contains reporterPath, requestSha256, observedProcess
{command,args} and observedVitestArgs. Record the actual Node executable and
argv; match Vitest args to the issued invocation after ONLY the declared local
npx/npm-script/platform launcher expansion, not arbitrary argument stripping.
Keep both launcher and child invocation identities. A differing test selection,
reporter/output path or extra flag fails acknowledgment-binding.
Startup diagnostics may have null anchor/anchorSha256 until anchoring finishes,
but cannot satisfy completed-run or timeout-only validation in that state.
`anchor` contains schemaVersion:1, kind:"test-runtime-anchor-v1", runId,
safe-integer wallEpochMs, finite monoEpochMs and
decimal-string hrtimeNs; anchorSha256 hashes its canonical bytes.
`workers` is sorted by registered workerId; each entry has workerId,
pool, testPath, inputsSha256, anchorSha256, all eight calibration samples (hrtimeBeforeNs,
performanceMs,hrtimeAfterNs), selectedIndex, and status `ready|error`.
`files` is the sorted selected-file inventory with path and state
`not-started|running|completed|failed|skipped`, initialized before dispatch and
updated from native collection/execution events. `reportedFailed` is the native
reported failed-test/file count; `bootstrapErrors` contains closed reason,
workerId (null for coordinator) and message. `complete` becomes true only after
native end-of-run inventory reconciliation, never because the process exited.
Unknown/malformed fields, duplicate workers/files, mismatched selected scope
and missing acknowledgments for started workers fail validation.
Every worker entry additionally requires the exact `observation` object from
the worker observation contract. It must agree with that worker's archived
provider/markerMetadata and workerSha256-linked packet.

#### Immutable runtime blob store and transport

The AUTHORITATIVE store is the selected journal-root/control worktree's
`.musubix/evidence/test-runtime/v1/blobs/<sha256>` (no filename extension).
Child, source-pair and detached roots only hold untrusted transport copies.
They cannot choose the authoritative root or append its evidence. The trusted
parent runner resolves control/journal root from the existing workspace
context, never from a child's environment or packet.
Each address is lowercase SHA-256 of canonicalBytes(object), including the
single LF; every object has schemaVersion:1 and the closed kind below.
No cache path is a durable reference. JSON bytes must already be canonical;
invalid UTF-8, unknown keys/kinds, wrong schema or filename/hash mismatch reject.
Validate the 64-lowercase-hex address before path construction and reject
symlink files/ancestors. Base64 fields must round-trip to canonical padded
base64, not merely decode permissively to the same bytes.

| Blob kind | Exact payload beyond schemaVersion/kind |
| --- | --- |
| stable-test-wall-clock-v1 | The exact approved top-level profile above; its address is profileSha256. |
| test-runtime-file-v1 | path, mode (100644 or 100755), size, rawSha256, contentBase64; decoded full raw file bytes must match size/rawSha256. |
| test-runtime-inputs-v1 | entries: path-sorted [{path,mode,size,rawSha256,blobSha256}]; exactly the 21 approved paths, each referencing a matching file blob; address is inputsSha256. |
| test-runtime-request-v1 | runId, commandRunId, commandName, origin (configured or standalone), context {repositoryId,changeId,generation,commit,role}, configuredInvocation {command,args}, effectiveInvocation {command,args}, executionBinding (the closed logical/augmentation/resolved binding above), selectedTestIds, selectedFiles, profileSha256, inputsSha256, dispatchSha256. Context uses explicit null for unavailable standalone fields, never an inferred CHANGE/commit. |
| test-runtime-anchor-v1 | runId, wallEpochMs, monoEpochMs, hrtimeNs as specified above; address is anchorSha256. |
| test-runtime-worker-v1 | runId, requestSha256, worker (the registered worker entry including observation), provider (StableWallClockProviderV1), markerMetadata (StableWallClockInstallV1 excluding installedNow); archive each packet separately, rehash observation references and compare its worker body with the aggregate worker entry. |
| test-runtime-dispatch-v1 | The pre-dispatch shape above; profile/input references plus ordered effective invocations, issued IDs and selections, never inferred successful groups. |
| test-runtime-ack-v1 | The closed ack shape above; workerSha256s is in workerId order and each digest resolves to the corresponding worker packet and matching run/request. Embedded anchor must equal its addressed anchor blob. |
| test-runtime-result-v1 | runId, requestSha256, effectiveInvocation {command,args}, executionBinding (observed values matching the issued binding), status, exitCode, durationMs, nativeReportBase64 (explicit null if the execution produced no native report); adapter-required reports cannot be null on accepted completion. Bytes and process outcome must match the existing runner's result, not values inferred from ack. |

The hash/byte identity for profile is exactly the pre-approved digest; do not
wrap it again. Input/worker/anchor/result objects each have their own hashes,
with the input inventory, ack and command outcome binding the transitive set.
Request context role is tdd, command, result, integration or standalone;
generation is a positive integer or explicit null, and commit is the existing
full Git object ID or explicit null. Standalone nulls never match an
authority-bearing context. Follow only the schema's declared hash references,
not hash-shaped strings inside source snapshots or reports.
After native termination, and BEFORE any child/detached/source-pair cleanup,
reset or removal, the parent runner reads the complete closure, rehashes and
schema/context-validates it, then publishes it to that control store. Validate
ack, file inventory, packets, input snapshots, effective invocation and native
process result; append journal/result references only AFTER publication.
Failure to read/publish before cleanup is blob-io and rejects, never a
success-shaped fallback. Preserve available failure diagnostics; do not
pretend deleted transport files were transferred. The same parent boundary
applies to isolated re-verification roots and integration attempts.
Archive partial timeout/error observations too, marked incomplete: they grant
no credit. An interruption leaving unreferenced blobs is not a terminal.

For publication, write canonical bytes to an exclusive (wx), private temporary
file in the blob directory, fully write and fsync it, then atomically publish
with a no-replace operation (e.g. hard-link the fully written file to its hash
name), perform the platform durability step below, and remove only the
writer's temporary name.
On EEXIST, reuse only after reading a regular non-symlink file and verifying
EXACT bytes/hash; never overwrite/repair a corrupt collision. Use the existing
supported durable filesystem primitives. On POSIX, both file fsync and
directory fsync are mandatory. On win32, match syncJournalDirectory's existing
platform contract: directory fsync is unavailable and explicitly NOT claimed;
require file flush, atomic no-replace publication and post-write rehash before
acceptance. Do not reject the existing Windows candidate matrix solely for
that documented absence. Failure of a required flush/no-replace/rehash is
blob-io. Record durability as posix-file-directory-fsync or
win32-file-flush-no-replace-rehash in the enclosing execution publication
observation, not inside the content-addressed blob, so platform does not
change the same content's hash.
The enclosing command testRuntime provenance adds publication
`{durability,closureSha256}`; closureSha256 hashes canonicalBytes of the sorted
unique reachable blob addresses, and the parent rechecks that entire set in
control before append. Transport observations never supply this confirmation.
References are appended through the existing journal-first evidence path only
after every required blob is durable. No shared CHANGE/projection/append lease
is held while runners execute. After a crash, partial temp files are never
accepted as blobs; exact complete objects may be reused without new credit.

Because this store is under .musubix/evidence/**, the existing evidence-input
exclusion keeps publication/transport out of source/test input fingerprints
and approval inputs. Command/evidence digests DO bind the blob references.
The store is never added to the runtime input inventory, avoiding self-hashes.
Before the new plan's clean-control requirement is evaluated, the control
writer commits published blobs AND their referencing journal/evidence together
with the authorized candidate base. Assignment commits still cannot write
.musubix/**: transport/publication is parent-controlled evidence work, not an
exception to assignment ownership. Later result/integration publications are
preserved by the control writer and committed at the official post-handoff
evidence persistence step, without advancing the frozen plan base early.
No new source ledger, source approval or source terminal is introduced.

At detached assignment submission, result verification, integration assembly
and handoff, transfer the full reachable closure of testRuntime references:
profile, dispatch, requests, inputs plus file snapshots, anchors, worker packets,
acks and results. Use the official evidence transfer path, with these blobs as
explicit dependencies, not ambient control-worktree reads or just Git commits.
The receiving parent publishes/reuses them in its authorized journal-root
control store under the SAME platform-specific no-replace rules and
rehashes every byte, schema and reference; check expected repository/change/
generation/commit/role/run selection against the enclosing command outcome.
Do not rebind results to the receiving root or new snapshot. Missing, tampered,
untransferred or foreign-context dependencies reject before result acceptance,
integration verification credit or handoff. A transfer manifest of sorted hashes
is not proof that its blobs arrived. Never silently fetch from the sender later.
Fresh verification executions create new request/ack/result identities;
transferring historical objects does not make them current verification.
Integration validation and handoff must resolve the entire closure in control,
not a soon-to-be-removed attempt root; missing transfer blocks acceptance.

For an ordinary source-pair executing a profiled command, the trusted parent
source runner prepares both independent variant requests and collects their
runtime closures before either pair root is removed. Publish both closures
to control first. Pair-local output inventories include canonical runtime
reference manifests (profile/input/dispatch/request/anchor/ack/result hashes),
so the existing source-pair report/output digest references bind those hashes.
Keep .musubix/evidence/test-runtime transport outputs explicitly outside the
pair's immutable inputs and do not require old/new run IDs or observations to
match; policy/input identity follows the existing declared pair semantics.
Archive and verify these manifests through the EXISTING source-pair output
contract: no new source terminal/approval fields, admission relaxation or
historical credit. If parent collection/publication fails, reject blob-io
before pair success/preparation is returned; retain the enclosing ordinary
source operational-failure behavior. Pair cleanup cannot discard required
blobs first. EVIDENCE-001 covers deleted pair roots after successful collection
and failed collection before cleanup.

After the runner reads and verifies these immutable objects,
persist optional command-provenance `testRuntime` with exact fields
`{kind:"stable-test-wall-clock-v1",profileSha256,inputsSha256,dispatchSha256,
runs:[{ordinal,runId,requestSha256,anchorSha256,acknowledgmentSha256,resultSha256}],
publication:{durability,closureSha256}}`.
The only additional optional member is activation with the exact closed shape
above, required only on a Green admitted by the legacy activation AND rule.
dispatchSha256 content-addresses dispatch.json; runs are in dispatch order,
with exactly one entry for a single invocation. DES-M5-011's TDD execution,
normal command result, parallel focused/result command outcome and integration
command outcome bind this same object in their existing journal-first
payload/digest path. Their validators resolve and rehash the immutable blobs;
acknowledgment cannot be substituted by a stdout success line. This extends
command provenance, not the ordinary source-supersession ledger.
For a new profiled phase whose runtime blobs bind its execution-time config,
Success/Green requires a complete valid acknowledgment and native passing
result for every dispatched invocation; genuine Red requires a complete valid
acknowledgment and the selected native failure. Apply provenance requirements
to that phase's config, never retroactively from Green's current config to
profile-absent Red. The exact serial activation transition above preserves the
old Red encoding through the closed six-condition inference, not an unavailable
config snapshot or manufactured runtime provenance. Partial acknowledgment after
timeout is diagnostic evidence only and cannot authorize Red/Green or credit.

Wire the same binding through focused native TDD, normal/compatibility test
commands, assignment focused checks, detached result checks, matrix and
integration verification. A normal command's unchanged argv hash alone is
not sufficient runtime evidence. Register the optional binding shape and
its digest participation under COMPAT-013 before enabling it; commands
without this test profile retain their legacy encoding/behavior.
TEST-M5-TEST-CLOCK-EVIDENCE-001 exercises config acceptance and the existing
runner through fixture commands: bind/reload each TDD/result/integration
outcome; mutate one input, request, anchor or worker ack; delete ack; reuse a
previous run's ack; and change the declared profile. Each mismatch must reject
before accepted evidence is appended. A command lacking testRuntime must retain
byte-identical legacy configuration projection/command encoding/digest.
Also delete each referenced blob kind, tamper payload/address, omit an input/
worker/result reference, and submit a valid manifest without transferring its
blobs. Check rejection in TDD, detached result verification and integration/
handoff; restore only exact original bytes and prove byte-identical reuse.
Verify existing approval projection identity with and without the approved
top-level instance, while the new gate fingerprint binds it. Reject effective
profile digest changes despite unchanged approval projection. Single/grouped
reporter composition belongs to TEST-M5-TEST-CLOCK-AGGREGATE-001.
The expected policy constant, normative design digest and effective config
must be identical; a deliberately changed constant/profile must fail the
regression without consulting a live approval record.
For a phase that declared the profile when executed, missing/tampered
bootstrap/anchor/ack cannot fall back to legacy. EVIDENCE-001 and AGGREGATE-001
also enforce the logical-hash equality, phase-local provenance, root-independent
augmentation digest and closed augmentation/activation rejection cases above.

Bootstrap errors fail the test command explicitly with
TEST_RUNTIME_BOOTSTRAP_INVALID and a closed reason:
missing-input, input-hash, unsafe-path, node-options, anchor-schema,
clock-domain, calibration, duplicate-conflict, worker-scope, acknowledgment-missing,
acknowledgment-schema, acknowledgment-stale, acknowledgment-binding,
profile-digest, reporter-missing, blob-missing, blob-schema, blob-hash,
blob-context, blob-io, augmentation-binding or phase-runtime-transition.
Check profile/digest before launch, reporter registration before workers,
and blob presence -> schema -> byte/hash -> context before evidence acceptance.
Acknowledgment checks use this precedence: missing, schema, run/request currency,
then content/anchor/worker binding. Never append accepted TDD/result/integration
evidence on these failures; retain actual failed execution observations.
Keep existing enclosing runner/CLI failure exits and no-passing-result rules;
do not map errors to passing tests or alter LEASE_FENCED/busy classification.
Record actual failures and preserve runner-free shared leases.

Existing development TDD uses transient workspace input capture/rechecks for
uncommitted implementation; it does not persist per-path config snapshots in
legacy phase records. New profiled phases persist the declared runtime input
blobs above. Before authoritative assignment/result/integration checks,
the bootstrap/config must be committed and match the selected candidate.
Package checks must prove these helpers/setup files are absent from dist,
package exports/bin and the npm tarball (the existing build includes only
packages and package files are allow-listed). No production module imports
the bootstrap. Type declarations for test tooling do not authorize shipping
the implementation. No new public runtime CLI or runtime source approval is
added; TRUST follows the read-only verification and fresh ordinary cycle described below.

All scripts/test-runtime inputs are .mjs with checked JSDoc and explicit .mjs
imports; no .d.ts or TS loader is permitted. packages/analysis/src/test-runtime.ts
is the typed command/blob coordinator and is covered by existing package
typecheck/build; it never imports the test clock at production module load.
Validate the three script files after implementation with node --check for each,
their actual Vitest/preload import regressions, and
`npx tsc --strict --allowJs --checkJs --noEmit --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --skipLibCheck scripts/test-runtime/stable-wall-clock.mjs scripts/test-runtime/vitest-setup.mjs scripts/test-runtime/coordinator-reporter.mjs`.
The ordinary tsconfig does not cover scripts, so ordinary typecheck alone
cannot claim script validation. These are targeted development checks, not
changes to configured command projection/timeouts. If checked-JS needs another
local file, STOP for explicit inventory/design revision rather than adding an
undeclared declaration. setupFiles uses its .mjs path as a string.
