Release manifests are computed from an immutable candidate Git tree. The
release approval record is stored outside that tree, and generated C4 renderings
are review aids rather than normative design inputs.

## DES-M5-023: Test-source supersession coordinator
Responsibilities: Own the explicit additive maintenance lifecycle, dedicated review/approval, current-snapshot synthetic proof, scoped admission, immutable source-terminal journal, prospective-ledger validation and idempotent recovery. Preserve all foundation checkpoint, finalization and concurrency obligations rather than treating this maintenance as a waiver or repair.
Interfaces: `prepareSourceReview(request, dependencies)`, `approveSourceReview(scope, artifactSha256, approver, confirm)`, `recordSourceSupersession(scope, artifactSha256, approvalSha256, dependencies)`, `resumeSourceSupersession(scope, requestSha256, dependencies)`, `replaySourceSupersession(scope, requestSha256)`, `captureSourceSnapshot(inputs)`, `spliceCanonicalTestBlock(node, currentFile, oldBlock)`, `verifySyntheticPair(snapshot, pair, runner)`, `deriveSourceRequestDigest(review, approval)`, `completeSourceSuffix(journal, liveLeases)`, `sourceSupersessionSummary(ledger)`. Implementation responsibility belongs to `packages/analysis/src/tdd-source-supersession.ts`; DES-M5-011 exposes it, DES-M5-002 supplies typed current approval/lifecycle/trace/runner/candidate evaluators, and DES-M5-007 owns pure schema and linkage validators.
Constraints: No general repair, adoption, waiver, force, skip-verification, direct projection editing, or historical chain regeneration option exists. Unknown/invalid pending data is never deleted or abandoned automatically. Admission requires current requirements/design approval; this proposed design is not authorization to execute the operation.
Requirements: REQ-M5-COMPAT-013 REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 REQ-M5-TDD-003
ADRs: ADR-0003 ADR-0023 ADR-0035 ADR-0036
Depends-On: DES-M5-003 DES-M5-004 DES-M5-007 DES-M5-TDD-005

### Source review and manifest boundary

New review/journal/projection records use canonical DES-M5-003 encoding,
schemaVersion 1, closed object keys and discriminated mode unions. Existing
TDD chain/order hashes retain their JSON.stringify encoding, with the exact
new chain field order specified below; historical bytes/hashes never change.
Hashes below are raw-byte SHA-256 unless explicitly identified as the
existing normalized test fingerprint. Store:

- Review: `.musubix/evidence/tdd-source/v1/<changeId>/g<generation>/<operationId>/artifact.json`,
  schema `tdd-source-review-v1`.
- Exact-hash approval: `.musubix/evidence/tdd-source/v1/<changeId>/g<generation>/<operationId>/approval.json`,
  schema `tdd-source-approval-v1`.
- Immutable content-addressed review inputs/reports:
  `.musubix/evidence/tdd-source/v1/blobs/<sha256>`; no extension, one verified
  content digest per filename. All prerequisite artifacts, old-block/hunk input
  copies, reports and blobs stay below this already evidence-excluded prefix.
  Do not place them in `.musubix/reviews` or introduce general path exclusions.
  Scratch roots are below the repository common Git directory at
  `musubix5/scratch/tdd-source/<operationKeySha256>/<invocationId>/old|new`,
  outside the scanned worktree, never an OS temporary directory.

`artifact.json` has exactly `schemaVersion:1`, `kind:"tdd-source-review"`, `changeId`, `operationId`, `scope`,
`mode`, `target`, `source`, `snapshot`, `reason`, `hunks`, `pair`, `replacement`,
`preparedAt`, `preparationInvocationId`, and `approvalContext`. `scope` has
exactly `repositoryId`, `changeId`, positive `generation`, `requirementId`,
`testId`, root-relative NFC POSIX `path`, `command`, `candidate`, `parallel`,
and `domain`. Top-level `changeId` equals `scope.changeId` and participates
in the canonical artifact hash, preserving DES-M5-006's closed release
ownership selector; a mismatch is review-schema. `parallel` is null for nonparallel or the exact
`planId/assignmentId/attempt/worktree/startCommit` tuple; `candidate` contains
the existing canonical candidate binding, not a new inferred identity.
`domain` is null iff domains are unconfigured. `target` has exactly `cycleId`,
`kind`, `order`, `payloadSha256`, `oldFingerprint`. Its identity is
`(cycleId, kind, order, payloadSha256)`, never fingerprint alone.
For CLI kind `green` or `refactor`, payloadSha256 is the exact unique matching
TddChainRecord.phaseEvidenceSha256 for that cycle and phase; for CLI kind
`migration`, match existing chain phase `migrate`. First verify it equals
SHA-256 of existing `JSON.stringify(cycle[phase])`, preserving its historical
property order and current algorithm, plus chain/order linkage; do not
canonicalize or rehash another subset. For kind `source-supersession`, it is
the new entry's phaseEvidenceSha256 over the canonical completed projection
defined below. Its `cycleId` is the effective original/replacement cycle.
Replacement redPayloadSha256/greenPayloadSha256 use the same existing
phaseEvidenceSha256 rule.
`source` contains exactly `nodeId`, `annotationStart`, `statementEnd`,
`currentFileSha256`, `newBlockSha256`, `oldBlockSha256`, `oldFingerprint`,
`newFingerprint`, `oldSourceDigest`, and `newSourceDigest`. Offsets are
zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets; compiler character offsets are converted before
splicing. Blob hashes cover raw file/block bytes; source digests are the
existing normalized authoritative block fingerprints, never whole-file hashes.
For behavior-change only, unavailable old raw block bytes/hash are null and
the old normalized source digest is the verified target fingerprint; no
whole historical file is falsely certified. `reason` is trimmed/nonblank.
`hunks` is the ordered array supplied by `--hunk-review`, each containing
`oldStart`, `oldLength`, `newStart`, `newLength`, `requirementIds`,
`assertion`, `threshold`, `failureSemantics`, `equivalenceRationale`, and
`supportingBlobSha256s`; coverage must match the actual block diff without
unreviewed hunks. It is empty for behavior-change. `approvalContext` fixes
current requirements/design manifest digests and owner domain at preparation.

`snapshot` contains exactly `manifestSha256`, `environmentSha256`,
`runnerSha256`, `configSha256`, `productionSha256`, `head`, and `stateSha256`.
The canonical manifest is `{schemaVersion:1, kind:"tdd-source-snapshot",
entries, excludedPaths, outputs, packages, runtime, environment}`. `entries` is sorted
by UTF-8 byte path, has unique NFC POSIX paths, and each item is exactly
`{path, mode, sha256, role}`. Start from the union of Git tracked paths
(`git ls-files -z --cached`) and untracked non-ignored paths
(`git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard`); include all readable regular
files, not only a guessed static import graph. Regular-file modes are `100644` or `100755`;
record absent tracked files as `{path, mode:"missing", sha256:null, role}`.
Unmerged index entries, NFC collisions, undecodable paths, escaping symlinks,
submodules or unreadable selected inputs reject `snapshot-unverifiable`.
In-root symlinks use mode `120000`, sha256 of their raw UTF-8 link-target
bytes, and include the resolved destination in the materialized closure;
cycles, dangling targets and out-of-root links reject snapshot-unverifiable.
Tracked ignored files are included unless explicitly classified as a declared
output below. Only these exact tree exclusions apply:
`.git` metadata, `.musubix/evidence/**`, `.musubix/cache/**`,
`.musubix/journal/**`, `.musubix/candidates/**`, `.musubix/trace/index.json`,
and `.musubix/features/*/trace.json`, plus the exact declared output roots
below. `excludedPaths` is the byte-sorted
fixed `{path, reason}` rule list using precisely those path patterns, with
reasons `git-metadata | evidence | cache | journal | candidate-metadata |
generated-trace | declared-output`; it is NOT an enumeration of files currently under excluded
directories. Thus publication of prerequisite evidence or unrelated journal
records does not change manifestSha256/stateSha256. Exclusions are input
metadata, not permission to consume pre-existing omitted data. A declared
output may be read only after this invocation creates it. No exclusion for arbitrary
reviews, logs, helpers, skills or config is invented.

Roles are `test | dependency | helper | runner | config | production |
environment`. The selected file has role test, the configured executable
runner, declared configuration files config, and lockfile-resolved installed
packages dependency; remaining repository files conservatively have role
production. Explicit helper/environment manifests may refine roles but never
remove entries. `productionSha256` hashes the canonical sorted entries with
role production or helper; `configSha256` hashes the configured command
definition plus all config entries; `runnerSha256` hashes the executable's
bytes, exact argv template, adapter identity and runtime object.

Ignored runtime inputs are not silently omitted: include materialized
node_modules, except the declared mutable cache roots, as separate entries in
the same manifest, enumerating every regular file and in-root symlink target with
byte/mode verification. The `packages` array fixes package-manager/version,
all workspace package.json and lockfile digests, installed package
name/version/path, lockfile integrity/resolution and the materialized tree
digest. Bind lockfile integrity/resolution metadata and verify the copied
installed tree against its captured hashes. This proves identity of the
current installed snapshot, not reconstruction or registry authentication of
that installation. No tarball cache, registry lookup or historical install
is prerequisite; missing required installed files fail snapshot-unverifiable.
Local workspace links are recreated only inside each isolated root.
Runtime fixes Node version, process.versions, platform/architecture, executable
digest and relevant OS/runner identity. Non-Node subprocesses need the same
executable/version binding. Do not install or fetch during the runs. Resolve
Node, npm CLI, TypeScript, Vitest and Git locally before preparation; use the
resolved executables, never an npx fallback that could download a package.

`outputs` is a closed ordered array of `{path, kind, producer, comparison}`.
For the SESSION runner declare `dist/**` as kind `build`, producer
`tests/global-setup.ts -> npm run build -> tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
comparison `pair-byte-equal`; `.musubix/cache/**`, `.test-work/**`,
`node_modules/.vite/**`, `node_modules/.vite-temp/**` and `.run-tmp/**` are
kind `ephemeral`, producer `selected-run`, comparison `inventory-only`.
The overlapping `.musubix/cache/**` exclusion retains reason `cache` (one
rule, not two); the other output roots use `declared-output`. No package
source, lockfile, runner, helper or config can be declared an output.
Each root starts without these outputs, including dist, and cannot fall back
to the original worktree's build/cache. The unchanged globalSetup rebuilds
dist independently with the copied local compiler. tsconfig.build.json
includes only packages, not the differing test block. After each complete selected run, the coordinator records that root's complete
dist inventory `{path, mode, sha256}`. Both post-run inventories must be
identical, nonempty and include the configured CLI entry. Use raw bytes/modes
and sorted relative paths, not mtimes or root-prefix normalization. Reject
missing, extra or unequal compiled outputs with pair-mismatch. No runner,
Vitest config, test, or globalSetup edit/suppression is used: the unchanged
configured runner invokes the unchanged globalSetup internally, starting from
an absent dist directory in each isolated root. The coordinator observes only
the runner process boundary, so it makes no unsupported claim about a
mid-run post-build state.
Ephemeral outputs may differ but are inventoried before/after, start empty,
cannot become another run's inputs, and cannot shadow dependencies.
Fresh musubix-json, Vitest and operation reports are ephemeral outputs under
`.musubix/cache/`; preserve their sanitized content-addressed copies even if
the runner removes intermediates. This permits SESSION's cache-local Git
fixture and globalSetup build without treating their expected writes as drift.

Environment is an exact sanitized allowlist of required runner variables,
timezone, locale and declared service/clock/randomness conditions; unspecified
ambient variables are removed. HOME, USERPROFILE, XDG_CONFIG_HOME,
XDG_CACHE_HOME, TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP resolve inside each root's `.run-tmp/`;
their logical values, not physical root prefixes, are hash inputs. PATH has
only declared local tool directories; clear NODE_PATH, ambient NODE_OPTIONS,
proxy/credential variables and inherited npm/Git configuration. Set
GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to a created empty run-local file;
set npm user/global config to created empty run-local files and offline mode.
These files have declared environment roles and stable verified bytes; their
containing temp root does not exempt them from input comparison.
Credentials and external mutable services
cannot be captured as proof: if required, reject snapshot-unverifiable.
`environmentSha256` hashes this canonical environment object.
`stateSha256 = SHA256(canonicalBytes({schemaVersion:1, head,
manifestSha256, environmentSha256, runnerSha256, configSha256,
productionSha256}))`. `head` is the exact current HEAD object ID; require it
unchanged from preparation through admission, including before/after each
run and immediately before append. Re-enumerate/hash the full input set so
creation, deletion, mode/content changes or ignored dependency mutation are
drift; independent evidence/journal/trace/scratch changes are not drift.
This is a current workspace snapshot, not a historical clean-commit demand.

Materialize two independent roots from verified blobs, preserving every
repository-relative path, executable mode, package.json boundary, workspace
link, node_modules layout, tsconfig/runner configuration and selected test
path. Run with cwd at each root and its copied runtime/argv resolution; no
symlink may point back to the mutable worktree. Bind logical report paths and
map physical root prefixes out of sanitized reports deterministically.
Only the selected block differs; pre/post input scans require all other
entries unchanged, with declared outputs checked by the rules above.
The guarantee is isolated roots, no links to mutable originals, sanitized
environment, and before/after declared input/output inventories, NOT OS
filesystem confinement or network isolation. Node subprocesses are not a
sandbox; manifests cannot detect arbitrary outside-root reads, transient
writes restored before scanning, or network traffic. Admission requires a
reviewed local-only runner/input declaration; known undeclared external input
or service dependencies reject snapshot-unverifiable. Do not claim that
absence of network traffic is proven by a passing pair or install-offline
settings. Stronger confinement is outside this contract. No historical runner
baseline is required.

For test-only, `pair` has `manifestSha256`, `oldReportSha256`,
`newReportSha256`, `oldRun`, `newRun`; `replacement` is null.
Pair manifest `tdd-source-pair-v1` fixes node/path, start, old/new statement
ends, old/new block blobs/digests, and shared prefix/suffix blobs, lengths and
digests. Run bindings contain invocation ID, selected test/command, start/end,
exit code, runner/config/environment digests, report hash, pre/post
source/production/input-manifest digests, and `outputs` containing
`beforeSha256`, `afterBuildSha256`, `afterSha256` of the declared output
inventories (`afterBuildSha256` covers build outputs only). Input comparisons
exclude declared outputs except the explicit environment files above.
Reports are fresh selected-only
musubix-json reports containing exactly this test with `passed`, exit 0, and
zero missing, skipped, error or unrelated results. They must be produced in
this preparation, never copied from TDD or another invocation.
For behavior-change, `pair` is null; `replacement` fixes `cycleId`,
`redOrder`, `redPayloadSha256`, `greenOrder`, `greenPayloadSha256` and the
matching Red/Green test fingerprint. A fresh selected-only passing run is
additionally required during record, not substituted for genuine failed Red.
Persist its sanitized musubix-json report and canonical run binding as
content-addressed blobs under `.musubix/evidence/tdd-source/v1/blobs/` before
journal append. Use O_EXCL, raw digest verification, file fsync and supported
directory fsync; an existing blob is reusable only on exact byte equality.
The journal's execution binding references these durable hashes. This
pre-journal prerequisite may remain after rejection/crash, gives no credit,
and is not a terminal/order/chain/projection write. Resume never reruns or
uses a mutable report path; missing/tampered blobs are invalid admission
evidence, not a fresh-report substitution.

Approval has exactly `schemaVersion:1`, `kind:"tdd-source-approval"`, `changeId`,
`operationId`, `scope`, `mode`, `target`, `artifactSha256`, `approver`,
`confirmed:true`, and `approvedAt`. Its top-level `changeId` equals
`scope.changeId` and the artifact's owner, and is covered by approvalSha256;
mismatch is approval-binding. Approver is nonblank after trim; `approve`
verifies the explicit artifact hash over canonical bytes and every referenced
blob digest. Preparation is not approval. The same exact bytes/actor replay
reuse the approval; changed bytes, binding or actor require a new operation,
not an overwrite. Both modes retain an auditable actor; test-only specifically
requires this dedicated exact-hash semantic review in addition to general
approvals. Reports fixed by that approval cannot be substituted later.

DES-M5-006 keeps `approval-normative-path-set-v1` unchanged: these dedicated
artifact/blob and evidence paths are not requirements/design normative paths.
The exclusion boundary is only the exact regular-file v1 artifact/approval
patterns above and digest-verified blobs referenced by valid v1 artifacts;
no general `.musubix/**`, feature, decision, CHANGE or specification exclusion
is added. Reject symlink ancestors, path traversal, schema/path mismatches and
unknown versions. Do not copy review content into CHANGE, requirements,
design, ADR or constitution. Dedicated creation/approval changes neither
general manifest hash nor its current judgment. Conversely a later general
approval never rewrites source approval: its integrity remains hash-bound,
while the ordinary general-approval cascade still independently applies.
This boundary does not add a release-manifest exclusion. Test exact hashes
before/after dedicated creation and general reapproval, plus tamper rejection.
The existing `.musubix/evidence` input exclusion also makes prepare/approve
neutral to Green/Refactor sourceFingerprint, quality input fingerprints and
candidate/gate input fingerprints; candidate commit identity itself is not
changed by these operations. Required fixtures compare each fingerprint
before/after prepare/approve/blob/report creation, and prove these writes
alone cannot satisfy the Red-to-Green implementation-change guard. This does
not exempt completed tdd.json projections from consumers explicitly hashing
TDD evidence, nor exclude committed source evidence from release manifests.

### Writer lease migration and preparation concurrency

DES-M5-004 supplies one `withTddWriteLeaseSet(scope, callback)` primitive,
composed by DES-M5-011 and DES-M5-023. Migrate every writer/replacer of
`.musubix/evidence/tdd.json`, not just the new command: Red/Green/Refactor,
algorithm migration, void, repair record/resume/abandon-pending, source
record/resume, legacy ownership-adoption writes, and import/materialization
or recovery paths that replace that ledger. Read-only validation/status never
acquires this set. No writer may retain a pre-run ledger object for final
write; reload, recheck target/request/conflicts and merge under the set.

For an active explicit or implicit CHANGE, identity is the existing
repository-common named CHANGE lease for its actual changeId; for existing
maintenance with no active CHANGE (including the selected-null-generation
maintenance exception), use the repository-common named `tdd-maintenance`
lease, not a fictitious active CHANGE or ownership adoption. Then acquire
the existing repository-common `change-projection` lease, then its append
session. Multi-CHANGE materialization retains its byte-sorted CHANGE set,
then projection/append and passes handles; helpers never reacquire. All
tdd.json writers share projection exclusion even when one is no-active
maintenance and another has an active CHANGE. Recheck active-selection
stability under projection; scope drift rejects before any requested write.
Existing no-active maintenance target selection and error precedence remain.

Long configured runs hold NONE of CHANGE, maintenance, projection or append.
Prepare expensive input hashes outside leases. In a short CHANGE (or existing
no-active maintenance) -> projection -> append critical section reload and
check scope, approvals, pending conflicts and target/predecessor identity;
capture a comparison token and persist only the ordinary command's required
pre-run intent, if any. Release the complete set before starting the runner.
After execution and outside-lock hashing, reacquire that order, reload the
latest ledger, recheck the actual active generation, approval hashes, relevant
source/input digests, target/predecessor and conflicts, then append/merge.
No stale pre-run ledger object is written back. Unrelated chain-tail/order
advances are merged, not compared as target drift. Changed same-test state
rejects with the existing normal-writer guard or source input-drift before
requested terminal persistence; generation loss uses CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE.
Crash before source journal append leaves at most prerequisite blobs and
ordinary pre-run intent, never a source terminal or reserved evidence order.
Optimistic target revalidation is sufficient: no per-test lease is introduced.
If two same-test executions race, only one still-current commit can win.
Existing pending-repair/integrity guards still apply. The shared-writer
migration must be integrated before enabling any additive source writer;
every write site, including supplied-handle materialization, is covered.

All these leases use 30s TTL, 10s renewal, 25ms retry, 10s acquisition timeout
and live owner/counter fencing before every persistence boundary. Lease
acquisition/fencing is a common primitive; diagnostic mapping belongs to
each writer's existing facade, not the primitive:

| Writer/context | CHANGE timeout | Projection timeout | Append timeout | Lease loss |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New source-supersession commands | CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY | CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY | TDD_SOURCE_LEASE_BUSY / append-timeout | LEASE_FENCED |
| Existing candidate TDD/maintenance, outside the approved lifecycle/finalization exceptions | CANDIDATE_LEASE_BUSY | CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY | CANDIDATE_JOURNAL_BUSY | CANDIDATE_STATE_OWNERSHIP |
| Enumerated lifecycle/checkpoint and finalization writers | Existing REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-006 / ADR-0026 mapping | CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY | Existing mapping | LEASE_FENCED |
| Other existing ordinary/no-active TDD maintenance | CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY | CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY | TDD_EVIDENCE_LEASE_BUSY | LEASE_FENCED |

All named mappings above are registered exit 1 domain diagnostics. The
ordinary/no-active migration adds `TDD_EVIDENCE_LEASE_BUSY` only for repository
append-lease acquisition timeout; CHANGE and projection acquisition use
`CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY`, and loss of any held handle uses
`LEASE_FENCED`. It does not introduce `TDD_SOURCE_LEASE_BUSY` on an old public
command. No source operation is permitted in no-active scope.
The source lease-busy reason enum is only `append-timeout`. Preserve existing
argument/domain guard precedence and ordinary messages/exits; migration is
not permission to change candidate ownership diagnostics.
Snapshot scans and compiler/diff work stay outside the handles. Locked
rechecks use prepared per-path hashes plus changed-path revalidation as in
DES-M5-022, yielding during necessary I/O so renewal cannot be starved.

Prepare and approve use the same short CHANGE -> projection -> append
sections for reload/recheck/publication; neither holds a shared lease during
snapshot construction, pair execution or report hashing. Recheck the frozen
input token and current target immediately before publication; approve
repeats hash and snapshot/target checks without a new run. Publish artifact and approval by create-only
O_EXCL staging plus atomic no-clobber publication, file fsync and supported
directory fsync. An existing identical artifact/approval returns its stored
timestamp, never regenerates it; divergence uses request-mismatch or
approval-binding/actor-mismatch. Blob creation uses O_EXCL and verifies an
existing content address. Concurrent same-CHANGE preparation/approval
serializes only publication; same-CHANGE runs, other batch checkpoints and
parallel transitions remain viable during a runner lasting over 10 seconds.

### Target admission and mechanical test-only review

Resolve the explicit active CHANGE/generation and requirement within its
fixed Requirements set. With no configured domains accept domain null;
otherwise resolve exactly one configured requirement owner and its current
requirements/design approvals. Reject missing/stale/wrong-domain approvals,
ambiguous ownership, foreign/prior-generation/legacy-unscoped targets, stale
or unconsumed parallel provenance and candidate-lineage mismatch. Compare
all parallel tuple members exactly; null/null nonparallel is valid, including
the SESSION motivating cycle. Do not silently invoke stale-parallel repair
or promote provisional provenance into release/cleanup credit.

Resolve exactly one current trace node and path and its deterministic test
statement. The authoritative slice starts at the beginning of its `@id` line
and ends at the existing statement-selection rule's target statement end.
No whole-file or next-annotation fallback is allowed when statement resolution
fails. New source fingerprint must differ from the target old fingerprint.
Verify linked valid Red and passing Green with Red order strictly before
Green and unique payload/chain/order linkage; reject voided/retired targets,
existing successors and conflicting pending work. For test-only the target
is the current selected terminal in the operation scope. For behavior-change,
it is the selected old terminal immediately before replacement Red; separately
require that the specified replacement is the current authoritative cycle.

For test-only splice supplied old block into the current file at that unique
boundary. Verify syntax, same `@id` and trace identity, exactly one target
statement, and that its end equals inserted-block end. Verify old source by
`testFingerprintFromText(currentNode, splicedText)` equaling the terminal
fingerprint, retaining existing CRLF/CR-to-LF normalization and trim only for
that fingerprint. A hash of supplied bytes alone is insufficient. Synthetic
old/new files share exactly the same raw prefix and suffix (length movement
of the suffix is allowed), and all other snapshot entries are identical.
Raw byte comparisons never normalize whitespace/newlines outside the block.
For review hunks, split raw block bytes into LF-terminated lines retaining
terminators and a final unterminated line; compute a minimum insertion/deletion
edit script by longest common subsequence, taking deletion before insertion
on ties. Coalesce adjacent edits with zero context into ordered hunks;
oldStart/newStart are zero-based line offsets and lengths count raw lines.
The submitted hunk list must exactly equal generated coordinates and cover
every edit. This diff never normalizes bytes; only the persisted fingerprint
uses CRLF/CR-to-LF plus trim.

Mechanical AST checks use the locked TypeScript parser version and the
existing node/statement boundary rule. Compare preorder token-kind/text
streams (excluding trivia) for the annotation IDs/requirement links,
registration callee/modifier chain, test title and command binding. Preserve
the ordered count and structure of every assertion call: expect or imported
assert binding, subject expression, matcher chain/modifiers and all matcher
arguments must be identical, including literal thresholds and message/failure
options, except the following bounded elapsed-clock substitution. Permit
only a paired change from `const started = Date.now()` and
`expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(10_000)` to
`const started = performance.now()` and
`expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(10_000)` (or the same
unchanged local identifier), matching the actual SESSION assertion shape.
Verify the identifier has exactly that unmodified initializer, no intervening
assignment, and the elapsed subject preserves subtraction operands/order,
millisecond units, matcher and literal duration limit. Both clock bindings
must resolve to the standard APIs with no alias, shadow or mock affecting
the measured interval. This exception changes only those two clock call
nodes, not assertion count, other subject nodes, control flow, expiry
assertions or block-local mocks. It still requires explicit human review of
wall-clock jumps, monotonic elapsed meaning and unchanged failure criteria;
the syntactic exception alone does not approve equivalence.
Changes to an expression referenced indirectly by an assertion
remain in the hunk review; equality of assert call syntax is not semantic
proof. Reject new or changed skip/only/todo/fails modifiers, fewer assertions,
dynamic assertion dispatch/aliasing that cannot be resolved, and any changed
block-local mock/spy/stub call or declaration (vi/jest mock, spyOn, fn,
mockImplementation/ReturnValue/ResolvedValue, sinon stubs, or aliases of
those APIs). Existing unchanged such constructs are not newly authorized.
Reject assertion guard/control-flow removals or newly conditional assertion
execution by comparing each assertion's enclosing control-flow AST ancestry.
Mechanical rejection uses `behavior-change-required` (invalid parsing or
identity/boundary uses splice-invalid); no approver can override it.
Human hunk attestation is separately mandatory for data-flow/elapsed-clock
semantics and failure equivalence that these syntactic checks cannot prove.
Unchanged `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(threshold)` can also preserve assertion
syntax while its data source changes; it needs the same semantic review,
not automatic approval. Changed expiry assertions or thresholds leave test-only.
Use the same admission-time current production/dependency snapshot, runner,
config and environment for two isolated fresh selected runs; require both
pass and zero declared production/input mutation before/after each run, plus
the measurable rebuilt-output equivalence above. Production zero-diff is
between these runs, not against historical Refactor production.
Historical commit/stash/helper reconstruction is not a prerequisite.

Reject test-only for any required/actual outside-block hook/mock/import/helper
change, runner/config difference within the pair, relaxed threshold, deleted
assertion, added skip, altered test/requirement/command identity, failure-hiding
mock, production behavior difference or unconfirmed equivalence. Approval or
both-pass observation alone cannot override these checks. Hunk review binds
unchanged requirement/assertion/threshold/failure semantics. SESSION can qualify only after its block is restored to the recorded Refactor
shape except for the paired elapsed `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`
substitution. The current `vi` import, Date clock spy, try/finally, replacement
expiry assertion, and added expectations are not part of that test-only
supersession and must be removed first. The stronger renewal-clock assertion is
out of scope for CHANGE-0017 because the current implementation already
satisfies it and its first execution would pass. A passing first execution is
not a Red and must never be recorded as one; any future assertion-only
regression coverage is non-credit unless a separately approved behavior change
provides a genuine failing Red. Wall-clock jump rationale remains separate
review evidence. An old block fingerprint match does not authorize
outside-block changes.

Behavior-change links a separately completed, current authoritative
replacement cycle with matching test, requirement, CHANGE generation,
command and candidate lineage, real observed failed Red and same-fingerprint
passing Green plus ordinary implementation checkpoints. It never relabels
old Green, intentionally breaks production for fake Red, relaxes tests for
Green, or changes tests after Red. Missing reconstruction or equivalence sends
the operator to normal requirements/design/TDD, not synthetic Red.

Revalidate source, entire input snapshot, approvals, HEAD/state, active scope
and selected target before/after runs and immediately before journal append.
For test-only these must match the approved preparation bytes; drift requires
new preparation and approval. All pre-journal rejections write zero requested
terminal/order/chain/projection records; already created dedicated review/
approval prerequisites and cache/lease metadata are not rolled back.

### Journal, order and recovery

Normal journal envelope uses exactly the DES-M5-004 canonical schemaVersion 1
fields `order`, `stream:"normal"`, `changeId`,
`kind:"tdd-source-supersession"`, `idempotencyKey`, `payload`,
`previousSha256`, `recordSha256`, plus `schemaVersion`.
The schema is `tdd-source-supersession-v1`; the exact key is
`tdd-source-supersession:<changeId>:g<generation>:<operationId>`.
`payload` has exactly `schemaVersion:1`, `operationId`, `requestSha256`,
`mode`, `scope`, `target`, `newFingerprint`, `reviewSha256`,
`approvalSha256`, `source`, `snapshot`, `pair`, `replacement`, `reason`,
`approver`, `execution`, `recordedAt`, and `fencing`.
The referenced source/snapshot/pair/replacement structures are the sealed
review values, not retry-time reconstructions. `execution` is null for
test-only (both preparation runs are in pair), or the fresh record-time
behavior-change run binding. `fencing` has positive CHANGE/projection/append
tokens for audit only. `requestSha256` hashes canonical
`{schemaVersion:1, operationId, scope, mode, target, artifactSha256, approvalSha256}`;
artifact/approval hashes transitively bind all source, reports, snapshot,
reason and actor. Generated recordedAt, journal order, fences and the fresh
behavior-change run are journal authority, not caller replay overrides.

The first durable journal append is the intent, deriving state `pending`.
Acquire CHANGE then repository change-projection then append lease; use
30-second TTL, renewal each 10 seconds, 25ms retry and 10-second acquisition
timeout. All acquired handles are renewed; all persistence boundaries check
owner and durable fencing counter. Record fsync is required, directory fsync
only where supported, and atomic replacement follows ADR-0003. No terminal,
evidence order, chain or TDD projection is written before the complete journal.
The journal envelope's own order is not the later evidence order.

The only durable completion suffix is: (1) exact operation evidence-order
append, (2) one atomic replacement of `.musubix/evidence/tdd.json` containing
BOTH the appended `evidence.chain` entry and `sourceSupersessions[]` entry.
They are in the same file and never separately persisted. Chain/projection
construction and validation happen in memory before that single rename.
Order identity is `kind:"tdd"`, `entityId:<operationId>`,
`phase:"g<generation>:source-supersession:<changeId>"`, `testId:<testId>`;
its operation key is the full journal idempotency key, not operationId alone.
Under append lease, reuse the sequence of the single exact valid matching
entry; with zero entries choose the current valid maximum plus one, never
cardinality, wall-clock or a reservation made before journal append.
Multiple matches, wrong payload/test/key or any invalid order fail closed.
Extend `tdd.json` additively with optional `sourceSupersessions[]` (absent is
empty for historical ledgers). Each canonical completed projection P has
exactly `schemaVersion:1`, `operationId`, `operationKey`, `requestSha256`,
`journalSha256`, `journalOrder`, `order`, `cycleId`, `scope`, `mode`, `target`,
`newFingerprint`, `recordedAt`, `reviewSha256`, `approvalSha256`,
`state:"completed"`. P deliberately contains no chain hash, terminal digest
or self-reference. Define D = SHA256(canonicalBytes(P)); this is terminal-(d)
payloadSha256 and the matching chain phaseEvidenceSha256. Effective cycleId
is original for test-only, replacement for behavior-change. Pending is
derived from the journal, not a completed projection.

The chain entry is a typed extension of existing TddChainRecord, not a new
parallel chain format. Add `source-supersession` to TddChainPhase and an
operation-key-bearing discriminated member. Its exact keys and construction
order are `sequence`, `cycleId`, `changeId`, `generation`, optional `binding`,
`requirementId`, `testId`, `testPath`, `commandName`, optional `parallel`,
`phase:"source-supersession"`, `operationKey`, `phaseEvidenceSha256:D`,
`previousSha256`, followed by `recordSha256`. Binding/parallel fields are
copied exactly from the effective cycle and omitted, not null, when absent.
Other identity fields equal P.scope and its effective cycle. It has no
schemaVersion/order/request/target fields outside the existing shape plus
operationKey; those are transitively bound through D. Schema designation
`tdd-source-terminal-v1` refers to this discriminated member and P together.
Retain existing `chainRecordSha256` = SHA256(JSON.stringify(payload excluding
recordSha256)), using the specified insertion order and no trailing LF.
Do not switch legacy hash encoding or reserialize historical entries.
Chain sequence is previous tail sequence+1 (1 for empty) and previousSha256
is its record hash/null. Its sequence is not evidence order: resume reuses an
old operation order while appending to the latest chain tail.

All typed loaders, chain validators, orphan checks, effective-currency
indexes, repair preflight/prospective validators and order-linkage consumers
in DES-M5-007/011/TDD-005 must recognize this member before it can be written.
Existing chain dedupe key remains cycleId:phase for all old phases; the new
member alone uses `source-supersession:<operationKey>`. Consume it through
exactly one P with matching operation key, D, scope/cycle identity and exactly
one journal/order link before orphan detection. Multiple source terminals on
one cycle are thus legal only with distinct operation identities and the
valid successor graph. A to B to A remains valid; duplicate operation, identity
self/cycle/branch, unknown phase or unmatched completed entry is invalid.
Existing phaseEvidenceSha256 checks remain unchanged for all legacy phases.
Evidence-order loaders retain their established shape/JSON.stringify hash;
extend accepted `testId` applicability to this exact source phase and verify
it plus the derived kind/entityId/phase identity against the journal.

Before legacy orphan/repair-pending checks, the shared read-only classifier
validates source journals and joins existing suffixes. A valid journal with
no order/P/chain, or with exactly its order but no P/chain, is scoped pending,
not TDD_CHAIN_ORPHAN, missing legacy phase or global invalid ledger. Such an
order is accounted for by its journal, not consumed as Red/Green evidence.
Only same-test conflicts then block; unrelated writers can extend the ledger.
Any chain-only or P-only on-disk state is corruption, not a supported crash
prefix, and cannot be repaired by inventing the missing half.

Result has exactly
`schemaVersion:1`, `operationId`, `requestSha256`, `state:"completed"`,
`scope`, `mode`, `target`, `cycleId`, `newFingerprint`, `journalOrder`,
`order`, `terminalSha256`, `artifactSha256`, `approvalSha256`, `recordedAt`;
`terminalSha256` is D (chain phaseEvidenceSha256), not the chain recordSha256.
Completed replay reconstructs byte-identically from persisted values.

Validate the prospective ledger containing journal, every partial fragment
and resolved/proposed order before writing any missing suffix. Partial data
must be one of the two valid incomplete states above; no reordering, overwrite, chain
regeneration or duplicate linkage is recovery. Chain predecessor is the
actual current verified tail, retaining unrelated appends. On resume acquire
fresh live fences, reread latest TDD projection and merge only this suffix,
preserving nonconflicting writers. A persisted old fencing token never
authorizes current writes. Completed exact record/resume/replay returns the
same result with zero appends only in the current active generation;
divergent request-key reuse fails closed.
Record encountering its exact pending key requires explicit resume; it does
not silently recover. Resume reuses all journaled timestamps/reports/approval/
target values, even when current source/approval has since changed within
that still-active generation; finish persisted admission and report current currency/general-approval failures
separately. Unknown operations and corrupt/branched/duplicated fragments are
never deleted, waived or guessed. Crashes after projection but before response
return the same completed result on replay.
Crash points are before/after journal fsync, before/after order append,
before/after staging tdd.json fsync, before/after atomic rename and before
success response. Before journal there is no operation record. After journal
and before order there is journal-only pending; after order and before rename
there is journal+order pending; after rename both chain and P are completed.
Staging leftovers are not ledger inputs and can be removed after verifying
the actual target; they never represent a persisted chain-only phase.

Successor graph nodes are full terminal identities. Every old identity has
at most one successor; new identity may not equal old or create any cycle or
branch. Replay adds no edge. Distinct identities and separately approved
operations permit A to B to A fingerprints. Existing cycle/phase/order/chain
bytes and journal files remain immutable; only append-only suffixes and the
derived additive projection change. Generation-4 order 3274 stays historical
non-credit; workflowWaivers stays empty and stale waivers stay inactive.

### Evidence digests, batch and quality currency

DES-M5-022 extends its selected `tddEvidenceSha256` input additively: retain
the existing selected cycles and chain ordering/encoding, include verified
source-supersession chain members for those cycles, and add
`sourceSupersessions` containing their canonical completed P entries sorted
by operationKey (UTF-8 byte order). A projection is relevant if its target OR
effective cycle belongs to the selected CHANGE/generation/requirement set;
include both endpoint cycles and their required linkage before validation.
Omit this new property when no relevant P exists, preserving old digests
exactly. Source journals, pending prefixes and review/approval/blob creation
alone do not change this digest; their independent integrity/pending guards
still apply. Never strip source chain members to preserve a stale hash.
Invalid linkage prevents a fingerprint result; it is not ignored as irrelevant.
Preparation and locked recheck use this identical selection function.

Completion changes the relevant TDD digest exactly once; replay does not.
An in-flight batch prepared against the old digest rejects CHANGE_WORKSPACE_DRIFT
without a requested checkpoint. Previously persisted checkpoint payloads
and their tddEvidenceSha256 remain immutable admission snapshots, not mutable
post-hoc hashes. Their replay uses the saved payload. Source completion grants
no new Red/Green, no batch checkpoint, and no quality credit. Current batch
Green must still pass ordinary approval/order/source/implementation/TDD
currency predicates: source supersession can clear the test-source predicate
only, not waive a changed batch fingerprint or the requirements/design cascade.
Any invalidated batch must be re-recorded through its existing supersession
identity using actual verification; retained valid cycles are counted once.

DES-M5-015's TDD evidence currency includes the same verified P/chain content
for its evaluated scope. Thus completion stales quality evidence bound to
the previous TDD digest even if test-only coverage count is unchanged;
recompute the normal quality evidence and full-set quality checkpoint after
all required batch Greens are current. Review artifacts remain source-input
neutral, but this completed-ledger dependency is not excluded. Unrelated
scopes do not stale a scoped batch/quality digest; global integrity still
fails closed. No historical quality hash or Green checkpoint is rewritten.

For SESSION specifically, verified test-only completion selecting (d) with
the current block fingerprint clears only its TDD_TEST_STALE source blocker,
not all concurrency/readiness blockers. Require the fresh selected passing
run, current affected batch evidence, rerun concurrency evidence on the
current inputs, and renewed quality after the cascade. Pending, approval
alone, a digest edit, or legacy order 3274 cannot clear that blocker. Exact
replay leaves all currency hashes unchanged; later block drift restores stale.

### Diagnostics, precedence and read-only projections

DES-M5-002 supplies exit-2 usage validation first. Then every source command,
including resume/replay and completed matches, resolves its explicitly selected
current active generation before lease acquisition or replay lookup; an
abandoned/superseded/inactive generation rejects exit 1 CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE
without persistence, per REQ-M5-LIFECYCLE-005. Next the source-aware
integrity classifier recognizes exactly the valid journal-backed prefixes
above, then runs existing global ledger-integrity and repair-pending guards
with their existing diagnostics and mutual precedence unchanged. Recognizing
a new typed member is not bypassing a real defect; malformed source data
fails as TDD_SOURCE_LEDGER_INVALID. No valid scoped prefix becomes a legacy
orphan or global pending. The new typed diagnostic code/reason enums are closed:

| Code (exit 1) | Closed `details.reason` values |
| --- | --- |
| `TDD_SOURCE_LEDGER_INVALID` | `scope-unreadable`, `journal-schema`, `journal-chain`, `order-invalid`, `order-multiple`, `chain-linkage`, `projection-mismatch`, `successor-self`, `successor-cycle`, `successor-branch` |
| `TDD_SOURCE_PENDING` | `same-test-writer`, `explicit-target-conflict`, `resume-required`, `completion-required` |
| `TDD_SOURCE_REPLAY_INVALID` | `unknown-operation`, `request-mismatch`, `not-completed` |
| `TDD_SOURCE_ADMISSION_INVALID` | `inactive-generation`, `foreign-target`, `requirement-outside-scope`, `ownership-ambiguous`, `general-approval-missing`, `general-approval-stale`, `domain-mismatch`, `candidate-mismatch`, `parallel-tuple-mismatch`, `parallel-stale`, `parallel-unconsumed`, `target-missing`, `target-not-selected`, `old-fingerprint-mismatch`, `unchanged-fingerprint`, `target-retired`, `successor-exists`, `trace-ambiguous`, `boundary-unresolved`, `splice-invalid`, `outside-block-diff`, `snapshot-unverifiable`, `input-drift`, `pair-mismatch`, `report-invalid`, `report-not-fresh`, `selected-run-failed`, `equivalence-unconfirmed`, `behavior-change-required`, `replacement-invalid` |
| `TDD_SOURCE_APPROVAL_INVALID` | `review-missing`, `review-schema`, `review-hash`, `blob-hash`, `approval-missing`, `approval-schema`, `approval-hash`, `approval-binding`, `actor-mismatch` |

Operational failures use exit 2 `TDD_SOURCE_IO_FAILED`, closed reasons
`read | execute | fsync | atomic-replace | append`, retaining baseline
unexpected-I/O behavior. Execution launch/timeout/transport failures are
operational; a successfully executed runner reporting test failure is the
exit-1 admission `selected-run-failed`. No operational failure is converted
to pass, pending success or an ordinary negative domain result. All other
table rows are exit 1.

For the new source commands, shared lease failure codes are exit-1 `LEASE_FENCED` and
`CHANGE_PROJECTION_LEASE_BUSY` (CHANGE/projection acquisition timeout for
this coordinator only); append acquisition
timeout is exit-1 `TDD_SOURCE_LEASE_BUSY`, reason
`append-timeout`. Existing migrated writers retain the context-specific
mapping table above, including protected candidate diagnostics. They describe the actual
failed lease and cannot be converted into success or a generic conflict.
Code/reason ties use the order in the table and then reason listing order,
except stage precedence below, which wins over table order. Existing
diagnostics from earlier guards retain their own details, not remapped enums.

After usage and existing guards, validate source-ledger structure/integrity
and determine trustworthy scopes. Unaddressable corruption is ledger invalid,
not global pending. Perform a read-only conflict lookup before new admission:
valid pending blocks only a TDD evidence writer in the same repository/
CHANGE/generation/testId, including another requirement or cycle for that
test, or an explicit operation/cycle/terminal changing that pending target
or successor. Different tests/CHANGEs/generations and ordinary change-record
batch checkpoints proceed, subject to existing independent guards and brief
shared-lease serialization. Prepare/approve perform read-only conflict
inspection and cannot create/replace review prerequisites for a pending target.
All mutating TDD writers repeat that conflict lookup under their acquired
CHANGE/projection handles immediately before persistence, so a pre-lease
lookup cannot race a newly journaled pending operation.

Exact operation-key lookup is an exception to conflict rejection, evaluated
before the new-admission checks: record compares request digest, completed
returns stored success, exact pending emits `resume-required`; resume with
exact key/digest completes or returns completed; replay exact completed is
read-only success, pending emits `not-completed`; divergent digest always
emits `request-mismatch`. Unknown resume/replay emits `unknown-operation`.
Within the current active generation these recovery/replay modes do not rerun current admission, fresh execution,
or general approval. For new prepare/approve/record, after conflicts evaluate
scope/ownership/general approvals/provenance, target, source-review integrity,
block/snapshot/equivalence/replacement/report conditions, then locked drift
revalidation and persistence. Approve performs no new test run; record
test-only consumes sealed pair reports; record behavior-change executes its
fresh selected pass. No pre-journal refusal mutates requested evidence.

Details always contain operationId (null when unresolvable), scope (null only
when untrustworthy), target (null only when unresolvable), and reason; pending
also contains the blocking operationId, testId, targetCycleId, requestSha256,
artifactSha256 (journal reviewSha256), approvalSha256 and resumeArgs. These nulls
are diagnostic unknowns and never wildcard scopes. I/O errors retain safe
path/stage detail and never report completion.

DES-M5-007 derives, DES-M5-011 exposes and DES-M5-015 renders
`sourceSupersessions` in gate/status as an always-present sorted array
(CHANGE, generation, testId, journal order). Each item has exactly operationId,
scope, mode, target (cycleId/kind/order/payloadSha256/oldFingerprint), cycleId,
newFingerprint, journalOrder, nullable order, state,
selectionReason, nullable terminalSelector, requestSha256, artifactSha256,
approvalSha256 and nullable resumeArgs. The three hashes are taken from the
verified journal (artifactSha256 aliases reviewSha256), never derived from
retry-time source. They are non-null for pending/completed entries; invalid
entries use null for any unverified hash and always have resumeArgs:null.
State is
`pending | completed | invalid`, and selectionReason
`pending-suffix | invalid-evidence | greatest-terminal | older-terminal |
void-bound | open-work | outside-scope | source-drift`.
Unaddressable corrupt records appear in diagnostics rather than invented
scope entries. Pending reports `completion-required`; invalid reports its
specific diagnostic. Only completed fully verified (d) is selectable;
partial journal/order writes do not clear `TDD_TEST_STALE`, confer open-Red
suppression or hide other tests' failures. A valid pending affects readiness
only when its repository/CHANGE/generation belongs to the evaluated active
scope (or selected integration candidate set); otherwise selectionReason is
outside-scope and the entry is informational. Evaluated pending makes gate
exit 1/status exit 0 ready:false. Addressable invalid completed/source-ledger
records retain the existing integrity failure policy; global/unaddressable
corruption is never downgraded by scope. Historical valid records grant no
active coverage; completed replay success is not gate readiness.

`terminalSelector` is null unless completed/verified and otherwise is the
same exact object as an entry in always-present `sourceTerminalSelectors[]`:
`{testId, cycleId, terminalKind, terminalOrder, terminalSha256, oldFingerprint,
requirementId, command, changeId, generation, selectionReason, cliArgs}`.
The latter array exposes every verified terminal (a)-(d) relevant to the
evaluated tests, sorted by testId then verified order, including legacy
Green/Refactor/migration targets even before any source operation exists.
`oldFingerprint` is that terminal's currently recorded fingerprint (new
fingerprint for (d)); digest derivation is defined in target schema above.
`cliArgs` is a JSON argv array for the exact TARGET options, not shell text;
human status renders safely quoted copyable options. Scope values that cannot
be confirmed (legacy unscoped) are null and cannot become admission authority.
Selectors never expose a pending, unverified or ambiguous target as valid.

For valid active pending, `resumeArgs` is exactly
`["tdd","source-supersession","resume","--change",scope.changeId,
"--generation",String(scope.generation),"--operation-id",operationId,
"--request-sha256",requestSha256]`; other states use null. Human diagnostics
render `musubix5` plus safely quoted argv and the resolved `--root` when needed.
The structured argv excludes machine-local root paths; the caller invokes
it in the same resolved control context. Thus a crash before any CLI success
response is recoverable from status/pending output alone, without digest
reconstruction. A historical pending item exposes its verified hashes but
no runnable resume guidance; show CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE and retain history.

Abandon/reopen do not auto-complete, delete or waive source pending. While
holding their existing CHANGE/projection/append handles they preserve the
immutable journal/order prefix and snapshot its generation as historical;
their existing workspace checkpoint recovery remains unchanged. A later
generation has no pending inheritance or credit from it. Explicit exact
resume/replay of an abandoned or superseded source operation rejects exit 1
CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE before lease/replay and writes nothing, even for a
completed exact match. No approved requirement permits historical TDD resume;
inspection is through read-only status, not a new maintenance exception.
The pending prefix stays immutable non-credit history. All source commands
require the current active generation. During an abandoned interval existing
CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE/non-ready rules remain. Reopen with valid historical
pending can progress; it remains informational unless immutable ledger
corruption independently blocks it.

### Verification responsibilities

Future tests in `tests/tdd-source-supersession.test.ts`,
`tests/tdd-source-supersession-recovery.test.ts` and
`tests/tdd-source-supersession-cli.test.ts` cover the above schemas/CLI,
SESSION stale to approved-pair to journal-first completion to exact replay to
renewed source drift, genuine behavior-change linkage, both mode/provenance
matrices, unique-node/path/boundary rejection, outside-block byte differences,
manifest independence and tampering, and A to B to A versus identity cycles.
Crash injection covers before/after journal/order, combined chain+projection
staging fsync/atomic replacement and success response; assert zero before journal, then exactly
one journal/order/terminal join and unchanged historical bytes. Interleave
same-test refusal, different-test success, different-CHANGE success and
ordinary batch checkpoint success; resume after their order appends must use
current max+1 when absent or its exact existing order, followed by two
zero-append replays. Separate helper/runner/config/production/HEAD/candidate
post-completion mutations keep terminal source-current; actual runner failure
is separately non-ready, test-block drift is stale, approval tampering invalid.
Run existing foundation/finalization/concurrency and repair regressions
unchanged; no review/checkpoint recovery responsibility moves out of ADR-0035.
Add fixtures for all migrated tdd.json write sites and no-active maintenance
versus active writers, lease expiry/takeover, copyable selectors for (a)-(d),
source-aware orphan/dedupe validators, journal-only and journal+order pending
with unrelated successful writers, and chain-only corruption rejection.
Fingerprint-invariance fixtures cover review/approval/report/blob creation,
including failure to satisfy implementation-change. Snapshot cases cover
tracked/untracked/ignored dependency/mode/HEAD drift, path/module resolution,
declared-input mutation and known external-dependency rejection (not claims
of OS/network confinement), deterministic hunks/AST rejections,
and durable behavior-change report recovery. Abandon/reopen with pending and
other-CHANGE gate evaluation must remain informational/non-credit; historical
resume/replay rejects CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE without suffix writes.

The following are explicit future verification fixtures, not executed tests
or new authoritative TEST trace nodes in this design-only revision:

| Fixture | Measurable pass condition |
| --- | --- |
| Runner-free shared leases | Pause an ordinary TDD runner and each source pair/behavior-change runner for more than the 10s lease-acquisition timeout; during the pause a different-test same-CHANGE TDD commit, same-CHANGE batch checkpoint and parallel transition all complete before releasing the barrier. Assert no runner-held CHANGE/maintenance/projection/append handles, intact unrelated updates, and rejection of a competing same-test or abandoned-generation commit at final recheck. |
| SESSION build/output pair | With installed dependencies present but no tarball cache and initially absent dist/cache, execute the unchanged codegraph-tests selected SESSION command and its internally invoked unchanged globalSetup in both roots without install/fetch. Both reports contain exactly TEST-M5-CHECKPOINT-SESSION-001 passed; the two post-run dist inventories match byte-for-byte; all declared input digests remain stable. Instrument coordinator subprocess dispatch to assert zero install/fetch invocations; do not describe this as an OS network audit. Deliberately mutate a post-run dist inventory, package bytes or a helper and assert the specified rejection. |
| SESSION assertion guard | First restore the recorded Refactor assertion/control-flow bytes and remove the outside-block `vi` import, leaving only the reviewed paired elapsed clock-call substitution in the actual inline expect(clock() - started).toBeLessThan(10_000) form. Accept that splice after exact old-fingerprint verification; reject threshold, subtraction, units, expiry assertion, clock shadow/mock or other assertion edits. |

Demonstrate that the current implementation already satisfies that proposed assertion and assert that no Red, cycle, order, chain, checkpoint or coverage credit is recorded for it. A first passing run is never accepted as Red. |
| Writer diagnostic compatibility | Inject each acquisition/loss failure for ordinary candidate Refactor/maintenance, ordinary non-candidate and no-active Red/Green/Refactor/migrate/void/repair writers, source commands and lifecycle/finalization exceptions; assert the exact writer/context code and exit in the mapping table, including append-timeout `TDD_EVIDENCE_LEASE_BUSY` exit 1, not only lock correctness. |
| Source review release ownership | Create two CHANGEs' valid artifact/approval JSON; verify top-level owner equality/hash binding, exact existing foreign-evidence exclusion and rejection of scope/owner mismatches. Keep the release selector and opaque blob inclusion rules unchanged. |

Do not assert detection of arbitrary host reads or network calls. |

Test abandoned/superseded variants return CHANGE_GENERATION_PHASE with byte-identical pending prefixes. |

Cascade-invalid batches and quality stay non-current until normal re-recording; replay is hash-neutral and renewed block drift is stale. |
